I just had my first chai tea latte, and it was delicious!  It doesn't taste like tea at all, nor does it taste like coffee or flavored coffee, or flavored milk for that matter.  It's a taste all it's own -- and sweet but not overpowering sweet (I can't stand anything too sugary).  This is going to become a staple in my household.  Even if you're not a tea fan, I'd say give it a try.  I am very pleasantly surprised by it.

I was able to taste this coffee, even though my Dolce Gusto coffee maker broke.  fyi, the Dolce Gusto has a user screen that over time, for me, started to fritz more and more, showing only a blank screen - the internal software apparently can fritz quite a bit.  That screen is where you choose the type coffee you want to make and also where you are told to insert the coffee capsules, etc., so when it's blank you have to guess.  The coffee tastes a bit stale, unfortunately.  fyi, when my Dolce-Gusto machine broke, the Dolce Gusto folks, after having me on the phone for an hour having me look at minute serial numbers and trying to noodle out where I bought it, made it clear that they are only in search of marketing info - but they only told me that AFTER wasting my time, when they sent me on to a different company to start the complaint process all over again.  The machine is going back, and I won't be buying this coffee anymore!  Having tried almost every flavor, none of them were good enough to justify the hassle or the per cup expense.  I also own a Senseo, that uses paper per serving pods instead of the Dolce Gusto plastic per serving capsules, and the bottom line is that I'll happily  stick with my tried and true simple, more  environmentally friendly, paper single serving pods Hamilton Beach brewer  Hamilton Beach Two Way Brewer Single Serve and 12 cup Coffee Maker

These breakfast cookies are absolutely delicious, handy if on the go, and not too fattening if watching one's weight.  Only 170 calories, and just as filling as a bowl of cereal but with less calories.  And what's not to like about a cookie for breakfast????

column9: Great organic crackers at a good price
column10: I ordered these crackers about two weeks ago, not knowing how they would be. Turns out they are delicious! A little plain tasting, which was expected, with just the right amount of salt for my tastes and a subtle but pleasant hint of olive oil. They seem to go very well with several cheeses, soup and on their own, too. I recommend them to anyone who likes Saltines or other plain, salted crackers - however I find these to be significantly less salty than Saltines. Enjoy.

I bought a package of these from our local natural foods store (at almost twice the price!).  My 4-year old loves Saltines with tuna salad, but I wanted crackers without all the additives and mystery ingredients.  These are a perfect substitution!The taste is very close to regular Saltines, close enough that my son didn't blink an eye when I gave these to him.  They're not as sturdy, to be sure, so it's not a cracker that can stand up to spreading a harder cheese.  However, tuna salad or soft cheeses go on just fine.  I tried them myself topped with thin slices of raw cheddar and they tasted delicious.I don't taste the olive oil at all.  The salt is lighter than Nabisco, but still well-seasoned. The small interior packages are nice for keeping each serving of crackers fresh and crispy.Now that I know Amazon carries these, I'll be signing up for the Subscribe and Save option to keep a nice stash in the cupboard.

These crackers are the best-tasting saltines we've ever had.  We LOVE them!  They are light, not too salty, with a delicate smattering of olive oil.  The ingredient list is short --only four items!  I buy them by the case for our family of four and they don't stick around long enough to get stale.  They are GREAT to take along to a party if you're serving crackers and cheese.  I strongly recommend them.
Used to have 'sea salt' and now just 'salt'.Still crumbly. Traces of sesame seed.New packaging is nice but I don't eat packaging.

I didn't want to buy a pack of 12, but I needed to find a healthy alternative to those super salty saltine crackers for my daughter. Wow these taste fantastic. Not as salty. They almost taste fresh! I think we'll finish 12 packs easily and we can order more. This is awesome!
These crackers are the best crackers I have ever tasted. We eat them everyday for snacks. I don't like to be out of them as I can only get them at health food stores and Amazon.
I love these crackers cause the ingredients are just wheat flour, olive oil, salt & water. Yummy too, I'm eating some now as I write.
These saltines taste wonderful. Light, crispy, lightly salty. They taste the most like conventional saltines made by Nabisco(?) of the two organic brands I've tried. I highly recommend them!

This order of crackers was burned, the entire case! The tops of the crackers were falling off because of it.If you like burned crackers, then these are for you.The price has also increased. Let's see now, burned crackers, super high price. Do you really want to purchase this item?Where oh where is Susie and quality control?
Crisp and tasty.  Plus, they are well packed and mine were delivered with basically no crushed or damaged packages.

column9: This has become my favorite cracker!
column10: I love this cracker! It's light and crisp. No more stale crackersbecause the crackers come in individually wrapped 100 calorie packets,10 per package. You can taste the olive oil but it's just right, notoverwhelming. I will buy these crackers again.
Low calorie for crackers, good taste, like how they are individually packaged per serving.

column9: Very Good Organic Saltine Crackers But Too Crumbly
column10: These saltine crackers taste very good but they are so crumbly that as soon as you take a bite, you end up with crumbs all over the place. I like the idea that they are organic and use healthy olive oil, but they would be more nutritious if they contained whole wheat flour instead of just wheat flour.Also, I would prefer if they cut down the amount of packages per box, so that I'm not opening a cellophane package for every 4 double-crackers I eat or serve.

I bought these bags to go with Exaco Trading ECO-2000 2.4 Gallon Kitchen Compost Waste Collector that I purchased on Amazon. The bags fit perfectly, but they seem to start degrading within a few days. If I took out compost every day, it would be fine, but I empty my compost bucket about twice a week. When I lift a bag to take it outside, it is dripping, so I have to take the whole bucket out and scrub it thoroughly afterwards to get rid of the odor. Previously, when I used a regular plastic shopping bag, leakage was almost never a problem, but it is a regular occurance with these liners. I like that the bags are biodegradable, but rather than purchasing these again, I'll probably go back to re-using plastic bags when my supply runs out--unless I find a sturdier brand. Any suggestions?

I use this to line the compost collection can I keep under the sink or I use one when I am doing a big cooking project to gather compostable items.  If I let things set in the bag more than 5 days the bags start to leak as they start to break down.  And breaking down is what I want them to do as I put them into my compost bin.  Even in winter I notice that they start breaking down rather quickly.  I am sure by spring when I am ready to use my compost these bags will be fully intergrated into my compost.

Here in San Francisco, we have to compost our food garbage, and these bags fit nicely into the compostable bins supplied by the garbage company. Even though they are only 1 gallon, a lot can be put into them. There is no smell as these bags are high quality.

Its not that these bags are bad - its really more that it takes some time to get used to a compostable bag!!  they aren't as 'strong' as the regular bags you're probably used to (and that goes for me too) so it has taken me some time to get used to the fact these bags don't stand up very long to let's say compost material - but I will say that if you are diligent about getting your composte down to the bin more frequently it is nice to be able to just throw bag and all into the bin!

column9: I have the opposite problem of most other reviewers...
column10: in that my bags don't break down at all.  I put them in my compost pile each week but over time (approaching 9 months since I put the first bag in) I've ended up with a compost pile consisting of about 40 intact bags - like having 40 separate compost piles.  I actually had to take the waste out of each bag and mix everything then throw out the bags themselves in the garbage.  I'll just get normal small trash bags at this point and empty the waste out of those each week.  That's what I've ended up doing with the "compostable" bags but at a lot higher price.I wished they worked ...

The way I understand it, these bags are biodegradable in your "municipality" and take anywhere from 9 to 24 weeks. I not sure if this is made for home compost use (taking a long time to decompose). If your getting them for your "garbage pick-up" and not pressed for time, these will be great!

I have recently started composting and have searched for several months for compostable bags that are sturdy enough to last until the bag is full. I have tried a few different brands, and so far been disappointed with bags that begin to break down as soon a bit of food scraps are thrown in, which makes for a yucky clean up at the end of a day or two when the bag is full and ready to go in my compost bin. I thought I had finally found a bag that was exactly what I had been looking for when I received these EcoSafe "Compostable Bags". They were sturdy and well made, and at the end of a couple days in my kitchen compost pail, they had not broken down at all! They were perfect. But, like my mother always said, if it seems too good to be true, it probably is. The reason these bags didn't break down in my compost pail is because they are not compostable at all! They don't break down in the compost bin either. I wondered what was going on, so I did a little research and discovered that these bags have no business going into a compost bin. They are made out of plastic and not "green" at all.  They "bio-degrade" into tiny pellets of plastic.  Personally, I do not like toxic plastic in my compost, being absorbed by my fruit and vegetable plants, so needless to say I am once again disappointed and feel that these bags are being falsely advertised as compost bags.
These bags are supposed to compost away after being used, however they also decompose while being used causing leaks in the bin. Quite messy when removed from bin.
These liners work great to use in our kitchen composting container.  When they're full, I just take it out to the larger bin and my container is clean and ready to be refilled.
No issue with leakage or anything, these are the BEST!!  And at a wonderful price.  I compost alot and these are very helpful, better bag that all the competitors!

Just received these bags today. The box they come in is very small and made of 100% recycled material. A bonus in my book. The bags seem to have alot of strength and dont seem like they will rip or break open easily. I just received them today so hopefully after a few uses I can submit more feedback with more positive outcomes.

I've been using these bags for more than a year, to collect organic garbage (fruit & vegetable peels, egg shells, etc.). It usually takes me 2-4 days to fill up each bag, and I rarely experience any leaks from the bags. Overall they seem to be durable, and do their jobs well.

column9: works great w Exaco 2.4 gal collector
column10: we've been using these bags with Exaco Trading ECO-2000 2.4 Gallon Kitchen Compost Waste Collector for a couple months now and they work great.my only gripe is I wish they were a wee bit bigger as it falls into the collector (or perhaps tighter around the top so it could stretch)other than that, they work fine!

column9: works as I need it to
column10: I have no problem with these bags.  They work just as I expected them to and do not leak at all will order again.
Perhaps it's because I fill them too much, but the bags leak liquid from fruits, etc. They seem sturdy but don't hold up to a lot of weight.

I bought these through another site. The picture of the bag composting was very convincing, but now that I've used them I can say that they don't compost per statement.  I have used these bags to collect food scraps to take over to my compost bin.  Over a year later they are still there.  I had my husband cut an opening of our compost bin thinking I could get some finished compost out on the very bottom. The plastic tears easier now but still in one piece, was thinking it wouldn't be identifiable.UPDATE I found info regarding "compostable" at plasticsindustry.org and here's a paragraph of what "compostable" means: "In order to breakdown, compostable bags must be sent to an industrial composting facility, not backyard piles or municipal composting centers. There are very few of these facilities in the U.S. and where these facilities are not available, compostable bags will sit in landfills because theycan't be recycled."  Shocking or what?!

column9: Pricey but couldn't find the smaller size in store.
column10: I bought these because I could only find the 33 gallon Husky EcoGuard Lawn & Leaf bags locally. While they are somewhat thinner than the EcoGuard, they do get the job done. For the $9.99 price at the time, I was able to purchase 25 of these 2.5 gallon bags for a little more than the price of 10 of the larger bags available locally.

column9: SERVE THE PURPOSE, BUT THEY LEAK
column10: I LOVE THAT THESE ARE BIODEGRADEABLE, AND I'M SURE IT'S BECAUSE OF THAT FACT THAT I HAVE MY ONLY COMPLAINT--THEY LEAK. WE DON'T CHANGE OUR COMPOSTER EVERYDAY (MORE LIKE ONCE EVERY 3-6 DAYS) AND THE COMPOSTER ALWAYS HAS FLUID ON THE BOTTOM. SOMEWHAT DEFEATS THE PURPOSE, BUT I CONTINUE TO BUY THEM ANYWAY...

These trash bags did not come close to fitting my 2.5 gallon bath trash can.  They did not fit and they were cheaply made.  I paid a big price for 25 trash bags.  I would send them back if I did not have to pay postage.Plastic grocery bags are much more effective and thicker.
These are not quite big enough for the ASIN:B0017WOFSI Exaco Trading ECO-2000 2.4 Gallon Kitchen Compost Waste Collector. They do compost well, though.

This makes taking out the compostables so much easier I wish I had started using them years ago. No more washing the compost can daily. Just grab the bag and drop it on the compost pile on my way to the car!

This bag is large enough to hold a lot of scraps for composting.  They do not break down to quickly and hold their strength in the container.  They do separate from the each other nicely, no tearing.  I do recommend them.
These are nice sturdy food can compostible bags.  They are better than any other brand because they are not flimsy and do not tear.  Would highly recommend.

column9: Bags don't fit my 2.4 gallon slimline compost bin
column10: These are supposed to be 2.5 gallon capacity but they don't fit the oval shape of my kitchen composter.Slimline Compost Caddy

I've used this product for over six months now and have had no problems.  The size is perfect for the compost container I have and the bags hold up terrifically.  I usually change the bag once per week and have never had problems with leakage.  I highly recommend this product.

I know others have had issues with the bags breaking down or leaking, however, I have not had this trouble at all. I dump my kitchen compost bin about two to three times a week and so far have had not problems with splitting or leaking bags. I am highly impressed by this product and just returned to purchase two more boxes.

These compostable bags are definitely that. They will break down, and so are pretty perfect for your typical compostable kitchen waste. However, they are super thin and will break down in your composting bin as well. Maybe not every time, but we have seen about 25% of them begin to break down and leak long before we actually fill it our bin. I would say the average time before the bag begins to leek is around a week. Like I say, not all these bags are apparently created equal, as some do maintain their integrity longer, but it isnt something I would rely on. You are better served changin it out at least once a week, and maybe more often. Dont wait just because you havent prepped as many veggies and fruit this week.

column9: Works well for 1 gallon compost pail
column10: We bought these to work with our 1gallon stainless steel countertop pail, I was worried the size would be a problem, this is not the case we simpy fold the bag on the outside of the pail. we have something to grab and tie te bag when the pail is full. No dirty hands and no need to clean out the pain each time we go to the compost pile.It's to early I say he long it will take for these to break down but at least they are biodegradable !
I bought these for my compost bin.  They work fine, but could be just a bit longer when the bin gets 3/4 full.

I purchased these "bio-degradable" bags for my son to use for a Science Fair Project.  According to the manufacturer specifications, these bags were supposed to decompose within "10-45" days; well, my son had 3 sections of a bag, outside, in the elements, for over 45 days and guess what? No signs of decompostion whatsoever!  My son was extremely disappointed as was I.  If you going to pay all this money to help save the enviornment then the product needs to really work!  I would NOT recommend these bags to anyone!

column9: A gift of a different kind
column10: What do you get for the person who already has just about everything? A nice gift basket would be nice, but finding one with just the right treats in it at a reasonable price is tiresome shopping. Amazon has a large selection of unique foods. When it comes to a gift... some things just gather dust or your intended receiver doesn't need another cell phone, mp3, or maybe doesn't have your taste in art, but I can always remember what a friend likes to eat. I chose Italian foods cookies and a nostalgic collection of candies from the 40s for my mother. She really enjoyed the gifts that arrived in time for the holiday. Best of all, I didn't have to haul everything down to the already overworked postal workers and keep my fingers crossed for weeks that everything would arrive in good condition.  Amazon and their associates have always given me good value and quick neat shipping. The customer service that the associates have given me is the type of service that even the pickiest person cold find no fault with. I am very pleased with my Amazon shopping experience.Amazon shopping gave me a way to get a gift to my mother in The United States while I sat at my computer in Brazil.  I also sell my books MAN'S BEST FRIEND and RED SKY IN THER MORNING: The Post KATRINA Cover-up, through Amazon and for reading on Amazon Kindle.Mark James Chappell

column9: Delicious product but made with ingredients from China
column10: I really do like these to snack on however I'm really put off by the fact that this company always imports their ingredients from China. I'm Asian and I just never purchase food products from China. Most Asians don't purchase food from China either. I know these are not made in China however you just never know what type of pesticides and what kind of contaminants are in their soil that inevitable ends up in nuts and fruits used in these products. Just to err on the side of caution I will not be purchasing this product again.
The nuts used tasted very fresh. The bite sized chunks were just right. It is lightly sweetened but not too sweet. Very satisfying = )

column9: Mrs. May's Dry-Roasted Snack, Almond Crunch 5 oz. Pouches
column10: This is such a delicious, nutritious snack--not too sweet, not salty. I often use it after crushing it a bit as a topping for desserts (i.e. pudding or ice-cream/fresh cut fruit/compotes) and always get lots of compliments for the desserts. It keeps indefinitely if kept sealed in it's convenient ziploc packaging, so I purchase a pack of 24 at one time.  My husband and children love it as a snack, too.

column9: For people who like almond snacks
column10: This product could best be described as pieces of almond brittle.  It is a Vegan snack comprised mainly of almonds, evaporated cane juice, and a little salt.  The main problem is that they list a "serving" as 7 pieces rather than one package.  Anyone opening a package will probably eat the entire package.  The 7 piece serving has 176 calories with 14 grams of vegetable fat (from the almonds), 4 grams of sugar (from the glaze), 4 grams of protein, and 2 grams of fiber.For comparison, one ounce of lightly salted almonds is listed as having 16 grams fat, 6 grams protein, and 3 grams fiber.The product is an attractive snack for any purpose.  It can be dropped into your travel bag, backpack, desk drawer, etc.  The product is reasonably durable (not overly sensitive to temperature) and is in easy to tear open foil packs.

I really love this as a simple, quick snack! It is very flavorful and best of all, it is good for you! No nasty, overprocessed chemicals, fillers and sugars. The little bite size clusters are fantastic! Love It!!

What a great snack product!  I love it because it is wholesome and nutritious.I would recommend as a good item for lunch and anytime snack.Mrs. May's Dry-Roasted Snack, Almond Crunch, 5-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 12)

column9: Tasty, HEALTHY, with LOW  carbs, low sodium TREATS!!!!!
column10: I had these at a meeting, and FELL in love with them!Low calories, TASTY, low carbs, low Sodium!!!And they are WITHOUT the wheat, whey and gluten additives and OTHER preservatives!I purchased some at Costco, here and they are SO liked, that Trader Joes's is also carrying them.They come in individual serving sizes to prevent over-indulgence.
These nuts are excellent, just a light glaze to sweeten tham a bit!
These noodles are delicious for cup of noodles. My family and I love them. We were buying them at the local superstore but they fly off the shelves!

I'm glad I only paid $1 for this product.  It wasn't the 6-pack, just an individual package.It was neither rich nor savory.  The broth itself had absolutely no flavor.  Then I added the flavor booster.  It smelled and looked like motor oil and made the soup very unappetizing.  I drained the "broth" and ate the noodles because I was hungry.  Don't waste you hard earned cash!

After trying just about every brand out there, I gave these a try.  Not only are they low fat and natural but both of my very picky dogs LOVE THEM! When you open the box, they actually smell really good.  I would recommend these to any dog owner but especially if your dog is finicky.

column4: Donna's Reviews "I Love Shopping on Amazon!"
column9: Great price but dog wouldn't eat them!~
column10: Great price but dog wouldn't eat them!~Blue Dog Bakery Natural Low Fat Dog Treats, Assorted Flavors, 20-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)....they're also hard as bricks!~

I was looking forward to providing these treats to our two small dogs but made the mistake of buying six boxes because I thought my dogs would 'for sure' like them based on the reviews. They ate them for a few days, then I started discovering them around the garden. Unfortunately, they didn't like them. Others have written about how good they smell, that they crumble easily etc - I don't think they're any different than any other dog biscuit. They're large, but they break into pieces just fine (without crumbling). I'd suggest you buy a single box to see if your dog actually likes them.
i was so excited to give these treats to my dog. she only nibbled on it for a second before walking away from it. she doesn't like any of the flavors.

column4: Scary Gertrude,  the Bad Sheriff for Life "Li...
column10: My border collie will no longer eat a snack unless it is one of the Blue Dog Bakery snacks.  Offered a regular snack, he sniffs and walks away.  This is a very smart dog and he knows what he likes.Honestly, once you open the package, you will understand.  It smells good.  Have you ever opened a dog snack and thought it smelled like freshly baked cookies?  These do.  I never, ever, imagined that dog snacks could smell so good.Lucky they don't make cat snacks.The only flaw with this product is that they do go stale.  I ordered a lot of a bunch of flavors on a Friday sale, I think, and the last box of six smelled a little stale to me.  The dog did not mind at all!

Cats aren't truly domesticated. They are wild animals who attached themselves to humans for comfort reasons. Deep inside, a cat is still a little tiger or cougar, ready to lash out at kids, neighbours or some poor sparrows.Dogs, on the other hand, now that's a domesticated animal, alright. Lazy, silly, funny and co-dependent. That's a dog for you. In fact, I'm surprised dogs even bother chasing cats. I mean, what's the story? If you give Fido this dog candy, I'm sure he'll forget about El Tigre in no time!But hey, don't open ten cans of dog food while you're away on holiday, the silly doggie will eat all of them at once, get the stomache ache of the century, and then probably die of malnutrition. They can't take care of themselves. Co-dependency, that's the word.Small wonder dogs have attached themselves to a certain primate known as "modern man". The similarity is striking. Like master, like dog.

column9: Blue Dog Low Fat Doggie Cookies
column10: They are cute to look at, made for the human people, not the canine people.  Toby liked them at first, then was hesitant and now he eats them only when he feels like it.

My golden is a finicky eater and didn't really care for the treats.  He seems to like the soft treats better than the hard ones.  And when he does eat one of the treats it ends up in little pieces on the floor.

Blue Dog Bakery Premium Natural Low Fat Dog Treats, Peanut Butter & Molasses, 20-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)These are an excellent product.  I first started buying them for my two large dogs, and both love their treats.  Unfortunately, they are both slightly overweight.  These are perfect, as they are low fat and made from natural ingredients.  They must taste great, as my dogs always want them at treat time.I highly recommend Blue Dog Bakery Premium Natual Low Fat Dog Treats to anyone who is looking for a healthy, low fat, appealing dog treat for their dogs.

The dogs love these, the only thing I would caution is that they are on the large size.  So though they would be a great snack for large active dogs, they are a bit too much for a puppy and a slightly overweight scottie dog. Some of the shapes are so large they make a meal for a smaller dog.  And they are not they easiest things to break apart. But as stated above the dogs love them, in fact they smell so good they could tempt a human.

column9: Blue Dog Bakery Cookies Get Four Paws Rating
column10: My Yellow Lab prefers these cookies over several other well known brands.  Yes, they are hard as several reviewers have noted - all the better for helping to reduce tarter thru chewing hard cookies or biscuits which in turn helps to promote healthier gums.  I find the hardness of these cookies no different from say Milk Bone Dog Biscuits which my Lab also loves.  I spoke to my Vet about these dry, hard cookies and, based upon the ingredients listed on the cookie box, he saw nothing wrong with giving them as a treat BUT as with any other treat, only in moderation.  He also surmised that the hardness of the cookies could help in reducing tarter buildup.  I give my Lab either one of the larger sized or two of the smaller sized cookies per day.  They make a nice treat after his evening walk.  (He gets a Milk Bone after his morning stroll).  I've purchased both the peanut butter & molasses as well as these assorted flavors cookies and my Lab loves them all.  He gives these Blue Dog Bakery cookies a "Four Paws" rating.

column9: My Lab loves them and my friend's picky Heeler does too
column10: I have a Chocolate Lab who admittedly likes alot (but not all) treats ... but he loves these and they are good for him. I gave a box of them to a friend who has a Queensland Heeler who has gotten old and very cranky about what he will and wont eat. Friend was delighted that his dog enjoyed them so much that he got all perky and happy when he knew he was about to get one.

column4: BILL MCLEAN "Only My Opinion - Compare with O...
column10: Sadie is a six year old German Shephard and comes to me asking for dog biscuits whenever she wants one.  I ask her if she wants to go outside and she just looks at me.  I ask her if she wants a dog biscuit and she sticks her tongue out.  That means "yes."Sadie really likes the Blue Dog biscuit more than any others.  I can tell because she asks for one three times a day.Right now it's very hot here in Medford, Oregon, and sadie only wants to go out to "do her duty."  I worry that she is getting too fat.  What a spoiled brat!

column9: Wow, are you sure these are for dogs?
column10: I've purchased Blue Dog Bakery treats before in the store and was pleasantly surprised by how wonderful they smelled.  I even tried a small piece myself - not bad, not bad at all!  Are you sure these are for dogs?I bought the Assorted Flavors here on Amazon because of the terrific value.  I am currently "dog aunt" to a couple of mutts and I take great pride in spoiling them rotten.  They love these treats.  I love that the treats are hard and crunchy, good for their teeth, and that they are made right here in America from all natural human, food ingredients.  As I said before, they smell great and you could probably chow down on these yourself - but I wouldn't recommend it unless you have strong teeth!  Will definitely buy these again for my buddies.

Well, I can't really say that first hand...but my GSD/Husky, Jake, seems to adore them!  He's proven himself a fairly picky eater when it comes to dog treats. Even the 5-star rated goodies have received an upturned nose from this pooch.  The Blue Dog Bakery treats are definitely an exception. They are sizeable morsels, but can be easily broken down when used for training.  They come in assorted flavors and all of them seem to strike a chord with Jake.  You can practically see the smile on his face, the swagger in his step, and the sway of his tail when he knows he's getting one of these morsels from Heaven. OK, I may be overstating it, but these are truly some dynamic dog treats that Jack and I would highly recommend to most the finnicky canine!

These are great, we bought the assorted and Tommy loves them. They smell yummy too. I bought it in the bulk, and they were still pretty fresh. I would definitely recommend them if your dog is a bit overweight or obese. Plus, change their food to organic, grain free diets. It works miracles.

First of all, I would totally eat these in a pinch... they smell SO GOOD! My Tibetan Terrier loves them He's a medium size and although the cookies are bigger, he woofs them down with no problem. The neighbor doggies love them too. They also come in smaller sizes.

column9: Excellent Treats- but cheaper at the store....
column10: I would definitely get these from Amazon, but they actually cost more than I pay for them locally.  However, these treats are healthy and my dogs love them.  They love the MEATY ones, not to keen on the molasses, veggies.

I bought this after looking for a healthy snack for my dogs for quite a while, and being impressed by the great Amazon reviews.I simply hereby proclaim, these are the tastiest dog treats I've ever had.  I make it a point to taste a little bit of everything I feed my dogs; with the exception that a little bit of this turned into a whole cookie.My dogs love them too.

My dogs go absolutely wild for the Blue Dog treats.  I get the assorted flavors, and there is not one that doesn't get inhaled.  I find them easy to break, but I'm just not fast enough for the pups.  I think they could eat a whole box in one sitting if I let them.  These are simply the best treats for your dog.

My little Milo absolutely LOVES these treats!He's a small dog (14 pounds), but normally I give him a whole treat. Are they bigger than normal treats? Yes, but he doesn't seem to get more.When I first got him, I was giving him Milkbones, which he loved. When I first gave him one of these, at first he didn't know what to do with it, but that quickly changed.He now licks the treat like Popsicles before actually eating it. I'm assuming that means he likes them more.Highly recommended.

column9: Genmai Cha Green Tea with Roasted Brown Rice
column10: Overall this is a great product if you are a loose leaf tea drinker.  I say overall because, like most things, there are pluses and minuses.  I have been drinking loose leaf teas for about ten years now.  I would not rank myself as an expert, but I have sampled many varieties and flavors which I suppose gives me some degree of knowledge.I usually purchase a different brand Genmaicha which I have grown accustomed to over the years.  In my research this other tea is about what you would expect from a Genmaicha: loose leaf green tea with roasted brown rice in about a 50-50 ratio.  The Shirakiku I am reviewing now is somewhat different.  This "Genmai Cha" (note the spelling difference)seems to consist mostly of roasted brown rice with some loose leaf green tea and the addition of Matcha tea.  If you are not familiar with Matcha tea is is a Japanese tea variety which is commonly used in tea ceremonies.  It is in powdered form and prepared by being whisked into water not brewed and strained like loose leaf tea.  Had I known that this tea was manufactured the way it is I don't think that I would have purchased it.  That said, I am still happy with my purchase and enjoy this tea on a daily basis.My critique of the drinkability of the tea itself is a mixed bag.  The flavor is "in the neighborhood" of my usual Genmaicha.  However it is definitely not the same.  The bready flavor of the roasted rice is overpowered by the Matcha tea.  In addition, to me Matcha tea is somewhat akin to instant tea.  Although many may disagree strongly with that statement, it is how I feel.  I simply prefer brewed loose leaf tea, and since I was not aware of the nature of this tea, I suppose I am a little dissapointed.  In the cup the tea is very cloudy.  Genmaicha in general is a cloudy cup due to the rice.  The Genmai Cha is about twice as cloudy, due in part to the Matcha and also the high percentage of roasted rice that I mentioned earlier.The other factors to consider with this tea is the quantity and the pricing.  The Shirakiku comes in two vacuum sealed bricks weighing 2.2 pounds (1 Kilogram) each.  That means that you get about 4.4 pounds of tea in total.  That's a lot of tea!  Which leads me to the price.  After tax and with free shipping through Amazon I paid less than $10.50 per pound of tea.  This is less than half of what I would expect to pay for my usual brand.Overall the tea is a great value.  Cost per pound is very low, but 2 Kilograms is a lot of tea.  And the flavor is very good.  So I would have to say that I took away two stars for the introduction of the Matcha tea, but I added one star for the amazing value this tea offers.Pros:Cost per poundFlavor is very goodCons:4.4 pounds of tea (you will be drinking it for a long time....)Not a true Genmaicha (at least not to purists)Lots of sediment at the bottom of the cup

column9: What a wonderful pairing of teas

The genmaicha portion is tasty, and the matcha (which always comes only as a powder, even for tea ceremony) isn't too heavy, with enough added in to give it plenty of flavor. This tea is good for drinking hot or cold, and can easily be made cup by cup or pitcher at a time.Sometimes there is confusion about matcha and genmaicha. Genmaicha tends to be a more subtle flavor, while often people describe matcha as "grassy" and "bitter", but the flavor changes a bit when added to other things, so it is a very complimentary flavor. Matcha is considered very healthy partly because, instead of drinking tea leaf-infused water, you are drinking the actual tea leaves, since the matcha is a fine powder. There are different quality levels of matcha, and while the matcha in this tea isn't the highest, it is still very tasty, and I have been drinking it for years. Additionally, there is no difference between "genmai cha" and "genmaicha." It's just where the translators decided to break the word. (Similar to "icecream" and "ice cream.") The "matchairi" in the label of the tea means that the tea contains matcha.

I just keep on drinking my SPORTea, and a cold never seems to arrive with any sort of significance.IT really works for me, and performs as it claims it will.  EXCELLENT BEVERAGE IF CHOICE !

A bit unusual, subtle fruity / herbal sweetness. Not necessary to add any sweetener. Two bags make 1/2 gallon. I've been drinking this tea for over 15 years and it is the most satisfying iced tea I've ever had! (Great if you're a diabetic!) Best if you let it steep over night before drinking. Best pricing at this time thru Amazon.
I would drink nothing but Sportea iced or hot if it was possible.  The stuff is fantastic, and so good for you.

I found SportTea locally at Alterra and couldn't get enough of it.  It's light, refreshing, and thirst quenching and has no caffeine which was especially appreciated since I am pregnant.  I usually drink about 1 liter a day and it really does seem to help me wake up a bit in the morning.
Sportea has a mild tea flavor - great for sipping on hot summer days or anytime you're thirsty.  I switched from soft drinks to this a few years ago and have never regretted the switch.
I love drinking this tea in summer. It's refreshing and has a little natural zip. It has enough natural flavor that you don't need any sweetener.

Once again, Amazon has saved me some big headaches looking for my favorite products. I used to order this direct from the manufacturer, and they kept trying to sell me a case, which is WAY too much. Then they add shipping. With Amazon's super saver shipping, I save money & time!Thanks again Amazon!

I've been using SPORTea for years thanks to the recommendation of a boss I once had. It's hard to describe the taste of SPORTea, it's very unique. It is clean and very refreshing especially as an ice cold tea for use in cycling (or any active sport). At least try it once if you are the sporting type.

I found this tea visiting Woodloch Spa in the NorthEast (awesome spa if you're interested.) Living in the South I needed to find a low calorie substitute to the traditional sweet tea that's everywhere. Sport Tea is wonderful! It is a very mild tea--it doesn't compare at all to sweet tea or Lipton. It has a light, gingery taste. I also love that you brew it overnight in cold water in the fridge--no boiling water!

I love tea, but I also unfortunately love coke..... This really keeps me satisfied as far as a flavored beverage is concerned.  It also meets all of my healthy standards (sugarfree, artificial sweetener free, not carbonated, etc.).  Love it.
SPORTea is the best drink around. After drinking at an aunts house for years, I was finally able to find it online. I would recommend this drink to anyone. Buy this product with confidence!!
I drink it when I bike and I love it. Great taste, full of nutrients...and no sugar.

We buy the larger bags & make "sun tea" with it (we put 4 in a large old pickle jar & set it out in the sun to steep). It makes a very refreshing tea. Very naturally energizing with little caffeine. We highly recommend this tea! So much so that we drink it very day.

I was introduced to SporTea in a restaurant in Colorado while on vacation a few yrs ago. I asked what it was. It took me about 6 mos of looking once I got home to KC, but I found it and have been drinking it every since. Finding it on Amazon was a blessing - I am now able to get 4 boxes for the same price I was buying 3 boxes at my local Wild Oats store.  Thank you

column9: if you ever go outdoors, this tea is for you
column10: Nothing beats thirst better than clean cold spring water. But if for any reason you need to boil your water, this tea would be just as good. And it tastes good too! Add a few drops of stevia to a tea and your kids will not ask  for Coca-Cola. Drink it cold at summer, or hot at winter, as a wake me up and as a cool me down.Try it during your next backpacking trip and you will not miss your coffee.

I am a Foodie and always looking for a unique staple product and this is one of those rare finds. I served at a recent get together and was asked where I purchased. It would be great if Whole Foods or similar stores would have them in stock.

I came across this brand while traveling and was thrilled to see it on amazon.  This is an incredibly delicious oil that adds flavor without overpowering the natural taste of good foods.  If you are like me and always on the lookout for a tasty, healthy way to improve your meals - look no further.  This is my go to olive oil.  I ordered several bottles today to give in holiday basket gifts.

column9: A Different Type of Olive Oil - Worth A Try!
column10: I've learned to like olive oils as dipping oils and sometimes for cooking but I didn't know that there is more to olive oils than meets the eye.  It's just like looking for fine wine.  This olive oil has a very subtle aroma with a robust flavor and slight bitterness to it (which I understand is more for cooking rather than for dipping.)  I'm excited to use this to enhance flavors with my pasta, salads and meat dishes.  If you love olive oils, you might want to try this because it is a different type of olive oil than what you are probably used to buying before.  It's made from 200yr old olive trees from Spain and I doubt if you can get the same taste anywhere else in the world.

Lovers of fine Spanish olive oils will appreciate the depth of flavors in this Extra Virgin Olive Oil. It delivers plenty of ripe flavors up front with a "robust" finish. The oil from the Picual olive is a bold, peppery and full-flavored olive oil, ideal for spicy dishes like stews and gazpacho. Highly recommended!

Tried this olive oil at a friend's house and it is DELICIOUS.  I usually do not like most olive oils but I have to say this was the best tasting olive oil I have ever had.  I cannot wait to get my own and I will definately be using it for my upcoming holiday gatherings.

It's a little odd to get 8 loose K-cups in a package, but I couldn't figure out another way to go through a number of them, from different brands, to see what I wanted before ordering 24 of them.  Glad I did... some of the items in this package tasted great, some of them were mediocre, and a few were vile, one brand of cider tasting remarkably similar to what Red Bull and shampoo mixed together probably tastes like.

So I had tried a few various hot cocoa k-cups from various brands, and they were all gross.  Obviously, I had picked the wrong ones, so I got this sampler pack - various flavors from various brands.  And guess what!  They're all gross.There's no two ways about it, folks.  While I can't name them (because after I taste them, I throw them away and forget about them as soon as I can), I've tried no fewer than 10 hot chocolate k-cups from different companies, and they're all disgusting.  Are people so far removed from what good tasting hot chocolate is supposed to taste like that they settle for this?  That said, if you don't mind:1.  A slight chemical taste.2.  A bitter taste.3.  An artificial sweetener tasteThen you might enjoy hot chocolate k-cups.  In the meantime:  buy some cocoa powder, whole milk, and unrefined evaporated cane juice (sugar), and make some deliciousness yourself!  You can even pre-mix the cocoa powder and sugar, so all you have to do is warm the milk and stir!  Not quite as easy, but at least you'll get something that tastes good.Not to place all the blame on this particular product, but I wouldn't recommend any of the flavors I received OR any of the ones I've tried that come in a k-cup.  Two stars instead of one because I'm feeling generous, and most of the cocoa had a pleasant aroma.  Bummer about the taste.
This is a good mix.  We are new to Keurig and I wanted to try a couple of mixes without buying a bunch of one kind.

I ordered this product to make rose flavored cupcakes.  I got the recipe from a cookbook by the owners of the Primrose Bakery in London.  The cupcakes were very delicious and I was so glad that Amazon deals with these distributors.  I did not have to pay a huge shipping cost, even though the rose water is from France.  I live in a town that does not have a gourmet food store.  I was lucky to have a friend who owns  her own bakery and gave me the great advice not to use too much of the rose water or it can make the cakes bitter.  So, use it sparingly.  I followed the recipe and it turned out great but I would have been tempted to use more.  It is supposed to be a very subtle flavor.  I also got the orange blossom water and it was a fine product too.
Scent of natural roses,I baked the french roulette with rose water flavor ,it was delicious! thanks to the seller and the maker!

column9: Delicious addition to my baker's pantry
column10: I have been having this coconut sugar in my tea each morning, and it adds an amazing rich flavor. It reminds me of jaggery, a coconut palm sugar used in Sri Lankan desserts. Today I made a banana bread with it, and it came out great. You can substitute it 1 for 1 with white sugar as far as texture is concerned. The added depth of flavor was a really nice addition to the bread. I could not tell the difference between the blond version and the regular version - they look and taste exactly the same to me. In baking I would use this to add a complex, caramelized flavor where you would normally add brown sugar, although I am not sure the properties would be exactly the same (since this sugar doesn't have the moist quality of brown sugar).UPDATE: I baked a lemon pound cake with the blond coconut sugar as a substitute for white sugar with great results again. The only difference with using either the blond or regular coconut sugar in baking is that the end product will be darker than one baked with white sugar. The dark coconut flavor is very subtle in baked dishes. Its best flavor comes out when stirred into your tea or sprinkled over oatmeal. It's definitely something I will use going forward!

Love this sugar enough to write a review for the shaker too even though I already wrote a review for the same sugar in a bag. This regular coconut sugar is recommended to replace brown sugar in recipes 1:1. I was skeptical as the texture is very different than brown sugar, but it worked great. The most impressive fact is that my 4-yr old, who LOVES brown sugar in her oatmeal (which is frequently requested not only for breakfast, but for dinner at times too!) loved her oatmeal just as much with this sugar instead. For me, that is the greatest test. Passing with flying colors just landed this as a permanent staple in our pantry.The shaker is great, especially for letting my little one try adding it herself while I monitor. I love offering her little ways to be independent and healthy!

I have been using both the blonde and regular for about a week now and really like the product.  I have recently started using organic products and this is one that I believe should be on everybody's list.  It isn't too sweet, which I really like, and it dissolves quickly in warm beverages.  I look forward to using it with my holiday baking!

I have tried both the blonde sugar and the brown sugar products.  Each has an interesting sweet-but-delicate flavor that leaves me wanting more.  So far, I have tried each in tea, but am excited to sprinkle the brown sugar on my son's next bowl of oatmeal.  I feel so good about anything made from coconut (milk, water, oil, etc.), that these sugar products are a no-brainer!

column9: Great organic sugar with lower glycemic index
column10: As a diabetic I have been looking for a natural sweetener that does not have a bitter aftertaste like some.  This product is a great-tasting natural sugar minimally processed and does not spike my blood sugar level.  It has a great taste in tea, coffee and baked goods.

The coconut sugar has a natural sweet flavor (no lingering after taste or too sweet taste). I love the shaker format for sprinkling on oatmeal, cereal and whole grain waffles. I can sprinkle just a tiny bit on my kids' non-sweetened breakfasts and then get very excited! They love the taste and I love that it is a healthier alternative to sugar.

It is great to find an alternative healthy sugar! I've been using it and it tastes delicious and feels healthy. I use it on my cereal, oats and sprinkle it on our ice cream for dessert, it is sooo yummy. I also tried it on a recipe of coconut rice and it was the best, all my family loved it!

I've been using Madhava's Agave nectar for several years, and was excited to try their Organic Coconut Sugar as an alternative to refined sugar.  I wasn't disappointed.  It's great sprinkled on waffles, added to hot cereals and perfect for baking.  I appreciate that it has a higher nutritional content than cane sugar, it tastes great, and I feel good about feeding it to my family.

column9: GREAT substitute for sugar and much better tasting
column10: I just started using coconut sugar as a substitute for regular sugar in my cookies and sweet bread. I love the caramelized flavor. I also sprinkle it on my lattes and oat meal...sooo yummy. Now I don't feel bad that my kids want to add "sugar" to their cereals and fruit since coconut sugar has naturally occurring vitamins and minerals. Love this new product!!!

column9: Nice product, tastes like brown sugar but smells different
column10: So, there really is nothing wrong with this product.  I didn't buy it because I'm avoiding sugar (it would be healthy of me to cut back, of course and I am trying) I bought it because it's made from coconut and that sounded delicious, exotic and new.  I gave it four out of five stars because it doesn't'wow' me.I love trying new foods, especially ones that I can use in baking.  Since I've had this coconut sugar I have used it in the following things;1.  Green Onion Naan - Naan is a yeasted bread, so I only needed two teaspoons of sugar to speed up the proofing stage, I subbed coconut sugar for the reg granulated sugar and the naan turned out just like they always do, puffy and flavorfull.2.  On a bowl of oatmeal - Again it tasted just the same, possibly because I included a liberal sprinkling of cinnamon and nutmeg, the subtleties of the sugar might have been overpowered by the spices?3.  Mixed into a cup of Tea with cream - ughh, something was not right, but then again, I use white sugar in my tea, never brown, so maybe the effect would have been the same -- tea dumped down the sink.4.  In a pan of green curry chicken - the curry tasted like it always does, yummy.I guess if you are thinking of buying this because you imagine it will impart a subtle coconut fragrance to your food, think again, I thought it tasted just like brown sugar, so tasty and sweet, but nothing new.  As for the health benefits, well, that I am unsure of.  I don't believe it would be any safer for diabetics than a spoonful of sugar.

column9: use it all the time now!
column10: I use this sugar in my coffee and love the flavor! I think the sweetness is more delicate and I taste hints of caramel. I use the same amount as I used to with regular brown sugar. The shaker is great and very practical. I also sprinkled some on my french toasts as I ran out of maple syrup and it was delicious! I adopted it and prefer to use it now.

I have really enjoyed this coconut sugar shaker!  My husband uses it for his morning coffee and cannot detect any flavor difference.  I use it while cooking.  I caramelized onions with it and it worked perfectly.  I will definitely buy again!

I have ordered the 1oz bag 24 count box twice, trying to be fair, from bag to bag the quality varies from burnt / overcooked, to soft and rubbery. the only consistent factor had been that only about 3 bags out of 24 were edible from each shipment. will continue to search for sweet potato chip that has a good flavor , crunch to satisfy cravings for chips.Good Health Glories Kettle Sweet Potato Chips, 1-Ounce (Pack of 24)

Chips were tasty, not overly salty.  3 bags were factory seaed bbut only had one or two chips in them.  One bag was totally empty.  I was going to return them to Amazon (just the bags that were empty)- but decided it would be to much effort.  I would purchase again, but probably not in the indivdual serving size.  I am sure it was a manufacturing problem... the chips we did get were great!

Five stars for taste, packaging, serving size. HOWEVER - Walmart has them individually for only 88 cents per one ounce package! So you would only be paying $15.84 for 18 packages! That's a deal! You'd be saving $3.17. Plus, you can mix and match different favors and you don't have to buy a whole lot of one flavor. :)

Finally a fruit snack that is healthy!  I like fruit snacks but am trying to make more conscientious food choices, and this one happens to actually taste enjoyable!  My husband even likes them, and he is really finicky.  Great for keeping in your purse for that extra boost during your day... for your, your spouse, or your child.

I love all the Buddy products. They are a bit pricey but I love that they are 100% fruit, and my toddlers both love them. I don't keep them around for snacking at the house due to the price but they are perfect for outings, and spending the day at friends houses. I keep a bunch in my diaper bag all the time, including the purees. I would recommend these to anyone with toddlers, they are the perfect quick, easy and mess free snack.
It's difficult to give a review on something I've eaten for years. I've made cranberry sauce and Ocean Spray is not only convenient but it tastes better than mine.
Good granola! The great flavor of crushed up oatmeal cookies, lots of raisins and a nice granola texture.

column9: Moist and chewy granola, 190 calories in 1/2 cup!!!
column10: I've been on the search for a granola that is moist and chewy and doesn't taste and feel like dried pegboard.  This is it!!!!  And check out the ingredient list!  Nothing that you can't spell or that contains more than 5 syllables.  I almost hate to recommend it because it is SOOOOOOO good and I don't want them to run out.  I was at Whole Foods last week and they only had the peanut butter.  Which was great but I like the oatmeal raisin better.  The raisins are chewy, not the nasty dried rock chips found in some other brands.  Erin, these are amazing!
I start off the morning every morning w/ a bowl of this granola; its great!  A touch of sweetness and a great crunch!  Also on Amazon Grocery it can be purchased at a great price!

Oatmeal raisin is my favorite type of granola and I have tried many different brands.  Erin Baker's is the best by far.  Very crunchy and not too sweet.  I like it right out of the bag as a snack and as a ceral with milk.  Great stuff!!

This is my favorite granola, hands down. it doesn't have that weird processed taste like so many foods do these days. It's the prefect combination of chewy, crunchy and sweet plus it's very healthy as a snack or on vanilla yogurt for a meal.

I absolutely love Erin Baker's Oatmeal Raisin granola. I eat it every morning mixed with Kamut Puffs and banana slices. The ingredients list is comprised of simple and all-natural ingredients. On a side note, I do not recommend snacking out of the bag. The clusters taste like little cookie nuggets on their own and they are wildly addictive!
Great tasting, I have eaten this granola every morning for a couple years now, it tastes like oatmeal cookies.Love it!!

This stuff tastes fine, but each package contained big chunks of the cereal, too big to eat with milk, but okay as a dry snack.  I had to put each pack in my food processor to break it up.  Breadshop and Bear Naked are better and less trouble!

Whether they're called Chick Peas, Garbanzo or Ceci beans I've eaten my fair share mainly at salad bars UNTIL this past year when I started buying them for use at home. I've tried various brands primarily based on sales. I'm so put off by the Chick Pea residue I usually drain and rinse them before I use them.PROGRESSO Chick Peas are heavenly...no thick residue! I can use them after simply draining the liquid from the can without rinsing them. Their firm, beige, beautiful and tasty. I've been making dips and salads using these beauties, making Meatless Mondays yummy and protein-rich. Of course they were on sale for less than a buck a can...winning!

i h ordered several coffe cakes and most came without a hitch i got 2 fruit cakes (which in never ordered) called dhl to pick up and the return labels were not good. one cake i ordered took at least 2 weeks to get here. i would like the fruitcakes to be replaced with the coffee cakes.(2) i would order more coffee cakes but will see how the mix ups are handled. john turner 971 11th st no naples fl 34102 (239)-262-8545

column9: Hard to find these yellow eyes beans
column10: My Mother grew up in Massachusetts and loved the baked beans her Grandmother cooked.  The recipe called for yellow eyed beans which are impossible to find in the south!  These are high quality dried beans.

I did not see a shipping cost for this time item until e-mail order confirmation was sent and noticed the shipping cost was as much as the product!  So much for a good deal...  Since it was within time specified by Amazon to cancel, I attempted to cancel; but it was processed anyway.  Not happy about this but will search for shipping cost before placing another order!  Buyer beware!
I grew up in Detroit and on Vernors.  I love this stuff and I'm glad I can purchase it on Amazon because it's difficult to find in Montana.

I feel sorry for those who can't get Vernors in their area. Fortunately I'm in the Detroit area and grew up drinking this stuff. It's the best!! I'm hooked on the diet version. Esp great after you've gone a bit overboard on drinks the night before.. the ginger soothes the stomach and it's the only thing I've found to quench my extreme thirst. Sometimes I think I am addicted to it. Is that a bad thing ? Not so sure all the ingredients are so good for you, but it's my only pop ("soda" ) indulgence!

column9: Vernor's is the best ginger ale on the planet.
column10: Vernor's Ginger Ale is a spicy wonderful drink.  I grew up drinking it in Niagara Falls, NY.  As an adult I live in Virginia and it is very seldom that we can find Vernor's around here.  Last summer my mom brought me back a case of Diet Vernor's Ginger Ale and it was just as good as the regular.Now, there are only 2 ginger ales on the planet that I like, Northern Neck Ginger Ale and Vernor's.  And, I will gratefully pay the shipping charge to have this wonderful soda to drink.
If you love necco products these hearts are for you!! Different flavored and are very addicting. You can't eat just one!!

column9: Much better than the fruit chews
column10: Having tried both I can say that the chocolate chews are much better than the fruit ones.  They are small, easy to eat and I am not having any problems.  I have had Gastric Bypass Surgery and I need the extra calcium.  Plus the price is very reasonable.

column9: Excellent! Wife now gets her calcium
column10: I could never get my wife to take the calcium her doctor says she must have to reduce the chance of osteoporosis. She loves chocolate, and really likes these chews... problem solved!

I occasionally purchase this product at the grocery store when I see it on sale.It has a nice orange flavor. No unpleasant aftertaste. A Dr. Pepper/7 Up product.From the web site:Diet Crush Orange has a ballistic burst of fruit taste that's sure to put a smile on your face.Contains no caffeineNutrition FactsNutrition Per 20 Fl ozNUTRIENTS AMOUNT % DV *Calories 0Total Fat 0 g 0%Sodium 120 mg 5%Total Carbohydrates 0 g 0%Protein 0 g* Percent Daily Values (DV) are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.CARBONATED WATER, CITRIC ACID, MALIC ACID, POTASSIUM BENZOATE (PRESERVATIVE), SODIUM CITRATE, ASPARTAME, NATURAL FLAVORS, ACACIA GUM, ACESULFAME POTASSIUM, ESTER GUM, YELLOW 6, RED 40.

I was never a fan of sardines, too strong, fishy and salty. My huband bought that awful stuff at the grocery store that even the cats wouldn't eat. But I wanted to start eating healthier foods and sardines seemed like a simple, mega-3-rich, quick and healthy snack. Seasons had great reviews so I took a chance. These arrived today and I am already addicted. The easy open container comes packed with 4 good sized fish in a light olive oil. The fish have a very delicate flavor as well as aroma and minimal saltiness. Thanks Seasons!

Season sardines are the best I've ever tasted. I particularly like the whole sardines in olive oil, but other varieties I've tried are also good.  They have a mellow taste, but not so mellow as to eliminate the sardine flavor, and they're salted just right.  They're also relatively inexpensive.

I was searching online for sardines in olive oil with a reasonable amount of salt (my rule of thumb is mg = kcal) - I could find only soybean oil at the grocery store. Received my first shipment today - beautiful! Delicious! And no bread needed to 'kill' the salt. And you know how sometimes, when you eat something like sprouts, that are just so alive and so good for you, that your stomach and liver immediately feel so... happy? (Or is it just me?!) I never expected to get that feeling from a canned food.

column9: OK, but King Oscar is the best brand.
column10: Reasonably tasty, kind of ugly in the can, no comparison with the King Oscar Brisling crosspack in olive oil (which is much more expensive).

column9: Easy open can is great, but this is not my favorite mid-size sardine.
column10: I've decided after two cans that this is the first Season sardine product that I'd rate just average.But first, at least someone invented a sardine can that's easy to open!  Just peel the plastic sheet back and there's your fresh sardines!  No metal top to snap back and splatter oil all over you.  Gotta love it!However, the Matiz Gallego Sardines in Olive Oil look better and taste way fresher, although the cans are made of heavier metal and are far harder to open than any other sardines I've tried.  So if you like these, you owe it to yourself to try the Matiz product.

I prefer the boneless and skinless, but these sardines are very good. And I love the easy opening lid--no more spills. The pure olive oil had a good flavor. With subscribe and save, they are a bargain too.

column9: tasty and meaty, but expensive because of no free shipping
column10: These are my favorite sardines thus far, but they are expensive because of not being able to get free shipping.  They are meaty and flavorful without being overpoweringly fishy and firm in texture.  Easy open can was nice too, as it was easy to open it without splashing like the pop-tops.  The only thing other than shipping price that I didn't like was that there were too many large/obvious scales in some cans, which was a turnoff as far as texture and visual appeal.  Despite this, they are definitely my favorite so far.

If you ever had Possum Brand sardines, you will love these. These can be quite large (3 fish in the can!). I don't mind that at all. The are sweet and mild and well cooked. The olive oil is very fine, too. You will love these. I just put them on crackers with tabasco and a coke. It's my comfort food!

column9: A tasty way of getting your Omega 3s!
column10: These are some very tasty sardines and I like the easy-to-open cans that they come in (nothing worse than those cans that are so hard to open that you end up with fishy-smelling oil all over the kitchen!) It's also nice to find sardines in extra virgin olive oil (and lots of it!), as opposed to the soybean oil used by many other/cheaper brands. These sardines are relatively expensive when compared to some other brands so take advantage of the free shipping option (when available - it was when I ordered them but now they are charging for S&H for some reason). I recommend eating those with a nice bowl of rice and some French bread. Enjoy!

the tins are easy to open, filled with large (for sardines) filets. the olive oil is very bland, not remarkably different from, say, corn oil (not a compliment!). the filets are boneless but they have the silvery skin on. there are about enough filets in a can to cover a smallish slice of toast--4 or 5 filets, with some small pieces as filler. the texture is pretty good--dense, almost creamy. (in fact, you could cream these easily with a fork.) the flavor is very mild, too mild for me, undersalted (easy to fix)...  i admit that i like an assertive, salty fishy fish. (i eat anchovies straight from the tin!)i eat them as a simple sandwich, well drained, on toasted whole wheat spread with lots of french mustard. or tossed with a big green salad and a mustardy vinaigrette. a tasty, very healthy meal, low calorie meal, done in a matter of seconds. i bought these at about $1.80/can, and they are a better price and better quality than the ones i can buy at my local grocer. all in all, a good product, but nothing special.

It was our mistake, but we thought we were purchasing the much better boneless/skinless club sardines from Seasons, which are very good.  These are not as good, although they are better than the cheaper branded sardines.
These sardines are larger and tastier than many I 've tried costing more. The taste in olive oil is purely lite and tasteful. Add some tabasco, for added pop.
The sardines are very good.  However Season consistently 'shorts' the product.  The can is about 2/3 sardines and 1/3 oil.Bad value.

The MOST moist, delicious, & sustainably caught sardines are, by and far, the Wild Planet Brand!I tried both the "Season" and "Crown Prince" brands and the difference in flavor and quality was light years away from the Wild Planet brand.I live in New England and can only find WILD PLANET brand in my local Stop and Shop.It's amazing that we have 3 "Whole Foods" Markets in my state and not one carries the Wild Planet brand! They are only carry what I believe to be the inferior quality brands that I mentioned.I'm sure that the Hoffman and Manischewitz families that own Crown Prince and Season brands wouldn't mind having the Wild Planet brand alongside their own, since they feel theirs are such great quality, right?Who knows, they just might learn something about having high standards from the lovely bunch of people that own Wild Planet in California.To top it off, all Wild Planet products are in BPA free cans...what more can you ask for?
notice for the last 25 cans less fish and more oil to make up the ounce weightstill tase good but noticeable difference

I really enjoy these sardines - great in salads for summer! I went ahead without trying them beforehand and got the 12 pack - good decision! They taste great, the olive oil makes dressing a salad really easy. I love that I don't have to take fish oil and I get it right from the source. They're also good on sandwiches, in stirfrys, and just on their own! I also like that I can just bring a tin to work since it's a peel off top!
Contained 3 biig sardines- very good quality. Great to bring at work to be eaten with crackers. Foil top is easy to open. Would definitely purchase this again!

Sardines:  Delicious.  Healthy.  Sustainable.If you're a fan of canned sardines, you ought to give Season(tm) brand a try.  This particular product, sardines in pure olive oil, is an excellent choice.  An alternate, or perhaps a gateway offering if you will, would be the Skinless and Boneless sardines in olive oil.
I did not know that I liked sardines.A friend of mine shared some of these with me and I thought that they were delicious.I enjoy them right out of the can and they are very nutritious. C.Jackson

column9: lots  of calcium instead of those dreadful pills...
column10: Try 1/2 tin instead of a calcium supplements , (dreadful gastric distress and fatigue),feel more humane since switched to sardines and yogurt.  Season sardines contain 70% calcium RDA if consume entire can....the natural solution suits me better at age 62...no no no,my politics are not leftie...in fact I could be considered a right-wing nut job.Season Sardines in Pure Olive Oil, 4.375-Ounce Tins (Pack of 12)job. Save the excess olive oil for the cat(s)....or dogs...Life before pet food was just as acceptible...as per my great grannie.  Cats won't cause you grief,or ruin your credit...keep them well-fed and happy..the same for dogs...get older and adapt to reality...older gals live in reality,and have eliminated males as their saviors...take care of yourselves and thrive! Keep the cats and dogs and say the hell with you all else!!!!

column9: Only two fish but very tasty
column10: I was surprised to find only two fish in the can.  They were very tasty but very expensive for two fish after paying for shipping.  I wish Amazon would stock Seasons products.

column4: S. P. Delorenzo "S. P. DeLorenzo Coffee Maven"
column9: Season Brand From Amazon.com sardines with skins intact.
column10: Sardines with skin are toooooo fishy to enjoy and the skin makes them basically inedible. I can only eat sardines with skin removed. I could not even eat one sardine out of the one opened tin.  I was assured before ordering the sardines that they would arrive without skins but,alas, they arrived with skins intact.  I sent the entire order back and requested a full refund . A bad experience.

is what my husband said this coffee reminds him of.  He likes a mid (not strong) taste.  I don't drink coffee hot. My idea of coffee is a wonderful smell in the morning that I will make and add to a latte or I guess I mean a chocolate/coffee smoothie that I make at home.  This one suits that bill.  It is a full flavor to me or strong.  I believe it would even make a second cup if I so desired.Would I pay a huge amount for it?  No, I think this coffee is relatively expensive. There are only 15 pods in the box and it happens to have Marley on the box.  Is that the reason for the cost or is pod coffee just expensive?Since I don't have a pod machine I boiled a cup of water and added it to the pod in a cup with a spoon holding it down.  Worked well for me.Good coffee but not worth what they want for it.

column9: convenient, low-acid, but a bit weak
column10: The first thing that hit me is that these appear to be a low-acid gype of coffee....I didn't get that icky feeling some coffees give you after you drink them.  That is a definite plus.  But the coffee itself isn't that strong either.  I'm not into Kona or really deep flavors, I like just a medium blend.  But this still seemed weak.  It almost came across as coffee-tea than a strong cup of joe.I don't think I'd order this particular blend again.

I had never used these coffee pods before and used them in my coffee maker without a filter.  I was really expecting the coffee to smell great when it was brewing, but maybe it is to mild.  If you like milder breakfast type coffee or chai tea you will love this coffee.  I added a little light cream and it was very good, be careful with the cream it needs very little.  My first cup I put to much light cream and it overpowered the drink.  I would buy this again, it is something nice to give as a gift or serve to company.

. . .A little fussy about my coffee, and this coffee did not disappoint me.  It has a rich flavor, I can control the strength by adding or substracting the amount of water I use (which you can do wih all coffees, I know).  The flavor - although I cannot pinpoint the difference, is very nice.  I'll definitely be buying more of this brand and I think that's probably the best review I can give it - I want more.

I made my coffee the usual way but it was not strong enough. I don't like my coffee overly strong, but I do like it to taste like coffee. I made another cup, but used 2 packets, perfect! It tastes exactly like coffee, nothing over the top, just coffee. I gave it 4 stars though because it is organic, and I prefer everything organic!

I'm still not a food reviewer. The problem is that I can't turn down free coffee. That said, this is good stuff, mellow with none of the bitter edge common with a lot of the cheaper stuff sold at the local grocery store. I subtracted one star from the review because of the ridiculously pretentious ad copy on the box. Drinking this coffee won't fix the world or make your life more fulfilling, I'm fairly sure.

column9: Roast is too dark for  a Yirgacheffe
column10: While the roast is  described  as medium it is actually a nice but slightly bitter dark roast which is completely without the promised floral notes that are expected in a good Yirgacheffe Ethiopian coffee. A true medium roast would have preserved the floral and fruity notes that are present in a good Yirgacheffe.  Otherwise, this is an OK feel good coffee for Senseo and Senseo compatible pod cofee makers.  It is both Fair Trade and Organic certified and promotes or sponsors the coffee kicks charity while trading on the Marley name.  However, there is a lot of necessarily sturdy packaging which blunts the organic and sustainable claims for me.  As is standard for Senseo pods, each pod has only enough coffee for 5-6 ounces of strong  coffee. Use two for a mug if you prefer strong coffee.

We saw that some of the coffee reviews said that the coffee was weak when "teabagged."  We put a few pods of Marley Coffee One Love, One Heart into our old-fashioned stovetop percolator and let the steam do its magic.Yum. Great flavor, and strong enough. Even though I prefer my coffee whitened and sweetened, I was surprised that I enjoyed the Marley Coffee black. This coffee was great alone, and would probably do well as a mixer for cooking or alcohol recipes.Next time, we may experimentally open the pods and try the in the Keurig; however, we *were* satisfied with the percolator.

First of, I didn't really know what to expect when I ordered this coffee.  Come to find out the "single serve pods" are flat, round cushions that require a special coffee maker.  I own a Keurig and Eco-Brew refillable cups that I really like, so I decided to open the pod and dump the grounds into the Eco-Brew cup instead.  It worked like a charm, and on the 6cc setting I got to enjoy a very bold brew with no aidic aftertaste.

One Love is a good, robust coffee - if you like a strong coffee in the morning, you should like the flavor. Honestly, I didn't really catch the hints of exotic floral and berry they advertise which is just as well as I enjoy a basic coffee. The single serving pods are handy but you can also use a couple in a regular machine and it works just fine as well. If you're environmentally concious, it is free trade certified and organic.  Partial proceeds are also donated to the charity kicksforcause.org.  Overall an enjoyable cup of coffee with decent flavor.

Well, I wasn't bright when I ordered this coffee and for some reason I thought it came in both single servings and pods. I had to tear the pods open and use just the coffee and that way, it is EXCELLENT coffee. Rich and dark, I really like the flavor. My only complaint is, no, they're not easy to open packets, I have to use scissors and really, does it need all that wasteful packaging? But the coffee itself is very good, though I don't know all the fancy words for describing coffee, I like strong flavor with caffeine, usually choosing medium roasts and this fits the bill.

This package of Marley coffee contains a bunch of "pods" designed for pod coffee makers. Look them up and boggle at the prices. I do not have one so my first try was with my French press - the purest way of making coffee. I put one pod into it and poured in a large cupful of almost boiling water. After poking it around for a while and leaving it to sit, I got a blackish coffee which tasted a bit weak.For my second attempt I cut open two pods and emptied the ground coffee into the press. The resulting coffee was quite strong, but as a quasi-European (English) that's the way I like it.What to say about the flavor? It was mild (no harshness) and fairly pleasant. The coffee in Denny's restaurants is better though.

Brewing Machine: Philips SenseoFirst thing I noticed was that the packet contained noticeably more coffee than my Senseo pods.  I thought great, I can use just one to brew my double serving cup.  Wrong, very weak when brewed that way.Second, tried to brew two servings at once, but two pods were much too large to fit in the two serving Senseo pod holder.  So, I used the single pod holder and brewed one cup at a time.  What a hassle.Taste wise, the coffee is okay, it tases sort of weak for my tastes and doesn't have a lot of flavor, and the price per pod you might as well buy Star Bucks (or favorite coffee house coffee).  I will keep using my Senseo dark roast pods which I think have better flavor and are much cheaper.

column9: not for french roast coffee drinkers
column10: i drink my coffee strong and black so this is too weak for me.  i do have the one pot coffee maker and i either have to decrease the water or use two of these.  this is not economical.  it is much easier to just wrap some french roast coffee into a paper towel and use that instead.  if you like very mild coffee pods, this i s fine, but not for those of us who can't get it strong enough.

While I am no fan of coffee, other members in my household love it.  This got rave reviews.This looks like it comes in a tea bag.  It's easy to make; you just brew it for a few minutes and wring it out.  You can make it the way you make tea by applying the bag concept.  This was a big hit with the coffee hounds..

column9: Needs more instruction but we figured it out
column10: Marley Coffee is an interesting product which comes in a tasteful display box/dispenser, and proves that one can have fresh rich coffee just about anywhere without dedicated coffeemakers or pod machines.Maybe the "One Love" variety is meant for two cups per "single serve" bag, or perhaps one is supposed to do something more than to "Stir It Up" little darlin', as recommended on the box (in homage to the song.)There wasn't instruction on the packaging on how to get the brew right with these large "tea bags" of coffee. The only thing clearly marked was which side of the bag should be faced down in the cup.The coffee has a good taste, but the first bag I tried brewed up so strong it gave me the jitters. Good thing there are 15 individual plastic-sealed bags in the dispenser. My husband fiddled around with them because he likes an occasional cup of joe in the afternoon but doesn't want to brew up a whole pot.I credit him with coming up with the "spoon test" to figure out when the coffee was at the perfect strength. We use a 16 oz. cup because the circumference of the bag is rather wide for our 12 oz, and we pour boiling water over the bag which rises to the top as the cup fills. Then we wait for it to steep. After a couple of minutes, he takes a spoon and starts lowering it into the cup just until the bowl of the spoon is completely immersed.
