I have had hazelnut flavored coffees from other producers and although I was not a fan of the flavoring they didn't have these off tastes.  Maybe the flavored coffees just aren't for me.  I equate this stuff to office brew.  It'll work in a pinch but not something I would buy.

I really, really wanted to enjoy this coffee; hazelnut Crème brûlée Delish! I absolutely love coffee and this has several things in its favor:*aroma*quality packaging: This comes in a plastic bag with reclosing strap, but you'll still want to store the bag in an airtight container.*ground fine: This is for richer flavor. The best brands do this.*image: If you delight in coffee and want to think of other parts of the world as you sip it, this company really shoots for that image.*Reasonable price.The aroma is probably the best part. It's a tradition for my husband and me to open fresh coffee together, and while he's never been a fan of flavored coffee, he says this one's "Not bad." He likes a coffee that gets his attention. Bitter coffee earns his respect. But the bottom line is, this coffee is very bitter and leaves an aftertaste. Now, is that bitterness from the bean itself, or from the flavoring? I'd need to try the regular and get a comparison to answer that for you.That said, the bitterness came as a bit of a surprise to me because the beans are grown at a higher elevation and the package states that the beans are never bitter. The higher elevation reduces the acidity in coffee and therefore the bitterness. So when you brew a cup and it turns out it is bitter...the image doesn't take that away or allow people to ignore it; rather, it lifts expectations only to disappoint.But elevation isn't the only issue. It also matters what kind of beans these are. Are these Arabica beans? Those are the good stuff-the ones you really want to buy because of their lack of bitterness. Grow them high-sure-but the bean still matters. So, whether or not these are Arabica, I don't know: I couldn't find the ingredients list on the package and it doesn't say elsewhere.So, all told, I really wanted to enjoy the creative crème brulée flavor since I love hazelnut crème brulée and coffee, too-but the bitterness gets in the way. Reasonable price, though.

Melitta Hazelnut Crème BruleeWonderfully complex, slight bitter finishI am about half way through the 11oz bag, and am still experimenting with the optimum proportions. Mind you I have found the flavor so far to be wonderfully complex. Perhaps out of all of the coffee flavors, the only ones that I find as complementing the natural taste of coffee are those of hazelnut and French vanilla. I ordinarily like the natural plain taste of coffee and have progressed from the instant, to the drip and occasionally dabble in grinding my own. The flavored coffees generally overdo the flavor, in this beverage category a "hint" of flavor is generally more than enough. Enough of the background, here are the specific comments that may help you to decide whether this one is worth trying.The big positive is that the flavor mix of hazelnut and crème brulee works very well together. The crème brulee part is a wonderful caramelized sugar and butterscotch aroma that underlies the hazelnut foundation. Like in a fine wine, this adds complexity to the brew, which makes you savor and swirl the concoction in your mouth to prolong the taste sensations. There is actually a hint of whiskey liquor as well, perhaps stemming from the vanilla and oak connection I often notice in wine. The brewing aroma is great and it permeates the house, a great wake up alarm. That is the good part, there is a slight downer as well, there is a slight lingering bitter finish on the back of the throat. Use extra milk or half and half to tame it.I noticed there is a bit of discussion regarding as to whether this coffee is weak or strong. I think I have an answer that may be consistent with all the observations. If you prepare it according to the measurements that you may be used to (say the standard measuring cup provided with majority of ground coffee cups), you will find it weak. If you prepare it to the directions on the bag, two teaspoons per 6oz cup, you will likely find it strong. So use more than you would normally but less than the directions say.Also pay attention to the "extra fine grind" on the package. They mean it. If you coffee maker has a setting for 2-4 coups vs a full pot, then use it. This setting slows down the rate at which water goes through the grounds, and you may need that with this coffee. It is such a fine grind that it tends to plug up the pores of the filter. Wwith a fast water flow, the filter may flow over.Bottom line is that this is a wonderful flavor combination, still a bit heavy handed, so go ahead and blend it with your regular coffee 50-50, and still get the special occasion/desert feeling.

I got my package in the mail today & see that it's extra fine grind so I can't use it in my coffee press. No problem as I plugged in a 4 cup coffeepot to make my first brew. What I would up with was a milder form of coffee than the bold & extra bold coffee's which is more like Breakfast Blend from that well known Seattle company. Tried my first sip black & it was ok, thankfully not bitter. Added the usual 2 spoons of suger & it tasted better but it won't be something I'll buy as it's too mild for my tastes even though I used the same amount of coffee as I always do when I made this 4 cup potfull. Couldn't taste any Hazelnut flavoring in the coffee even in that first black sip before I added sugar. All I can say (on my sencond cup as I'm writing this review) is that it's a light coffee with some body to it & that there are no unpleasant aftertaste flavors. It does seem to be weaker in the caffeine department than what I'm used to drinking but some people might like that. All in all I'll finish the bag but as I've said before I'm not going to buy this coffee for myself.I also couldn't get the bag open & had to cut below the seal in order to get at the coffee then I had to pour it into a coffee can I happened to have in my pantry which means I couldn't use the bag that the coffee came in as there was no way to seal the bag up after I had cut it open. So you might want to have an 11.5 oz or larger coffee can with it's lid if you order this coffee from Amazon.

Although I am a "one cup a day" coffee drinker, I have a slight allergy to hazelnuts, so I put this coffee next to the coffee maker in our break room with a sign that said, drink up and tell me what you think. Here's what the committee came back with:J: It was really good. Very smooth and the hazelnut flavor was delicious. I like hazelnut coffee and drink it all the time and this was the best I've had.M: That coffee was very good. Me and the girls were talking and we want to have it on a regular basis. When are you going to get us some more?E: It smelled great while brewing and tasted excellent. The coffee and hazelnut flavors complement each other and make a great cup of coffee.H: I liked it. D had a cup and said, I never drink more than one cup of coffee in the morning, but just before lunch, I caught a whiff of that aroma and had to have another. It's wonderful!So, I think the public has spoken and this is a tasty, well received brand of coffee. Three of the four respondents also asked: Where did you get it? This is definitely the most popular flavor and brand of coffee in our company in the last four or five years.

My bag of Melitta Cafe Hazelnut Creme Brulee Ground Coffee arrived in the mail yesterday and this morning I brought it to the office. Needless to say, it was excellent. I like hazelnut coffee anyway, but this was fresh, tasty, and delicious. The aroma was inviting, and it prompted others in the office to visit my office in search of a cup of it. I'm happy to share. This coffee is a delight.
BAD BAD COFFEE - HORRIBLE - HORRIBLE - DISGUSTING - BOUGHT 2 ORDERS - VANILLA & HAZLENUT - BOTH HORRIBLE - NAMES SOUNDED SO DELICIOUS TOO!

I purchased this coffee at a local store a few months back and loved it.  It is by far the best coffee I have ever had and I'm not a crazy coffee drinker like some.  I got this on auto delivery and saved even more $$  Yum I'm already for a cup now!

column9: Measures up well to my favorite Green Mountain coffee
column10: I have been drinking Melitta's Hazelnut Creme Brulee ground coffee for a bout a week.  I find it pleasant, complex, and fills the kitchen with a very pleasant smell.The grounds have very fine grind, however I had no issues with it plugging up the filter. I have been experimenting with the amount of grounds I use for each cup, and I found that I like a heaving measuring cup.  So a little more than I use for my favorite Green Mountain Hazelnut coffee.If I use less the coffee is a little weaker than I like, if I follow the instructions on the package (2 teaspoons per 6 oz cup) I find it a little too strong.  I would recommend experimenting to find just the right strength for your own taste.I love flavored coffees and Melitta measures up well to my favorite Green Mountain coffee, while being less expensive.  I will be ordering it again in the future.Ali Julia review

"A European classic. Sweet caramel and rich vanilla infused with the flavor of wild hazelnuts." - from the package of Melitta's HAZELNUT CRÈME BRULEE coffee"... Melitta brings to life the feelings of the most romantic European Cafés." - from the package of Melitta's HAZELNUT CRÈME BRULEE coffeeReally?There were logistical problems getting this review written. My wife brewed-up and quaffed down the entire original package without giving me the opportunity to sample. She likes her cuppa Joe in the morning, while I drink the stuff only on those occasions when I want something "different." In our house, it's apparently "every man for himself and the devil take the hindmost."So, she opened up a fresh package of HAZELNUT CRÈME BRULEE this morning under my close surveillance.Granted, my wife is more attuned to a coffee's subtleties than I am. But we both agree that this blend presents neither the nuanced aroma nor flavor of anything containing caramel, vanilla, or hazelnuts. It's a decent coffee inasmuch as it's not bitter, but that's all it is - simply coffee-flavored coffee, which brings to life the romance of any ordinary brew station anywhere in the world, e.g. the customer waiting room of Bob's A-1 Auto Repair and Tires down on the corner.And do "wild hazelnuts" taste any different than the cultivated variety?

I like coffee with flavor- and would rather just use milk instead of buying expensive flavored creamers.This coffee tastes very good- some very good flavors mingled together.The only one complaint, as others have noted is that you have to use a bit more than plain coffee to get it as "dark".All in all, one of my favorite flavored coffee now!
i had never used Melitta coffee before, so when this arrived, we were anxious to taste it and see. We generally enjoyed the flavor, but it was definitely not as good as other coffees we enjoy.

column9: Great Hazelnut Aroma but Strong and Bitter Taste
column10: When you first open this bag of coffee you are met with a wonderful hazelnut aroma with a slight hint of caramel. Upon brewing my first cup I noticed that the aroma intensified a bit and had more of a coffee overtone and less of the previous hazelnut and caramel..  Unfortunately the taste was a bit strong and bitter.  It was almost like having strong dark bitter coffee with some hazelnut coffeemate to tone it down.  The second cup was made by brewing a bit lighter and the taste became much more smooth and pleasant.  There is still a slightly bitter undertone but a little bit of milk smooths things out very nicely.  Overall this is a strong and bitter coffee with a hazelnut flavor so make sure this suits your taste or you like your coffee with dash of milk.*** Positive Points: ***- Great hazelnut aroma- Pleasant taste once adjusted for bitterness*** Negative Points: ***- Strong and somewhat bitter taste- Rather expensive

I've tried various flavored coffees from different companies and the 'Melitta Cafe Collection Hazelnut Creme Brulee' has to be one of my least favorites.My primary problem with this coffee is that the flavoring is so pronounced that it drowns out the coffee taste and completely overwhelms with Hazelnut and Creme Brulee. In my opinion the flavoring should be subtle and compliment the coffee. Not the case with this coffee at all. The aroma when brewing this coffee is superb but one taste and I was immediately not a fan.Also, this coffee comes packed in the bag equivalent of a plastic clamshell container. In other words the package impossible to open without scissors which defeats the purpose of the resealable bag.

When brewing this coffee you can really smell it - it's a wonderful smell. Sweet, chocolaty, very welcoming.However, don't think this is not coffee or will taste like some sort of latte. The coffee is strong, and the flavor is mainly what you will expect, coffee with a hint of hazelnut. It might be sweeter than regular ground coffee, but it's by no means sweet in flavor - again, it's real coffee.Everyone in the house liked it, and really enjoy the smell of it.There is really nothing bad to say about this coffee - it's an interesting (in a good way!) flavor, with a wonderful dessert-like smell that makes the entire household crave a drink.

This is really one of the best coffees I've ever had. The aroma is beautiful; the taste is wonderful. It is true that there is a bit of a bitter finish, but, frankly, I like that. I'd have to say that, overall, this is a very strong coffee, and I mean that in a positive way. I love strong coffee. I highly recommend this coffee!

There is no question about the fact that I honestly adore a nice and simple tasting cup of coffee to start my day. But Melitta has not been a great company that produces the best coffee filters, but they've also got some really strong coffee flavors to call their own. That comes with their cafe collection, and their Hazelnut Creme Brulee. The taste is absolutely very smooth and mild to the taste buds, yet remain sophisticated and strong from the first time you simply whiff the smell and aroma. I absolutely loved the taste of it from the very first sip. I absolutely recommend this as another delightful flavor in your morning cup of joy in the morning. Melitta does do their best, and they still know how to delight anyone with coffee.Price: BTaste: B+Overall: B 1/2+

column9: I'm not happy with it, my family didn't like it either, not recommended
column10: I finally got around to brewing this Melitta Hazelnut Creme Brulee (after all kinds of fun in getting the package open) using my Bodum coffee press.  While the aroma is good, the taste left me wondering what they use to flavor this stuff.  It just didn't seem "right" to me.  Over the next few days, I brewed it again and I was left with the same impression - it just tasted artificial to me.  I served it to my brother with no pre-discussion and he didn't really go for it either - so it wasn't just me.  I would have to say pass on this one.
... but the flavor is VERY strong.  I like it best cut half and half with unflavored coffee.  Still, a nice smooth cup of coffee.

column9: Flavor is too overpoweringly artificial for me
column10: The package says "natural and artificial flavors," but to me there is an artificial taste that is overpowering. The problem isn't that I don't like hazelnut-flavored coffee. I've had coffee with the hazelnut flavored creamer (which is probably also artificially flavored) and loved it.I really felt cheated that I disliked this coffee too much to even finish the bag because getting into the bag was a real battle. It made me wish for "frustration-free" packaging, or at least a pair of gloves to protect my hands from the very sharp foil edges left when I finally had to resort to scissors. I won't be ordering more of this variety. I also tried Melitta's Supreme ground coffee and liked it very much, but I won't order it again either because of the packaging.

I recieved both this and the Melitta Cafe Collection Blanc et Noir Ground Coffee, 11-Ounce Bags (Pack of 3) to try - while I LOVED the Blanc et Noir, I found the flavor of this one to only be so-so.  Still it's better then the free stuff I get at work - I would buy the Blanc et Noir before purchasing this flavor.  Maybe I just don't care for Hazlenut or something.  There wasn't anything wrong with it, and I'm sure there will be many who adore this coffee.  I simply preferred the other flavor.  The coffee is pre-ground and very fine, almost (but not quite) to the level of espresso.  Now even though I preferred the other flavor, this was good enough for me to finish the whole bag no problem.  Several of my friends actually preferred this to the other.The packaging however - remains the same - you need to find a greek god to simply pull the package open or you need to go at it with a pair of scissors.  True, you don't have to worry about any of the grounds escaping before you open it... but trust me, just use the scissors.Final opinion - 3 for the flavor 2 for the packaging.  I am sure there are many who will consider this a 5 star coffee and you may well be one of them.  If you like Hazelnut then this is probably right up your alley as the hazelnut overpowers the creme brulee flavoring.

column4: Laurence T. Baxter "Step Up to the Call"
column10: When I got to try Melitta's Hazelnut Creme Brulee coffee I wasn't expecting much. Any "flavored" coffee I had ever tried had been overpowering. I'm a big coffee fan, and like flavors like hazelnut or french vanilla from time to time, but usually via creamer so I can control the strength. With Melitta's coffee, I was pleasantly surprised on two counts.First, the flavors were not overpowering - that's a refreshing change! In fact, the hazelnut and creme brulee worked surprisingly well together. It definitely had a unique and complex taste that was more than the sum of its parts.Second, the taste of the coffee was really quite nice. (This was less of a surprise as I've been pleased with Melitta's regular coffee products.) Once prepared the coffee was really very smooth, flavorful, and lacking in bitterness. I brewed it three different strengths before posting this review. At 'medium' strength (2 tablespoons per 10-12oz coffee mug) the coffee was very good, smooth and flavors well blended, and no bitterness at all. At a weaker strength (as my spouse would make it) the flavors still come through but as you would expect the coffee flavor is off. At recommended strength (2 tablespoons per hypothetical 6oz cup) the taste was also very good - the coffee taste excellent, the flavors slightly on the heavy side (especially the creme brulee) and just a hint of bitterness that one would expect with strong coffee. In an office environment where the strength depends on who brews the pot that day, tasting good at any strength is a definite plus.The only (minor) downside at all was the packaging. It was ridiculously hard to open the package. I appreciate the strong seal for the sake of freshness, but I also like to be able to open a coffee bag :)If you're a coffee purist who has never liked flavored coffees, this one will not change your mind. But if you do like flavored coffee and have shied away from prepackaged flavor coffee because the taste has been overpowering, you should definitely consider trying Melitta's flavored coffee.

column9: For a flavored coffee, it's good
column10: First things first: if a company is adding flavor to coffee, don't expect the underlying beans to be Blue Mountain or Kona quality. Just as you don't add mountain dew to a single malt scotch.That said, this stuff has a nice sweet taste, and if you like vanilla and coffee combined with a nutty aftertaste, here's your java.It tastes like what it says it is, and certainly beats out the flavored instant coffees by a mile. You don't get the exquisite levels of taste and clean buzz that Kona etc will give you, but then this stuff ain't aimed at that market, so there you go.Use scissors to open the bag and save yourself plenty of hassle.

column9: Artificial flavor overwhelms the coffee flavor.
column10: First the good stuff:  This coffee is very smooth.  It doesn't have even a hint of bitterness even if one uses far more product per 6 oz. portion of water than the instructions call for.  It is strong, too, in the sense that it delivers a full caffeine load despite tasting 'light.'The problem I have with it is that the coffee itself is infused with so much artificial flavoring that it leaves a metallic, saccharine aftertaste that lingers, actually dwells, in one's mouth for long after the drink is consumed.This would taste better if there were just a bit less flavoring in it, I think.Brewed using Melitta's own single cup system with melitta filters.This is not something that I would drink regularly but is interesting although not particularly satisfying as a novelty.

I really like this coffee, although I have always been a fan of flavored coffees.  What I liked about this coffee is that it is not too strong, not too bitter, and doesnt come with an aftertaste.  So many times flavored coffees do have a kind of pungent aftertaste  I used to think I made the coffee too strong but it would persist no matter how weak I made the coffee  I am not sure if they have used a different process in creating the hazelnut cream flavor than other coffee makers, but they really nailed this one.

I am no expert when it comes to coffee and of course everyone has their own preference as far as strength and tastes go, but I really enjoyed this coffee. I typically do not like flavored coffees or creams, but the hazelnut is very mild and does not overpower the coffee. My wife enjoys it and the price is very fair. Also I like the smaller size of the bags because they wont sit around for a long time losing flavor and freshness.

This is a decent ground coffee with a mild hazelnut flavor.  I would give it a good solid four stars.  What I did not appreciate was the difficult packaging; I believe in freshness too, but this took me a long, frustrating time to get into -- yikes!!

My husband loves coffee and he found this product to be very good. The first thing he notice when he opened the  package is the wonderful rich coffee smell, and yes it tastes as good as it smells. He uses 7 1/2 to 8 scoops for a 12 cup pot since he like his coffee a little on the stronger side. He stated that this coffee is low on acidity, plus he has tried the Gevalia coffees, they taste good, but were too acid for people with a sensitive stomach. Once you open the can, store it in the freezer, take it out only when you need to make a pot of coffee, then put it back in the freezer and the coffee will stay almost as fresh as the day you opened the package.Though I am more of a tea drinker, I do have my share of coffee. I personally enjoy the Hazelnut features a delicate aroma. A flavor like this is perfect dessert coffee; it is a sweet reward anytime. Vanilla Almond is another flavored coffee I enjoy time to time also.Overall, it's a consistent, smooth, delicious coffee. It does not bite back at you and it doesn't "challenge" your palate. It stands alone (black) and holds its own when mixed with milk and sugar. If I HAD to present a criticism, it might be that the ground stuff is sort of fine which does not make it compatible with certain types of coffee makers. For us, it works wonderfully with my good old Mr. Coffee.

Not much to say about the Melitta Cafe Collection Hazelnut Creme Brulee coffee.  The coffee itself was decent enough, although I thought the hazlenut flavor was a tad strong.  It wasn't the best coffee I've ever had but was decent enough for an everyday brew. That being said, I wouldn't pay $20 for this product again since I consider it no better than average.

column9: Tasty!  We like to add a scoop or two to enhance regular coffee
column10: Hazelnut Creme Brulee is tasty, especially as an add-on to enhance the flavor of regular coffee.  I am a big fan of flavored coffee, but my husband prefers plain coffee.  However, he really enjoys this when blended with regular coffee.

Being a very picky coffee drinker, I can say Melitta is one of the best coffees on the market. It's rich, strong and very tasty. There is no after taste and very flavorful. If you enjoy Maxwell House or Chock Full O Nuts, I recommend you try the Melitta brand. The Hazelnut Creme Brulee flavor gives it a nice kick. A near perfect coffee.Katiebabs

column9: Decent flavored coffee if you like that sort of thing
column10: Melitta Hazelnut Creme Brulee is a decent coffee, but not a great coffee. I like coffee that is a bit stronger, fuller and smells like full roast coffee. This coffee actually does smell like vanilla, cream and hazelnuts with a hint of caramel. It smells like a specialty coffee drink at Starbucks or better. The issue I have is that the taste doesn't live up the smell. It tastes like a pretty normal medium roast coffee. That is not to say it's bad. I will finish off the pack, but will probably use most of it for company that prefers this sort of thing.For my own personal taste, I like full roast coffees, black with no sugar. Peet's French Roast (yes, I know it is sorta "burnt" to some of you). What I really, really like are artisan roasted beans from small shops or from Italy and France. One of my favorites is Castroni, from Rome. This is all to say that this coffee is drinkable, but if not for the Amazon Vine review process, I would not have bought it myself.For a better cuppa from Melitta, try the "Blanc et Noir" which is somewhere between medium and full roast. Very smooth and satisfying and you can share it with those who like somewhat less than full-on strong coffee.
This is a delicious, rich, highly aromatic coffee.  The hazelnut is subtle, not overwhelming.A real treat.

column9: Hazelnut Creme Brulee Coffee- What's Not To Love?
column10: Let me start by saying I'm not really a coffee connoisseur or a coffee snob.  I'm not difficult to impress when it comes to coffee, but with that being said, I have my definite likes and dislikes.  I dislike coffee that features anemic flavor, for instance, or coffee that has to be disguised with cream and sugar just to be palatable.Hooray that the Melitta Cafe Collection Hazelnut Creme Brulee Ground Coffee has a good balance of being strong enough to stand up to a little cream and sugar, but not so overpowering that I feel like in drinking it, I'm putting hair on my chest as well as on my teeth.  The hazelnut creme brulee flavor comes out a little more, in my opinion, when there's a little sugar and cream (or skim milk or any dairy variation in between the two extremes)added, but I wasn't overwhelmed, drinking this coffee black, either.I tried brewing it using the Coffee Duck for my Senseo single-cup coffeemaker, and it worked quite well- in fact, as I don't own a bigger coffeemaker, this is my preferred means of making coffee.  I also tried it in my French press, but two things worked against me there- first, I'm just not that skilled yet with the French press, and second, I think the grind might be just a little too fine for French pressing.  It still tasted quite good, but was silty.Overall, I'm really pleased with the flavor of the Melitta Cafe Collection Hazelnut Creme Brulee coffee.  If you like flavored coffee, give it a try!

column9: Starts like a candle, ends like a flavoring for my excess of sugar and milk
column10: First off, it had a strange scent when I opened the bag.  Something fake, but not even dessert like.  More like a Yankee Candle, wax and all.  I decided to try it anyway.  I was very careful with the brew, since I have read other reviews. I got it to only have a slightly bitter aftertaste by stopping brewing a few minutes early.  I am thinking the fine grade makes it hard to brew, where whole beans would be better.  After weighing it down a bit with sugar and milk, it's ok.  Not horrible, not great, ok.  I've heard good things about this company, but wouldn't buy any other coffees from them if they are like this.

column4: Miz Ellen "all the letters of my real name"
column10: I have to limit my caffeine consumption. Because I can't drink very much coffee I want the coffee I drink to be absolutely superb. A large part of my whole coffee experience is enjoying the aroma of coffee as it brews and as I inhale the steam from my cup.The extra fine grind of the MELITTA HAZELNUT CREME BRULEE package meant that I could use less than half the recommended amount of coffee and get a robust, strong brew. The flavor was so smooth I did not need sugar or sweetener to enhance it. I love the way this coffee smells. As I sit writing this review, I smell the wonderful aroma wafting from the kitchen and take small sips of the coffee from a mug that was a gift from a friend. This is civilization and comfort of the highest order.I love cream brulee. This is a great coffee that can be substituted instead of dessert, or with dessert if you must. I recommend using real cream or milk in it rather than non-dairy coffee creamer. I also recommend this coffee for breakfast as a companion to cinnamon rolls, cereal or pancakes with real maple syrup. It's great iced and would make a wonderful flavoring for homemade ice cream or milk shakes.

column9: Bitter, artificial and just plain awful
column10: Bleech.That's how I'd describe this coffee.  To be fair, I'm one of those purists that grind their own beans and shy away from artificial flavors.  However, I'm open minded and gave this a try.  For a treat sometimes, a flavored coffee can curb some of those urges for a sugary treat.Opening the back I was instantly hit with the smell.  Strong and overpowering.  The smell wasn't of coffee, it was of some air freshener you'd find in a gas station checkout.  I still decided to brew it though, so I could be fair in the review.I tried it via standard drip brew, toddy, aeropress and french press.  No matter what I tried, the brew came out overly bitter.  This is partially due to the extremely fine grind.  When I tried it with creamer and/or sweetener, the brew was more tolerable.  I was still tasting the artificial flavor more than coffee accents.If you generally like the swill most companies server in their breakrooms, then this is definitely a step up.  For those of us with a bit more refined coffee palate, take a pass on this and add your own Torani syrups to achieve the hazelnut and vanilla flavoring.

I have the Creme Brulee flavor of this Melita coffee.  It brews a great cup, I did not taste any bitterness in the flavors.  I tend to use slightly less than the recommended amount when I brew a cup of java.  I make my coffee with french vanilla creamer, and the creme brulee mixed with the creamer made my cup of coffee extra sweet.  It was like dessert which I loved but may not be the preference for everyone.

I've had this coffee a few times, both on ice and hot.  It has a great aroma, and tastes very good - not too sweet, but the hazelnut flavor is definitely there.  My coffee purist roommate didn't like it, but he doesn't like any flavored coffee.  You can't go wrong with this coffee.
brews up fine.  strong coffee with an almost overwhelming hazlenut flavor and aroma.  if you love hazlenu; you will love this.  i like my flavored coffees a bit more subtle.

column9: Very Good, but at what price?
column10: This is really a good coffee, but perhaps not for a true connaisseur.  Nonethless, this is quite good:  it is very smooth, and has a good flavor of hazelnuts.  It is not smooth enough to make truly strong; it starts to get a bit bitter.  If you are an afficionado of coffee houses, this may not be for you, but if you will settle for higher-end grocery store coffee, this is a good pick.  The package is 11 ounces so the price per pound is 42% higher than per package.  Still, at this price, not a bad buy.

I've tried a lot of coffee in my life. I'm not a huge fan of plain, black coffee so I generally stick with flavored varieties. Hazelnut can be hit-or-miss. Sometimes the hazelnut flavor can be so subtle you'd almost forget it's flavored coffee. Other times, the flavoring hits you over the head and tastes like you're chewing on a nut instead of drinking coffee.This coffee is a wonderful balance. You can definitely taste the hazelnut, but you can also taste the creme brulee, which mellows it out nicely. It has the perfect mix of nuttiness and sweetness with the bite of coffee in there too.I really enjoyed this coffee and will definitely buy it again in the future.

We've tried and loved other flavored coffees, but were a little worried that the Melitta version would not be very good because it costs so much less.We were pleasantly surprised, the coffee itself is a very smooth and rich blend, and my husband (who loves hazelnut creamer) is absolutely enamored of this Creme Brulee Hazelnut flavor. I'm not a fan of nutty-flavored  coffee, so it's not my favorite, but I can't wait to try some of the other Melitta versions, like the Vanilla Bean.

I mostly enjoy bold and extra taste coffees. Among the flavored ones, I like hazelnut flavored ones better. So I expected something really good from melitta's hazelnut flavored. I have never tried one before, but I knew they make good coffees and the prices are not that cheap either.However, the taste of my first brew was not that great. It was too strong, bitter  and sour. I thought I might put too much coffee, although I knew I put right amount of coffee for my daily ritual. So I tried second time with less coffee and same amount of water. It still had this very sour after-taste with less bitterness. Finally, I tried putting more water with less coffee and now the taste was too watery. However, there was still strong sour taste left behind in my mouth. Since I am not a coffee expert, so to speak, I could not figure out what made this coffee so sour. I even checked the expiration date, but  it was still valid.After all, it took little bit of time to get used to this extra ordinary taste, yet it was not too pleasant coffee experience for me. Maybe it can be better with sugar and creme, but unfortunately, I enjoy black, nothing added coffees.

column9: Depends on your tastes, but I like this
column10: Different strokes for different folks.  I am not a certified coffee sommelier so I can only give you my average "joe" opinion.For my coffees I happen to like slightly bitter, slightly sweet coffees with a hint of nut so this one was in my wheelhouse.  I found this cup of joe to my liking with slight bitterness and subtle hints of hazelnut and caramel while not being too overpowering in any one area.  I would buy this coffee again.  Minus one star for being bit higher on price side.

column9: Wife loved it but the jury is still out for me.
column10: I know that people today are looking for unique and different flavors for everything they ingest.  Because I am not against trying new things, I am willing to try most.  So, when I found this coffee, I thought, what the heck.  I made it 2 ways.  First, I made a hot version which with a little cream and sugar, made for an okay cup of coffee.  Secondly, I made it as an iced coffee which, when prepared the same way, I found to be a little better than the hot.  My wife, who only drinks flavored everything, liked it a lot and said she would like to get more of this.  So, while I liked the flavor, to me, nothing beats good old fashioned "coffee flavored coffee."

This coffee tastes great!  The hazelnut is subtle, which I liked and the creme brulee taste was a really nice addition.  I made it two ways: one was with my 12 cup drip coffee maker and the other was with a 6 cup french press.  The taste was consistent both ways.  The coffee was smooth and never bitter.  I will definitely get this coffee again.

column9: For those who like a sweeter cup of java
column10: I am pretty hard core when it comees to my morning cup of coffee.  A Starbucks addict, I grind my own, and prefer the more robust blends.  No cream, no sugar, just black bold coffee.  So, it was a step out of my comfort zone to try the Melitta Hazelnut Creme Brulee coffee.The coffee comes packaged in a foil vacuum sealed bag.  Smells delicious when you can finally get it open.  The grind is perfect for my French press, and would also work well with a coffeemaker.  I use the "usual" amount of coffee for brewing and the result is a smooth, if rather sweet, cup of delicious coffee.Flavor:  I can't speak to whether it tastes like real hazelnuts or creme brulee from a fine restaurant, but it definitely has the scent and flavor of other "hazelnut" flavored coffees.  I did not find the flavoring to be overpowering, and thought it enhanced the coffee nicely.Acidity:  A very smooth cup of coffee, which no bitterness, and no heartburn.Use:  This is a little too much for me for my morning cup of coffee.  When I'm not awake, I'm looking for my standard Starbucks.  But later in the morning, or sometimes in the afternoon, this is the perfect cup of coffee.It is possible to "subscribe" to this coffee, and Amazon will kindly deliver it to you on a regular basis.For those of you who like a lighter, flavored coffee, you will probably love this.  You may be able to skip your coffee additives and drink it black.  While it won't replace my regular morning brew, it has definitely found its place in my house.

My wife and I tried Melitta Cafe's Hazelnut Creme Brulee with three different coffee machines, even had it iced once, and the results were pretty consistent across the board: A rich coffee with *hints* of hazelnut rather than an overpowering flavor, ideal for a quiet weekend morning.That the flavoring didn't dominate the coffee was a welcome change from flavored coffees that seem intent on telling you, "WE'RE FLAVORED." No need to throw it in the drinker's face. Here, the flavoring is a small enhancement, tempering the coffee's natural bitterness (most noticeable here in the aftertaste) and adding complexity to the aroma. It's very nice.For those who enjoy their coffee iced, this was especially good prepared that way. Over the course of a large cup I tried it just on ice, then with sugar, then with sugar and cream. Very tasty in all three variations.Recommended for those who'd like a flavored coffee without being hit over the head with artificial-tasting flavors. Maybe a few bucks more than you'd normally spend, but worth it for a change of pace.
I love the smell and flavor of this coffee. It's rich, indulgent and delicious. The hazelnut flavor didn't register so much with me as the caramel. That's just fine since I love caramel.
Sorry, but I was not a big fan of this flavored coffee.  The smell was too sweet and the flavor had an artificial and bitter taste.  It was drinkable, but I think I will stick to my Starbucks.

column9: Good coffee but takes trial-and-error re: amount to use.
column10: I brought this coffee up to my parents' cabin on a vacation and we all drank it for about a week. No one in my family is really a coffee connoisseur (including myself), so I can't really speak to the complications of the flavor or anything like that.We did all think it was good coffee, the hazelnut flavor was clearly present but not overpowering, and it wasn't too sweetsy as some flavored coffees can be.Downsides are the proportions of coffee / water seem to be a little different than the plain ol' coffee my parents normally use. I couldn't tell if it was too strong or too weak, but something tasted a little different to me (I mean besides the hazelnut flavor). I think this coffee might require slightly more to be added to the maker before brewing to bring out the hazelnut flavor as opposed to the amount you'd add for normal coffee.This coffee tastes good w/ cream and sugar, if you're into it, or black, as I prefer. One thing I'd caution against is mixing it with those flavored 'Coffee Mate' creamers. My mom and sister were doing that and had some pretty nasty cups (Pumpkin Spice and Caramel were nasty to me). Best off drinking this stuff black or with normal cream/sugar. Probably obvious to everyone else, but some people in my family are addicted to Coffee Mate.Anyway, that's it. I'm no coffee snob but do think this is good coffee, with a nice hazelnut flavor. A little pricey compared to the good sales I can get on coffee at my local grocery store, but worth a shot if you're interested.

I did find that I needed to use just slightly less than what i usually prefer (which is a tablespoon per cup).It is rich and flavorful coffee, and the hazelnut flavoring is not overpowering.The single pack that I got seemed to be very fresh and very finely ground.

I could die happy just sticking my face in the bag and smelling this stuff.  Ecstasy!  It brews up just as tasty as it smells.  Not bitter, just the right strength with the normal amount of grounds I usually use.  My standard fare is plain coffee with a ton of Hazelnut Coffeemate.  This coffee I could almost drink black.  ...almost... ;-)

column9: Nice Coffee, Not so nice package
column10: I tried this coffee with a bit of trepidation. I'm not a fan of hazelnut. I've always found the flavor to be a bit overwhelming which is odd because I really like hazelnuts. Not so here. This was a very tasty hazelnut. The smell was subtle and not at all over-powering. The flavor was nice, nutty without getting into oily & nasty. The coffee in the package is a nice dark color. It's very finely ground so should work well in capacino machines. It brewed up very nicely in our french press and our drip coffee machine. I really enjoyed the experience.The bag on the other hand, I struggled for quite a while to get it open and finally just had to cut the top off. Which made it more than bit difficult to use for later storage. I understand that to retain the freshness, sealing the bag is very important, but in order for me to consume the product, opening the bag is equally important. And since I may be under the assumption that I can continue to store the coffe in the bag, like other brands, making it so I have to partially destroy the bag in order to open it seems slightly counter-intuitive.Anyway, great coffee, not so great packaging. If you get it, make plans for alternate storage.

column9: Excellent flavor and aroma - beware of overbrew
column10: The first batch of this coffee was made with more grounds than needed - and ended up foul tasting and bitter as one would pretty much expect.  However, after letting that fall from my memory, another batch was brewed (correctly), and the flavor and aroma was outstanding.Would recommend to anyone that enjoys flavored coffee.

column9: Good coffee, but needs a bit of cream
column10: Melitta Café Collection Gourmet Coffee: Hazelnut Crème BruleeFirst of all, a summary, for those of you who only want the brass tacks: using a high-quality drip coffee maker, the result was a pleasurable but not perfect experience, and so I give this coffee four out of five stars. If you are willing to add good cream to your coffee, then I would even venture to give this blend a full five-of-five rating.Before I even opened the package, I was hit by the smell of its contents, the strong scents wafting through every tiny opening. The smell, however, was of cinnamon rolls, not of coffee. Cautiously cutting open the container, I put it to my nose and was rewarded slightly by the previously noted sugary odor mixed with a very gentle smell of ground coffee beans (the package didn't indicate the date of their grinding, but, having received them for review, I assumed they were relatively fresh.)I have to admit that I was a bit concerned about using the drip coffee makers because of the fineness of the grind, but nonetheless I approached them hoping for the best.One of the first things that struck my attention was the fact that the instructions on the side of the bag indicated a measure of two teaspoons of coffee per six ounces of water. The standard measurement for gourmet coffee is two tablespoons per six ounces. (Although two tablespoons per six ounces provides too strong a flavor for many people, it pulls out the best taste with the least amount of bitterness. Extra water should be added AFTER it has been brewed to lighten the coffee to the desired level. NEVER decrease the amount of coffee to make it less strong!)To properly determine the appeal of the coffee to the typical buyer, I decided to prepare the beans two ways:  (a) via a high-quality drip coffee maker using the "two tablespoons of coffee grinds per cup of water" measurement, and (b) via a more standard generic  drip appliance, using its recommended "two teaspoons of coffee grinds per cup of water" measurement.  I first tasted the results straight (without any added flavoring), and then with cream.Using the high-quality drip coffee maker, the results were quite satisfactory. The taste of smoky wood was definitely there, and the flavor brought to mind fire-roasted beans, slightly burnt to enhance their essence. The hazelnut flavoring was more of a scent than a taste, lingering on the tongue and in the nostrils after the rest has been swallowed.Good coffee prepared correctly should never be bitter. Never. So I was disappointed to find that there was, indeed, a small amount of bitter aftertaste in the cup I drank.Also to my disappointment was a bit of a sourness that permeated the entire experience, like the beans had been left to ripen a bit too long.To my surprise, one sensation that was not there was the sugar and cinnamon that hit me so hard when I initially opened the bag. I can only assume those flavors were run across the beans to provide a pre-brew experience to tantalize the potential buyer, but they didn't make it across after the water had been applied.So, as stated at the beginning of my review, using a high-quality drip appliance the result was a pleasurable but not perfect experience, and a good start for my tasting process.With the initial "pure" tasting complete, I added some cream to my coffee. The result was wonderful. All of the bad tastes were washed away instantly. No more sourness or bitterness. Granted, a coffee drinker should not have to rely on something external to wash away unpleasant side flavors, but in this situation it produced a cup I eagerly look forward to drinking again. Five out of five stars for that experience.Next, I turned to the "department-store" brand of coffee maker and used eight tablespoons (the equivalent of 24 teaspoons) with 12 cups of water. The result was passable. It retained most of the flavors of the stronger brewing but in a watered-down state. Unfortunately, the bitterness and sourness - the two worst flavors - came out in full force. Judging purely by this taste test, I would give the coffee at most three stars.Next I added cream and, to my pleasant surprise, it again completely wiped away all of the unpleasant flavors, leaving behind a delightfully light cup that flowed smoothly down my throat. Once more, five out of five stars.I should note that I gave the lighter version (with cream) to a friend who generally does not enjoy coffee, and she loved it, going so far as to say it was one of the best cups of coffee she had had in years.I generally don't like flavored coffees, but this one won me over as a good attempt and something I'm happy to keep on my shelf. Again I wish to note that I am disappointed that the addition of cream was a necessity in removing the very noticeable bad tastes from this blend, but at least they could be removed, which is more than I can say for many coffees out there."Black as the devil, hot as hell, pure as an angel, sweet as love."-- Charles Maurice de Talleyrand (1754-1838) speaking of the perfect cup of coffee.Reviewed by BriannaFootnote from Grey: I agree with Brianna's review. This coffee is much improved with the addition of cream. However, I got a very noticable hazlenut flavor from the coffee.

I am a coffee junky, so this was perfect. It was good, though very rich, so easy on the cream and sugar if you use it. I also had to add a lot more than usual to make it a robust brew. Other than that, it's coffee!

The packaging looked like the usual pull open coffee bag but was very tightly glued closed. I had to use scissors to open it then put the whole bag in a zip lock bag. This is a pretty good coffee, it makes a nice morning brew. The caramel and hazelnut flavor is  rather subtle but it grew on me. This is not as aromatic as some  flavored coffees. The coffee brews up quite strong and has a bit of a bitter edge at full strength  which one does expect from Creme Brulee flavored products. Though it was  not ecstatically wonderful it was a satisfactory everyday coffee which we enjoyed throughout our coffee drinking day.

For my taste, it is mild coffee: I needed to use two tablespoonfuls per 8 oz cup instead of two teaspoonfuls per 6 oz cup as recommended on the label.  Aroma is not strong either. Hazelnut flavor is a question of personal taste but I prefer it and creme brûlée  with desert. It is very finely ground coffee and may not work with all filter less coffee makers.Conclusion - just an average mild coffee, nothing extraordinary.

I generally just drink coffee to have some caffeine and a warm drink in the morning.  Fancy coffees generally don't do any more for me than Yuban.  I do like hazelnut coffee though.  And this was one of the better ones that I've tried.  It's not bitter, and the taste doesn't try to overwhelm you.  Sure, I'll buy it again.

column9: Warm and flavorful and especially good with desserts
column10: I enjoy a good flavored coffee from time to time and Melitta coffees are a solid choice for natural tasting flavor that isn't overdone.This coffee is a warm creamy nutty flavored blend that goes well with desserts like brownies or spice cake. I would use it to serve after a dinner party or brew a pot during a wintry evening to warm up. Even tones and a smooth finish make it easy to drink and I would definitely buy it as a change of pace.
Superb coffee with Hazelnut Creme Brulee flavoring. Well packaged. Excellent taste and smell. Mouth watering good.

For mass-produced coffee, this is some really good stuff.  My husband, who is notoriously picky about the coffee he'll brew, scoffed a little at the flavor, but asked me if I'd buy some more when the bag was gone -- which is really high praise coming from His Coffee Snobbiness.The acid level was a little high for my stomach without milk, but other than that one little thing, I'm a convert, too.  Well roasted, subtle flavor.

column9: Delicious coffee after a long day at work...
column10: I had never tried this particular brand of coffee before and I must say, I was impressed.  To be honest, most times I don't go for the flavored coffees;  to me they tend to be a little too artificial tasting or overly powerful in aroma and weak on taste.  While this coffee is not for my everyday morning, this was a great treat to have after dinner.  I liked that it was smooth, flavorful, and not overwhelming.  It even replaced any ideas I had had about having a dessert or a snack because it was so fufilling.  My husband even wanted to try some after the smell of the coffee lingered into the living room, and he is not a coffee drinker at all.  I would definitely recommend this to anyone I know and I already have.

I think I have a new coffee!  This coffee brews up perfectly each and every time. It's not bitter, but exceptionally smooth, flavorful and honestly, has now become my morning coffee.  If you're not overly fond of hazelnut, don't worry about it in this coffee.  You can hardly note it's presence with the creme brulee, it just acts more of an enhancer than anything else.  I honestly hate hazelnut anything and was quite wary of trying this coffee. Am I ever glad that I did!  I can't wait until it's done brewing every morning, if that gives you some idea!  It's not overpowering, just a very rich, flavorful, smooth way to start the day or even finish with an after dinner drink.  I take mine black and even those friends who don't, love this coffee black.  The true test of the flavor of an excellent coffee.  Highly highly recommend!

Actually a 3.5.As others have said the bag was quite impossible to open. I gave up and had to cut the top of the bag which makes the little wire reclose hinges useless. So that was annoying.The coffee smells wonderful in the bag & when it starts brewing, it smells even better. So great smell all around.The flavor has hints of nut, but not necessarily Hazlenut. We didn't get any creme brulee, but the flavor is fine.For the price (6$ a bag) it's about the same as a good bag of flavored coffee from our local grocery. Were this there, I would buy it for this price. Comprable to "Eight O'Clock" or Dunkin Donuts. Give it a try.

column9: "It's all right, I guess. Nothing I would rush out to buy."
column10: I have measured out my life with coffee spoons.~T.S. EliotHe was my cream, and I was his coffee -And when you poured us together, it was something.~Josephine BakerI'm more of a tea girl than a coffee girl, but I definitely like some java on occasion and tend to associate it with good things: warmth on a hot day, sitting around the table with friends and loved ones, that extra jolt that helps the world make sense. And I really tend to like flavored coffees. I tried this product twice and it really left me feeling right down the middle. I didn't love it or hate it, but it was okay. The first pot was made after Sunday dinner and drank black and the second one was made yesterday morning where I drank it on the front porch while I read and bird watched while the rain fell gently and I had it with cream and sugar. These are two nearly ideal set-ups to evoke good coffee feelings, and I just wasn't impressed. There was mild gratitude for the caffeine during the morning session.Yes, it tasted like hazel nut, and I guess Creme Brulee, and I like both of these flavors and the coffee was smooth, but the end result wasn't as pleasing as it should be, as I anticipated it being, as the random cup of coffee at one of the local restaurants is on any given Sunday.Later on in the day, my husband asked me about it since he was the won I conned into brewing the second pot. I told him pretty much what I said here and that I'd probably assign 3 stars. I asked him what he thought, "It's all right, I guess. Nothing I would rush out to buy. 3 stars sounds about right."I'll drink it, but like the man said, I won't rush out to buy it.

Okay coffee lovers, this is a wonderful product!First, this is a very smooth blend, which means that there is no bitterness, no bad after taste, no acid burning later. The low acid in the bean selection is especially excellent. Also, the hazelnut flavor is great, but the touch of creme brulee is wonderful! The flavor makes this coffee very rich and full-bodied tasting. I usually like creme and sugar in my coffee, but this particular blend is very nice without the extras - that is how good the flavor is for me.I highly recommend this particular Melitta coffee blend.

I drink a lot of coffee each day and I drink it black with just a bit of sugar.  I prefer to drink organically grown coffee but I made an exception for this one.  My first impression was the packaging - it's terrible and I ended up having to open it using a pair of scissors.  After brewing several pots of it I have to say I'm not that impressed with it.  It's smooth enough, with no bitterness but the overall flavor is weak and bland.  It's not a bad coffee but it's by no means the best coffee I've ever had and once this bag is used up I wouldn't buy any to replace it.

The flavor is not at all subtle, even when I reduced the amount of coffee to make it less noticeable. The hazelnut definitely tends to overpower the coffee flavor. That being said, I still like this coffee so much I don't mind. It smells great while it's brewing, and I feel like I'm having a treat, rather than a regular cup of coffee. The grind is very fine and the coffee is smooth. I always add a little cream to my coffee, but I also tried this black with sweetener and it was still very good. In fact, I like it so much it's the only coffee I'm using right now and my regular brand is staying in the cabinet.As others have commented, the packaging wasn't so great. I gave up trying to open it and used scissors. Other than that, a great product.

The moment you open the bag, the room is filled with the fragrant aroma of hazelnut.Mixed with the intense coffee smell, it makes you want to sip a cup of nice coffee right away.The coffee after brewed, is not dry like Columbia.  It's not dark like French.It's a desert coffee as it is meant to be, hazelnut flavor.It is smooth, doesn't leave a bitter after taste in your mouth.Highly recommended.

My favorite flavored coffee with cream and sugar is hazelnut and there's nothing I found that compares to this flavor until I tried this coffee.  Melitta's Hazelnut Creme Brulee is like a decadent dessert.The only drawback I found was that it was impossible to open the bag; you have to cut it open with a scissor.  Other than this, I highly recommend this coffee.

If you are like me and like your coffee "strong and black" you have to be careful as most coffees tend to become bitter when strong and black. MELITTA HAZELNUT CREME BRULEE has a bit of a bite to it, but not as bad as most coffees. The coffee is pretty smooth, but the flavor is not as rich as I would like for it to be. This is an ultra fine grind so you won't use as much coffee. Overall, this is not bad coffee, but I was hoping for something better.

column4: James Beswick "In my day, we had 9 planets."
column9: Fine hazelnut taste but weak coffee
column10: I'm not a fan of flavored coffee, but the hazelnut flavor was balanced well and didn't get overpowering after the second (third, fourth then fifth) cup. My only issue was that the coffee is quite weak - and I'm comparing this again Peet's standard brew blend and Costco's ubiquitous-but-cheap Kirkland Signature coffee. If you enjoy flavored coffee to taste more like the flavor that the coffee, this may be a good choice, whereas if you prefer a hint of flavor then you may be wondering where the coffee went.

The Melitta Creme Brulee Coffee is bland and flavorless, despite its flavored nature.Whether drinking it black or with a bit of creamer, I was hard-pressed to recognizethis product as coffee at all. It might be OK for those with weak palates, but I wantmy coffee to TASTE like coffee. The Melitta Classique Supreme is a far better choice,especially for the price...how can that one be so good and this one so lame? I don'tknow, but I hereby advise you to walk away from Creme Brulee toute de suite.By the way: the package is difficult to open without spilling some contents.

I'm not a coffee drinker but My Husband is a very big coffee drinker.He likes to grind his own beans, and usually is not into these types of flavored designer coffee's.That said,He was pleasently surprised. He enjoyed this coffee. It was not too sweet, and he never adds sugar or cream to his coffee.The flavor was not so strong, that it was sickening sweet. or over done so to speak.It was nicely blended for a full flavor.I have to say, the smell went all through my house, but it was not an unpleasant smell.It was a very yummy scent.We used this in our electric coffee maker, not the Melitta.It does not give any ingredient on the bag to this coffee,if any sugar has been added etc.!It does say: Extra find Grind.Hazelnut Naturally & Aritificilly flavored! (of what?) A European classic, Sweet Caramel and rich vanilla infused with the flavor of wild hazelnuts.Flavored coffee.Would We buy this again? probably not, or maybe for the Holidays or to give as a gift to bring to a someones house for dinner.

This was a great, light coffee. There was no bitterness at all to it, which made it perfect for me, and the smell is just amazingly good. If you're someone who really needs a strong coffee that hits you like a slap in the face in the morning, this isn't for you, but I found it to be really perfect for an after-dinner cup, or a 10am cup. Really tasty, and a treat for the senses.

column9: nice flavor (if you liked flavored coffees), but packaging is not so good
column10: If I could, I would give this product 3.5 stars.  I do think the flavor is good -- though not exceptional; if you like flavored coffees, you'll probably like this.  The coffee flavor underneath the "hazelnut creme brulee" flavor is mild.  The beans are finely ground -- a little more finely than prepackaged beans from Starbucks, for comparison -- which makes this product suitable for drip coffee makers but unsuitable for percolators or any other coffee maker that requires a coarser grind.What prompted me to knock my rating down to 3 stars rather than rounding up to 5 stars is that the packaging is not very good.  How can this be?  There are many, many brands of coffee that use similar, vacuum packed, foil lined bags.  With very rare exceptions, these bags are easy to open without tearing and easy to reseal.  This Melita bag, on the other hand, seemed like it was glued to keep children out.  When I eventually got the glue to give way, the bag ended up with a few large tears around the top, making it difficult to get the beans out of the bag without making a mess.

I was hesitant at first when I saw this coffee. I'm not a big hazelnut fan since most companies over do the hazelnut in the coffee and creamers. But I admit that I was pleasantly surprised. This is a fine grind coffee that smells rich and slightly sweet. I loved the smell of the brewed coffee and the taste was better than the smell. The crème brulee made the coffee slightly sweet and I didn't need anything to sweeten my coffee for once. Also, there is a hint of hazelnut and that just adds to everything.If you like a slightly sweet, bold coffee, you will like this. The price is also pretty good compared to the cost of other flavored coffees. I think I'm going to have to start ordering my coffee from now on.Shawn KovacichCreator of numerous books and DVD's.

Bag is tightly vacuum packed in a sturdy plastic/aluminum pouch.  It has a strand of aluminum wire so you reseal its top every time you use it.  Important, as coffee looses much of its aroma and freshness when not properly sealed. I also regularly replace it back to the refrigerator once opened.This coffee is good, but not exciting enough.  The flavor is somewhat a little bland. The aroma likewise does not have a strong punch to it.  I do like the hazel flavor coffee, but the taste here is very subtle.

I received one 11 oz bag of Melitta coffee from the Vine program. I had requested Hazelnut Creme Brulee and that is what the shipping tag indicated. However, the coffee bag shows it to be Blanc et Noir so that is what I am reviewing. I am a morning coffee drinker and usually have one or two mugs. This blend of light and dark roasts is a fairly average coffee blend. It is somewhat heavier and darker than what I am used to having. I find it to be slightly more bitter than what I prefer. The aroma is somewhat pleasing. For a fairly inexpensive coffee it is a somewhat interesting change from my usual brand which is Gevalia. I would not use this on a regular basis but for a change of pace it offers an acceptable different experience.

column9: Husband Loves this Hazlenut/Creme Brule combo but it's Too Sweet for me
column10: My husband has fallen in love with this coffee. He has always added Hazlenut flavoring to his morning cup of joe & Creme Brule is is favorite dessert, so I decided to give this a try. For him, it's a total winner. We have a high-pressure brewing coffee machine that makes all coffees taste better, so don't know if he would like it as much in a regular drip coffee maker.How do I like it? Not so much, at least for mornings; it's just too sweet for me. I gave it 4 stars based on my husband's rating - 1 star off based on my thoughts.

Hey! This is good stuff. I like it!  It is tasty cold or hot.  The flavoring is subtle yet distinctive.  A perfect caffine pick-me-up. I frequently use flavored creamers but this is better.  The coffee is good quality with no bitter aftertaste.  I drank it hot with and without milk.  Both ways were tasty.  I found I didn't need sugar at all.  I also made a big glass of iced coffee, topped with whipped cream --- better than the local coffeehouse.  For my final taste test before writing this review, I tossed a strong brew in the blender with some dark chocolate ice cream.  Yum!  Ok, that's enough, I gotta go order some more of this stuff before I run out...  let's see, what else can I make ... bye!

So I brought this coffee into the office to get a few opinions instead of just one. First of, some people may like their coffee REALLY strong, but if you don't, don't follow the instructions on the pack. The recommendation on the pack was to use 2 teaspoons of coffee per 6oz of water. I went by the instructions and the coffee packed some punch! I could only drink it after diluting it with a LOT of creamer.My favorite part about this coffee was the aroma while it was brewing - the whole office smelled awesome. We all liked the taste alright. It definitely had a hint of hazelnut and was even better when combined with hazelnut creamer. All in all, I'm giving it a thumbs up!

The Melitta Cafe Collection coffee is billed as being 'extra fine grind', which made me a bit worried, since I've had problems in the past with coffee that is little more than powder.  I was happy to find that the extra fine grind is only a little bit finer than the regular ground I use every day at work.The hazelnut flavoring imbued in the coffee tastes very good, with a nice finish.  Sometimes these flavored coffees are overpowering, making it seem as though you are drinking coffee-flavored spices rather than the other way around.  This is a very nice balance of coffee and hazelnut.  It saves me from using an additional flavoring, such as in the creamer or in a separate syrup.Melitta has a winner here.  I'm looking forward to trying the french vanilla flavor (Melitta calls that, 'Parisian Vanilla').  If it's anything like the hazelnut, I expect another winner.

I don't typically drink coffee much these days as 1) it's a bit too messy at home to grind and brew and 2) I like those flavored sweeteners and sugar is on the *no* list these days. That said, I decided to get this when it showed up on Vine and brought it into the office to share with everyone and see what they thought - and the opinions were all over the board. The boss hated it, but he doesn't like the flavored stuff at all. The lads at the sales counter were thumbs up (of course, after the Folgers they usually get anything's a treat).Me, I'm kind of *meh*. I picked up on a sharp, bitter taste and while it was OK enough it didn't bowl me over. I prefer to stick with freshly ground Starbucks with a vanilla flavoring added to sweeten the pot. And since I can't have that I'll stick with my morning tea. Two stars from the boss and I, four from the lads, rounded out to three.

This is the first time I've ever reviewed a food product so bear with me...My first experience was with trying to open the package. It was very frustrating as it wouldn't pull apart cleanly. I eventually took a pair of scissors and snipped off the top and poured it into a different container. Not the best start to things. But, the coffee brewed up nicely, is very finely ground, and made a delicious cup of flavored coffee. It was a good blend of hazelnut and creme brulee as I could taste both flavors in each sip.I look forward to more mornings with this nice blend.

'Melitta Cafe Collection Hazelnut Creme Brulee Ground Coffee' was delicious.  Overall it was a good dark roasted coffee.  The aroma of the grounds was nice (to me the coffee drinker and my non coffee drinking friend) and the extra fine grind was perfect.  After brewing, I found the taste to be really well done-- it wasn't too strong and the little bit of aftertaste could have been far worse!  If you're in the mood for a good flavored coffee, try Melitta's Hazelnut Creme Brulee!

Hazelnut Creme Brulee sounds like it might be too sweet, but it is smooth and flavorful, not at all bitter and makes a very enjoyable cup of coffee.  I have used it in both a Melitta one-cup drip and also in a french press with success, but the french press demands that you use a little more coffee to begin with.  I drink my coffee black but I can easily imagine cream or milk turning this into an almost guilty pleasure.  I also intend to make it a little stronger, chill it and add ice for a refreshing iced coffee on a hot summer day.

column9: Delicious Coffee with and Incredible Smell...
column10: I really enjoyed this coffee.  I thought the coffee was delicious and the smell incredible.  My only complaint would be that it was a bit on the weak side.  I enjoy a stronger coffee but for those that want a mild coffee then I think this would be an excellent choice.

column9: Makes a most enjoyable cup of coffee.
column10: I am pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoy this flavored coffee. I like it both as a dessert type after dinner coffee as well as an anytime coffee. I only drink coffee sweetened (preferably with honey) and with half and half, and that is how I sampled Melitta's Hazelnut Creme Brulee. My coffee of choice, which I've been drinking for about 2 decades, is Peet's brand coffee (which I get shipped to me and of which I enjoy and drink several varieties, with my top favorites being French and Italian). I always buy whole beans and grind beans one cup at a time. I then make it in a filter cone, and every once in a while in a French press or an espresso machine. If I'm making coffee for 2 or 3 people, I either use the French Press or I make each cup separately, using a separate filter cone for each cup. And I'm always careful when measuring beans and ground coffee so that I can keep the flavor and body of the coffee I drink day after day consistent. (The Melitta Hazelnut Creme Brulee is ground to an "Extra Fine Grind," which means it's unsuitable for use in a French Press.)On a caffeine buzz scale, I find that Melitta Hazelnut Creme Brulee weaker than any variety of Peet's (or Starbucks), but that's fine with me because I don't always want or need a caffeine buzz as strong as the kind I get from a tall cup of Peet's (or Starbucks). Sometimes I regret getting a strong caffeine buzz because it leaves me feeling a tad headachey. So it's nice to know that there's a tasty, good quality alternative that is less intense on a caffeine buzz scale.I would, and probably will, buy Melitta Cafe Collection ground coffee on occasion (e.g., if I'm running low on Peet's or money to buy Peet's, or if I'm asked to bring ground coffee to a holiday gathering where it will be prepared in a coffee maker of some sort). I would like to try the Melitta Cafe Collection Parisian Vanilla variety, as well as their Vienna Roast (Peet's Vienna Roast was one of my favorites but they discontinued it) and Blanc et Noir (which, according to Melitta's site, is "Deep with a Rich Finish"). I have tried their Classique Supreme variety (and will review it separately), and like it as much as I like the Hazelnut. I received free samples of the Hazelnut Creme Brulee and the Classique Supreme for review purposes, but based on the prices listed at Melitta's site and here at Amazon I'd say that the price is right and is lower than I would've expected for coffee of this quality.Update: I spoke on the phone with a Melitta customer service representative about the difficulty I had opening both 11 oz. sample bags of their Cafe Collection coffee I received, and she said that Melitta recommends using scissors along the top. I found it impossible to open either bag without tearing holes in the upper half of each bag.

column9: I can't believe I'm reviewing this, but....
column10: ...it's just one of those awesome little things you have to share. I was stationed in Hawaii for more than 8 of the last 24+ years at different times and one of the joys of Hawaii (among many) is the great local food. The downside is that finding the particulars that make local Hawaiian cuisine so fun and tasty are hard to locate in one place in most of the rest of the USA. A common favorite is a dish called Ahi Poke. Though you can Poke lots of other fish, Ahi Poke is the most frequently enjoyed. Ahi is just tuna, though a slightly different type. The one used for this dish is a sushi grade raw Ahi. The part that is Poke is a blend of various spices, oils and a specific seaweed and it gives an absolutely unique and delightful flavor. It is a firm family favorite whether we simply scoop some over a dish of rice or make it into a sushi wrap. Most people who like any sushi at all love Ahi Poke. Alas, thinking I should be able to find all the various spices and ingredients in any big city I didn't bring any with me from Hawaii. Getting all of those ingredients in one spot proved impossible. Even just consistently locating all of them anywhere was an exercise in hours of cross city driving and frustration. So, on the off chance one day I typed in a search for the brand of pre-packaged Ahi Poke mix I used in Hawaii..Noh..and voila: Amazon had it! I bought a case just in time for my nephews birthday and he was absolutely gobsmacked to have a nice big bowl of his favorite food.  This package makes THE Ahi Poke. You can find recipes using more common seaweeds or other substitutions all over the net, but this is the real deal. That same rich and exotic flavor blend you remember from that shabby shop on the North Shore is right in this package. Each individual package is labeled to work for 1 pound of fish but I found that using 3/4 of a pound gives about the correct flavor. A pound makes it a tad weak. Of course, that's a lot of fish anyway. We tend to think in terms of hamburger or steak but the richness of raw Ahi means people will generally eat significantly less in ounces than they would other meats.  Love this stuff and I certainly recommend it. The price may seem high for a packet of spice, but the bulk prices on that seaweed, when you can even get it, is pretty high so this is actually quite reasonable. Happy Sushi!

column9: NOH Brings the taste of Hawaii to You
column10: Every time I traveled home to Hawaii I use to buy bags of Limu seaweed and Hawaiian salt in bulk and take them home. The Limu seaweed is the main ingredient of Poke and I always felt Limu seaweed had to be kept frozen if it was not consumed immediately. Although I prefer mature Limu seaweed, the NOH Poke mix will not disappoint you.

column9: Enticing if you can tolerate the %of cocoa

I've become somewhat of a dark chocolate snob :) ever since I changed my eating habits for the better. Now a piece of dark chocolate after dinner is my dessert (instead of cake, ice cream, etc - not that I don't splurge once in awhile :)I've tasted big brands, local brands, organic, you name it. Ok, I feel like a really cheesy commercial writing all of this - but that's how much in love with this chocolate I am!The first reviewer was correct about bitterness. But you *can* train your tastebuds to like the higher percentages. My kids have done this. I recommend starting off at 50% then going to 68%, then 72%.But you'll really only get the healthy benefits of chocolate that your'e always hearing about (antioxidants and what not) when you're able to go above 80%. So aim high :) And this is the perfect brand to do so :)

column9: wait, you mean...chocolate i can eat any time?
column10: i'm sensitive to what i eat, and for many years i've avoided sweets except sometimes right before bed (and then only when i'm sleeping alone) because the sugar crash they give me within about 15 minutes of eating them pretty much renders me useless for interaction with other carbon-based lifeforms. while i imagine it has less to do with this particular brand than with its relatively high cocoa and low sugar contents, still, it's wonderful to be able to wake up in the morning (or the afternoon, or whenever i wake up) and have some delicious chocolate with my wake-up tea and not have to go back to bed and nap a quarter of an hour later. this chocolate allows me that luxury.as at least one other reviewer has said, chocolate with an 85% cocoa content takes some getting used to; you might do well to work your way up in steps, rather than try to slam yourself straight from milk chocolate, or much lower-cocoa-content dark chocolate, to this. the sweetness of this chocolate is *very* subtle compared to more mainstream options, and at your first taste you might wonder why anybody would eat this stuff on purpose. but stick with it...give it time, let it melt in your mouth...and you will certainly become very fond of it. this Vivani chocolate is German-made (why Germans would want to give their chocolate an Italian-sounding name, i don't know, but these Germans did) and very fine; it's rich without being too sweet, and as smooth as any chocolate i've ever eaten. and now that i've grokked its subtle charms, i don't know if i'll ever eat sweeter chocolate again.now if you'll excuse me, i have to go EAT MORE CHOCOLATE!nom.
