DESCRIPTIONThe product is actually a mostly-sugar syrup with black specks of ground vanilla beans.  I expected a more intensely "vanilla" product than "extract", but the "paste" is actually less intense.EQUIVALENCESAccording to the label: "1 Tbs. vanilla paste = 1 Tbs. vanilla extract = 1 vanilla bean".  In reality, my guess is that the paste is about half the strength of "extract".  Caveat, the alchohol in vanilla extract is probably a substantial portion of the vanilla-ish flavor in "extract".USINGLike any syrup, it is slow to mix with cold ingredients or in cold water.  It generally requires warming or vigourous mixing to mix uniformly.COMPARISON TO "EXTRACT"> "Extract" is vanilla flavor in alchohol. "Paste" is ground vanilla in sugar syrup. In my limited experience, "extract" is more intensely "vanilla" but the alcohol flavor interferes with use in uncooked (or lightly cooked) desserts---for example, in home-made ice-cream, or in a glass of vanilla-milk, or pudding.Example: I make a faux-chocolate pudding with a tropical fruit called "black sapote", milk, Knox Gelatin Knox Original Gelatin (32-Count Envelopes), Unflavored, 8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 2), sugar, and vanilla (extract).  I've always used Massey vanilla extract, but the alchohol flavor detracts from the chocolate flavor.  I look foward to trying the paste for this purpose.> The "paste" has the advantage of not evaporating (which can happen to extract kept for a year or two).RECOMMENDATIONUse "extract" for deserts which will be substantially cooked (enough to drive the alchohol off).  Use "paste" for uncooked (or lightly cooked) deserts.

I should have read the one star review first and then Googled it to verify. Normally I do, but this time I just bought it on a whim. I was hoping for just ground up vanilla bean, but this is all sugar. Actual vanilla bean is the 2nd to last ingredient. Really not thrilled and I wish I could send it back.

I saw this on a website and knew I had to get a bottle. Sur la Table in Omaha carries it, the flavor is so much deeper and more sophisticated than regular vanilla extract. This is all I use anymore. I've given it as gifts to friends that have also made the switch to using this full time.

Love this brand.  I use Nielsen-Massey 32 oz. Madagascar Bourbon Pure Vanilla Extract. also (32 oz. seems like a  lot but it calculates to roughly a little over $1.20 per ounce.  Um, CRAZY SAVINGS.).You can use this as a substitute for vanilla beans for the most part but if you use this with extract you can punch up the vanilla flavor to a sinful degree.  I love using this to make vanilla bean frosting (via a Cupcake Project recipe) that tastes like vanilla bean ice cream.Whoever said vanilla was boring?!  ;D

I really like this stuff. I got it for Christmas for a friend and use it all the time. I like it because you can use it in recipes that call for either vanilla extract or vanilla beans (it has a guide on how much to use on the back). I think it would make a really great gift for anyone who likes to bake.

I used this extensively in baking. My cookies are incredibly better with this stuff. It's very addicting. I mostly made cookies with this substituted for vanilla extract. They tasted better and people would gobble them up. I also added it  to French Toast. That was incredible too. This lasted me about 3 months with baking every week or every other week. I plan on buying it again but buying a much bigger container this time. If you are hesitant about this, I would recommend trying it. I ran out and don't like to eat my cookies as much without it. Just a fantastic product.

This Vanilla Bean Paste is amazing, I substitute this almost everywhere that Vanilla Extract is called for.  It has an Extract/Whole Bean conversion guide on the bottle.  The depth of flavor is outstanding, and I find that it leaves no alkaline taste in food.  I just wish that Nielsen-Massey would make their Tahitian and Mexican Vanilla varieties in a paste as well.

This is the best vanilla you will ever use.  Say good-bye to alcohol-based vanilla and hello to this thick, delightful paste.  An even exchange for vanilla extract in recipes but a much truer vanilla flavor.  Be aware, however, that the vanilla bean specks will show in foods like shortbread cookies - I like the look but, for some, it might take getting time to get use to.
This stuff is great. We use it in the place of vanilla extract in almost all the baking that we do. It is also really great in pancakes and waffles. Get this and you will definitely not regret it.

column4: Miss Betsey Trotwood "Only bad witches are ugly"
column10: This is the product that you've been searching for all of your baking life that you didn't know you wanted. I love that it doesn't have that strong alcohol bite. I love that it is a strong (but not too strong) punch of vanilla.I've used it in cookies, and it added a deep vanilla flavor. I have used it in my Zoku to make Vanilla Latte bars - excellent! I like this product so much that I ~almost~ added it to mashed potatoes last night (and no, I am not pregnant). I have added a thin film to a PB&banana and thoroughly enjoyed it.I will never buy vanilla extract again. The magic of this product is, that unlike extract, you don't have to add heat, cook, bake to get it to taste yummy (with extract you have to burn off the alcohol). I estimate with weekly use this jar will last me for nearly a year. I only wish this product were the standard years ago and we all learned to make Toll House cookies with this instead of vanilla extract.

The description states: "Labeled specifically as a Pure Vanilla Extract".The actual ingredients are: Sugar, Water, Vanilla Extract, Vanilla Beans, Gum Tragacanth (a natural thickener).Nielsen-Massey is that what you call, "pure"? I don't, I call it false advertising.I use Batko Vanilla extracts, they contain no sugar and I rate them just as good as or better than Nielsen-Massey.

If you are a baker you will know the difference between good and bad vanilla paste, this paste is a good product just a little pricy.  It's hard to judge what 4 oz is, not very much, 3 stars for the price.

I use this Vanilla Bean Paste in place of extract in all my baking, plus I use it in my daughter's applesauce. It's sweet with a wonderful vanilla flavor and tons of tiny seed flecks. Wonderful stuff and goes a long way. I use it regularly and my previous bottle lasted a year.
I was used to using vanilla extract when I would make creme brulee. What a difference when you switch to vanilla bean paste.

column9: Too much vanilla can be too much.
column10: I love the concept and look of this stuff but my advice is to use less than suggested -- at least the first time when you can decide for yourself.  Suggested conversion from liquid vanilla is exactly the same (1 tsp liquid vanilla to 1 tsp vanilla bean paste) which I did for a favorite cheesecake squares recipe and it was too much.

It has good flavor, but I do not think that it lived uo to all that I read that it was. I could have just bought some pure vanilla exctract and saved $10 and 5 days of waiting.I do love its thickness and texture, but I wouldn't buy it again unless I saw it on a store shelf. It wasn't worth the wait and the shipping cost.

All I have to say is I will never buy anything other than this paste. It is so delicious in Anything u use it in. The flavor is so intense that u can taste it in everything but it's also subtle too. I love it
Used this product to make a vanilla bean cheesecake mousse and it was so, so good.  Much easier to work with than with vanilla beans and the measurements are right on the bottle.

The vanilla bean paste is exactly what I was hoping it would be.  It is certainly less alcohol tasting than extract and even though it has a little bit of sugar it doesn't mess with the recipes.  It does, however, impart a wonderful rich vanilla flavor in everything I have added it too.  It is also a much larger bottle than I was expecting, so I was doubly pleased.
This vanilla bean paste subs 1:1 for extract and adds sophistication to any dish!  Love the little vanilla bean flecks.
The smell is fantastic, great for puddings and creme brulees. Different from tahitian vanilla. Good purchase, the packaging was correct.
Something that I love about this are the vanilla sees, but a do not like that this one have a lot of sugar!, and the flavor is not strong, so you have to add a lot of vanilla

The first bottle I used I loved.  The second bottle was inconsistent with the first; I ended up have to triple the amount attempting to match it to the flavor that came from the first, altering my recipe.  It still could not match the product I received in my first bottle.  This one contained more sugar syrup than it did the vanilla bean/vb flavor; and I also noticed a clear visable difference as well in my frosting/batter...requiring so much more and not as many vb specks, greatly altering my end product.  disappointed.
This is the best vanilla for sugar cookies! One time trying this delicious paste with actual vanilla bean flecks and you will be hooked!!!
Exactly how I expected, but more gel than paste. Actually, no paste at all, just gel.Like Vanilla Bean extract, but without the alcohol bit.Great.

column9: love it, but I use more than I thought
column10: I LOVE the product, but at the same time I think I use far more of it than I expected.  I was reading I would be using the same amount as I would in extract.  I find myself using more for sure, but the flavor it superior.
Best vanilla I've ever tasted.  I used some in a creamy rice pudding I make and it was absolutely the best I've ever tasted.
A requirement for all Bakers :o) LOVE this stuff!!! makes everything more tasty! The quality is great as well...purchase you won't be disapointed!

i really wanted to like this. i'm a baker and always looking for new better ways to get vanilla and this seemed amazing. i was really disappointed. its like a sugary syrup with a very faint vanilla taste. ever used pure vanilla bean? the vanilla taste should be intense. this wasn't. i also tried buying vanilla powder from williams sanoma and that was even a bigger waste of money. omg it was like they just ground up the peels or something because it had NO flavor and hardly any smell. what a disappointment. so i continue on my search. i saw this website called Vanilla Man that i want to check out. He's in Africa i think. so i'm hoping that will be the real deal. he has vanilla syrups, powders and grinders. so we'll see. could be another waste of money. but i'm always trying till i find something good.

The vanilla flavoring you get at your local grocery store is exactly that...flavoring..and often it is past its prime.  If you want your homemade vanilla ice cream to taste great then buy this now!  If you ever asked yourself, "why does this recipe call for vanilla, I never taste it in the finished product?"  The buy this now and you will know why!Yes, I know it is expensive but you get what you pay for!

This product is basically sugar with lots of gums and bits of vanilla.  Kind of liquid gummy bear.  I was hoping for actual ground up vanilla beans in paste form which is available from Bright Earth Foods, unfortunately not available on Amazon.

I should it read the reviews and the whole description not just go by the description of the product on the bottle which it saids vanilla paste this is not a paste is a syrup and honey is thicker than this .

column9: Ok for toddlers, but not for infants
column10: These are pretty good size pieces and are very hard and do not become soft like a lot of similar items.  They taste decent have a mild banana flavor.  This product requires your child to have some molars to be able to chew these up, my 18 month old has some trouble with them and prefers other things much more.

column9: Best curry powder for bean soup
column10: This is one of my favorite curry blends and is especially good for bean or lentil soups. It is both mild and flavorful. I add extra heat with cayenne if I want a spicier dish.
This is really good sauce. Had no idea it was Organic until I got it. But the flavor is really good. Buy this and you wont regret it. Ships on time too.
I am very happy with this organic tomato sauce. I've tried diffent ones in the past, but this one taste really good. I Will be buying this case often.

column9: great taste, but hard to open
column10: these are great tasting candies for a sugar-free variety, but they get sticky and very hard to take out of the individual wrappers, especially without getting the candy all over your fingers.

For anyone who needs to send a gift to someone with a sweet tooth.  This is the 3rd time I have sent these whoopie pie to my mother in SC, she loves them. I have had no problem with the cost of the product or the freshness of the product.  I always send 4 at a time, I know that my mom has 1 and put the other 3 in the freezer to have at a later date.  It is a great gift for her and she loves when I send them.

I had looked for weeks for Sumac.  Because I trust Amazon, I ordered from Amazon.  The spice was fresh, sealed in a plastic bag, and quantity-wise was more than I had needed.  The delivery was rapid - totally satisfied.  Would recommend to anyone looking for a spice that's fresh and delivered quickly.
The spice arrived fresh and there is a lot of it. It is a MUST for Middle Eastern cooking! Great taste!

Wanted to make my own Zattar. Needed sumac, got plenty!  We have used it on fish and chicken, adds that a nice touch of tart that makes everything taste good. A little goes a long way so this will last.

The sumac is very flavorful and tastes very fresh. I made some great za'atar with it, which has been lovely sprinkled in sandwiches, on salads, and mixed with olive oil and baked on sourdough flat bread.
This was prefect. I have been looking for this spice for many years. I make my own zartar recipe and haven't been able to find the ingredients. Thank you. I am sure I will be ordering more.
I was expecting the sumac to be a bit more powdery, but it turned out to be a little courser than I thought. Otherwise, the spice is fine.

This is a magnificent tea and I have noticed it has helped clear up my skin. That along with Supercritical Omega 7 by New Chapter, my skin looks 10 years younger at 40! This tea contains Dandelion which is beyond exceptional for liver detox and skin health. I have also noticed a caffeine like feeling after just one cup because of all of the nutrients. Excellent flavor! It's the only detox tea I drink.

This was some of the best tea I've ever purchased! I'm usually pretty loyal to green tea or peppermint but the detox was wonderful. It wasn't bitter and the flavor wasn't overpowering. I've already reccommend this to many of my college friends after long weekends.
I drink mighty leaf organic detox infusion tea every night, it is perfect because it is caffeine free. It has a delicious mint aftertaste. I 100% recommend it.
I absolutely love this tea. It doesn't get bitter if you leave the teabag in for a long time. It has full flavors. The tea does not dissapoint! I will continue to buy this brand of tea.

Each tea bag is filled very generously and brews very strong if you let it! It has a very minty/basil flavor, I don't even bother buying my usual peppermint tea anymore, because this is so much better! I look forward to buying other Mighty Leaf teas, they are really a top notch company.

Mighty Leaf Detox Tea is fantastic!  It is so soothing and the delicate flavor is simply delicious.  I have recommended this flavor, along with many other Mighty Leaf flavors, to all of my friends. Might Leaf has completely enhanced my tea drinking experience!
Drinking this tea was a very relaxing experience. I loved the combination of the basil and mint flavors. This tea felt like a day at the spa. I recommend it to all!

column9: Best Detox Tea I've Tried Yet...
column10: I have tried a bunch of detox teas for those hangover days or just feeling run-down days... They are always a little bit off, too bitter or too minty or just plain gross. This one is the only mild, well-balanced detox tea I've ever tried! I love it for rough mornings, it's always a great pick-me-up!

This tea was a great mix of mint and basil. It was a refreshing, natural tasting mint, which was not too strong, and didn't overpower the other spices. The silk bags were also really cool as you could see the whole leaves as the tea steeped.

Fantastic! Makes the best blood-orange margaritas and martinis ever... and mixed in with a bit of key lime and pineapple juice and a pinch or two of spices, a wonderful Carne Asada style marinade!The frozen concentrate is ultra-easy to use, and a wonderful way to keep fresh-tasting juice that's normally pretty hard to find, close at hand! :)Super-fast and courteous shipping by seller, too! First-rate!

This blood orange purée is all the rage in my home town! I ordered 3 and then defrosted one of the jars and poured them into little containers to freeze.  (My friend told me to do this) This Purée makes the best margaritas!  Fill a pitcher with ice...pour 1/3 tequila (or less)...2/3 Margarita mix and enough purée to make it a nice sunset color..and voila... adjust to your taste. It is not too sweet for some reason...just perfect and  A HUGE HIT!!!  Everyone wants to know "what is that..it is perfect....where did you get that!!!"  The shipping is expensive..but it arrives totally frozen in dry ice...and is sooooo worth it!!! Seriously!! It would make a great hostess gift also!!YUMMY!!! (do not drink and drive!)

While more of a puree than a juice concentrate, this wonderful product did exactly what it was purchased to do .. it produced an awesome margarita!  Deliciously different, blood orange margaritas make for a wonderful summer drink.  I would buy this product again.

Due to the horrendous shipping charges (which I can't really knock them for since I knew about it before ordering) I naturally ordered 3 purées.Passion fruit, prickly pear, and blood orange. Blood orange was my last choice, and they were all to make margaritas and other smoothies.But after sampling them all, we LOVE the blood orange. Perfectly balanced between citrus and sweet. The one thing they all have in common is that these purées smell and taste like we are eating fresh picked fruit. Amazing.
A little goes a really long way.  I made blood orange margaritas for my wedding.  It was a big hit!  I have 4 more jars in my freezer left.
Really great! Found a local dist. working our way through the flavors and multitude of recipe options.
My small dogs love these cookies and look forward to getting them after their meal.They are wholesome and healthy.
This went with the coffee I purchased as a gift for a friend. The Fr. Vanilla went well with the coffee.

This is a super fine sugar that is fantastic. They also told me from the manufactures that there is no gluten, soy,or dairy in this caster sugar. Thats always good news for allergy people. Will buy again.

Going over my list of baking recipes for this Xmas season, I came across a recipe that specifically asked for caster sugar.  Since I was making this recipe for the first time I purchased the caster sugar.  At around $4.50/lb it is very pricey for a sugar product.  Further research at cooking websites and blogs, I found that many people use regular granulated sugar with acceptable results.

I was disappointed to find caster sugar is not available at grocery stores in the US having grown up cooking with it.  I wanted to make fairy cakes and a victoria sponge cake for my son's birthday so I purchased this online.  It is well packaged and arrived intact.  My cakes turned out perfect!

column9: Wonderful Assortment and Great Gift! Highly Recommended!
column10: Godiva is nothing less than a Party in your mouth!! It's the best chocolate I've found and I'm as finicky as theycome! This particular assortment is full of wonderful tastes, one just as good if not better than the next. Godiva alsopackages their product quite lovely for gift giving, assuming you can deny yourself the temptation to open it for yourself!I got greedy, just once, and that was the end of me! Now I'm hooked and have to buy one for myself every time I buy one foranother gift to give. Ah well, I've reached the age where my husband says I deserve all the treats I want and he won't divorceme if I get fat! Indeed, I've been blessed!Pica

Honestly, you cannot go wrong with this.  Godiva is the God of chocolate, and this assortment box should please any chocolate lover.  With Russell Stover's or other low-end chocolate assortments, there are always a few "gross ones" in there, and it definitely doesn't taste premium.  Godiva chocolate melts in your mouth and there is not a bad piece of chocolate in this box; it is 100% heavenly chocolately goodness.  Great variety and the box is beautiful.  Great gift for any chocolate lover, without a doubt!

If you want to buy chocolates buy from Godiva they do it right it is packed in ice and you always get what you payed for they are a A+ in my book I love Godiva always have and always will.  I am a chocolate person and they are the best out there trust me they are the best.

column9: Godiva uses gmos to save money on product???
column10: I used to buy Godiva chocolates for friends as gifts. Whe I lived in S.F. I took the bus to get to their downtown store.I used to think that Godiva was the BEST chocolate ever, that is until I found out that they use gmos in their candy, because its cheap. Why am I paying a premium price for sub standard candy?  Hersheys uses gmos; the very same stuff Godiva uses. I expect that from Hersheys. Their candy bars are 75 cents compared to Godiva at $3.oo!What a ripoff! Shame on you Godiva!  I already found a better chocolate to replace you and its cheaper and tastes better!They are called Theo Chocolate Company and are NON-GMo vefified.

Always looking for a robust decaf and this product is a good example.  Have not been disappointed in Coffee Bean Direct products and they are a good value.  They do not overcharge those of us who have to have decaf and they provide some tasty flavors.

While I am not a coffee expert, I appreciate French roast coffee.  Upon opening the bag, it was apparent that the coffee did not look like French roast as it had brownish hues, not black, and it did not have an oily sheen.  I made the coffee in a French press and my observation was confirmed, it did not have a French roast flavor.On a positive side, the coffee was well packed in resealable bags for those who don't have, or choose not to use, airtight containers.  The coffee was not bad, it simply was not what I expected.

After downing mass quantities of full-bore French Roast for years and years, I suddenly couldn't handle the caffeine and embarked on a search to find a decaf simulacrum of the real thing. It's never been clear to me if the process of decaffeination is responsible for the insipid flavor of much decaf coffee or if the roasters conclude that anyone drinking decaf is a weenie and doesn't deserve and would not appreciate a robust brew. Anyway, finding something with flavor at an affordable price point is a real struggle. We're on our third three-bag round of Coffee Bean Direct, and are really happy with it.The packaging is excellent. The coffee comes in a plain brown wrapper, as should all decaf. I have never mastered the skills necessary for resealing the tin ties on conventional bags, particularly near the end of the bag, and find that Coffee Direct's integrated zipper seal secure and easy to use for the life of the bag. Sucking down decaf is bad enough without feeling mechanically challenged as well.

I've purchased coffee from Coffee Bean Direct for several years. I have never been displeased. I always get it shortly after it has been roasted and usually buy multiple bags since shipping is a large portion of the cost. That made this 3-pack of 1# bags nice, and going the subscription made it even better ($29 vs $46) delivered.The bags seem top quality, especially in comparison to some premium brands. They also were properly evacuated.All the Coffee Bean Direct products I've bought had a roast date label. Two of the bags I received had the label removed completely (but it was apparent, and one had part of it removed. It appeared to still be 2011 roasted, but would still like the label left in place. It is sort of like getting any other consumable and having the "Best by" date obliterated.That said, I served this Friday evening to friends who are very in-tune with highest quality coffee and espresso. They loved this coffee, as did I, and are ordering it. They have been buying locally from a name brand store known for "charring" their beans :-)

column9: Nothing but good things to say about this deal.
column10: Nice to know I can get good espresso in quantity for a good price other than from eBay.  The coffee arrived pretty fast and taste great.

Between my wife and myself we during at least 6 cappuccino's per day. I have ordered Coffee Bean Direct several times and the product is great. Amazon has gone to FedEx for shipping and they are the worst.  What used to take one day with UPS now takes 4 days with Fedex.This is the last time I buy this from Amazon!!

This is Swedish but also a delight in Denmark. They come in bite size pieces as well as bars (I prefer the pieces not available here). It is a mod-sweet chocolate wrapped around a barely crunchy-caramelly tasting inside...literally  melts in your mouth. When I go to DK, I buy bags for friends...like a dozen as this is the preferred souvenir! They are quite satisfying and make a great 'guest' chocolate as they are very, very fancy tasting candy even though the wrapper is playful. Enjoy!
Doesn't even compare with Skor!  Daim is a one of a kind, addicting, and a little bit of heaven in your mouth. Worth the cost. Ikea is not carrying anymore.

column9: It gets stuck between my teeth
column10: Daim, previously known as Dajm, is a dangerous piece of Swedish chocolate wrapped around a crunchy piece of caramel (or something similar). In Sweden, they are usually sold in packs of two, known as "double Daim". When I was a kid, getting hold of a "dubbel-Dajm" was considered very cool indeed.Daim is VERY tasty, but constantly get stuck between my teeth, and at other impossible places! LOL. Don't tell me I didn't warn you. But yes, Daim is definitely worth five stars.Still, I'm disappointed that Amazon doesn't sell Co-Co, the ultimate chocolate bar of my childhood. ;-)

super small candy bars, with high priced shipping. just buy a few "score bars" at your local 7-11 for a fraction of the price and a third larger toffee bar!!! these bars are real small, about 2/3's the size of a regular candy bar, and with shipping came out to $3.00 a peice!!! tase good, but not THAT good!!!! dont waste your money- IKEA used to sell the jumbo size bars, for $4.00- that is what i thought i was getting, not these 3 bite bars

I found a recommendation of Honest Tea in a book and wanted to try some.  Thought that $ 34.99 for 12 ($2.92 each) was a lot of money but the stuff is all natural.  But then I bought 3 bottles at a local gas station for $2.09 each.  If it can be bought a a gas station convenience store for less than amazon there is a problem.

This is SO refreshing! I find myself thinking about it even when I am not thirsty. It's not too sweet yet it has an unmistakable "tea-ness" which other bottled teas do not seem to have, and is a great thirst quencher. The fact that it is lightly sweetened goes over well with me, and the fact that there is no lemon in this tea is yet another plus.The price is ok -- I get them at work for $2.00 a bottle, so the case price of 12 is reasonable.

column9: Excellent! Very Light and Pleasant Green-Tea Taste.
column10: I often pick up an evening meal at my nearby Fresh and Easy Neighborhood Market and when I do I often select a beverage to go along with the meal. I might add that I enjoy trying things I've never had before. This time the beverage was Honest Tea / Honey Green Tea in a 16.9-ounce bottle. Please notice that my review is for the tea only. Whatever the cost per bottle is and the shipping costs are your own personal business. Personally, I don't buy heavy things like this that can be easily found nearby, but that may not apply to all people.This Honey Green Tea is quite good. Excellent! It has a very light  and pleasant green-tea taste and is just a tad sweet with honey, as they claim. It goes down real easily, believe me. I think I could pull down a whole bottle in one long swig, if I wanted to. But I enjoy sipping it in small amounts and savoring the excellent taste.Gary Peterson

column9: Are you serious with this price?
column10: $39.99 for 12 bottles?  That's $3.33 per bottle, PLUS shipping!!!  I can buy a bottle of this stuff in my local grocery store for $1.50 a piece!  I shop online for DEALS, not to be robbed.

There isn't anything particularly wrong with the product - the dog liked it well enough, but I'm guessing that will be the case with just about any of the bully sticks you'll find here. My issue with the fact that this project is labeled as Bully Stick"s" (plural). You get one - one 6 inch stick despite the fact that the product name and picture implies that there are more.Combined with the shipping cost, it's kind of a ripoff for just one stick. Scroll down to the "customers also viewed" area and find yourself one that might cost a dollar or two more, but comes with 5 or 6 sticks instead of 1.

My dog has always loved these, but because they were cheaper and available at the local market - for a while I was buying her generic biscuits.  Well, it turns out the poor dog has major food allergies! Now these are all I get for her.  She knew best!I recommend this product because it is a larger size than anything I've seen available through pet stores.
Perfect for my 13 week old Lab who wants to chew on EVERYTHING.  Takes her quite a bit to get thru these which is why I bought the "large" size treat.  Healthy, cleans her teeth.  Highly recommend

I'm writing this review, however, if my dog could write it, or say it, she would positively rave about this treat! I have a 6-year-old Bichon Frise who loves these dog biscuits - or as she knows them, "cookies"!  She loves the flavor of peanut butter, which is why I bought these originally to try. However, I was pleased to know that the other ingredients in these dog biscuits are oatmeal, eggs, apples and carrots and that everything is made natural. I want my dog to have good snacks (and food!) - and I want her to enjoy what she's eating, too. I have made my third purchase of this product as she loves them - she never hesitates to gobble the "cookie" quickly. She loves them and I know they're good for her - we're both happy! And to top it all off - the price is definitely right! I buy the mini-size as my dog is small. I highly recommend this high-quality dog treat!

Exceptionally wonderful transaction. There was a mix-up in items, but 1 contact with the seller & the issue was resolved so simply & easily. I'll tell you, if you have a mix-up, then you REALLY get to know how professional the seller is, and this one is top notch!

I don't drink soda, but somehow I got suckered into trying this, and now I am seriously addicted.  It is a little bitter, not too sweet, not too bubbly and unfortunately 130 calories a can.  I buy it at Costco (sorry Amazon) where I get a case of 12 orange and 12 lemon for $14.00.  I like the orange better than the lemon, but somehow, I am still buying a case every 2 weeks.  I am just weak.

It speaks for itself. San Pellegrino with a slight touch of orange.  Funny thing about it...when you're thirsty, it does two things. It quenches your thirst and gives you a sense of a fresh cut orange thrown smack dab in your face.

column9: truly superb -- very thirstquenching and not too sweet
column10: Stack up on this drink -- especially on hot summer days.  It is something you will need and need more of.  I haven't used it with any booze, but I'll bet you could mix some interesting drinks with it -- a kind of mildly flavored, not too sweet, just a soupcon of bitterness with the sweet and sparkle.  Very Very refreshing

I love this beverage because of the slight bitter taste.  It's an adult orange soda that I would not have liked as a kid.  Yesterday, I bought some egg nog at Safeway, and they had some cold bottles of Southern Comfort alongside the egg nog (smart cross-sell).  I bought both (sucker).  Frankly, I didn't like the taste of the Southern Comfort in the egg nog.  Today, I tried a little Southern Comfort straight up, but found the smell and taste, slightly peachy or bubble gum - not grossly so, but too sweet.  I did a review on the Southern Comfort and others also describe the peach aroma and taste.  I probably would not buy Southern Comfort again.  Then it struck me that it might go well with the San Pellegrino Aranciata in my refer (kind of like a fuzzy navel).  Of course, often an idea doesn't play out that well.  I poured about 1 ounce of Southern Comfort onto the ice in a cognac glass and then added 2 ounces of the San Pellegrino Aranciata.  It smells very nice, tastes delicious, and the bitter of the orange peel balances out the sweetness of the peach in the Comfort - it's much more subtle and drinkable than a typically syrupy sweet fuzzy navel - a more sophisticated version.  This is a great all-season sexy drink that everyone will like.  My only caution would be that it tastes too good and goes down way too easily.  I was playing with a name for this drink:  Southern Italian, Southern Gina... Orange Comfort!  Anyway, with or without the alcohol, I love San Pellegrino Aranciata, and I now have a reason to buy more Southern Comfort.
This is the best product ever. If you havent tried it you should. The service was great as well. Got here on time!

column9: The best for decaf iced tea!
column10: If you're at all familiar with the south you'll know that we tend to take iced tea rather seriously.  When I was growing up my mother made iced tea from Lipton tea bags but when I discovered Luzianne tea there was no going back to Lipton!  Formulated specifically for making iced tea Luzianne delivers a consistent product that is not bitter and has a pleasant aroma.  These days I use one regular tea bag along with one Luzianne decaf tea bag to make our iced tea in this manner:Steep a quart to a quart and a half of water almost to boiling.  You don't want to use boiling water as it will singe the tea and create a bitter flavor.  As long as the heated water is steaming, it's hot enough.  Add 1 family sized (or 2 regular sized bags) of each variety of Luzianne tea (caffeinated and decaffeinated) to the water and allow it to steep all day and come to room temperature.  If you're making sweet tea add the sugar to the bottom of the pitcher before adding any liquid.  Then add about 2 cups of the room temperature (or warm) tea and stir to dissolve all the sugar.  At this point, fill the pitcher with ice.  Pour the brewed tea on top of the ice and stir gently to combine.  Add water as needed to fill your vessel.  Your tea will be clear, sweet and refreshing with no bitterness or after-taste!

I found this to be a good alternative to whey based protein powder. I have only used this product for 30 days and am reordering. Before I get into my review, I might mention that I never thought of myself as whey or lactose intolerant, but after 3 months of taking quality whey protein I knew that what I was experiencing was not typical. (I'm talking about bathroom habits including frequency and consistency). I asked a few older guys in the gym what there experience was with whey, most if not all where fine with it and experienced no problems or side effects. One natural BB that is about my age late 30's suggested this egg based protein product and noted that one of his training customers found it to be an acceptable alternative to the milk based protein products.I did some research and to be honest the manufactures web site for beHealthyNFit is totally useless and outdated with little or no useful information. Their poor web site almost made me not buy this product. It sure didn't invoke any consumer confidence and in my opinion is totally unacceptable.How does it taste? I bought the chocolate (I'm not a chocolate lover but I think chocolate flavoring is the best option for protein powders) The flavor is chocolate but its defiantly not a rich milk chocolate and it wouldn't fall in the same category as a dessert. More of a taste that you can get used to.  I have also seen this flavor described as chocolate with a hint metallic. I'd agree with that. It has an after taste that some may find metallic.How does it mix? I mix this with water directly in a 16oz. ready to drink water bottle. I drink 1 or 2 ounces, usually down to the top of the label. Then I place a funnel in the top and dump in one scoop. Usually I will need to shake or tap the funnel to get the powder to pass through. Then I screw the top on and shake well. I have found that if the water is very cold the powder will clump more often and mix poorly. Room temperature water or water that is cool but not ice-cold works best. I use a wine fridge to keep the water at 50.( I don't like clumps) Note: The consistency is exactly like water, if your expecting this to be a thick or heavy drink then will be disappointed.I found that if you live in a humid state like Florida you will need to make sure that you screw the lid to the protein power on tight. If you expose this power to high humidity you will have a terrible time with it clumping and mixing properly.General tips for drinking protein drinks. I have found that eating a granola bar while drinking a protein drink helps. First biting the granola bar then taking a drink. I found this to work for me and it makes the occasional protein clump less noticeable.Is there room for improvement? Yes, loads of room for improvement. Is there anything better? I haven't found it yet but I am still looking. I will give this high marks until I find something better. Please leave a comment if you find a better non whey protein product.

In my opinion, this is the best protein powder out there.I've used a lot of different protein products, from Dymatize to Optimum Nutrition (Gold Standard) and CellTech (MuscleTech), BSN, many others as well. Sure it is good, and the protein is not bad, but it can be better.For those who have issues with dairy, whey is not an option.  Whey is a dairy product, and actually a bi-product of diary production.  Dairy is not the best choice of protein out there, many may disagree with this but it is a fact.  America has an infatuation with dairy and sweets.  If you look at any tables that show protein absorbtion effeciency in our bodies you will see this fact.  Eggs and Fish are rated at the top for best absorbtion and usage in the human body.  Eggs are around 88% effeciency, while fish is around 70% and chicken around 60%.  Whey and dairy are below all of these, this is precisely why whey is so cheap, and that is why it is so popular.  Sure the egg protein is going to be more expensive, but it is a better product.As far as taste and texture, I find it just as good as the whey products that I have used, and even better then some.
