Gyokuro as simply the best tasting tea we've tasted - and we've tasted plenty.  I've had this tea (English Tea Stores brand) and the Teavana brand Gyokuro.  I'd say both are excellent teas.  The Teavana brand is definitely a higher grade tea.  This can mostly be discerned from the slightly more illustrious flavor that the Teavana Gyokuro provides.  Additionally, the English Tea Stores brand tends to be less forgiving of improper brewing temperature - it gets bitter easier.  I noticed that the English Tea Stores brand tended to be a little drier and more brittle.  Teavana gets the tea into your hands while the leaves are still *moist* and in whole strips.  The English Tea Stores Gyokuro was starting to crumble and you will end up with more sediment in your tea.Once we started brewing the English Tea Stores brand Gyokuro in our new Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter Stainless-Steel Cordless Electric Kettle, the tea came out acceptably close to Teavana's Gyokuro.  The flavor is outstanding in both cases.  Over time, our purchase of the Electric Kettle will pay for itself because the English Tea Stores brand is much cheaper.  Now we can enjoy the wonderful flavor of Japans greatest tea all the time without emptying our pockets on the best of the best Teavana Gyokuro.  If you do use the Electric Kettle: we use 2 tablespoons of tea (could use less for a milder brew), set the kettle for green tea, put the tea in the water then set a timer for 30 seconds, then remove when the timer goes off.  We also use a cast-iron tea pot that we preheat with a little bit of the water from the kettle, so that might make a difference as well.Overall, this tea is an acceptable replacement to the Teavana brand teas.  If you have the money to buy the tea you want, stick with Teavana.  If you are on a tighter budget, the English Tea Stores is an acceptable trade off if you brew it properly.Ps. The Cuisinart tea pot is AWESOME!- Gyokuro Devotee

column9: Gyokuro Green Tea; excellent flavors and fragrance.
column10: This Gyokuro green tea tastes really good and it has a pleasant clean fragrance similar to other Gyokuro teas I have enjoyed. I regularly drink Gyokuro teas and I do like this one. The Gyokuro teas are naturally without the bitterness of Sencha or other teas; naturally sweet. I make the tea with hot water that has been cooled down to be hot; but not boiling hot to the touch otherwise bitterness comes out of Gyokuro teas. I just add a little room temperature water to boiling hot water to bring the temperature down.I have made many infusions of this tea from just three table spoons of tea in my (Tokoname, Fukugata) Japanese style tea pot (kyusu) with a ceramic sieve which I use just for Gyokuro teas. I have found the "rishi-tea" and "dens tea" as good Japanese tea pot sources which I have brewed this Gyokuro green tea in. I really like this tea; so I expect to order more later.

I love Pumpernickel bread. It was difficult to find a commercial bread I liked, so I make my own. Using a combination of bread flour, light rye and Bobs Pumpernickel flour makes a fantastic hearty bread. Bob's Red Mill makes the best flours and grains on the planet.

I made an all-rye bread using Bob's Organic Dark Rye Flour and Rye Meal Pumpernickel.  Yeah, it's supposed to look somewhat broad and dark, but I'm working on that.  It is truly a tasty, dense, dark, moist, chewy bread that goes well with cream cheese and lox; it's great toasted with butter.  I learned to sour some rye flour for about 24-36 hours with water and a little yeast and create the dough from there--helps to create a good rye that bakes well.  I don't use caraway, but this last time I added a tablespoon or so of dried onion flakes to the dough as I mixed it.  That was tasty.  It's hard to find dark rye flours and pumpernickel meal in Texas, and finding the flour really helped a lot in my escape from white flours.  I used to call this "linoleum bread" when I bought it for my husband.  No more name-calling, no more buying.  If you work without a recipe, remember that the dough will be sticky to knead; I usually use half again the amount of yeast I'd use in a white loaf.  Bob's products made a wonderfully tasty loaf of bread.
My local store quit stocking this item; So I get it here now.Top quality. This makes my baked goods stand out. Brings flavor and fiber to my homemade works of art!

column9: Not as awesome as I'd hoped
column10: These were disappointing. Not much cinnamon flavor for being cinnamon marshmallows. I had such high hopes for some amazing cinnamon rice crispy treats, but after the lame first batch, I ended up adding extra cinnamon to the mix. Why bother with special marshmallows?

Knowing that I like ramen my sister suggested that I give these a try. I'm on my second order as I really enjoy the flavor and texture. The noddle's in this Yakisoba have a different flavor and texture then what I am use to in the ramen packets that I normally eat but are very tasty. As with most of these type products it is easy to prepare and the flavor can be adjusted to your taste by the amount of seasoning used. I reason for only 4 stars has to do with the container that is used. After it is cooked in the microwave and the lid is peeled off there is a sticky adhesive left around lip. Not a problem if you are going pour the contents into a bowl but kind of gets in the way when eating directly from the container.

column9: Tasty. Available at Wallmart in TX.
column10: It tastes good. Try it. Dry vegetables included. Some flavors not spicy at all and it is a big plus for me.
I just discovered these noodle dishes, and I love them. The price is right with my very small food budget.

My family is very picky on the flavor of French Vanilla Cappuccino they will drink.We have tried and thrown away many gas station drinks when we couldn't find an Exxon on the run.Yes, it must be an On the Run store and nothing else.All the others use a different version and/or brand.If you like Exxon On the Run then this is the matching drink.I saw the package one day while at the store and this matches.BTW... ours is closing so now I'm on my second case.The flavor is great.We use 3 tablespoons per 8oz which is much more than it calls for.
Ritter Sport Chocolate is excellent chocolate.....30 plus years ago I had it shipped to me from my family in Germany....so happy to see it here.....for true chocoholics...enjoy!

column9: Not as good as the Mini version & not what the photo leads you to think
column10: I know, it IS weird that I would prefer the mini version of Ritter Sport Milk Chocolate with Butter Biscuit bars.  But here is why:  the mini has a more pleasing ratio of chocolate to cookie.  Plus, the parts of the mini become one in my mouth, whereas with the larger bar, the cookie slides away from the chocolate.  The larger cookie is not all that great IMO, being very dry and uncomfortable against the teeth.  I much prefer the Gestalt sort of experience the Mini provides; who wants deconstructed dry cookie moving around all over the place.  Unfortunately, I bought a whole box of these big bars, but thankfully the chocolate is most highly edible.Now, take a look at the picture ... doesn't it look like this bar will be a cookie filled with gooey melty chocolate?  My husband picked up my first Mini for me as a surprise, and I honestly did not find the picture appealing, so I set the Mini aside for a few days.  (First time I've ever done THAT with chocolate.)  But the mini pleasantly surprised me for the reasons I've already mentioned.Definitely worth a try if you already like Ritter Sport.  But compare it to the Mini version - I'd love to hear what other people think.

I had been buying these for years at a regular store, and happened to find them for a great price at Amazon.  This is the best chocolate I have ever had, now if I can just figure out a way to make them healthy I'll be set for life.
This popcorn was great however a little pricy. Will be reordering in the future but have to space it out as we at it quickly.
These are a good value for a large bag of treats, however, the treat itself was smaller than I expected; and I don't know if it really helps the bad breath that much.

This is the only brand of flour I use for my pasta, and it comes out perfect every time.  It's pasta, so there's not much more to say than that...  I like the smaller bags, because I can keep extras in my freezer without worrying about them going bad.

I tried these at a local health food store with pretty low expectations. I was pleasantly surprised by the taste and texture of this vegetarian jerky. When I gave up meat I didn't have too many regrets, but jerky was something that I missed. I am delighted to find a replacement!

column9: Great Protein Snack: Less Fat & More Nutritious.
column10: I've tried all the flavors of the primal soy jerky, and this is my favorite. It has less protein than some of the others ('Hickory' has the most, I think), but still more protein and nutrition for the fat it brings compared to meat jerky (which has much more fat, less calories, and much less nutritional content). My biggest problem with the other Primal jerky is not so much the flavor, as it is the consistency. When you take a bite from the 'Hot & Spicy' you just get that bite. With some of the others (especially 'Hickory' and 'Texas BBQ,' you snap off more than you intended). I also don't like my hands to be sticky if I'm out hiking, on the gun range or somewhere else running water and soap isn't easily available. Some of the more 'juicy' primal jerky make it difficult to take along as a trail or road snack. To me, that's what it should be for--Otherwise I'd just eat real, hydrated food.

Coco Lopez is OK, but Coco Casa is much better.  Unfortunately Coco Casa is harder to find so when I run out I often have to resort to Coco Lopez.  Everyone notices the differences, whether told in advance or not.

I searched multiple sites for this product as I could not find it in any of my local markets or specialty stores for a reasonable price, and this is the best price I could find BUT every single can arrived dented and/or damaged.  Need to package their products better.

column9: Coco Lopez..the best for Pina Coladas
column10: I would of given this product a 5 star review but since the shipper failed to put adequate packing in the box, the majority of the cans arrived dented. Luckily, none of the cans had failed. Coco Lopez is an excellent product and the price was very good.This same problem was cited by another Amazon customer.  I decided to give this company another chance, too bad they haven't solved their packing issues.

Cans of cream of coconut were very badly damaged, some so bad I had to throw them away.  They were damaged before they were put in the box for shipping because the box was in really good shape. Wont be ordering from here again.
The product is good.  All cans arrived dented some of them quite a bit.  More of a shipping problem.
Coco Lopez is by far the best cream of coconut. If you like Pina Coladas, there is nothing better. Great for coconut flan and protein shakes too!

column9: It's really superior than the other
column10: I have tasted several cream of coconut to use it for prepared drinks and its flavor is simply superior from the others. I always recommended it.
The packing was bad. EVERY can was dented. You pay for it to be packed right and it wasn't. You can not use these cans so I wasted my money = NOT HAPPY!!!!

column9: Pay more in your local grocery store.  Don't make the mistake I made and order from this online store.
column10: Ordered 12 cans.  All 12 were thrown into a box together with 25 cents worth of bubble wrap.  All 12 cans were dented.
This product taste great but I recently found it at walmart for much cheaper then Amazon prices. Also I saw they had a light version with less calories (have not tried that version yet but will soon)

I have been using it for many years. THE BEST THING FOR PINA COLADA AND FOR COCONUT FLAN.I am glad I was able to find it in Amazon because some times is not easy to find. Be aware that Liquor stores have it in the mix drink section,

My Coco Lopez came to me without any damage, so for those that had the shipping issue, seems they fixed that.  Not only do I use this for my pina coladas, etc, I use Coco Lopez in my smoothies.  Yummy stuff.
Love this cream coconut, makes the best coconut shrimp and you don't need to deep fat fry it either.  Would highly recommend!!!

Product was old.  Some liquid in the cans was separated with an off smell.  Several cans were downright rancid.  All was thrown out.  I will order from another supplier (Gristedes of New York) next time.

column9: I have yet to receive this product. Can you help?
column10: I can not review this product as I have not received it. As you know I ordered it on Nov. 21, 2007. Please contact the supplier and expedite the shipment. Thank You .Thank You B. G. Youngman

I found the sesame bagel crisps as fresh as those purchased locally. Very flavorful eaten as a snack, but not so overpowering that the chip fights with a dip or spread. Actually, too good -- no worries that they will go stale because the bag is emptied too soon. Only problem was that Amazon shipped in the original case meant for store display - which means there's a large perforated flap across 2/3 of the front of carton -- opened during shipping and 3 front bags were bagel dust rather than chips. Back bags were fine for party fare.

column9: New York Style made in Bulgaria
column10: not good, dry and tasteless. Considering that it was  imported from Bulgaria, I wonder how fresh it could be.

I like Raisin Bran, but this is so much better. I don't know what it is, but this tastes so good. The cinnamon flavor really comes out. This is the flavor of RB I will be buying from here on out. My husband really liked it too.

column9: Nice change from the regular version
column10: I found this to be a very tasty alternative to the regular raisin bran. The flakes are crunchier - not as crunchy as the Raisin Bran Crunch version, but certainly more so than the regular version. A nice compromise.The cinnamon flavor is nicely balanced - not too strong, but you don't have to wonder where it is. There's a good amount of raisins, but the almonds are rather sparse.The downside is that this version has a bit less fiber than the regular version. It has 5g per serving (which is 21% of the recommended daily amount) versus 7g per serving (28% of the recommended daily amount) in the regular version. The Cinnamon Almond version has about the same calories as the regular (200 per serving, which is 1.25 cups versus 190 per serving in the regular, which is 1 cup). Fat and sugar content is the same for both.I'm a big raisin bran fan, and really liked this. Nice change of pace.

The original Raisin Bran will always and forever remind me of my paternal grandmother. Without fail I would have Raisin Bran or cinnamon spice instant oatmeal for breakfast whenever I visited her. Now with cinnamon in the Raisin Bran it gives me a combination of both tastes that bring back happy memories.The flakes and almonds stayed crunchy in my milk the whole time I was eating. The cinnamon is just right and not too much or too little. Of course there are also plenty of raisins to keep the ratio of cereal to raisins consistent throughout the whole bowl. The almonds weren't overly crunchy in fact you could hardly taste that they were there. There was just a little extra crunch from them. I highly recommend this one for anyone who loves original Raisin Bran and wants a new tiwst.

I am still a fan of old school cold breakfast cereal, the kind that just needs milk.  Even as an adult I still love it.  I have my favorites, mostly embedded from my childhood and new varieties that are newer to the market.  I would say that Kellogg's Raisin Bran would be considered a favorite from childhood.  Therefore when I saw this new spin on "Raisin Bran" I was quite interested.This "Raisin Bran" has the addition of almond slivers and dusted with cinnamon.  Well I cannot express my disappointment with this cereal. First and foremost the cinnamon, I am not sure I would use the term "dusted with cinnamon" rather "dumped with cinnamon".  This is all I tasted was cinnamon and it was very, very sugary.  Secondly the almond slivers were pretty much nonexistent, which is sad considering it is promoted on the box.  Thirdly this is "raisin" bran right?  Where are the raisins?  Did the two scoops that Kellogg's has built their reputation on been reduced to two tablespoon scoops?  The taste itself isn't bad per se, if you love cinnamon.  I would rather just have a bowl of normal "Raisin Bran".Kellogg's did a find job with their "Raisin Bran Crunch" so I am not sure how they dropped the ball on this cereal.  And not for nothing, but the box that the cereal comes in itself is very small.  This seems to be the case for most companies nowadays smaller packaging, higher prices.  But in the case of this cereal there is some major deception.  The cereal is supposed to have almonds, raisins and cinnamon.  Well there are barely any almonds or raisins and tons of cinnamon.  So it appears that Kellogg's is getting away cheap with this product.  Simply by charging more, making smaller packaging and skimping on the almonds and raisins and bulking up on cinnamon and bran flakes.  I would be really surprised if this product is still on the shelf in six months.

The Raisin Bran cereal with cinnamon and almonds is a great flavor upgrade to the original cereal. The almonds add a crunch to the cereal and the cinnamon adds a light sweetness. The raisins were soft and fresh like it always is in the original cereal.Like with any other cereal, it's enhanced with needed vitamins and minerals and it claims to have 5 grams of fiber per serving which is a plus. However it is less fiber than the original version. I just wish the box was bigger. My family basically inhaled the entire box within a couple days. I will definitely buy this again if I see it at the grocery store.

column9: Great flavor upgrade on a classic!
column10: Barring an unfortunate allergy to either cinnamon or almonds, this is a great pairing of flavors to spice up Raisin Bran with that should not be missed if your a fan of the original(and who isn't?!).  I've always enjoyed Raison Bran, even at the risk of it's somewhat serious side effects, most notably sugar shock and/or your stomach turning into an atomic bomb.  Of course like anything else, if used responsibly these effects can be avoided-- yet here I sit eating my fourth bowl... and in ten minutes my world will be upside down.  Still, great cereal, worth the risks, and highly recommended(just eat with caution)!

column9: Cinnamon almond flavor makes old bran favorite new.
column10: I have always liked Bran flakes, so I was a little hesitant to try this "new" version of Rasin Bran. I turned out to be pleasantly surprised to find that adding the cinnamon and almond made this cereal taste great. There was just the right amount of flavoring to make the cereal taste different. Adding the almond seemed to also make the texture of the cereal less grainy, which is a good thing if you don't normally go for the texture of bran cereal.  I wish the box was bigger, because I really enjoyed eating this. I would definitely purchase this again as it is a great healthy cereal that tastes good as well.

The Cinnamon Almond version of Raisin Bran tastes great!  I just wish it had a little more nutritional value to start off my day (the regular version is a bit better in this regard).  Not one of the nutrients exceeds being 25% of your daily value.  The raisins had perfect flavor and the almonds stayed crunchy while the cinnamon added just the right amount of sweetness.

column9: Disappointing variation of an old favorite
column10: As a huge fan of the original Raisin Bran,I was looking forward to trying this new flavor. I did not think of this brand as 'sugary sweet' like some other cereals on the market. Unfortunately the sweetness in this new variation was way too sweet for me. There was too much cinnemon in this cereal for me, and I may have enjoyed it more, with a touch less. I ended up discarding the rest of the box. A positive was that it didn't get soggy and was very crunchy, but I will be sticking with the original flavor.
I really liked the combination of flavors. It was sweet and cinnimony (if that's a word!). The raisins were chewy and fresh. I blew through the box in a couple of days. Will buy again.

I'm not much of a cereal eater, but have always been a fan of raisin bran.  So, I was curious about this new version.  It's delicious!  Plenty of almond taste, plus raisins, and plus these little sweet crunchy clusters.  The cinnamon flavor was light, not overpowering at all.  I had some for dinner the other other night, and it was so good I had a second bowl.  I will definitely buy this in the future!

This cereal is good. The cinnamon and almonds provide enough sweetness to enhance the bran and raisin flavor without being too overpowering. I would definitely recommend to those who are looking for a healthy cereal but prefer one with a little sweetness.

The cinnamon is light and tasty in these, and while I don't really taste the almonds, I can sure see them! Note--unlike most raisin brans, this one has nuggets. As usual for Kellogg's, the raisins are soft and delicious. VERY highly recommended!

I like Raisin Brand and I love almonds & cinnamon but I did not care for this cereal. I found very few almonds in the two bowls I ate and the cinnamon flavor was overwhelming. The cereal did seem to stay crisp longer in the milk but the powerful cinnamon taste was just too much for me.

column9: Should've thought to do this sooner!
column10: I always thought that Raisin Bran would be better with cinnamon (or that Cinnamon Toast Crunch should have raisins in it on something for variety), so I was happy to see this! Not much to say other than... it's sure enough Raisin Bran with cinn & almonds... and it's good! If you're not familiar with Raisin Bran--it's bran flake cereal with sugar-sprinkled raisins in it.

I already loved Raisin Bran but this is even better.  I love the almonds and there are crunch bits that stay that way through the whole bowl.  The flavor is the same Raisin Bran that I love with a little cinnamon flavor boost and extra crunch.  I think it is awesome.

While no worse than your average bowl of Raisin Bran, I was disappointed that I didn't find this to be noticeably better. The flavor of cinnamon could certainly be stronger (for my tastes, anyway), and the little slivers of almonds didn't really add to the "crunch" in any sort of meaningful way. And unlike the experience of some other reviewers, I found that this Raisin Bran got soggy remarkably fast after the milk was added, turning to slurry by the last few bites. I've definitely had other Raisin and Bran products that remained crisp longer.I was also a bit taken aback by the box, which holds only 14.5 ounces of cereal. It's the same height and width as the regular cereal box you'd see on the store shelf, but to hide the fact that you're not getting much cereal, the box is so skinny that I actually had trouble getting it to stand on end a time or two. And maybe this is common to a lot of cereals these days - it was just new to me.Overall, I've got nothing bad to say about this product...but to give it a rating of more than 3 stars, I'd have to feel like it was "better than average" somehow. And it simply wasn't.

Cinnamon Almond Raisin Bran somehow managed to have less taste than the regular version. Although I am a big fan of anything with cinnamon, in this case, it seems to take away from the overall flavor. Not only do the almonds lack any flavor, they don't seem to make a difference to the texture either. You would think they might add a crunch to the cereal, but that isn't the case.Definitely, my least favorite Raisin Bran.

column9: A delectable way to have dessert with fewer calories and more nutrition.
column10: My favorite desserts are cake and ice-cream, but lately I settled down for spicy, fruity cereals with low fat milk in hopes of avoiding some calories. The Kellogg's Two Scoops Raisin Bran Cereals had been a favorite at my home for years, but this new addiction of Cinnamon and Almonds is an auto buy. My daughter loves it, and I had to remember that it has calories too, otherwise I would be eating a whole box in a couple of days. I highly recommend it.

This box of cereal didn't last long in my household.I have always liked Raisin Bran, and his new version tastes as good as the regular Raisin Bran but with a welcomed new taste of cinnamon.  And there is the added benefits of additional protein via the almonds, which adds to its crunchiness too. And for me, any cereal with fiber is a good idea.  It's on my grocery list now.Highly recommended.

When I first saw this, I thought, "Why are they adding cinnamon?" I mean, Raisin Bran is a classic. However, it was pretty tasty. In fact, I would've liked a bit more cinnamon. It turns out that Raisin Bran and cinnamon are delicious together.Compared to regular Raisin Bran, this is the same but crunchier with milk and having a light cinnamon flavor. It doesn't come off as sweet. The almond slices don't get soggy, so you end up with some crunch all the way through your bowl. I like this even better than the original. So, if you like Raisin Bran, you should definitely try the Cinnamon Almond version.

I've eaten Kellogg's Raisin Bran for years. It's one of my favorite breakfast cereals. Now when it comes to most foods I have a very open mind and am always ready to try something new, but when it comes to cereal......not so much. So I was just a little bit apprehensive approaching this re-work of a classic cereal. I'm happy to say I was more than pleasantly surprised. I found the cinnamon flavor to be at just the right level. Not so strong that it overpowered the mix, but not so weak that it was just a "hint" either. The sliced almonds added a nice flavor note and a great change-up in texture. Overall, I'd say this is now one of my top three cereals. Highly recommended.

column9: Made me eat cereal for breakfast
column10: I don't eat raisin bran.  I got this box of Kellogg's Raisin Bran for my husband who has a bowl of regular raisin bran nearly every night.  It turns out that I am eating more of this cereal than he does. I get tired of regular raisin bran; it is just a little boring. This has cinnamon on the raisins and sliced almonds, neither of which I just love, but with the raisins and bran flakes it all works.  Neither the cinnamon nor the almonds are so strong they take over.I am not normally even a cereal breakfast person, but this has an extra crunch, plenty of raisins, a sweet, but not too sweet taste and has been exactly what I needed the last few mornings.  I got this box through Amazon Vine, but I like it enough that I will buy another box.  Does my husband, the raisin bran authority, like it, yes, but he said it is difficult to improve on Kellogg's Raisin Bran.

This is a delicious cereal with cinnamon, toasted almonds, and raisins. I recommend using a table spoon of sugar and a cup of milk with a cup full of cereals. It tastes crispy and crunchy and the toasted almond kicks-up a notch in flavor: Highly recommended.1. Cascadian Farm Organic Raisin Bran Cereal, 14-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)2. Total Raisin Bran Cereal, 18.25-Ounce Box (Pack of 6)

column9: Not bad, but too sweet for me
column10: I read a few other reviews here, one said there were hardly any almonds, and another said the cinnamon was barely noticeable. Maybe they each got a bad box, because the one sent to me has lots of almonds, and I could instantly taste the cinnamon.It's a surprisingly nice combination of flavors - bran flakes, raisins, almonds, and cinnamon, but as I always find with most, if not all, breakfast cereals, it's way too sweet. If they eliminated half the sugar, I'd probably be a buyer, but not as it is.

I'm a big fan of Raisin Bran. I like the serious, healthy flavor of bran, I really like raisins, so it's all good until about halfway through the bowl. At that point, it stops being a healthy breakfast option and turns into a bowl of soggy mush with hard raisins in it, and I have to stop eating.This new incarnation, Cinnamon Almond Raisin Bran, is crunchy and surprising, with the almond rescuing it from the earnestness of traditional Raisin Bran. But the real delight is whatever they've done to make the flakes stay crispy through the entire bowl. It's fantastic with whole milk and a little Sugar in the Raw (just a little).Delicious.

Okay, everyone knows the breakfast staple, Raisin Bran. It's as ubiquitous as Corn Flakes or Wheaties. So, there really isn't a whole lot I can add to the cultural dialogue around this old breakfast standby. But I can say that adding cinnamon and almonds to the formula really kicks the cereal up a notch, making it something new and even more delicious than its fore bearer. Good stuff.

column9: OK, but not as good as Special K Cinnamon Pecan
column10: I've eaten regular Raisin Bran for about a year now, a few times each week (always with skim milk).  I've also eaten many other varieties over years.  One of my  favorites is another Kellogg's cereal, Special K Cereal, Cinnamon Pecan, so I can't help but compare these two, and for me, the Special K Cinnamon Pecan is far better.  This review is purely what I think tastes best (I'm not a nutritionist, so I'm not going to try and compare which is better for you).I suppose I like Pecans better than Almonds.  I also think the Cinnamon Special K flakes taste a lot better, and stay crisper in milk longer than the Cinnamon Raisin Bran flakes do, and the Special K flakes have more cinnamon glaze on them than the Bran flakes do.

column9: Like eating candied almonds for breakfast
column10: Cinnamon Almond Raisin Bran adds...cinnamon and almonds to your Raisin Bran. Plenty of people on here think it tastes amazing, so I'm a bit in the minority. I think it tastes...okay. It's a bit too sweet for me and a little too strong on the cinnamon. If you want a good analogy of what it tastes like, this cereal basically tastes like you're eating a bowlful of candied almonds. It's been a couple years since I've eaten regular Raising Bran so maybe things have changed or maybe it's just this cereal but I always remember the raisins in Raising Bran being a bit on the small side and kind of firm; in my box of Cinnamon Almond Raising Bran anyway the raisins are fairly large and are soft, making for a bit of squishiness. This is a pretty good cereal that kids and people with a sweet-tooth will probably love. It really does taste just like you're eating candied almonds. Worth trying if you like cinnamon, almonds, and Raisin Bran on their own.

I've been watching my nutrients for the past year in order to lose some weight. I find that I can do a good job with every component of my diet except one--fiber. Calories, fats, sodium--no problem. But I often come up short on fiber. When I do, well, let's just say that I've reached that stage of life where a shortage of this component causes me not to be a regular guy.Original Raisin Bran is a great weapon in this fight. I've tried other high-fiber cereals, but I always come back to the old standby. It gives me what I need without a lot of strange ingredients like chicory root extract (inulin) or soluble corn fiber. It tastes good too. So, I was very happy to try this new version of my old friend.It's quite good. A lot of cereals add cinnamon to boost flavor, but they tend to hit you over the head with it, adding so much that it becomes overpowering. Not so here. There's a nice, balanced flavor of cinnamon, almonds, and the original raisins and bran flakes. I find it very appealing. It has a few more calories and a bit less fiber than its un-spiced forebear, but overall a worthy addition, I think.In 58 grams, you'll get 200 calories and 5 grams of fiber.

column9: Excellent Twist On an Old Favorite
column10: I'm a big fan of Raisin Bran. so I was happy to try this newest spin on Kellog's classic. The cereal is still one of the healthier ones that Kellog's puts out but it now tastes even better. The almonds gives the cereal a little added protein as well as an extra crunch. The Cinnamon flavor is understated yet you will still instantly notice it, especially if you routinely buy the original version of the cereal.The cereal is low fat, although the almonds add a bit more than regular Raisin Bran has. It has 5 grams of fiber in every serving, but also 18 grams of sugar. It's high in Iron, B vitamins, folic acid and other essential nutrients, so although it's a bit more sugary than most cereal that my family eats, it's still one you can feel good about eating. My rabbits really want to eat it too...All in all, if you're a fan of bran cereals, definitely give Raisin Bran: Cinnamon Almond a try. It's quite tasty and a nice change from the original version.
having always loved regular raisin brand, I had to try this new twist. The cinnamon make is taste so much better. The almonds, while I liked it, I would rather have just had it with the cinnamon.

Raisin Bran is one of those cereals that has been with me since childhood, but has never made much of an impression.  It is good and satisfying, but also pretty boring.  This new version adds only what it says in the name: cinnamon and almonds.  The amount of cinnamon is just right to give the cereal an interesting and delicious flavor.  On first bite, I thought, "This is delicious!"  I have never done that with the original, and rarely do it with cereal in general.  The almonds politely play a minor role, elevating the flavor a bit, but not getting in the way.  This is not a cereal that will make you feel like you are eating a spoon of slivered almonds.I would recommend this cereal to both people interested in a fun new cereal and those that eat Raisin Bran for health reasons and fall asleep shortly afterwords.  It kicks up the notches in just the right ways, tasting like this was how it was always meant to be.

This new Raisin Bran with Cinnamon and Almonds is the right step in differentiating the class Raisin Bran, but the cinnamon is far too subtle and the almond slices too few to make a significant impact.  Bolder flavors and textures are needed.It's not as good as Raisin Bran Crunch, and definitely not as good as Honey Bunches of Oats: Raisin Medley.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column10: I dislike almonds. I've never known quite why. There's something about them I've just never cared for. So I approached this product with more than a little trepidation.Thankfully my concerns were meaningless! This is tasty, crispy, crunchy and good. The almonds are all very smell, and with almost no taste of almonds at all. In fact, I really, really liked it, not just tolerated it. I liked it well enough that, if I were at a store and saw this for sale, I'd probably buy it, and that's really saying something for me!

Great tasting cereal that stays nice and crisp.  Raisin Bran Cinnamon/Almond has a good cinnamon flavor without tasting artificial.  Comparing calorie counts, you get a quarter cup more cereal and it is still lower in calories than Oatmeal Squares and has no saturated fat.

Boy, do I LOVE this cereal!  It's not overly sweet, has a wonderful cinnamon flavor, with wonderful clusters that are not saturated with spices, and just enough almonds for crunchiness.  Just a perfect blend of flavor and raisins!  Raisin Bran has always been one  of my favorites and this one is definitely at the top of the list.  A wonderful improvement, the box barely made it two days in this house.  Highly, highly recommend!

I really like this cereal: great crunch, flavor, and just the right amount of sugar.I was afraid it might have that artificial almond, marzipan flavor; but no, it has real slivered almonds, and the amount of  cinnamon flavor is just right. Very good indeed.

column9: Good balanced flavors; I prefer it without milk
column10: The cereal is not "sugary sweet" (meaning that the primary flavor isn't sugar). The raisins are soft and plentiful (I remember eating Raisin Bran as a kid, when the raisins were like little rocks). The slivered almonds add to the overall crunch, but their subtle flavor is somewhat lost to the taste of raisins and cinnamon. The bran flakes are crispy, but they rapidly wilt when milk is added. For that reason, I prefer to eat this cereal like "trail mix"...there's no law that says you HAVE to put milk on cereal, but if that's the way you prefer it (and if you eat at a normal pace, as opposed to wolfing down your meals) you may wish to seek out a heartier flake. That said, for my personal tastes, I'm still giving the product five stars.

It's difficult to write a cereal review when the contents get eaten within 3 days, but I'll do my best!To start, the bran flakes didn't get soggy immediately, which was a huge plus. The cinnamon flavor really came out once the milk was poured, and it was just the right amount - not too light, not too overpowering. The raisins tasted fresh, and the sliced almonds gave that little kick that makes a great-tasting cereal even better!Reaching the bottom of the bowl, there were plenty of almonds and raisins to be found, so our bowls were empty but our stomachs were full. Everyone loved the taste and we will definitely be picking up more of this cereal...my wife and child were ready to fight me over the last bowl!Enjoy!

I knew I was going to like this cereal, what I wasn't pepared for was the fact that I was gonna love it!I imagined raisin bran and almonds together. Pretty yummy, right? But add in just the perfect amount of cinnamon, and you've got the most absolutely delicious breakfast cereal.I give Kellogg's Raisin Bran Cinnamon Almond cereal Five Stars and a big THUMBS UP and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys Raisin Bran!****DISCLOSURE: This product was provided by Amazon Vine in exchange for an independent and non-biased review.

column9: Better than regular Raisin Bran which i like
column10: The cinnamon and almond enhanced Raisin Bran appears to be slightly sweeter and crunchier than the standard Raisin Bran.  The cinnamon taste is bold but good. The crunch of the almond is excellent as is the cereal itself. I like this product very much.

Here's a real winning combination - good old Raisin Bran and now some almonds - and the raisins are cinnamon-coated.  Pour on some Almond Milk and it is so good, you won't want to eat anything else!  I usually add a banana as well.  This is definitely an adult cereal - the kids can't possibly appreciate it, so let's keep it all for ourselves!

There is no question that Kellogg's has made some really excellent cereals from the past several years. But there have been some cereals that weren't that good like their newest cereal Krave. But with the classic Raisin Bran, it has never lost its taste and quality all these years. They have upped the ante with Raisin Bran again with their newest edition of the Raisin Bran family with their Raisin Bran Cinnamon & Almond cereal. The taste is quite good, and is delicious with each and every bite. It shows that Kellogg's isn't afraid to add some zest to a already classic cereal. I thought that it was delicious from my first bite, and definitely shows it. You honestly will not be sorry with this cereal. I definitely recommend Kellog's Raisin Bran Cinnamon & Almond cereal.Price: BTaste: B 1/2+Overall: B 1/2+

I eat Raisin Bran regularly, so I was interested in trying the Cinnamon and Almond version. I was not disappointed.Some cereals overcompensate with their flavoring, but the cinnamon seems just right. It isn't overpowering at all. The almonds didn't add much to the flavor, but I'm an almond fan. The flakes stayed crunchy in milk long enough for me to finish most of it before they got soggy.I'm also in medicine, and while cereal alone isn't the best breakfast, this version of Raisin Bran is good enough to be part of a healthy breakfast. There is a good amount of fiber, with relatively low levels of sodium and sugar.There are so many variations of cereal out there, and I usually buy the bagged versions to save money, but I will make an exception to have this one as a special treat from time to time.

I like the original Raisin Bran and it was a staple in our home growing up, but I think I really like this much better.  When eating the original Raisin Bran I actually added a little extra sugar, not sure why exactly, but I always felt that it needed it.  No extra sugar needed with this new Cinnamon & Almond Raisin Bran.  It has the right amount of sweetness, crunch, almonds, and cinnamon.  I was afraid the cinnamon would be overpowering, but it is a perfect balance.  Not sure if the flakes turn soggy, like the orginal flakes, because I keep eating it too fast to find out.  My six year old was eating it straight from the box last night and he said it was delicious.  I would definitely purchase this cereal again!

I have to admit I am a major Raisan Bran fanatic. I've been eating this cereal almost every morning for over 20 years now. I switch up here and there but not for long, I just love the raisan and wheat combo. This new twist really excites me because it adds almonds and cinnamon, two of my other favorite things. The best part is they got the cinammon mix just right, it doesn't overpower the rest of the flavors, it just adds character. I am sold on this. Great job Kellog's. Now when I sit down to write my children's book seriesTales of Wordishure: A Book Of Christian Bedtime Stories, it's with a bellyfull of sweet crunchy goodness, who wouldn't be happy with that?

column9: Delicious - whole box gone in one sitting
column10: I gave this to my teen daughter and her friend when they were camping out.  They ate the whole box in one sitting!  She says it was delicious - not too sweet - and the raisins were plump and juicy, not overly-dry and hard like they sometimes are.  The cinnamon flavor was just enough but not too much.  She urged me to buy more....

column9: Add Fruit and Fat Free Milk and You Have the Beginning of a Healthy, Delicious Breakfast!
column10: Nutritionists have always said that if you're going to eat cereal for breakfast, choose one that is high in fiber and has nuts and dried fruit.  Kellogg's Raisin Bran Cereal is high in fiber and has dried fruit--raisins.  Now, it also has cinnamon and almonds.  Let me say that cinnamon is a nutritious spice.  Whenever I go to Panera Bread, I sprinkle cinnamon and ginger in my coffee.  Cinnamon is hailed as a spice that has a wide range of health benefits.  It can be used to treat digestive ailments, it is a preservative (Egyptians used it for embalming royalty), it improves brain function and also helps control type 2 diabetes.  I like to eat yogurt with my cereal and an occasional piece of fruit such as a Golden Delicious Apple.  (See the photographs that I have posted on this web site.)  I added blackberries and blueberries (all berries are high in antioxidants, which prevent cancer) to my Kellogg's Raisin Bran, Cinnamon and Almond, Cereal.  It was delicious.  The almonds made the cereal very crunchy and the cinnamon made it very sweet, almost too sweet.  If you don't like cinnamon, then you won't like this cereal.  It is not a hint of cinnamon, it is a strong taste of it.  I ate this cereal for dinner and I took some to work for breakfast; I carried it in three separate containers from my Lock&Lock BPA Free Airtight Container Set(Lock&Lock BPA Free Airtight Container, 28-Piece Set / 14-Containers).  (See my posted photographs.)  At work, I ate some yogurt with my cereal.  Kellogg's Raisin Bran, Cinnamon and Almond, Cereal is highly recommended for healthy conscious people who love the taste of cinnamon.  If you love cinnamon buns and cinnamon flavored coffee, then you will want to try this cereal.  It's delicious and nutritious, especially if you add berries and/or eat yogurt with it.  When my box is empty, I plan on buying more.  It's a type of cereal that even my elderly, finicky parents will enjoy.  They eat Special K and Cheerios but none of their varieties.  I think my parents would buy Raisin Bran, Cinnamon and Almond, after they learn how nutritious it is.Joseph B. Hoyos

Raisin Bran is one of the cereals in my breakfast rotation but I was a bit hesitant of their new Cinnamon Almond flavor because I am not the biggest fan of nuts.  But I could barely taste the almond (or the cinnamon either) and it really just came across in my mouth as just a crunchier version of the original.  This new flavor is highly recommended if you enjoy the original brand but are looking for a change in your morning breakfast.

column9: Is good but too much cinnamon
column10: I love the raisins, almonds and the bran but be a little lighter on the cinnamon please, it was slightly too strong, a little less sugar would be good too, it is just a little too sweet. It is high in fiber, the raisins are good and the cereal was fresh and crisp.

column9: How does Kellogg's improve raisin bran ?
column10: I've been eating Kellogg's raisin bran long before the dr. said "more fiber ! More fiber!"So how does Kellogg's improve a staple like raisin bran ? Well , they add cinnamon and almond !I've had to subsequently search for this product , as grocery cereal aisles are already burstin' at the seams , but now that I know where I can readily purchase it , I will always have an extra box on hand.The cinnamon and almond GREATLY enhance what was already a staple of my diet. "More fiber , more fiber!"

I have always been a long time fan of Raisin Bran, just plain old fashioned Raisin Bran.  Now we can add in cinnamon and almonds to the mix? Yes, please! I really liked that the cinnamon is very understated and enhances the taste of the almonds, the bran flakes and the abundant raisins.  As always, every bite is full of something delicious and you don't feel cheated and packed with bran makes this a winning breakfast cereal.  I like to start my day with a bowl of this cereal and I stay full for a VERY long time.  Very good!

I love the orginal Kellogg's Raisin Bran Cereals - always a nice bran flavor and great texture. When you add a the great taste  Cinnamon and Almond it is a nice change to the morning. Will pick up this flavor again.

Raisin Bran has been a staple of the American breakfast table since its introduction in 1926! This new take on that venerable cereal had me a bit dubious. They've produced lots of variations of breakfast cereals, and most of them disappear after a quick test run.This cinnamon and almond Raisin Bran is actually surprisingly good. It has a wonderfully rich bouquet, smelling rather like a nice cinnamon bread. And a big surprise is that it tastes as good as it smells. As I ate the cereal, I kept thinking to myself, "I've tasted this before." But, I never could place it. Perhaps I had a raisin-cinnamon bread before with the same taste - I don't know.Anyway, what I do know is that I rather liked the taste of this cereal. It's nice and sweet and flavorful, and definitely will buy it again!(Review of Kellogg's Raisin Bran Cereals, Cinnamon and Almond)

column9: Not usually a fan of raisin brain, but this is good stuff
column10: I'm not generally a fan of raisin brain, but I decided to try this, and surprisingly -- at least to me -- it's pretty good stuff. That's why I'm giving it 4 stars. Perhaps a fan would give it five, but it still suffers from one major flaw, and that is, it tends to get soggy in milk. However, I will say, this one stays crisper longer. So good work.

Sorry to say, this was not my favorite.  There is nothing wrong with it, and it tastes very good. It's just not my thing.  I like the classic Raisin Bran. I know companies are always looking for product improvement, but Raisin Bran has been around forever, because most people like it the way it is. If you like cinnamon cereal, you'll probably like this very much.

For me this cereal hits it right in the right spot. I now eat it everyday. They have come out with the exact balance of almonds and cinnamon any chemist would be proud to have been a part of. Believe me try a box and that will be it. You will be on it like I have been . It's the best.

I've always like Raisin Bran, but I wouldn't go out of my way to buy it.  Kellog's took an ordinary so-so cereal and added cinnamon and almonds.  The addition of that little spice turned it into something spectacular.  I like the almonds too, but it's the cinnamon that really makes the difference for me.

I really enjoyed this cereal.Being a big lover of raisin bran cereal I was concerned that the cinnamon would be too overpowering and mess up my classic bowl of Kellogg's Raisin Bran. But no, they did and excellent job of keeping the cinnamon nice and light as a compliment to the cereal and added in some little cinnamon roll flavored pieces that gave it just a nice flavor that blended in well. I really enjoyed it and would buy more in the future. If you like both raisin bran cereal and cinnamon I believe you will find this one to your liking. Yummy :o)

There's nothing fundamentally wrong with Kellogg's Raisin Bran with Cinnamon and Almonds. It is exactly as advertised, but the Cinnamon goes into a witness protection program for consumables when placed in milk, which reduces the product essentially to Kellogg's Raisin Bran with Almond pebbles. The product has a good taste and the flakes maintain their crunch, though they have a decidedly sweetened taste when just eaten fresh from the box, that may be overpowering to those sensitive to sweets. Mixes really well with fruit as well, I used strawberry and banana on one occasion, was a perfect morning treat.

Very tasty and lots of bran fiber to help clear you out.  It tastes like a bran version of Honey Bunches of Oats with Almonds, especially when you get a spoonful without raisins.  Pretty good stuff.  200 calories per serving (1.25cups).  Like all cereals, lots of carbs: 47g (5g dietary fiber and 18g sugar).  No high fructose corn syrup.  Your standard cereal vitamin fortification.  Good stuff.

column9: Tastes too good to be good for you
column10: I've always loved Raisin Bran and now that Kellogg has enhanced it with cinnamon and almond slivers, it's better than ever.  The bran flakes themselves have been lightly frosted with sugar and to my taste at least, need no further sweetening.  Actually, I could have done without the extra sugar (18 grams per recommended serving), but it's certainly not overwhelming and this cereal just plain tastes good.  Even my husband who can be difficult to please, enjoyed this and would buy it.Taste aside, Raisin Bran really is good for you.  It's a rich source of fiber from whole grain wheat while being low in fat and it supplies measurable percentages of required vitamins and minerals.  Cinnamon and Almond Raisin Bran is a pleasant way to start the day and a painless avenue to better nutrition.

Regular Kellog's Raisin Bran is one of the cereals I buy pretty often, so I was curious how the addition of almond and cinnamon would change the taste a lot or not. I enjoyed the combination, but overall I have not noticed  that much difference. I mean cinnamon taste was pretty noticeable, but not overwhelming, I would not say that I felt almond a lot, it was a little bit crunchier but not much, and all together it was mostly the same, but I enjoyed the taste and would buy it for myself.

column9: OK, but wish it wasn't so sweet
column10: I've always been a fan of Raisin Bran, so I was happy to try Kellogg's Raisin Bran Cereals with Cinnamon and Almond.  Though I enjoyed this cereal, it wasn't quite as good as I would have hoped.Specifically, I liked the added touch of cinnamon and almonds, though I'd note that I wish there were a bit more almonds in the mix.  What I got and didn't really want was the added sugar.  This new Raisin Bran is sugar coated, making the taste of the flakes closer to Frosted Flakes.  I'm sure this will make this new cereal popular, but it's not really to my taste.  But if you like Frosted Flakes or other sugar coated cereals this may be a good choice for you.

column9: Raisin Bran Cinnamon and Almond Cereal
column10: This is actually the second time that I've tried this cereal.PROS: It's lightly sweetened. It's crunchy and tasty. The cinnamon flavor comes through nicely. My daughter likes it.CONS: It could use more almonds and crunchier flakes. These flakes grow soggy quickly. I prefer the flakes in Raisin Bran Crunch.3.5 - 4 STARS: These are good for the occasional change up, but they are not my preferred cereal.

This is a tasty new version of Raisin Bran cereal. Whole grain wheat, rice sugar, and raisins are the first three ingredients.  Almonds are the 7th ingredient and even though I saw them in the cereal, I could not taste them. I was a little surprised by the strong cinnamon flavor being that cinnamon is the 13th ingredient on the list.It was impossible for me to eat just 1/2 cup.  A 1/2 cup serving is 200 calories and 240 calories with skim milk.My box arrived somewhat crushed so there was a lot of bran dust due to the flakes being crushed.  However, I doubt that is typical.Overall, I really liked the flavor, body, crunch and taste but would have liked a few more almonds in the box.

Kellogg's is definitely marketing the new Cinnamon Almond version of its classic Raisin Bran cereal as a "Heart Healthy Selection," which the front of the box announces, along with the claim that it's an excellent source of fiber (which it is--one serving contains 5g of fiber--or 21% of the RDA) and that it's made from whole grain. Don't let these assertions scare you away. Yes, this is a healthy cereal, despite the somewhat high calorie count of 200 per each one-and-a-quarter cup serving; in fact, a one-cup serving, which yields 160 calories, is plenty. But it's also very tasty, very crunchy, and rather filling. I ate it with a half cup of almond milk (so perhaps that augmented the almond flavor a bit), and it served well as the centerpiece of my breakfast for quite a few days. I'm definitely adding this to my regular rotation of breakfast cereals.

Between my husband and me, there are literally over 100 years of eating Kellogg's Raisin Bran (he is 70, and Medicare has introduced itself to me).  We both tried the Cinnamon Almond version for breakfast today.  My husband gives it four stars, and so do I.  The amount of cinnamon is just right; you know it is there and nothing more.  The picture on the box shows way more almonds than I found in the cereal.Comparing only the differing nutrition facts between the original and the cinnamon version:Original:  1 cup (59g) is 190 calories; sodium 250 mg; potassium 310 mg; dietary fiber 7g; protein 5g; Vitamin C, 0%; phosphorus 20%; magnesium 20%; sugar is the fourth ingredient listed.Cinnamon:  1 ¼ cups (58g) is 200 calories; sodium 220 mg; potassium 260 mg; dietary fiber 5g; protein 4g; Vitamin C, 2%; phosphorus 15%; magnesium 15%; sugar is the third ingredient listed.The 14.5 ounce box holds about five servings, considering what we ate this morning, although the box says it is supposed to be seven.  Now as to the cost on Amazon, $7.55 a box, that is just too much; I will be looking for this in the grocery stores, but the price will have to be half.  All things considered, my husband would prefer to eat the original version anyway; I would eat this only if the price compares to the original.

column9: Tasty, but needs more raisins and almonds
column10: Both my husband and I sampled this cereal and each of us had a different reaction based on how we felt about the original Raisin Bran cereal. He likes regular Raisin Bran and felt that this didn't have enough raisins or as strong a cinnamon flavor as he might have hoped for. He couldn't really taste the almond much at all. Both of us agreed that the sweetness level was about right such that additional sweetener did not have to be added nor was it cloyingly sweet. I'm not a fan of regular Raisin Bran and I thought that the cinnamon was noticeable and added flavor depth, but was not overbearing. I could taste the almonds, but wished there had been more slivers of them (but I love almonds and he does not). All in all, I thought this was a very good cereal and I enjoyed it more than regular Raisin Bran because the cinnamon and almonds added complexity to the flavor profile. My husband still prefers the original and probably wouldn't eat this again. I'd give this 5 stars and he'd give it 3, so I settled on 4 stars.

This cereal is really extremely tasty.  I ate it out of the box by the handful instead of the bowlful because I did not feel the need for milk and sugar.  It is very sweet just as it is but after reading the ingredients list, I understand why it's so sweet.  The 3rd ingredient is sugar, the 6th is brown sugar, and down on the list is dextrose, malt flavoring, and honey.  Of course raisins are high in sugar too.  Though I thought the almonds, raisins, whole grain wheat, cinnamon, and wheat bran along with the long list of vitamins and minerals in it made this a really healthy breakfast choice, I have to rethink that opinion.  After eating this and then testing my blood sugar shortly afterwards, I realize this is definitely not a cereal for diabetics. I can not personally reorder this product but if you have no problem with insulin reistance, I think most people would find this cereal delicious.

I love cinnamon and I regularly eat Raisin Bran Crunch so I was looking forward to trying this cereal.  For the most part I was disappointed.  The flakes are much thinner than the Crunch flakes.  I'd equate them to the consistency of Grape Nuts Flakes.  The flavor was okay but I'd prefer something more substantial. I would have liked a stronger cinnamon taste too but as it's easy for me to add more that didn't bother me too much.  The real killer for me was that there were so few almonds. I got only a couple of them in each of my first two bowls.  Once I removed the inner wrapper from the box I could see that they really skimped on the quantity of almonds.  So, even ignoring my preference for a thicker flake, considering that they went too light on the cinnamon for my taste and really skimped on the almonds I can't see ever buying this brand.

I like Rasin Bran cereal normally so when I saw this new flavor I thought that I would give it a try.  I am not really a fan of almonds but there are not alot of them so they were not overwhelming.  The cinnamon flavor could have been a bit more pronouced for my taste since I really do like cinnamon.  The cereal stayed crunchy in the bowl and didn't get soggy.  I did find the almonds a bit hard for my liking (yes I know they are nuts but they were a bit hard for me).  The cereal left a slight aftertaste in my mouth.  It wasn't a bad aftertaste but an aftertaste none the less.  I may get this cereal again if I have a coupon for it but I doubt I would buy it at regular price.

To me, this cereal tastes no different than regular raisin bran except for the fact that it contains almonds. I really could not taste the cinammon; however, I do like regular raisin bran, so I will eat the rest of the box.

column9: Almost LIke An Oatmeal Cookie in my Bowl
column10: This new offering from Kelloggs has good crunch and nice cinnamon flavor.  The almonds were a welcome addition.  It stood up well to soy milk and was tasty on its own.  The flavor is reminiscent of an oatmeal cookie and gets added kudos for the fiber content and being low fat.I did think it was a tad too sweet and I wasn't thrilled with the sugar content.  The almonds were hard and overall it would have benefitted from more almonds and raisins.I enjoyed this cereal and will add it to my breakfast rotation.
It's sweet, very sweet. And I think that's a good thing. I've had it both with milk -- it stays crunchy -- and straight from the box, and really liked it.

Really, enjoyed trying Kellogg's Raisin Bran's new flavor, Cinnamon Almond, with Silk Pure Almond Vanilla Milk. I also, tried this cereal dry. In both instances, the cereal was incredibly good and crunchy. As a huge fan of almonds, I would have loved to see more of them. The ones that were in the cereal were very yummy, though.If you are a fan of Kellogg's Special K, Vanilla Almond Cereal and like raisins, then you definitely should try Raisin Bran's Cinnamon Almond. When the box runs out, I will surely be adding it to my grocery list and so should you.

column9: A Nice Alternative to Regular Raisin Bran
column10: Kellogg's RB has been one of my favorite RB's for years, and this version does nothing to change that.The flakes are crisp and hold up well in milk. The raisins are soft, plump, and don't get hard in the milk like some do. The cinnamon coating has a nice flavor that is not overpowering. The almonds...oh, there's a couple...are crispy with a sweet coating.In the bowl with milk, the cinnamon flavor nicely compliments the bran flakes and raisins. The almonds don't really add anything to the mix. There aren't that many of them, and you really can't taste them when you get a couple in the mix on the spoon, hence the four-star rating. At least Kellogg didn't any dubious claims about added antioxidants from the added almonds.Bottom Line: I'd buy this variety.

column9: Tasty, but needs more raisins and almonds.
column10: I tried Kellog's Raisin Bran, and this cereal is very tasty. There is just the right amount of cinnamon and sugar in the product. When the bran flakes are mixed with milk, I must admit the cinnamon and sugar tastes are awesome.  The reason why I only gave this product three stars is that the raisins and almonds are a little sparse. The raisins are plump and juicy, and the toasted almonds are crunchy and complement the cereal well.  Unfortunately, this cereal is mostly bran flakes. I think Kellog's needs to add more raisins and ramp up the almond content to the amount found in the Honey Bunches of Oats Cereals.  Then this Raisin Bran would be outstanding.

Kellogg's Cinnamon Almond Raisin Bran is a distinct improvement on the original.  The flakes are tastier, with a sweet cinnamon flavor, and the almonds give addtional flavor and texture to the mix.  The weak link with this cereal is actually the raisin content.  The raisins ARE plump just as the box says.  A little too much.  The contrast of the crunchy flakes, semi-crunchy almonds, and the soft, almost squishy raisins is a little too jarring.  If the raisins were actually a little drier and chewier they would work better in this mix.Still, once you get used to them it's actually not that big of a deal - this is a very good breakfast cereal.  One good enough that I found myself eating some as an afternoon snack!The cereal stays somewhat crunchy in milk, and for those who like their cereal dry it has excellent flavor.Kellogg's definitely came up with a winner here.  Give it a try.

column9: A way to expand breakfast choices
column10: This might be a way to expand breakfast choices for cereal eaters. I like the regular brand but find the cinnamon a bit too strong for my taste and the almonds and raisins a bit sparse.

column9: Nice new touch to Raisin Bran
column10: I feel like Kellog's Raisin Bran has been has been around forever. I admit at times I thought the cereal was getting a bit boring next to its competitors, such as Total. However, I do like the idea of adding a touch of cinnamon and almonds. It's a relatively subtle and healthy way to add some new flavor to this classic cereal brand. And it tastes pretty good too. Overall, a nice balance.

column9: Perfect if you hate soggy cereal
column10: I'm not a big cereal fan, mostly cause soggy, mushy cereal makes me want to hurl. But by the same token, I don't want to feel like I'm chewing tree bark. Anything with raisins is a win with me - at least if the cereal part is icky, you get a consolation with the raisins.My favorite cereal was and is Raisin Nut Bran: the right amount of raisins, the right texture of bran to milk.Kellogg's Raisin Bran with cinnamon and almonds is a close second. The amount of 'extras' (i.e., raisins and almonds) is perfect. The bran is crunchy, perhaps a bit TOO crunchy. It certainly pass the non-soggy test (but I'd also like to keep my teeth.)I used a bit more milk with this than Raisin nut bran, and the bran was still VERY crunchy (like grape nuts crunchy.)And it also tastes great!My only real issue is with how NARROW the box is. I know we're in an era of inflation and we don't want to keep hiking the price of things, but c'mon, Kelloggs. If you made the box any more narrow, it'd need an easel to stand upright!So if you like this stuff and can find it on sale, go for it. Otherwise, try Raisin Nut Bran (still my fave!)

I have always been a fan of Raisin Bran, so it was nice to see a new twist on the product. I really liked this, though it was a bit on the sweet side. The raisins provide enough sweetener, in my opinion. The cinnamon and almond are a very nice touch that breaks the monotony of regular Raisin Bran. Have you noticed how the cereal boxes have gotten skinnier lately? This is no exception. For $5 you get seven 1.25 cup servings, which seems a little pricey. Hopefully they'll be a generic brand of this soon. But I still recommend that you at least give it a try. It's different.

column9: If you like Cinnamon this is a great cereal
column10: I don't like regular raisin bran, but i love this with the cinnamon flavor.  My teenage girls also love it.  The cinnamon is very noticeable so if you don't like cinnamon, you won't like this.

column9: A fairly tasty cereal but overly sweet
column10: So many cereals and so few mornings to enjoy them!  I remember the time when I would choose between Cheerios or corn flakes, now my pantry probably has 15 different cereals including oatmeal; however I have always been a raisin bran fan and often could trick myself into thinking I was eating something healthy (bran). 18 grams of sugar is not a small amount and with the addition of cinnamon added to the coated sweetened raisins the pandering to children's taste buds is ridiculous.  I admit I like the addition of almonds, but I believe this has been done before?  Using my box of puffed rice (naturally sweet) as a sort of base comparison, I was astonished to contrast it with the Raisin bran ingredients.  Puffed rice has no added sugar but is sweet enough, while the raisin bran has sugar, brown sugar, dextrose, cinnamon and honey.  (The last 4 items are under 2% but who needs them.)Could I become addicted to this cereal, probably yes.  But even after the first taste test (A full bowl of just raisin bran Cinnamon Almond) I knew I would have to mix it with something else (Shredded wheat for example) to bring down the sugar count and the calories (240 with milk).  My general advice is don't give up on basic raisin bran but stay away from the expanded raisin brans.  This new product will not revive the cereal industry, but push us more toward generic healthier cereals.

column9: New twist on an old favorite
column10: I love raisin bran and often throw in some extras, including nuts. This new cereal does that for me as well as adding a hint of cinnamon.  I'm not such a big fan of cinnamon for breakfast but the cereal was still very good, maybe a little too sweet for my tastes.  I usually use an extra raisin bran cereal with no added sugar.  Recommend that people who are looking for something different give this cereal a try.

I like regular Raisin Bran and this new version doesn't disappoint.  There is just a hint of cinnamon, not overpowering at all.  I definitely like that.  The almond clusters give this cereal some extra crunch and added protein boost. This isn't dramatically different from regular Raisin Bran, but it is a nice change of pace.

I like Raisin Bran anyways, but this new flavor with cinnamon and almonds is really good. The almonds give it some extra crunch that I really enjoyed. The cinnamon was pretty intense, which was good, but you really cannot each more than one small bowl at a time. It was perfect for breakfast for a snack.

column9: great, but these come in a box without a liner...
column10: great candy, just as you would get in the store, however they came shipped in a corrugated cardboard carton direct from jelly belly without a liner ( literally, the candy was just in the box with nothing else- no plastic bag, etc), which was a bit off-putting. However, I assume that if this is how I get it, this is how most retailers get it, meaning I've been eating jelly beans direct from a cardboard box my entire life. I ordered four different flavors of jelly bellies and they all came this way. No one got sick, so I assume this was sanitary.

I've had nutritional yeast once before in the form of a "Mac and Chreese"-in-a-box product and loved it. While it wasn't as much cheesy as it was garlicky, I had high hopes that "nooch" could satisfy the instinctual human need for Velveeta-style "cheeze". I could never find it at a grocery store OR a health store so I finally ordered this on Amazon.Wow. Yeah, I said wow. I used this in a recipe for "Cheeze Sauce" that was fat-free and it was amazing. Plus it had tons of protein, fiber, and of course the illustrious vitamin B-12! There are other similar recipes that call for LOTS of margarine that sound even cheesier and richer.This bottle lasted me about 2 recipes with a little leftover for sprinkling, so if you're new to cooking with nutritional yeast this is a good size to start with. I've since bought a 22-oz container of a different brand, but this brand is just as good.In conclusion...buy this, make lots of cheeze/chreese or any intentional misspelling of "cheese" you desire, be nice to animals and get 150% of your daily value of B-12.

Whoever said healthy food does not taste good, never tried this stuff! I am a life long vegetarian but only started using nutritional yeast last year. This stuff tastes great and is so easy to use. I use it to make scrambled vegan eggs (with tofu). So many vegan recipes call for this stuff and I can see why. It's a powerhouse of nutrients and tastes like cheese!

column9: great on savory dishes as a salt substitute
column10: I may have strange taste buds, but i find adding Red Star Nutritional Yeast to salads, soups, fresh veggies and dips adds a nice savory, earthy flavor.  I've started using it as a salt substitute.  Gotta love that!

After my husband had a heart attack I started looking for healthy, low-fat, low-sugar snacks... that he would actually eat.  In Cooks Illustrated I read about the healthy snack of nutritional yeast flakes sprinkled onto popcorn.  I bought some to try and can happily report it is delicious!  Hubby was even licking his finger to get the last bits off the bottom of the popcorn bowl.  Nutritional yeast has many other uses which can now be explored since it passed the critical taste test with hubby.Being unable to find this product at health food stores I bought through Amazon.  The price was fair and shipping was FREE.We highly recommend this product.

column9: Great Nutritional yeast for a great price!
column10: This little bargain was worth every penny! I like the freshness of the nutritional yeast as some places only offer it in bulk at these prices! I have used this brand's yeast for baking and took a chance and I was pleasantly surprised.I used this for cheezy sauce,and in some vegan burgers to add a savory flavor;-)

column4: James Beswick "In my day, we had 9 planets."
column10: We only started using this product about a month ago and have already burned through two containers. It's rich in vitamin B-12 and other nutrients but more importantly imparts a cheesy flavor similar to Parmesan. It's effective at dressing up salads, vegan mac-and-cheese and pasta sauces but it really shines as a topping for vegan pizza. As an aside, it's a shame this isn't currently an Amazon Prime product since the shipping doubles the cost.
Shipped promptly.  Very tasty.  I was a bit skeptical but the flakes taste great on everything I have tried them on including baked potatoes and cottage cheese!

This is a great cruelty-free alternative to dairy cheeses. I use it on everything I used to use parmesan on, mainly Italian sauces and dishes, but it's also good in tofu scrambles, and cheesy sauces. Plus it's also packed with B vitamins, including B12, which I need ways to sneak into my diet after having gone vegan. It did take me awhile to get used to, but now that I have, I can't get enough of the stuff.
I am loving nutritional yeast flakes. It has kind of a cheesy flavor. there are other brands that have less cals. this has 70 cals for 1 & 1/2 tablespoons.

This is very great yeast.looked all over to get it and found it on amazon..I use it in a lot of products..Great on popcorn and veggies..It has a lot of b12 vitamins in it..very good for you.i also make a topping of yeast, water and grapeseed oil, and put it on baked potatoe,,yummy..Red Star Nutritional Yeast..p/s ( grapeseed vegenaise spread)
OMG!!! I just love this stuff!!! I haven't had it in so long I forgot how good it was!!! lol!!! So glad I bought it!!!

I use nutritional yeast for two purposes: I sprinkle it on tofu scramble, first of all. It's tasty that way, and if you're vegan, it's a nice alternative to Parmesan cheese on spaghetti. I also use it, though, on top of cat food. One of my cats has a stomach condition that makes her a really picky eater. Nutritional yeast sprinkled on top of her canned food, though, really helps her to get down to the business of eating.

During my transition to a vegan diet I began coming across recipes that called for nutritional yeast. This was the first brand I tried, and I absolutely fell in love with it. I have tried a few other brands since then, but keep coming back to Red Star. Not only is the flavor great, but the price is very reasonable compared to some of their competitors. It's great in all sorts of foods, far more than just tofu scrabble, pop corn, and mac and cheese. I put in cereal, cakes, french toast, soups, salads, smoothies, cookies, sandwiches, etc.

I like this a lot as a topping on my popcorn instead of butter. It's very good and has kept well in the refrigerator after several months. I will order more.Update:I bought a second batch. I didn't have room in my fridge so I've been leaving it in the pantry. I've had it a few months now and it still tastes great.

This product is highly recommended for vegetarians and vegans to get a sufficient amount of vitamin B12. At a molecular biologist working with yeasts I'd say it might be a better choice to get the required nutrients, you cannot get from vegetarian diet, from this product than from nutrient "pills". It tastes also not bad if you put it on your food. But careful, dissolved in water it tastes awful :P
Love it! You can put it on anything really and the taste is great! I use it for my Roads End mac and chreese as well as salads and zuchinni tacos.
I use this product in my cashew mac and cheese and love it. It adds a  lot of nutritional value
Red Star has a great flavor and can be easily added to many food.  It is great for a cheesy, vegan flavor.  It also contains B vitamins.  Definitely a win-win.
We loved this product!  It made cooking better as it gave our vegan food much more flavor!  We recommend this to anyone.

Although I always make my own guacamole, I was in a hurry one time and saw this in the produce section so I thought I'd try it because I really like Chef Bayless and I thought it would save me some time.  I read the ingredients and everything looked great.  Although i don't normally add tomatillos, I thought why not because I generally like tomatillos in other things.  I mixed this with the avocados as instructed, tasted, and it just wasn't very good.  It lacked flavor; especially the flavors one normally tastes in traditional guacamole:  garlic, tomatoes, onion, and lime, to name a few.  It should be noted that some of these are listed in the ingredients list on this bottle.I ended up chopping up my own tomatoes, garlic, and onion, and basically everything else I normally do when making guacamole to "fix" the guac.  It actually took longer than if I had just made the guac like I normally do.

Bought a pouch of this mix at our local grocery store.  After mixing with three avocadoes, it created the oddest tasting guacamole I've ever had.  After a few spoonfuls my husband and I determined it tasted like applesauce.  Very strange.  We ended up adding  a bunch of other spices from home to try and salvage it.  If you are going to use a mix, I'd recommend sticking with the dry packets you can find in the produce section.  This was a tasteless disappointment.
We had some over the weekend.  I mixed it with 4 large avocados and we had plenty for leftovers.

column9: Loved the flavor - very good to use in a pinch
column10: We love guacamole and always make it for parties, however, it can be time consuming.  I make the standard guacamole - tomatoes, cilantro, onion, garlic, jalapeno - because it is the only recipe I have used for years and always comes out good.  I saw a pouch of Frontera in Target with Rick Bayless' name on it and thought it must be good.  I loved it!  Mixed the pouch with 2 perfectly ripe avocados and a little salt and had delicious guacamole in minutes and really liked that it tasted different from the usual stuff.  You can use the pouch alone or also use it as a seasoning and add the other usual stuff.  I really loved the flavor - great to have if you need a time saver for a party or to whip up a quick batch on taco night.  I like it just the way it is for a change of pace from the standard guac - the only change I might do is to add a little more chopped fresh cilantro for an extra burst of fresh flavor and better presentation.

We love guacamole at our house, however it's always been a long process to make.  I found this by accident at World Market, figured I'd try it.  I thought this was very easy, generally one jar is for 4 avacodo's.  So if I have 2 I'll use just half the jar and save the rest for the next time.  However, the only down side, I don't think it tastes the same the next day, not sure why.  So I only make what I'm going to use that day.  It is hard to find in stores, Wegman's is the only local place I've found it.  If you want a quick, easy and good dip, I rate this a 5, leftovers I rate it a 2.
If you want a quick easy way to make perfect guacamole then this is the product.  It arrived very promply and nothing broken.

We're big guacamole fans, but have always preferred restaurant fresh.  For some reason my homemade guac tastes flat, but have ocassionally made do with a dry mix.  We discovered this Frontera product by chance and boy are we glad!  It tastes really different, with a smokey undertone I wish I could duplicate. I don't think it's the cilantro -  maybe the tomatillos?  (I confess to not having used those at home before.)Anyway, teh Fontera is a little pricey to have all the time, but it's a special treat for my family.  I'll get 4 avocados - 2 really ripe and 2 not so ripe.  We'll have half the jar of mix with the ripe ones and the the rest of the mix a week later after the other avocados are ripe.)The mix seems to last in the frig that long OK.)I know folks who eat this mix it out of the jar with crackers.  Sigh!
