I pack a few with my husband's lunch, he loves them too.My only complaint is that the cookies were thrown around in the package and I had to put them back in the slots.

column9: for when the girl scouts and your stash are gone....
column10: When the girl scouts are gone and your thin mints are just a memory, you may be able to find a bit of solace here with these new oreos.  I tried the peanut butter ones.  You get a thin oreo bottom, creamy peanut butter center enrobed in chocolate.  They are basically the same size as a thin mint cookie but with a delicious filling.  I can't speak for all the flavors (yet), but the look of joy when I ate this cookie made my hubby grab the box to make me share.....We agree....this one is a keeper, especially if you love chocolate and peanutbutter flavors together.  Not that you would be looking, but the calorie count on these are 170 for 3 cookies.  I would definitely buy these and would consider trying other flavors, perhaps hubby's favorite flavor....mint.

It's like my two favorite girl scout cookies of all time got together and had a baby.  That would be thin mints and tagalongs (ugh to the new names).  I tried the Peanut Butter version. These cookies have the light crispness of a thin mint and the fudgy peanut butter omf-goodness of a tagalong.  They are irresistibly yummy and impossible to stop eating.  The pack I opened yesterday is gone. finito. even crumbs are scarce. These win 5 stars on taste alone because we all know they are so not good for you. Do not buy if you are trying to diet at all, because you will not be able to resist.

I'm a big Oreo fan, but I didn't care much for this new version. On paper it sounds pretty good - chocolate covered peanut butter on an Oreo. What's not to like? Well, the chocolate for one - it's rather waxy-tasting. Just didn't hit the usual chocolate spot. The peanut butter is also lacking in flavor. In fact, if I didn't know it was peanut butter from the package, it probably would have been third on my list of guesses based on taste.The bright spot was the cookie base. Good to see Oreo has not lost their touch when it comes to the actual cookie.Perhaps this would be better in the mint version? In any case, I'd suggest giving the peanut version a pass. Good concept, but not well executed.

column9: tasty -- like an Oreo cookie mixed with a Reese's cup
column10: DISCLAIMER:  I have a *BIG* sweet tooth.I must say that I enjoyed these cookies a lot.  There's a nice chocolate coating on the outside that covers a peanut butter flavored creme coated Oreo cookie half.  It's just the right ratio of cookie crunch to peanut butter creme to chocolate coating.My only issue is that these cookies are a tad messy to eat.  It's fairly cool where I live right now and I noticed that the outside coating on these was already a little soft even before I picked up a cookie, and then the coating definitely rubbed off on my fingers as I ate the cookies.  This isn't an issue if you can wash your hands as soon as you're done eating, but if not -- such as if you snack on these while driving -- you could end up making a mess.

if you are looking for big Oreo taste, these are not going to give it to you.  There is only one Oreo wafer in these, AND the wafer isn't even as thick as one side of a regular Oreo.  I suspect they were trying to cut down on calories, but give me a break, it is a cookie, covered in chocolate, with PEANUT BUTTER.  Are you REALLY thinking about calories while eating these?  Likely not.That said, they are yummy!  Hubby said NOM NOM NOM...he claimed that could be the extent of the review.  They taste very similar to a nutty bar, hubby, son and I all agree.  Quite good, but I LOVE Oreo wafers, so I could have done with a little more of that.

These cookies are so tasty.  I got the peanut butter creme to try and I will be buying them again!  The cookies are relatively thin since they aren't a "sandwich" cookie.  The actual cookie part is very fresh and a crisp bite under the peanut butter and chocolate coating.  They are rich and satisfy that chocolate craving with a single cookie!  These are nothing like traditional Oreos, but they are very, very good!

I love the combination of chocolate and peanut butter, so this cookie sounds like something to get excited about.  It didn't quite live up to my expectations.  You've got a thin layer of chocolate cookie covered by a layer of peanut butter spread with the entire thing thinly coated in chocolate.The chocolate is slightly on the waxy side.  The word fudge wouldn't have popped into my brain at all if I hadn't seen it written on the package.  And peanut butter?  Well, I guess I was expecting more flavor, although the texture  of the cream is nice and smooth.Don't get me wrong, I don't think this is in anyway a bad tasting cookie.  It just doesn't live up to my imagination of what it should or at least could taste like.  I could be thinking too much of Reece's Peanut Butter Cups here.Would I purchase them?  Probably not.  I'm guessing the price of the cookies is inflated by its packaging which keeps each cookie separate from the others.  It seems to be a large package for 27 cookies of that size due to the spacing of the cookies.  Even though some cookies decided to visit other cookies and not stay in their designated spot, none appeared damaged due to shipping or my own jostling of them when I took them into work.Would I eat them if offered to me?  I certainly wouldn't turn them down.

This cookie in the Oreo family is certainly tasty if not healthy. There is a layer of chocolate surrounding a peanut butter delight and what appears to be one original Oreo. This latest addition to the Oreo family is not as peanut-buttery as, for instance, a Reese's peanut butter cup; but it has a nice texture and flavor.  You don't have the two great chocolate cookie crusts and the filling as in the original Oreo that has delighted people forever, either with a glass of cold milk or in a pie crust or nestled inside a cheesecake so it is okay to like this one without forsaking your allegiance to what, as I recall, is the most popular cookie in the United States. It certainly has my vote, even above the best of chocolate-chip cookies.If you are avoiding fat and sugar, look someplace else as this little number is high in both.

This is a goooood cookie. They just arrived today, and when you open the box, they totally smell like peanut butter. Made with the Oreo taste, only with just one side of the chocolate Oreo, and has a layer of peanut butter, and it's covered in chocolate. Very good, but requires milk! Very good tasting, try one, you won't be sorry. Not for peanut allergy sufferers though, sorry guys!

Those familiar with regular Oreos (and, really, who isn't?) won't find anything too terribly unfamiliar with these peanut butter Oreo Fudge Cremes.  They consist of a single wafer which is topped with a layer of peanut butter creme, then enrobed in a fudge coating.  The wafer is thin and nicely crispy.  The creme is purportedly peanut butter-flavored, but, to be honest, I was unable to pick up any of that.  It was still tasty, just not as peanut butter-y as I'd hoped.  The fudge coating was not too thin, not too thick, just nicely adding a hint of creamy chocolate goodness.What else can really be said about an Oreo?  Although I might wish that the peanut butter flavor was more intense, I was still quite happy to nibble on them.  I certainly wouldn't mind doing so again.

column9: Tasty New Twist On An Old Favorite
column10: These tasty new Peanut Butter Fudge Cream Oreo cookies have the same look as Girl-scout 'Thin Mint' cookies.  Each cookie is like a single chocolate top of a standard Oreo cookie - but with a dollop of peanut butter, then dipped in fudge.  They are quite delicious - and are 3 to a portion.Some nutritional info:Calories 170 (80 from fat), Cholestorol 0MG, Sodium 100MG, Potassium 80MG, Total Carbs 23G, Protein 2G.Of course, those with nut allergies should avoid this product.The flavor is very good, and they go very well with milk.Give them a try, you won't be disappointed.

In short, these cookies are very rich, indulgent, and delicious.  That said, they really taste nothing like Oreos.  Instead, I see these Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Cremes becoming an ideal way for Girl Scout Cookie fans to enjoy Tagalongs year-round.  While not an exact substitute, the taste is far closer to Tagalongs than traditional Oreos.Basically, these cookies consist of half of a Peanut Butter Oreo dipped in chocolate.  They taste incredibly rich, so much so that the recommended serving size of three cookies appears a little too much for me (and I'm a big chocolate, Peanut Butter, and all-around cookie fan).  I've only been able to eat two in one sitting.  They are good but a little goes a long way.  For those interested in a healthy snack, look elsewhere.  At 4.5 grams of saturated fat for a mere three cookies, a bag of these can easily blow a diet.  And while they boast zero grams of trans fat per serving, the ingredients list shows clear signs that they're walking a fine line: hydrogenated oil (trans fat) is a prominent component.Alas, there is one problem: these are messy little treats.  Each cookie comes fixed in its own little slot in the plastic tray, and if left at even room temperature for more than an hour, be prepared for about one-fourth of the chocolate coating to be wedged at the bottom of the plastic tray.  Smudges on fingers is a given, and even though these are best eaten slowly (two to three bites), the messy factor begs for them to go straight into the mouth whole.  No way am I putting these in my kids' lunch boxes!  This is strictly an at-home snack, served with plenty of paper towels.

Wow - not what I was expecting at all. I thought these would be Oreo cookies with fudge in the middle. I didn't realize that they're more like the Girl Scout Thin Mint cookies laced with fudge. The package I received contained the peanut butter flavored fudge cookies, and they all but melt in my mouth. They are borderline decadent. It will be hard to restrict myself to a few cookies a day. Great taste, creamy fudge texture. Yum!

I am a long time fan of Oreo cookies...just about any flavor, antime. Thus, I was anxious to receive these and see what was new in the Oreo lineup. I was a bit disappointed but that may be because I apparently didnt read the description carefully.These are definately not the Oreo's most will be familar with. These are a wafer type, appx. 11/4 inch in diameter, covered with peanut butter and fudge toppings. The peanut butter is rich tasting and the fudge topping is dark and tasty. However, I repeat this is not a traditional Oreo cookie. While the package says it is covered in Oreo type cream, and it may well be, it is lacking in the traditional taste of the usual filling type cream we associate with Oreo's.The cookies were fresh and tasted OK but were nothing out of the ordinary and certainly not your traditonal Oreo and will take a bit of getting use to. My package contained partially melted cookies and was a mess to try to take from the package but the taste did not seem to be affected.All in all an OK product but at least for me not up to the Oreo standards. If you prefer wafer type peanut butter and dark chocolate tasting cookies this should work for you.

column9: I would serve as a Candy  rather then a cookie.
column10: I love peanut and chocolate and was pleased to try these cookies... Well they are very similar to Thin Mint Girl Scout cookies with peanut butter filling vs mint.  That said I would consider these more of candy treat vs a cookie.. Very thin wafer cookie topped with sm amt of lightly flavored peanut butter and the whole thing encased in very chocolaty coating.Just 1-2  is more than enough and I wouldn't serve these as a after dinner cookie  but perhaps a mid meal light treat with large glass of milk but only occasionally.  Not as peanutty as I expected but very clearly peanut flavored.I wasn't thrilled with the packaging. it has  a new type of pull tab opening that flips open the whole top of the cookie package exposing all of the cookies at once.. when opened more than 1/3 of the cookies had flipped out of their slots in the cookie holder and some were smashed against each other and had to be pulled apart. Can't imagine this would survive in the heat of summer  if it can't make it through this mild spring weather.. Looks like they might be a melty mess in warm weather.. I enjoyed these but not sure would be a repeat order for us.  Due to the candy-like nature of the treat.  and we live in a warm climate and this just looks like a mess in the making for our climate..

In another addition to the Oreo cookie line, Nabisco added Oreo Golden Fudge Cremes.  These are basically a thin chocolate waffer with peanut butter filling covered with chocolate fudge.  This naturally creates a high caloric and fat content cookie.  My biggest complaint with these are that they left a bitter aftertaste probably from the chocolate waffer.  My kids didn't seem to mind but this is not a cookie that I would go out of my way to buy.  There are similar better tasting cookies out on the market today so I can only give this an average rating.

So when I got these in the mail, I opened the package and felt like a lunchlady opening the door on what was mere moments ago an epic food fight.Goo, slop and general dishevelment.So having these delivered on a warm Florida day through the mail seems (at least in my one-time experience) to be not the best idea.That said -I was not expecting much - AT ALL. Gimmicky "remixes" of established classics...in my experience, a recipe for disappointment (Monterey Jack Cheez-Its anyone? I didn't think so...blecchh!)But these are like Girl Scout Tagalongs, except "all year long."In fact, they are MORE chocolatey, because of the chocolate (and not shortbread) cookie inside.The chocolate covering was surprisingly fudgy with a fuller chocolate body and flavor than I ever would have expected.The peanut butter filling is delightful, nicely balanced and sweet but still rich.So basically if you are a fan of Tagalongs and also a fan of chocolate, these represent a beautiful little crossroads.Just order them on a cool day. :)

Like many other Vine reviewers I was sent a package of Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crème, 11.3-Ounce (Pack of 3) cookies to try out.  Let's start off with the fact that these are not traditional Oreos.  We found them to be quite tasty, but they aren't traditional Oreos with two cookies and creme in the center.  So what are they ?While we were trying out this new Nabisco offering, I had a sneaking suspicion that I'd had this cookie before. A cookie with peanut butter...  covered in chocolate...  Ya know, if I didn't know any better, I would swear this was a Girl Scout Tagalong.  True, the Scouts don't use a chocolate cookie for their base, but the end result was very similar. They were even packaged the way the Girl Scouts sell them in individual slotted trays.Now that's not to say the Peanut Butter Oreo Cremes weren't tasty.  In fact, they disappeared rather quickly around our place.  Everyone seemed to enjoy them.  I just couldn't help but feel that they should have been delivered by the local Girl Scout troop.

I remember when the white chocolate dipped Oreo first came out some years ago.  Or at least...I remember my first experience with them.  I saw this new Oreo flavor and thought I might get a repeat experience of mind blowing taste delight.I didn't.Other reviewers have commented and I will make the same assertion: the peanut butter is just a bit off.  Somehow I had hoped/expected it would taste as magically addictively delicious as a Reese's PB cup.  The missing element here, to me, is SALT.  They're just not salty enough!  Combined with how bad these things are for you, I consider them to be just OK and will stick to traditional dipped Oreo cookies for now.

column9: Chocoate AND Peanut Butter AND Cookies!
column10: These cookies are great, the only thing wrong with them is they are a bit addictive! I tried the peanut butter, fudge covered flavor, and really enjoyed them. Picture the bottom half of an Oreo, but about 70% as thick as a regular cookie. This is topped with peanut butter filling, probably 80% or so of a regular cookie. (I actually have peanut butter Oreo cookies at home to do a comparison.) Then, the entire cookie is covered with fudge. The cookie reminds me a little of Girl Scout cookies, but not as crisp or crumbly.The package is an easy-open top, which is helpful because the cookies are set individually in a tray. I store the cookies in the refrigerator, and highly recommend this--they taste even better cold.This is a great cookie for Oreo lovers, people who like peanut butter, and probably just about anyone that likes sweets.

After receiving these today, I gathered the household testers together (aka, the missus and munchkins) to try these cookies.  First, let me describe them.  They are about the circumference of a normal oreo.  On the inside is one chocolate oreo-type cookie, about 1/2 the width of a normal oreo cookie, with a thin layer of creme on one side.  Then the entire cookie is covered with a chocolate/fudge.  Althogther, they're slightly smaller than the typical two cookies with creme inside oreo cookie you're used to seeing.The testers and I agree that they taste pretty good.  The cookie on the inside has a bit of snap to it when you bite into it, and the creme and fudge work well together.  And of course, almost anything tastes better when its covered with chocolate.  I won't go into the ingredients here, but a single serving of 3 cookies has 170 calories.This is an interesting new product from Nabisco, and I like it.  Five stars.

column9: Be careful or you will get fat - or fatter :-)
column10: THIS IS NOT A HEALTH FOOD; but I probably didn't need to tell you that. The first ingredient is sugar and the second is palm oil. I just received and openedthis treat and had my first cookie. If you like Reese's peanut butter cups (who doesn't?), you will probably like these. They taste almost exactly like aReese's but are shaped like a cookie and have a thin cookie crust on the bottom. So, to describe it, It's a cookie crust bottom with peanutbutter on top, then the entire cookie/product is covered in like a dipped chocolate similar to what you'd get if you went to Dairy Queen and had your vanillssoft-serve cone dipped in chocolate. They use the word "fudge" on the packaging but I personally would not claim that they have a fudge-like taste.Betcha can't eat just one - LOL

column9: Good Balance Of Chocolate And Peanut Butter
column10: I think I was supposed to receive the Golden Oreo Fudge Creme Cookies, but what I actually received was The Peanut Butter Fudge Creme Cookies, so my review will be based on the peanut butter ones.The packaging was fine, but most of the cookies in my package were not in their individual slots, so quite a few of them had two cookies stuck together, or the cookies were broken.I did enjoy the combination of the smooth peanut butter, balanced with chocolate.  The cookies are thin and crisp.I would definitly buy these cookies again, but in a store.  Maybe products like this are too hard to ship intact.  They did ship is a very large box with air pillows, but I think the cookies got bounced around, so that is probably how they got stuck together, or broken.The cookie package was sealed, but bulging, from the cookies being jostled, so that they couldn't lie in their individual slots.A great cookie, for when you want the taste of peanut butter and chocolate together.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column10: Oh, dear lord... merely looking at these was almost enough to send me into a diabetic coma. They are so incredibly rich it's insane. I was able to eat about three before I was willing to say "Yep, I'm done!" These really aren't as good as regular Double Stuff Oreos and you don't get very many. I counted, and you get 28 cookies. That's all. For the price you're paying you can find better. Heck, you can do what I suggested with the mint creme Oreos and buy normal ones and dip them into bark chocolate.Overall these aren't bad, but I didn't like them as much as the mint ones. They were way too rich for my tates.

The Oreo Fudge Creme cookies are pretty good, but could be better. The chocolate coating is a little on the waxy side, but does have good flavor. The wafer is a standard Oreo half, so you probably have had them before. The peanut butter filling is not a candied concoction like in a peanut butter cup, but more like plain peanut butter (if anything it's a little on the thin side). I posted some pictures of the package and the cookies so you could get an idea of the package size and opening and the cookie dimensions.

column9: Not As Yummy As I Had Hoped
column10: Previously, I had tried the mint Oreo Fudge Cookies and they gave the Girl Scout's brand a run for their money.(especially at $3.50 for two tiers.)  But, I can't say the same about Oreo Thin cookie filled with peanut butter and coated with fudge.  These would be so much tastier if the filling was peanut butter and there were two normal size Oreo cookies surrounding them.  The thin cookie is a bit harsh, the peanut filler bland, and the fudge topping fine.  It just wasn't something I would buy again as the flavors don't blend well.Maybe Oreo will take my idea and run with it.  I am sure that would sell better than these.

I admit that I've never met an Oreo I didn't like. Oh, I might have strayed a bit now and then--a bag of Chips Ahoy now, another of Cameos there, but I always returned to the one true love of my cookie life, ever since the days when I twisted them apart, ate the filling and dunked the outsides in milk. So be aware of my bias.The package I have of these is peanut butter. I can take or leave the peanut butter/chocolate union most of the time; I eat one mini peanut butter cup at Halloween, and that's about it for the year. But these are exceptionally yummy. there is a chocolate Oreo cracker there, and a layer of peanut butter, and the whole thing is dipped in a nice dark-ish fudgy chocolate to create a new rich type of Oreo goodness.It's tasty.  Well, more than that; it's the experience of being taken into a cookie-dominated plane of existence where there is nothing but you, the cookie, and deep regrets (kind of like Casablanca, except you can find what you're looking for at the supermarket).But beware: this is not a light cookie experience. These are dark, and rich, and dense, and they have--I swear--a very strong gravitational pull. Beware the tides!Oh, and to descend to the practical and prosaic, the bag has the best plastic self-resealing flap I've seen so far.

column9: Delicious addition to the Oreo family
column10: This review is for the Fudge Covered Peanut Butter Oreos that were shipped.Caveat up front - I did not eat these, but gave them to my resident cookie critics (one of which is a one-type-of-peanut-butter-only young lass). Said cookie critics are huge fans of original and Double Stuff Oreos and "dippy milk" (a true Oreo fan/critic cannot mix "drinking milk" and "dippy milk"), but haven't been that excited about other Oreo types. I was very interested to hear back from them on these.Immediately upon receipt of the cookies, some were put into the freezer for a few hours (as I understand from these critics that it's the preferred way to eat a fudge covered sandwich cookie). After an appropriate amount of time (also known as "after dinner"), the critics turned their highly tuned critical senses to these fudge covered treats. Both frozen and room temperature cookies were devoured in a very un-critic-like manner, and promptly given two thumbs up, tons of smiles and "yummmmms" and highly recommended for future purchases.Who am I to argue with them? Our recommendations are to freeze them for maximum enjoyment.

column9: Hit the back button before it's too late...
column10: Seriously, walk away....These cookies are nothing short of amazing!I don't really eat cookies, and if I did eat a cookie, It wouldn't be an oreo (not really a fan).However, I was offered the chance to try out these cookies, and WOW...At first I didn't know what to expect, I figured I'd eat a cookie or two, and move on (and let someone else eat the cookies).Sadly... that wasn't the case!I ate one cookie, (OMG) the taste was extravagant... creamy, tasty, smooth, and just so wonderful...Shortly after I realized I just finished off an entire row, panic set it (there were only 4-5 more rows left), I ate a few more (self control flies out the window when eating something oh so nice, especially when combined with a coffee)...Luckily I was saved, some friends were coming over and I was able to shove the box in their faces and they helped me out...I think the box lasted all of an hour, and it was all I could do to not run out and get more!These cookies are fantastic, once you start you won't stop.Bottom Line:  Fantastic cookie, great taste, nothing like an Oreo.Tip: Eat the cookie upside down, tastes much better (don't ask why!)Con:  50 some calories a cookie (I find this out AFTER finishing off the box!)  OH well, you live and you learn :P

column9: This is for the peanut butter creme, not golden variety...
column10: This might sound weird, but if these cookies were marketed without the Oreo name, they might taste better. Or, if they were called "Oreo Crisps," I wouldn't have been hoping for that classic Oreo taste.My first impression was that these are "weak-sauce Tagalongs" (Girl Scout cookies). They're thinner, and don't taste super peanut buttery. The package clearly says "Peanut Butter" with "Creme" in small letters next to it, so I've theorized that the "creme" part means it's the familiar Oreo creme that has *some* peanut butter flavor added.The cookie texture is nice. Very crisp and tasty. It's just when everything is put together that it's kind of disappointing. I have hope for the original flavor, Oreo Fudge Cremes, 8.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4), but have yet to try them.That said, I do keep eating them. They kind of grow on you, so that's why I think my expectation of what a regular Oreo is gave me a bad first impression. I don't think, though, that I'd put one in my shopping cart if I came across it again.

We ordered and received a containter of the peanut butter Oreo Creme cookies, and my family all enjoyed the treats.  The cookies are much better than the similar kind that the GScouts of America make, and there are more in the container.  We will definitely buy these cookies again!

column9: Where is the peanut butter or the fudginess?
column10: We're  giving this item a 3 for several reasons.  First, while it is desribed as "Peanut Butter Creme," we could not taste any hint of peanut  butter in the chocolate covered wafer.  Secondly,it is described as "Fudge Cremes", sorry, the wafer is covered in  chocolate but  it is  simply that - not fudge.  We  thought the packaging was an excellent idea because all you have to do is pull a tab and then the tray of cookies is revealed.  Problem was that although it was not shipped in warm weather a good  bit of the chocolate coating came off on the aluminum foil when it was lifted.  The manufacturer did an excellent job in designing this package as the cookies are on a tray separated by plastic  bars.  Problem is if the package is turned upside down then the chocolate comes off on the cover.  We  would not recommend these for youngsters as the chocolate immediately  comes off on fingers. So, serve them outdoors unless you want sticky brown fingers around the house.  Since the taste is relatively mild they  might be nice served with ice cream or sherbert for dessert.  However, they simply don't have the  distinctive taste of the  original Oreo cookie and shipping them is certainly  problematic.  Sorry we could not have been more [positive because we truly love to eat!  - Gail Cooke

column9: Tasty cookies, one star off for outrageous price
column10: These were nice cookies. Peanut buttery, chocolatey, rich, with a little crunch. The filling was a little too glue-textured but other than that, very decent. The price they are being offered for on Amazon is nuts, though. Is this a savings off of the grocery shelf? If it is, then just barely.

column9: Oh. My. Goodness!  HEAVEN in a Cookie!
column10: I've been an Oreo fan when Oreo was just one kind of cookie.  And while I've tried the different varities created over the years, I never found one that could top that original.Until now.Oh my goodness!  Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crème has to be the best cookie I've ever eating!This Oreo is a wafer topped with a layer of a rich, creamy peanut butter then both are wrapped in the sweetest tasting fudge to ever touch your tastebuds.Not only have I found something to match the orignal Oreo, but Oreo Peanut Butter Fudge Crème actually BEATS it!  I now have a new cookie addiction - YUMMY!

Got these fast from amazon, opened them up... and 10 minutes later, they were all gone. Ok, I handed them out to some people, so I did not eat them all.Out of the 10 or so people who ate them, 8 said they enjoyed them (came back for seconds). The other two were not impressed.Overall, I thought they were great, and will buy again.

In the cookie flavor category there is none greater. I wasn't expecting anything special when I opened the pack using the special pull out flap across the front giving you access to only a few, or the whole tray. The I popped the first one in my mouth, took a bite and wow it hit me. The crunchy thin somewhat resembling a thin mint but of course a little thicker had a burst of flavor that I would have to say is a cross between peanut butter, coffee and chocolate. I am sure all three ingredients are in there. They really scored 1000 on this one. I couldn't stop eating them. I have about six of them, even though I am on a diet. I just had a big bowl of fruit with pineapple, apples, blueberries, and honeydew melon. Well after about 5 minutes I got a stomach ache. I guess a stomach full of fresh fruit, and a fudge covered peanut butter cookie is not a good mix. Since I was on a diet, I gave the rest of the box to my brother, who ate the whole box in about one day. He gained a pound, but didn't have any stomach problems, so the fruit mix with these must not be a good idea.They have a nice crunch, a good amount of fudge flavor, are thin enough to make you not feel bad about eating a half dozen. You are going to have a hard time finding a cookie that beats these guys in the flavor department. My hat is off to Oreo, I think they just created the next Oreo with these things.

The cookies are really good. They are crispy and not overwhelmingly peanut buttery. It has just a slight taste and it is very creamy. The best way to describe these is that they are like a chocolate covered nutter butter but round and thin with a crisp. It has very little oreo taste. I am not that big of a fan of oreos. I like the golden oreos but these have a thin chocolate oreo cookie that is not too much to have. They do seem like some girl scout cookies but many products are similar anyway. If you like peanut butter you will really like these.

As a person who loves both chocolate and peanut btter, any product that contains both will have my approval. Thus, this new Oreo cookie is just right for me. It's delcious, but I would wish that there were more peanut butter in it; it's rather thin. Other than that, I think you will enjoy this product very much!

column9: Indulge on Peanut Butter & Fudge with a crispy oreo cookie crunch
column10: Review for the Peanut Butter Creme Oreo Fudge Cremes:Picture one of the tops of an Oreo cookie thinned down half its size to form a wafer, then put creamy peanut butter on top, followed by submerging the whole thing in a choclate fudge coating. Still half the thickness of a oreo regular cookie, but packs a bigger and satisifying taste. Flat on the bottom and round on top these cookies are simiply delicious and guarenteed to be a crowd pleaser! Each 11.5 ounce box contains twenty eight cookies. Can't wait to try their other flavors!

I tried out the peanut butter creme version of these.  My first impression was that the fudge coating looker rather soft and would be messy if left out on a warm day.  On tasting, the overwhelming sweetness was predominant. Aside from the sweetness the flavor is more Butterfinger than Reeses.  The slight crunchiness of the cookie portion also made it texturally similar to a Butterfinger.  The chocolate flavor isn't that present and is drowned out by all the sugar. The "fudge" coating seems to be more chocolate flavored than actual chocolate.The excess sweetness of these cookies makes it hard to eat more than one, which is a good thing considering the nutritional information.  Overall, these cookies are much too sweet with a taste more like a candy bar.

Oh my goodness, these are phenomenal.  They taste like a combination of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups with the texture of Girl Scout Cookie Thin Mints.  They are melt-in-your mouth delicious.  In my tasting-party of seven people, we all gave them a huge thumbs up.

I admit it.  I just love snack foods.  And amongst my favorite snacks to eat are cookies.  I can't think of a year that I haven't ordered Girl Scout cookies and Oreos are amongst my favorite cookies (especially double stuff Oreos).So I was excited to have the opportunity to try the new "Peanut Butter Creme Oreo Fudge Cremes".  While I think that they could shorten the name of these cookies a bit, the bottom line is that they are yummy.The only description on the bag is "fudge covered chocolate cookies" so they could probably expand on that a bit.  But basically, it tastes like a single cookie wafer with peanut butter creme stuck to the side and then the whole thing covered in a soft fudge.The bag I received was 11.3 ounces, which is a generous size.  It is also resealable, so not only is it very easy to get at the cookies without a knife, scissors or your teeth, but it's also easy to reseal the bag and keep the cookies fresh.  Of course they probably won't be around long anyway, because you're going to gobble them up.  At least, that's what I expect to do.I really like these cookies.  If this was a Girl Scout cookie, I'm sure they'd sell very well.  I definitely do recommend them.  Just try not to eat the whole bag at once!
These taste great if you like chochlate and peanut butter :) and my husband loves them I thinkk I got to eat one out of the package and he has eaten all of the rest and wants more :)

column9: Continuing with the Girl Scout Cookie Theme, Mint are Better
column10: So a few months ago, I tried the Mint Oreo Fudge Cremes and they were fabulous. I even sought them out at my local grocery store--where they are on sale this week! Less than you can find them on Amazon, which is nice.The Mint Oreo Fudge Cremes taste a lot like Girl Scout Thin Mints.  In keeping with the Girl Scout theme, these taste a bit like the Tagalongs.. only thinner.  Honestly, I didn't like them as much as the Mint Oreo Fudge Cremes.  The peanut butter is overpowering, and I barely tasted any chocolate.  I think this would work better as a traditional Oreo sandwich cookie (chocolate cookie top and bottom) then covered in fudge.  Instead, one has a very thin wafer (thinner than a typical Oreo top or bottom), with a disc of peanut butter, covered by a chocolate shell.If in a store, I had a choice between "regular" Oreos and the Mint Oreo Fudge Cremes, I'd buy the Mint Oreo Fudge Cremes quite often. (Although, you can't go wrong with the classic Oreos.)If in a store, I had a choice between "regular" Oreos and the Peanut Butter Oreo Fudge Cremes, I'd always buy the regular Oreos.... or the Mint Oreos.Miss for me on this one.  And I love peanut butter.  If you do like these or the other Fudge Cremes, be sure to check your local store's sale flyer.  They were under $3.00 where I live--which is a great deal.

column9: Super Yummy! Get 'em away from me!
column10: Okay, these are really great.  A favorite Girl Scout cookie of mine is very much like these, and they're only available once a year.  This is Nabisco's answer to the same product.  In fact, I might like Nabisco's product better.  It has slightly less peanut butter, which makes for a more balanced taste, in my opinion.The nutritional content being what it is, I would definitely make these a rare treat, as the 56 calories per cookie can add up.  A special dessert, not a daily snack for sure.One warning-- I wouldn't recommend ordering these online.  By the time these got to me on a warm spring day, they were a melted mess in the box.  All I did was pop them in the fridge to solidify and they were fine.  But they weren't very pretty and were all stuck to the plastic container.  I would recommend buying them from your local retailer instead.

When I want to eat an Oreo....I expect an Oreo..not a cookie that tastes like peanut butter.I haven't tried the mint which I could possibly like, but I'm reviewing the Peanut Butter ones at the moment.My teenager says they should get 4 stars since she is eating one as I type this..and she hates peanut butter, but I think they should give them a different name....An Oreo should just be an oreo....an oreo is two disk-shaped cookies with white creamy filling sandwiched in between, hence it's called a sandwich cookie.  This is one cookie with a peanut butter topping dipped in chocolate, and it's a dark chocolate which is not my favorite.  The peanut-shaped cookies you can buy with the peanut butter filling are way better when I have a craving for a peanut butter type cookie.  When I crave an oreo, I want the original!

column9: Where Have You Been All My Life?
column10: These are fantastic. My wife and I and our kids just love these. i especially like the peanut butter in the middle--just a perfect blend of chocolate and peanut butter. Our family killed the package in a couple of days. Highly recommended.

In the mood for something extra, extra, extra sweet? You will enjoy this cookie then. Otherwise just buy when you have a big crowd. The first cookie isn't bad but all others after that just add up to an unpleasant eating experience.As far as taste is concerned, past the super sweetness, it does taste pretty good with plenty of chocolaty peanut butter flavor.But, wow, are they sweet! How did Nabisco pack so much sweet into such a small cookie?The cookie is about as thin as one side of the Oreo creme filled cookie. Kudos to Nabisco for actually covering the whole cookie with fudge and not just the front side. There is a thin layer of some sort of peanut butter creme on the top side of the cookie under the fudge coating. The PB seems to be where most of the awful sweetness is coming from.I'm not someone that reads every nutrition label for everything I buy and usually I just take it as a given that a treat like a cookie is not super healthy. But these little jewels are so sweet it will make you wonder exactly what you are eating.Dang. 3 cookies is 9g of fat and 170 calories (80 fat). Contrast that with the traditional Oreo: 15 cookies for 160 (60 fat) and 7g fat.I think it is worth mentioning since I couldn't find any nutritional information on the product page.I'm not a fan of the eat healthy band wagon but good Lord. Surely a warning label should be required on something that looks so innocuous. Maybe the outline of a hugely obese person and a fat playful exclamation mark.Let me also point out that if you buy this from Amazon you need to have someone available to get the package as soon as it arrives if it is moderately warm in your area when you purchase them. My shipping package was left out in the sun a while and some of the cookies that had come out of their slots were somewhat melted and stuck together. Nabisco did a great job with the tray they ride in but shipping may unseat them and then the heat will glue them together. I threw mine in the freezer for a bit to solidify the fudge before I opened them.Oh. I have to say that I like the resealable package. I guess I haven't bought that type of package before or if I have all the cookies were gone before they could be resealed. It works very well and is much easier than the usual zip lock type resealable package.1 star for an excessively sweet taste in an excessively sweet cookie that could be a poster child for bad industry.
These crispy toasties are great in the morning or anytime.  Although, there were none of the familiar toppings I grew up with in Holland, it's still great with strawberry jam.

column9: Perfect for salting the rim of your bloody Mary glass
column10: My wife and I wanted to find something to salt the rim of a bloody Mary.  This seasoned course salt is perfect!  The spices mixed with the salt are just what a bloody Mary needs.  The product comes in a resealable plastic pouch inside a nice metal can.  I keep the contents in the plastic container and only pour out the amount we intend to use.  We put this on a small plate so the remaining salt stays dry and fresh.  (We rarely drink, so we want the salt to stay fresh for a long time.)  When we make our bloody Mary, we put a little lemon juice around the rim of the glass and then turn the glass over and place it on the plate with the salt.  This will pick up just the right amount of salt for the rim.Everyone who has had one of our bloody Marys made with this rim salt loved it.  I highly recommend this product.

If you care to enjoy a premium rum then is is one you simply must experience. I prefer it neat. It can be complemented by a good Dominican cigar or if in mixed company with good quality dark chocolate.

column9: Excellent rum, one of the finest in the Caribbean

I have never had any problems like that with other grinders.  So I hope the company reads  comments and come up with a label that will withhold the use.  As of now, when I refill the jar I need to somehow mark it with what type of salt it is.  (NOTE: all other information regarding what the contents are etc. are gone.)

column9: The freshest dried tarragon I could find anywhere

I don't know if they are good or not. What a disappointment. Shouldn't perishables be shipped another way? I won't order these chocolates again till maybe November.

Yet the product description tells nothing whatsoever about the age of this cheese!I absolutely would not consider buying this product without that information as to me Manchego that's been aged only 3 months is not even worthy of the same name as that aged 8 or 12 months.
This is a very good gluten free pasta, you need to cook with it a couple of times to get your cooking method right but it is worth the learning curve.  Use plenty of water to cook it.
We use this for baked penne, and it is fantastic! We are so excited to be able to have a lot of our favorite Italian dishes again without sacrificing taste.

My grandson is celiac and when he came to visit for summer, we needed to have a whole selection of GF foods for him. He loved this pasta and always asked for seconds. We reserved it for his use but if there's any left when he goes home, I will eat it.  It's delicious!

I enjoy this brand and type of gluten free pasta.  It holds shape well and texture is nice.  I feel that it goes well with a variety of sauces: white, red, or pink.  It is not my favorite to have "plain", that is to say with just butter and Parmesan cheese.  For that type of meal I prefer the brown rice pastas over the corn.  All in all I do enjoy and recommend this pasta as a great gluten free option to add variety to your meals!

I am a goof ball, I was so happy to find a gluten free pasta with all positive reviews, and was so fast in buying the pack, so I didn't notice it was made of corn! I dislike corn with all my heart, besides, I am slightly allergic to it. I have tried it though to try to make it up for stupidly buying something I should have not. And it tastes bad - I mean, it has NO taste whatsoever. I thought I would have a gluten-free alternative to a nice taste of pasta, instead I have got the corn horror with no gratification to my pasta cravings. I am very, very sad, but it's my fault: I should read "labels" better. I would have returned, it, but it's way to heavy to pay for shipping. Sadly Sad.
I love the taste of corn pasta over other gluten free pastas I've tried in the past.  Sam Mills is a low cost and tasty brand.  I will be purchasing more!

I had this pasta for this first time this week and it was phenomenal!  I've tried other brands before and was never impressed and would just throw it out but with this pasta I had seconds! I only purchased 1 bag from the grocery store and this brand was very inexpensive compared to other brands. I believe it cost about $2.35 a bag. I will definitely purchase this brand again and I am excited to make baked penne with it. Make sure to cook it al dente too!

column9: Couldn't be more satisfied with this pasta!
column10: Bought this for my girl friend who has celiacs. Not only is the pasta extremely cheaper then anything you can find in stores, it's actually her favorite GF pasta to date. I would highly recommend this pasta.

Quite honestly I ordered a case of this pasta because we are on a tight budget and it was the cheapest. We have been gluten free for about 2 years. This pasta is actually very good and I plan to continue to purchase it!! Very tasty!

I recently order the 72 count hearts from Penguin Mints.  Upon receiving my order I discovered there was only a 36 pack in the box.  After contacting the company after hours, I received a phone call and email the next business day.  They explained the error and quickly corrected the mistake.  Everyone involved was professional and followed thru on everything that was stated.  The customer service is outstanding- and although I had a glitch with my order - I would highly recommend ordering any of their products.Karen H.
Great BBQ sauce with a hint of sweetness and some smoky flavor. Not to smoky though. You can taste some of the bourbon as well. I have only used it for pork but I'm sure it's good on everything.

I ordered this grain because I am following the Ultra Metabolism 21 day detox phase...ok, stop the eye rolling. It's basically about removing potential allergens (diary, etc.) and cleansing yourself from processed foods -any sugar, hydrogenated oils, white flour...and although I dont eat that stuff in general, it's amazing how many "all natural" foods have high fructose corn syrup (many Marie's dressings, etc.)Anywho- my amaranth arrived quickly but one bag had burst open - the packaging was a joke! Amazon shrinkwraps books so they sre sealed air-tight, yet bags of grain soar freely in their big Amazon box, begging to explode.The other bags remained in tact - the stench from the grain takes getting used to. It smells swampy to me, but my sister says that's just "earthy."It's a complete grain and it cooks up nicely as a hot cereal - and it pops like popcorn, too.

I make a wonderful hot breakfast cereal with amaranth, a chopped apple, milk, cinnamon and a little stevia. Just remember that if you want salt in your recipe, don't add it until the amaranth is done cooking. Salt inhibits the grains from softening.
This little grain is a complete protein, quick toprepare and delicious to eat!  It can be combinedwith veggies and olive oil or eaten like the usualhot cereal with honey and cinnamon.

column9: product is fine- packaging is problematic
column10: Amaranth is a good grain for my celiac daughter to eat- but one of the four packages arrived torn and the grain spilt in the mailing box. I recommend better packaging. Otherwise, no complaints

These have such delicious flavor, it is really like a really gooey peanut butter and jelly sandwich, with about a third of the calories (two tbsp of peanut butter is usually around 190). One bar is 110 calories, 30 from fat, 95mg of sodium, 5g fiber, 7g sugar, and 2g of protein, with 10% daily value of calcium as well. Great for taming mid-morning hunger pangs or post-workout.
It doesn't taste right, not sure if it's from sitting and the spices get bland over time or if it would still taste like that right off the factory line.

column9: Buckeye beans country split pea soup.
column10: An excellent product; locally made and sold.  I'll be returning again and again to make sure I have some in my pantry.

In about a 3-4 quart saucepan, I lightly sauteed, in butter, a large diced onion, diced carrots and celery. I then added the split peas, the entire seasoning packet and the amount of water the recipe called for...threw in a couple of bay leaves for good measure... and cooked, covered on low, according to the instructions printed on the box. After simmering for about 30-minutes, I added a couple of fistfuls of cubed ham that was left over from our Christmas dinner. This is the best split pea soup I have ever eaten. My husband has always claimed he does not like split pea soup so he was more surprised than anyone to discover how much he really likes THIS split pea soup. I plan to stock up on more of this soup and some other varieties from Buckeye Beans & Herbs. Since I can make soup this good with practically no effort, I cannot wait to taste Buckeye's other soup packet mixtures.
Thanks for providing a source for a childhood memory!  Bought this a a surprise for a friend who had a longing for this pudding from her childhood but couldn't locate a local source for it.
Excellent light tasting tea and it's cool how the little balls unroll after steeping.  Package says it can be used for 3 steepings but I find it's at it's best the 1st steeping.

This is my favorite tea to use for making iced tea, but it is also very good consumed hot.Its taste is very mild, but the jasmine flavor is prominent.  It is not earthy at all, which for my mouth is a very happy thing as I find earthy teas to be quite reminiscent of brewed dirt.If you like mild teas, you'll love this one, but if you tend to prefer stronger tasting teas, I wouldn't recommend it.  I brew it double strength for iced tea (two teaspoons per 8 ounces instead of one) which makes a great flavor, but I have tried to make it stronger and using more tea really doesn't add more flavor.
This is my second purchase. Good tea, smooth taste if your brewing does not exceed more than 4 mins. Overall I am happy with this product

I give this stuff out at work so much that I never seem to have any for myself.  It has a sweet, pleasant taste and makes sore throats feel so much better. If you look at the ingredients, you'll see that it contains licorice. I hate licorice, but I can't taste it at all in this tea.

My throat was killing me today, and on and off this week.  I decided to make myself some tea despite the heat and sort through my old tea collection to cull some teas that the food pantry can use up better than I can.The Yogi cold sampler nearly went straight into the food bank box until I saw "Throat Comfort."  I scanned the ingredients and liked what I saw:  all recognizable and nothing that I'm aware of being an allergy risk for me.  (eg, no lemon grass . . . though companies can change their ingredients, so check the label on your box!)The relief was immediate.  I made a little surprised, happy noise at the first sip.  The pain relief doesn't last long between sips, but oh my, this feels good on a sore throat!This tea has an almost artificially sweet aftertaste to me, though there are no ingredients I recognize as sweeteners on the box.  It's probably the organic fennel seeds and organic licorice root, which are the top two ingredients.  I have strongly mixed feelings about licorice and will skip black jellybeans, but I always liked fennel.  This tea is delicious, and maybe a little too sweet or anise-y to take seriously as a regular daily tea, but for a sore throat it's heaven.I wonder which ingredients get the job done, as I have to confess I'm now a full believer in the product.  I drink green tea almost every day at work, and it's wonderful stuff but didn't help my throat like this did.

column9: I wouldn't go through a winter without it
column10: This tea is the BEST for alleviating cold symptoms and soothing a sore throat. I ordered this case for my sister and have previously given boxes of this tea to various friends and coworkers. Everybody raves about it!

This coffee isnt available any longer but it was  my absolute favorite flavor and I dearly miss it!!!!Van Houtte no longer has a United States office so we can no longer order all of thier flavors unless Keurig carries them !!

This has been a "tried and true" favorite.  I can count on this flavor!  I may go off on a taste testing spree to find "others" that I might like, but I know that I can always come back to Vanilla Cupcake and it won't disappoint!  I will add a packet of Splenda and a dash of cream to make a delicious "dessert".  It satisfies my craving for something sweet and I don't have to feel guilty about it!

I am not a very big coffee drinker, but do like to have a cup every once in awhile. I definitely don't like a bold, strong coffee. I like a very faint coffee taste. So I figured I would try this brand and flavor to start. I really like it. It has such a nice, rich, warm vanilla taste to it. Depending upon how much milk and sweetener you put in it, it could almost be like a vanilla latte. I am glad I tried it out, it has a great taste.

column9: One squirt is all it took
column10: I had never tried this product before nor heard of it until I came across a vegan recipe I wanted to make.  Incredibly, low sodium soy sauce has an astonishing 575 mg. per tbsp.  Bragg's Liquid Aminos only has 160 mg. per 1/2 tsp.  One squirt adds a lot of flavor.  The first time my husband and I tasted it, we were impressed.  It is better than soy sauce.  Has an all natural mild taste loaded with flavor, but not too salty.  Would be excellent on vegetables, soup or  rice.  Liquid Aminos also contains 16 essential and non-essential amino acids.  I had a hard time finding this product in a regular grocery store.  There are no health food stores near, so I was delighted Amazon carried it.  I will never go back to soy sauce.

A worthy alternative to soy/tamari. I've used this stuff for years as a base for a spirulina/cayenne breakfast drink, and I'm still buying it. As a condiment, the spray head makes even application and portion control a reality.

When I purchase this I thought it would probably taste like water downed soy sauce but it didn't. It tastes exactly like soy sauce but better for you. I love that it is in a spray bottle. It is perfect for sauteing veggies.

If you have to watch your sodium, this is the product for you. It seasons your food with a nice umami seasoning, sort of like pot roast, just a nice hearty "beefy" flavor that is kind of hard to describe but you know it when you taste it. It is especially good if you are transitioning to a vegetarian diet and learning to get along without meat. This will help you feel like you aren't missing a thing. Add it to soups and casseroles, put it in stir fry, season the water that you cook rice or quinoa in. There are so many things you can use it for. Best of all if you have to watch your sodium for health reasons, this product will season your food without adding sodium the way soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce does.

I think that this is a great, healthy low cal staple to keep around.  You can use it on meats or veggies.  I personally wasn't into it as a salad dressing, but that is just me.  Others may feel differently.  I want to try the Bragg's dry Seasoning next for the salad.

I use this product in bulk when stir frying and got this to take with me and spray it on food when I eat out.  I like to cook my own stuff, but it feels ok to eat out when I am not using products that have too much fat and salt.  Love it.

column9: not so much a spray as a stream
column10: The liquid spilled in transit so the label and bottle were all sticky.  Also, I was hoping this would be a spray, but it is more of a stream or squirt.

I'm a recent convert to Bahlsen cookies, and these little wafers are a standout among a product line that's hard not to love.  The crisp. toasty, slightly nuttly wafers surround a very light, not-too-sweet creme layer; the combination is an incredible, multi-dimensional treat that would pair nicely with coffee or milk.  The only thing I would think that would make this product better is a resealable package, but the wafers aren't going to last long once opened anyway.  The package size is good in the sense that it's enough to share with one or two other people, but if you eat the whole thing yourself it's not an utter disaster ;)

These crackers are a great way to get whole wheat into your diet & into children's.  They are low in fat & sugar, and they taste great.  I haven't met a child yet who doesn't like them.  The ingredients are good as well.

1.  I love  Amazon's grocery/makeup/cleaning products subscription service.  It is only beta now, but I truly hope they will continue it.2.  This cookie is amazingly delicious.  I like sweets that aren't too sweet, with just the right hint of sugar.  These are cookies just like that.  Like Creme Brulee -- barely sweetened, but if it is done right, the sweetness makes it the best food in the world.  I'm not saying these cookies are Creme Brulee, but maybe they approach the creme brulee of cookies.
The Bahlsen Delobas are my favorite so far. Call them biscuits or call them cookies they are just plain good. Light and pastry like with a nice burst of sweetness from the red current jam. Try Them!

I had these cookies in Germany, but I had a hard time finding them in the US.  I was amused to discover I could order them from Amazon.  They seem to be most closely related to pecan sandies, but they're a little richer and a little moister.  I wish it were possible to order a single box instead of 12, but I already knew I liked them, so ordering 12 wasn't really a problem.  A bigger problem is trying not to eat them all immediately.
Great texture and balance of sweet to butter is just about right. Adults and kids both love them. Recommended

The title says it all! These butter biscuits are DIVINE! Everyone loves them--my parents, my students, my colleagues, and, of course, me! You will love them, too!

These cookies are fabulous. Flaky, not too sweet, fluffy not gooey layers. Small but not too small. Suggested serving size of 6 is good. Lots of things these days have completely unrealistic serving sizes. I know they have sat fat but I really don't care. I have been unable to find anything like them. They remind me of REAL bakery cookies.

These are every bit as good as the other two reviewers stated. Awesome butter cookies!!! There's a lot of butter taste in these cookies and they're not overly sweet. Just right! I'll be buying again when the 12 pack runs out. Amazon please make sure you keep these in stock on a continuing basis!

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column10: These Bahlsen Butter Leaves are the best cookies! Not too sweet, not greasy, soooo "just right!" Order extra! They go fast!
I love this chocolate covered cookies. The chocolate is pure and tasty. Not too sweet.

These cookies didn't disappoint.  They are delicious and go really well with a cup of tea or coffee.  They have just the right amount of sweetness...not cloying.  (I think American desserts usually go overboard on sugar).  I highly recommend them.
Love these tea biscuits. The price was great for a box of 12. I hope you continue to carry.

i tried bahlsen chocolates in europe, but you can't find them very often in the states. these are unlike any usa chocolates i've eaten, the wafer is wrapped over itself 4-5 times. you can't beat the crunch these make, delicious.

Many of Bahlsen's cookies are too sweet and floury for my taste, but these light flaky cookies don't taste stale and are not too rich but are nice and do not taste like sugared cardboard.  I don't crave these but when you eat them, you realize that these are better than the average boxed cookies and unexpectedly delicate and fresh tasting given the supermarket price.

The title says it.  Some of the cookies arrived with the chocolate melted.  Others were stuck together or had the wafer separated and stuck to the chocolate top of the cookie below.  It appears that the box was a little overheated and banged around somewhere along the way here.  It was 65F here when the package was delivered.

Having grown up on these cookies I was pleased to see that they now come in the more healthful whole wheat version.  Same great taste...light on the sugar...even my husband who hates sweets will eat these with his ice cream.

Rich, dark chocolate thinly covering a tart orange marmalade-like substance on a soft sponge cookie. It melts in your mouth and leaves you wanting more. Chocolate and orange are an addictive combination.  There are other brands out there of these sponge cookies, but the Bahlsen brand is by far tops in the quality of the ingredients used.

Have always enjoyed Balsen products. Found  the nuss-dessert cookies while on vacation at Sanibel Island Florida. We were really excited to find them on Amazon, we had searched through out the Chicago area since last April.They are the best. Taste like fresh hazelnuts and are great with either coffee or tea. (or later with wine).So good that I bought a case, but they are reserved for special moments(like now).

This is without a doubt the most incredibly addictive packaged cookie in the world. The dark chocolate dipping at one end is a great contrast to the rolled wafer of the cookie itself. Why did I ever buy a whole case! Bless Amazon for carrying the Bahlsen line of fabulous cookies because it is not available in Montana.

If you are looking for a sweet, try this cookie.  It is extra lightand has a nice crunch to it.  I buy these cookies by the carton.They last for one month between my husband and I.  He likes cookieswith his morning coffee.  We are both satisfied with these cookies.Would buy them again and again.Mary
These are soo good with a nice cup of coffee. They are light, buttery and very flavorful with the finely chopped nuts.
better than grahm crakers and they do not spike your blood sugar (at least not mine.)

Once you try this piece of chocolate you will fall in love with it. Probably one of the best nonbar chocolates produced in Switzerland and Europe as a whole. And I think it is rather cheap for the quality you get.
We've ordered for them every month and only once the package inside the seal had a small hole and wasn't as fresh.

The first time had these cookies was when I visited NYC.  One box of these cost me around $7, so when I found these on amazon.com for about $1.40 per box, I was so exstatic!  I could eat an entire box without feeling full of sugar or guilt.  Perfect with tea as I am not a coffee fan.  There are several reviews that I have read that were complaining about the number of boxes they received (12)- it says right in the product title how many boxes come in the order! I am appaled by some people's idiocy until I remind myself that I live in the United States.  Besides, why would anyone complain at $1.40 per box?  I HIGHLY recommend these to anyone, I would give 10 stars if I could.  Oh, and be glad they come in shipments of 12 boxes, they will be gone before you know it!  Thank you, Amazon!

My husband and I have been buying these cookies locally for years because we love them so much; they are far better than the milk chocolate version (but then, we love DARK chocolate!). In the past couple of years, our local grocer has stopped carrying them, we would request them, they would get them for a few months, and then they would stop carrying them again. I am so glad to see that I can get them via amazon.com! These are wonderful cookies with warm milk, cold milk, or a little Scotch . . . mmmmmmm!
This product was delivered on time and included more than I thought I was going to get - a full 16 packages. I first purchased these in England and have loved them ever sense.

I grew up eating these cookies.  Got a case for a great price.  Will be looking for them again this fall.

Leibniz cookies are truly my favorite, beyond what I make, I am a passionate cook. The whole wheat version of these are particularly superb with a subtly greater flavor than the original and a lovely, slightly more crumbly and grainy texture. It has been a wonderful discovery. Bon appetit.

column9: Great cookies--don't buy in the summer
column10: These are positively the most delicious cookies ever--smooth milk chocolate covering meringue biscuits.  However, when we received them--albeit in the Texas summer--they were fused together in the packaging. They are now not only less attractive, but also hard to eat.  So I would not recommend ordering these in the summer with the way they are packaged by Amazon.
It tastes perfect. I like it.You would "feel" the butter in the cookies.
Great cookies.  Not overly sweet as most American cookies can be, with a hint of citrus.  Could not ask for more.  There is only 12 or so cookies in the box, but a decadent treat.

column9: YUM- like a perfect Rice Crispy
column10: If Rice Crispy bars were made with good chocolate, and didn't taste like wax, they might taste like this.  Wow- What a yummy treat.  These are coated with a LOT of chocolate, and for me are more like a candy than a cookie (and I don't have a problem with that!)  I would not have wanted to order them in the summer, because I feel sure they would have melted.  The chocolate taste is wonderful, and I love the crunchiness.  The Sell By date is not until 9/2010 a full 8 months from today (1/21/2010), so I'm pleased with their freshness.  I don't think they will last very long in our house, but still, it's nice they are fresh.  These are packed very well, so they should not arrive crumbled or damaged in any way.  My cookies are perfect.  If you like crunchy chocolate treats this is for you!  Delicious!

column9: Great- and good Sell By date
column10: I'll start with something really important to me- the sell by date.  I bought these cookies in January of 2010, and they are good until 9-2010, which is important to me, since I hate eating rancid food, so I just throw it out.  I've always loved these cookies, and my market sells them for much more than the subscribe price, so I'm happy to subscribe and save.  I love currants, and it's hard to find things flavored with them.  I have to admit, the currant taste is not strong, but they are delicious anyway, and I love the puff pastry.  Further, I'm allergic to GMO corn starch (genetically modified corn starch)- and just try to find cookies in US stores without corn starch (and 95% of all corn is modified in the US, and does not have to be labeled so).  So these are a real treat for me- since they are a cookie I can actually eat.The cookies are flaky, as puff pastry always is, and slightly sweet.  As other people have said, this is not a terribly sweet cookie, but it is quite sweet enough.  I enjoy mine with tea, and I also take them in my lunch.  If you take them in your lunch, put them in a little box- because they ARE delicate, and you might end up with delicious crumbs if you don't protect them.  I know this because I squashed them once.

This very crispy sugar wafer is perfect with ice cream, or with coffee or tea.  It's got a lovely burnt marshmallow flavor.  I really like these- they seem to harmonize with anything.  I'm allergic to GMo cornstarch, so it is hard for me to find cookies I can eat.  This one is lovely, and it's safe for me to eat.

These have a delicate, nutty, warm, faintly sweet wheat flavor, and a pleasing texture.  Satisfying without guilt, they're truly addictive.  I prefer them to digestives (much less Graham crackers), and even Leibniz's standard butter biscuits don't come close.  The whole wheat is especially good with green and pouchong teas - though predictably satisfying paired with a cup of Assam or English Breakfast. Also great with cocoa or milk, cheese or apples.... a slather of peanut butter..... !They're one of the few biscuits I'd definitely offer to children.
these cookies are a perfect treat....very light and crunchy wafer sweetened by  the right amount of chocolate....great price and fast service

If you've had these cookies already - no one needs to sell them to you. I would just recommend that you keep them in the freezer. That way they're sort of hidden from you (and others) but for some reason freezing them brings out the taste and consistency of the chocolate. Try it!

column9: Bahlsen Dark Chocolate Cookies -  A Treat
column10: I don't know what Bahlsen was thinking over the last several months, but I looked high and low for these cookies in supermarkets and specialty stores...none were to be found. Then, after checking with Amazon (and its tracking mechanisms), Voila! I ordered a whole case and that should satisfy our deep appreciation of these cookies... a perfect blend of high quality dark chocolate and a crisp, thin "chocolate vehicle"--i.e., cookie.

These are great!  And they can get to be habit forming if you are not careful.  I bought the whole case, because you save overall  versus going to the supermarket.  Very rich dark chocolate, crisp cookie.  Worth every penny.  Oreo, eat your heart out!

These cookies are just wonderful!!! The chocolate is deep, dark, rich and melts very nicely in your mouth.  I would say that it is a bittersweet chocolate and very finely made. These cookies give the chocolate lover a satisfying chocolate experience. Do not hesitate to buy them!

These appear to be, on first glance, similar to Nutter Butters.  On taste, however, they are lighter, more delicate, and infused with hazelnut.  There is more air in the cookie, so when you dip it in coffee, it becomes saturated rather quickly and the cookie folds into your mouth, with the sweet center taking center stage.  Nuff said.

I am very happy with Amazon service including the speedy shipment. I am also very happy the product Amazon is carrying. This product is only available in selected specialty stores in the area. And tend to be expensive. Sometime they only carry small selection in store. You have to wait long time for a special order. Amazon is making the product available with a wide selection of variaty and affortable. Thanks.

A light and crisp flaky cookie surrounding a brightly flavorful nugget of jam. The only problem - I can eat a whole box without stopping to breathe! And buying them by the case makes them very affordable. My next order is already in...

I first had these cookies at our Oktoberfest where they were giving out samples.  I loved them and could not find them at World Market so I went to the internet and found them available at Amazon. They are very light and flaky.
When we couldn't find these in our local grocery store anymore, we were very glad to find them available through Amazon. these are light and delicious and a true treat!

However, since they follow the  European trend of using  natural ingredients, they are full of saturated fat from butter and cream.WHO CARES?They are the best cookies, for me, in the world, comparable only to"Feullitees Doree," which can be bought on in France.

I have not opened all of the boxes yet of course, but will hope to find a couple that are not all broken up to give to my dad.

I really like these cookies.  They are made with pastry dough - lots of thin, flaky, crispy layers with a very light coating of honey (or something like honey).  The jelly center rounds the cookie out with a delicious bite of sweetness. It's a robust burst of flavor that makes you want to smile. I am rapidly getting addicted to these fine flavorful confections -- bet you can't eat just one!

I am an adventurous person who likes new things and when Amazon began selling the Bahlsen line I tried a number of their products and found them to be enjoyable and tasty, but the Hannover Wafer Cookies are, to my palate, rather bland and tasteless. The texture is pleasing, though a little grainy tasting and the creme filling has little flavor. They're very high in saturated fat, and  devoid of flavor..Think I'll stick with the Bahlsen Delobas'.

column10: Delicate ground hazelnut cookies for a Ladies tea, NOT for children or most men! Appreciated only by sophisticated palates, because they are neither cloyingly sweet or fatty. Set these aside for unexpected guests you'd like to impress.

These crackers are no longer available at my local grocery store.  They are so good that they are worth ordering a case.  Only 3-1/2 grams net carbs per cracker.

column9: Contains Partially Hydrogenated Soybean Oil - Check the label!
column10: Was shopping for some crackers to use as snacks with my diet.  Saw the "Saturated Fat Free" rather than the "fat free" printing on the front of the box.  Checked the ingredients.  This contains Partially Hydrogenated Soybean Oil.  Makes me not trust Ry-Krisp.

column9: Another great Dorset product, with tons of raisins and a berry twang
column10: I am on the record elsewhere saying that Dorset Cereals are the best mueslis in the world, and I'll stand by that. For my personal taste, however, the nuttier mueslis outpace the fruit-packed ones -- such as this one.This muesli has a strong fruit taste, but despite the "berries and cherries" name, the fruits are mainly raisins and related types like sultanas. Berries, blackcurrants and dried cherries provide a distinctive and tangy flavor that outweighs their relatively small volume in the overall product mix. Still, I docked a star from the review because I feel the name is a bit misleading. Berries and cherries actually account only for a very small percentage of the fruit mix.Despite my nitpicking, however, this muesli -- with its walloping 50% ratio of fruits, nuts and seeds -- still stands head and shoulders above most other types, except the nuttier Dorset brands. If you prefer a fruity to a nutty muesli, jump all over this one, it's made for you.
Excellent muesli. My two-year-old loves fruit, so this cereal (50% fruit) is a real hit.

column9: Excellent cereal, if a little expensive.
column10: This cereal is one of the best available. In fact, all the Dorset Cereals are worth a try. From a nutritional point of view this is a well balanced breakfast that you can feel good about eating. My only gripes are: 1. There's almost too much fruit, making it sweeter than I'd like, and 2. It's still a little expensive compared to other breakfast cereals, although I realize that it's not necessarily fair to make such comparisons. A price of less than five dollars a box would be ideal. Highly recommended, buy with confidence.
couldn't find any whole wheat for bread makers in any of the grocery stores.  tried this wheat in our oster 5838 and our whole wheat bread came out perfect with a number of recipes.

If you order this "bread" flour, they ship flour labeled "Whole Wheat Flour."  That's a very different product from bread flour.  They say it's simply a labeling issue, and that it's all the same thing.  Anyone who bakes bread knows the difference.
My friend got this for making cookies for my dad since he is allergic to real flour. Cookies tasted amazing and you couldn't tell the difference. Item comes HIGHLY recommended. :)

We used to pick this product up retail but it seems all three stores we patron stopped selling it within the same week. I suspect collusion on their part... Anyways I was thrilled to find that Amazon not only offers the kit, but at a subscribe and save discount.Some have mentioned that you could piece this together yourself cheaper/better/healther, and that is a valid point, but one thing you cannot buy in a store (I've looked) is the old el paso somewhat spicy cheese sauce that you cover the top tortilla with. Without this sauce the kit is worthless, it's a great balance of spice and salty cheese and comes out so smooth when baked. I usually separate the bottom two and top two layers of my portion, I eat the bland-er bottom layers first (with frank red hot sauce) and save the top layers for last since this concentrates the cheese flavor even further.This is also a good dish to experiment with. Adding some black or pinto means to stuff the layers more, or whatever shredded cheese might be lying around the fridge, is a great way to increase it's yield and flavor. Between me and my girlfriend we split one of these for a meal, it's probably our entire sodium intake for the day in one meal (maybe 2x) but I can see how adding some sides like refried beans and rice would let us feed our family of 4 when the time comes. (Luckily the little ones are still at the formula/baby food stage, so we can hog it all)Overall, if you haven't tried it yet and as such aren't addicted to the cheese sauce, make it with your own ingredients, if your already hooked then this is likely the cheapest way to get your fix.P.S. I do have to mention that the S&S price did just jump up about $5 in one month (from 10.80 to 15.08) but at almost $3.xx a piece retail the price still comes out better from Amazon.

column9: Not what I expect from Old El Paso
column10: The quality of the kit over buying the contents separately is not great.The seasoning is the biggest sticking point. It's not the same as the normal individually store bought seasonings.It's lighter in color and pretty much tasteless. The cheese sauce is adequate, as is the soft shells.This is not an item I would purchase again.

The product is not yet available in stores in my area and I was thrilled when I found it on Amazon.  I used one of the packages to fix supper and the entire household liked it as much as I do.  Thanks, too, to the seller who sent it immediately.

this is a family favorite in our house.  we love it! i make it with ground turkey and then add beans as well.  we also always serve with a dollop of sour cream and black olives.  a great meal that you can build into a caserole or even serve just with meat and then put rice / beans on the side for anyone who likes it on the plain side.  excellent creation!
All I can say is YUM!! They stopped carrying this at the store that I shop at and I was so happy to see it on Amazon.com!

Of course, all the kits are great, but I think it is better to purchase the tortillas, the ground beef, seasoning pkt (we double the meat and seasoning)and shredded cheese instead of the cheese sauce.  I think the shredded is better in flavor as well as more traditional.  And sooo yummy.  Made this 2 wks ago and making it again tonite.  OPen a can of refried beans and some rice..wallaaa...great easy cheap!
These are one of my favorite flavors of tic tacs.  The flavor is a true sour cherry and quite intense.  You really get a lot of flavor out of one 2-calorie treat, which can satisfy for quite a while!
The cherry flavor is delicious. It's not something to give you fresh breath - go to the MINTS for that - but these are YUMMY. They're also hard to find.

quality ingredients,  brewed per instructedand is fermenting for 3rd week now @ 54 degrees. All is going well and I will transfer this week to secondary.
