This stuff is great.  It might be more expensive than the "cinnamon flavor" or "cinnamon extract" you get in the grocery store, but it is so much more concentrated that it works out to be cheaper in the long run.  I made cinnamon hard candy.  To 2 cups sugar and 1/2 cup corn syrup I used 1 teaspoon (see update below) cinnamon oil.  That made a strong cinnamon flavor without being really hot.  Yum.Update:  The first time I made this I added the cinnamon oil when the candy was still 290F.  I got a cloud of cinnamon steam in my face and perfectly flavored candy.  I just tried it again but I let the candy cool slightly before adding the cinnamon.  I got less steam (but still a lot) and candy that was WAY too spicy.  I assume that the first time a bunch of the cinnamon oil evaporated, so the amount you need depends on the temperature of the candy when you add it.  Next time I am going to add 1/4 or 1/2 teaspoon to the slightly cooled candy.

I've been retired for a little over 4 years now. When I was in grade school, we used to go down to the local pharmacy and buy "Pure cinnamon Oil" and would soak toothpicks in it overnight. These "Hot Toothpicks" got hotter as you sucked on them. I saw a write-up recently where some folks were using them to control smoking and for weight loss. Well, I quit smoking 17 years ago, but I sure could use some help with weight loss. I went to my local Rite-Aid pharmacy, but they said they no longer carry cinnamon oil but that I could buy it in the "Spices" section of any supermarket. They were wrong! you can get Cinnamon EXTRACT, but that's just for cinnamon flavoring when you are making baked goods or candy. I wanted the Hot Stuff, the Pure Cinnamon Oil, and that's exactly what I got when I ordered the 8 oz bottle of it from Olive Nation, using Amazon.com. It works so well that I ordered a larger bottle, the 16 oz version the next time I needed to get some more. BE VERY CAREFUL IF YOU HAVEN'T EVER USED THIS CINNAMON OIL, OR IF IT HAS BEEN AWHILE SINCE YOU'VE USED IT ---you can burn your lips and tongue if you are not careful. YES, I know this from experience! My suggestion is to start small ---- put several toothpicks in the oil for six hours. Take them out and let them air-dry (caution: don't dry them on paper or cloth towels or the towels will absorb much of the oil.) I dry them on mosquito netting. Try those. If that's not hot enough, double the soaking time. I normally leave mine in for 72 hours, then dry them for 48 hours. I've also found out that the flat toothpicks absorb better / quicker than the round ones. But you can chew on the round ones longer before they start to splinter. --- Good luck!
What a product. I made the mistake of tasting it first. Won't never do that again. I made a Moonshine drink called Apple Pie with it. Wow, what a drink....

I've been a consumer of LorAnn Cinnamon oil for over 20 years and I've never found anything as potent or as expensive.For 8oz, $25 was too cheap NOT to try. That makes this product 8 times cheaper. In my opinion the flavor is about 90% and potency is about 85% that of LorAnn's version. Since LorAnn oil is powerful enough to actually cause dangerous reactions (like extremely hot chili peppers), that can actually be a good thing. I'm conditioned to both well enough to consume things most people wouldn't dare try and this oil is still strong enough that I handle it carefully. The flavor is a bit more like that of "RedHot" hard candies rather than overly-intense cinnamon (which is the best way I can describe LorAnn cinnamon oil).If you're into cinnamon toothpicks or candy flavoring, I can't imagine this being anything less than sufficient and for 1/8th the cost, you have to at leave give it a shot. They have smaller quantities if you don't want to risk $25.I'm not sure I'll ever spend the premium for LorAnn again now that I've had this, but then again, I have the equivalent of 64 drams now and I don't think I've used that much cinnamon oil so far in my life so it'll be a while before I have to purchase again :) The only reason I didn't give it a 5 is because it's not a 100% substitute for LorAnn cinnamon oil, but I wish I could give a 4.5 or 4.75 stars instead of just 4 out of 5.

My mother had trouble finding a cereal that she really liked, that is until Red Mill Gluten Rolled Oats. It is not only gluten-free, but wonderfully delicious, too.Most oats & oatmeal are naturally free of gluten - oats do not contain gluten. Because of where many oat crops are grown (adjacent to other grains that do contain gluten) and how they are processed & packaged (in facilities that also process things like wheat), it's not so simple to label oats as gluten-free. Bob's Red Mill Rolled Oats really is. Mother approved!Ali Julia review

Easy to microwave quickly.  Scrumptious and healthy.  I like adding some blueberries, a few walnuts, and some unsweetened coconut flakes.  Some agave syrup or fruit juice sweetened jam, also.  I buy 8 packs of the 32-ounce bags at a time, so it makes for a fairly inexpensive breakfast or snack.  Very good buy.  I can't get this price at the stores.  And without a car, I certainly could never bring home so much at one time.

I was excited to find out that GF oats existed so I knew that I needed to try them.  I have to say that I'm very impressed. We have been eating them as oatmeal and I also used them to make an apple crisp.  You can't tell the difference between these and regular oats (which can not be said for many GF products).  The price on Amazon is great, and the 4 bags come packaged in a Bob's Red Mill box, inside of an Amazon box so you don't need to worry about them making it in once piece.  I would highly recommend these to anyone who has gone GF!
I can't say enough great things about this oatmeal.Such a simple item, yet sorely missed from my menu choices!Wonderful texture and hands down the best oatmeal I'veever eaten!!

column9: Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Oats Review
column10: Product arrived in a timely manner in store showcase packaging.  Good quality and is exactly what I expected.
My daughter was diagnosed with food allergies that included wheat, and this oatmeal has saved us!  And with the subscribe and save, you just cannot beat the price (if you can, please tell me how!)

It's Wednesday! You know what that means? Grocery shopping, coupons, and grocery sales!About every so often, Safeway puts the oatmeal 50% off and I go crazy! I stock up because the oats (Quaker or general store brand) are 2 for $6. I soon stop purchasing Safeway oatmeal because I recently discovered that gluten and wheat makes me break out like crazy. I get painful cysts and a few ton of pimples (gross I know. TMI i am sorry).So, I decided to go gluten free and I so happened to find Bob's Gluten Free Oatmeal as I browsed Amazon. I just cooked some oats awhile ago (1/2 c. of oats, 1 1/2 cups of water, 1 TBS of cinnamon, 1 green apple and 1 packet of Stevia. Apple pie in a bowl of oatmeal <3  ).I never imagined there would be a difference in oatmeal. Oatmeal was oatmeal. Just like water was water. There is a HUGE difference between Quaker and Bob's oatmeal. Bob's oatmeal is thicker and has a more filling effect.I HIGHLY recommend these oats. :D Cheapo oats are in the trash bin (trash day is tomorrow).Enjoy!

It turns out that I'm not terribly fond of cooking up the plain whole grain rolled oats; either I cook them too long or not enough, and I was kind of sad the first few mornings. Then I got the bright idea to toss a few cups in my mini cuisinart, and pulse for 10 seconds or so until it was a rough oat meal. I also put in a healthy amount of cinnamon. I put a 1/4 cup of the mixture on the stove with 1/2 cup of water, and it gets nice and bubbly and creamy in a couple of minutes. Then I add as much milk as I want, stir a bit more, and eat. Loads of flavor, no sugar, no gluten, just a good warm breakfast.
This is a great product! It is easy to microwave or cook on the stove top.  We have made no-bake cookies, they were delicious.

I had stopped eating oatmeal altogether before being introduced to Bob's Red Mill GF Whole Grain, Rolled Oats. Who knew that oatmeal had gluten in it? I didn't! Though these oats do require a longer cooking time, I'd much rather wait for them to cook than wait for the horrible discomfort to go away after eating "regular" oatmeal. I especially love the texture (or bite) and the lack of sliminess. My children and husband like this oatmeal. I am so very thankful someone gave me a sample to try. I even use it in when I make buttermilk pancakes; I grind them very well first. I use 1/2 oats and 1/2 flour of choice.I am a subscriber for this oatmeal.

I use a stick free pan and cook the oats until they toast on the bottom . . . amazingly good. This oatmeal is, literally, the best I've ever eaten. It has a lovely, nutty quality that really sticks to the ribs. I've lost 70 lbs in the last year, and this is my daily breakfast along with a scrambled egg and cranberry juice. I don't get hungry again until afternoon. Highly recommended. Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Whole Grain, Rolled Oats, 32-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4)

It took me a long time to realize that, not only do I need to avoid gluten to avoid feeling sick, but I also need to avoid the tiny amount of gluten that's found in regular oats.  Sheesh!These are a lifesaver.  They make an excellent oatmeal (I usually soak them for a couple minutes in hot water, then microwave, since I'm too impatient to put them on the stove), and most likely are a fantastic add-in for whatever other recipes you might require oats in.Best of all, they really don't make me sick.  Wahoo!  These are worth a shot, especially through Amazon.

I got a pack of these to eat while I did a gluten-free experiment, and like the texture so much more than regular oatmeal that even after I determined I don't have a major gluten intolerance, I keep buying these. They don't get as gummy/starchy as other oatmeal seems to (which I actually didn't even notice until after I tried these and then tried regular oatmeal again!). Also, even though it says to cook 10-20 mins, I always cook it the same amount of time as other oatmeal -- 5 mins and let sit covered for 2 mins -- and it's perfect. Just wish it were a little less expensive.

column9: Bolb's Red Mill GF Rolled Oats
column10: These oats are delecious and I can eat them without worrying about them being cross contaminated with other gluten grains.

Make sure your not looking for the quick cooking type of oat if you purchase these! This is the real deal of old fashioned, rolled oats. The quality is so fresh, much better than the rolled oats I used to purchase before my Celiac diagnosis twelve years ago! These oats appear to me like they just came out of the field and were rolled a week before they arrived on my doorstep! Thank you Bob's Red Mill for taking the drastic steps needed to create a gluten free oat! I understand how you have to create an entire separate part of the mill, with machinery dedicated to the oat only, have a clean field to grow in and clean transport as well! My two celiac children and I are happily eating oatmeal again!

I have recently had to go gluten-free and it's been difficult to say the least.  Gluten sneaks in a lot of foods.  I turned to someone I trusted.  Bob's Red Mill!  I used to eat store brand quick oats.  They were okay, and they were quick and worked.  But when I wanted to go totally Gluten-Free, I bought Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Whole Grain, Rolled Oats.  Although they do take a few more minutes in the microwave, they actually have such a rich wonder taste to them that my husband has actually started eating breakfast with me every morning!  A bowl of these with a little cinnamon sugar on top.  And some Oscar Meyer Center Cut Bacon (3 slices on some paper towels top and bottom of bacon in microwave for 2 minutes for total crisp bacon bliss!).  So to summarize, takes just a few minutes longer but the taste and health benefits makes this an AWESOME breakfast, lunch, dinner, whenever food :)
We always buy this because my wife has Celiac disease and has a gluten intolerance which sometimes reacts to oats as well. Not this one, this is some great oatmeal!

column9: Love Bob's GF oats - and this is a deal!
column10: Was excited to discover these oats on Amazon.  The price can vary from store to store - and can be up to $2 more per bag.  I make a lot of granola and granola bars, as well as oatmeal cookies from time to time, so I appreciate the savings.Good deal.

I had been eating oatmeal 6 days a week for breakfast for over 5 years when my doctor told me I couldn't have them any more because of GF cross contamination. I was bummed.  I found out GF oats existed but they were soo costly that I used Bob's Red Mill triticale for almost 2 yrs. Now, I can get the GF oats and they are soo good. I'm glad they are back in my life.  I miss the texture and the taste and now totally don't mind eating them without milk.  My favorite add-ins are diced prunes (preferrably from Trader Joe's) and pecan pieces and a little almond milk.

column4: J. Loscheider "No one knows I'm a radical"
column9: Fantastic for granola - and that's actually all I use it for...
column10: Of all the things you have to give up on a gluten-free diet, the ones that surprised me most were soy sauce and oats. That also cuts down substantially on your convenience foods. Forget about Chinese takeout, learn how to make your own (either with a gluten-free soy sauce or a substitute sauce of molasses, brown sugar, rice vinegar and corn starch).For oats, that means giving up my favorite breakfast - granola. And granola bars, granola bites. Forget about all the fruit bars I can't have now because of oat flour...So Bob's Red Mill GF Oats are very welcome in my pantry. And there's nothing so good as a bowl of homemade granola - especially with coconut flakes, almond slivers, dried cranberries or raisins, and a homemade sugar syrup.Yes, they're pricier. It's the testing, as well as the quality. No cracked or stale oats here.
These are really great oats.  They taste just like regular oatmeal does and they're gluten free.  Much better to buy in bulk because they happen to be about $3 cheaper per bag.

I've been buying 3 lb. bags of Gluten Free oats from a company in Canada. The price was $18! I found Gluten Free oats in the same size for $14, too. So, a 2 Lb bag for around $5 is a bargain.As others have said, the texture and quality are better than any other brands; even the expensive imported oats. Worth it!

I have been eating this oatmeal for about a month now and have no problems - it seems to be as advertised - no gluten. I get severe stomach pains when eating anything with gluten it it and this oatmeal does not affect me at all. It is the best tasting oatmeal that I've eaten and I grew up on oatmeal, am now 69 years old. In the past I've always bought the Old Fashioned oatmeal and prefer to eat it raw with apple juice on it, cinnamon and raisins. Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free oatmeal needs to be cooked as it is straight grain that has been steel cut, not refined so it would be a little hard to eat raw. I only cook it for about 4 - 5 minutes and love it. It has a consistency that is different than store-bought oatmeal - seems to have more substance, which the store stuff must have stripped from the grain, even the old fashioned kind. I highly recommend this product to anyone that loves oatmeal, and I can only say that this is the only oatmeal that doesn't give me stomach pain.

column9: Would Absolutely Go Into Mourning if these EVER disappeared!
column10: I have Celiac and have been eating these for YEARS!  Every single day I have a bowl of these Rolled GF Oats topped  with Bob's Organic Ground Flax Meal and Wild Blueberries & Cinnamon!  It is what I do for my self and health every day!I don't boil these.  I pour a pile in a bowl, cover with water, and "nuke" them in the microwave (1 min 30 seconds in my micro) and wait for them to start rising up in the bowl.  Then I pour the flax meal / frozen wild blue berries / cinnamon / sea salt/ and sometimes sweetener / on top and stir - and I'm off with my day!The quality of these rolled oats is one of the reasons I love them.  Not much "oat dust"  or small flakes - these are wonderful large whole flakes - So superior to ANYTHING I have found out there and they do not bother my stomach at all!I keep these stocked in my pantry!  They are the most important food "to me" in my home!

Buying these from amazon saves me almost $2 per bag over buying from a local source. We make this several times a month in our rice cooker, on the normal setting, with 5 cups (the rice cooker cup) oats, 7.5 cups of water, about 1/4 teaspoon salt. When its done season to taste. it is perfect every time!

I'm gluten free, and haven't had a problem with this product. Since eating this everyday for three months, my HDL count has raised from a dismal 17 to a almost bottom end 34. My doctor recommended these oats specifically to raise my HDL levels without medication.

column9: Another great Bob's Red Mill product!

column9: Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Whole Grain Rolled Oats
column10: Product fresh and very satisfactory, except for a few hulls. A nice firmer texture and nutty-like taste in a fruit crisp, not as mushy as the quick rolled.

I am on my second box of this and am quite pleased with it.  It seems cleaner than the Quaker stuff if that makes any sense.  But I do put it into an old Quaker box because the bags that this comes in just don't cut it for storage.

You really dont know what oatmeal taste like till you try this. Throw your Quaker instant in the garbage; this stuff is 10x better!Add a little butter (butter is NOT bad for you in small quantities), little brown sugar, little milk, banana pcs, lots of cinnamon (I love cinnamon) and you have a perfect b-fast or snack.Annnnnnnnnd GLUTEN FREE! No bubble-guts from this guy!

Once I found out that there was a gluten free oatmeal available, I was immediately enthralled by the idea of once again eating a normal healthy balanced breakfast. My husband and I typically eat this oatmeal 3-4 times a week, so we go through these bags very quickly. I use 1/4 cup of oats in the protein smoothies I make for breakfast, and these have been  great. I use them raw, but they break down great when blended and don't leave a gritty or thick after taste, and having them in bulk is great.

column9: Gluten Free Whole Grain Rolled Oats

column9: What I eat for breakfast everyday

My son has multiple food allergies and this is the only oatmeal he will eat.  In fact, he eats it every morning and would have it for dinner if I'd let him.

Having a large selection of gluten free products, you have to trust them to continue to buy. Nothing has ever caused me to get sick and I'm so glad they have an oat option!

Recipes, Gluten-Free Snacks and more!
We are very happy with Bob's Red Mill GF rolled oats. Consistently good quality and taste for the two gluten-intolerant members of our family.

THIS IS A GREAT PRODUCT AND I EAT SOME OF THE OATMEAL EVERY DAY.  I AM COMING BACK FROM A BAD INJURY - WAS RUN OVER BY A CAR LAST JUNE - AND THIS IS HELPING ME TO GET BACK TO NORMAL.  LOVE THIS PRODUCT AND WISH IT WAS CARRIED IN THE GROCERY STORES. I HAVE GIVEN SOME TO FRIENDS AND THEY LIKED IT TOO.

I have started making homemade gluten free granola since the premade brands are so expensive.  These oats are wonderful and a great price. I will continue to buy.
I love Bob's Red Mill GF oatmeal! I eat it for breakfast almost every morning. I also use it in GF granola bars, cookies, etc. I always keep it in stock at my house!

Bob's Red Mill old fashioned rolled oats, tastes good.I'm glad I bought this product and expect to keep ordering it for a very long time.It cooks fast just like indicated on the bag. The directions are easy to follow.

column9: Bob's Red Mill products are some of the very best!

column9: great oats for the gluten intolerant
column10: I would have really missed oats if I didn't have this. I'm non-celiac, but "intolerant" of gluten. Fortunately I seem to have no problem w/ gluten-free oats. Love 'em!

So far of all the things I tried that was gluten free, I'm happy to say that this product was gradifying. I love to eat oat mills and to be able to try one gluten free and loving the taste was quite extroadinary...since I've been disappointed with other gluten free products. This one is a keeper. column9: Love Bob's Red Mill, LOVE Amazon's subscription service!
column10: I love Amazon's subscription service!!!  I am a Celiac so finding safe, gluten free food locally is always tricky and expensive.  Now I get my core supplies automatically shipped to me at regular intervals so I'm never without! These oats are AWESOME!  You cannot tell they are GF... they cook perfectly in the microwave, on the stove, and are perfect to add to any recipe!  LOVE them!

column9: The BEST oats - just like my grandma from Ireland made
column10: Hearty and filling.  Didn't think I'd ever find oats to make oatmeal like my grandma made (I'm over 50, so we're talking "old school" here).  This is as close as it gets.  Nice to know it's made in a gluten-free plant for those with celiac disease.

I am so thankful for this Gluten Free Oatmeal. We use it all the time. We use it whole, we grind it up. Very pleased with the taste and texture.

column9: Great oatmeal at a great price!

As a gluten sensitive individual, I have found Bob's Redmill gluten free oatmeal allows me to use oatmeal in many recipies and just as acereal that was off limits to me before.  It's a very good product.This was an Amazon verified purchase.

column10: I CAN NOT RATE A PURCHASE THAT I NEVER RECEIVED AS I FIND IT HARD TO WRITE A REVIEW FOR.

column9: Our dog's favorite toy and a great, fun tool for rescue adoptees
column10: The Booda Soft Bite Medium Carrot Dog Toy is our dog's favorite toy!  She adores it! More durable than most of the toys we have tried, this carrot is one of the few toys that she has not destroyed within 24 hours.  The squeaker has a great sound, better than those in other squeaker toys we have tried.  The squealer is easy for her to work and loud and interesting enough to keep her interested but not so loud or irritating to be obnoxious --- which is a real plus since she loves to play with it over and over and over again.  Our puppy loves the sound so much that she enjoys experimenting with the different sounds she can make even more than chewing it!  The shape makes it easy for her to carry it in her mouth for such games as fetch. She also likes to cuddle with her head on this soft toy.We adopted a rescue puppy who was terrified of just about everything, including toys.  Her initial reaction to this toy was wonderful!  This toy helped her come out of her shell and be less afraid of noise in general.  I was not sure if the toy would be scary or not but once she found the squeaker noises, she just loved being able to play and make noise herself, making all sorts of variations and rhythms.  Although there are many additional things we are doing to help her, this toy was an important step in breaking through her fears.  Playing with this toy seemed to embolden her, bringing out this sense of delight and play in her.  In addition to an overall very high recommendation of this product for puppies in general, I would add a special recommendation for special needs or rescue puppies as a possible tool to help initial bonding to the owner and to help him/her break through their fears.  We now order this product in multiple quantities so we can have one in every room!

I don't know if it is the color or shape but they are all crazy about it.  Each will pick it up and just carry it around in their mouth forever. If you're going to make a dog toy (and ours is not a huge chewer, they simply fell off while she was carrying the carrot around in her mouth by the leaves) you should make it sturdy!  I would not suggest this dog toy.

column4: D. L. Brown "A Knower Of Good Things"
column10: I liked this Lasgna, however, I was a little disappointed with the portion size, it is quite small.  I found it more appropiate for one's lunch than a dinner or meal for two. The tase was good, it is easy to heat and serve, it was just small for the price charge, so, I was kinda disapponted.

Omaha Steaks 1 (22 oz. tray) Roasted Vegetable LasagnaMy husband and I were trying to be good and lose weight. I thought this would be a nice treat for us. The lasagna was a nice portion for two or if you were on a diet, could be made into smaller portions. Tasty, I loved the roasted veggies.  They even used vegetarian lasagna noodles.  I only wish there was more marinara sauce, as I love sauce.
I bought this on an impulse and I was not disappointed.  It was a tasty little lasagne that easily fed my mother and me.

I have vegetarian friends and wanted to send them a special gift for Christmas.  They enjoyed the roasted vegetable lasagna. The tray was plentiful for two with left-overs for 2 more meals. In fact, with a tossed salad, the lasagna was a complete meal. This couple enjoyed the vegetable lasagna so much that I will send it to other friends. I enjoy the meat lasagna myself.

I have received two cartons of this macaroni so far.  The first had broken open in shipping and arrived with one flap hanging open.  Fortunately, all 20 boxes of macaroni were still in it, and only 3 or 4 of them somewhat damaged.  The second arrived taped together with clear plastic tape and only a little over half full, with eight boxes of macaroni missing and a couple of the remainder damaged.This macaroni is packaged too poorly to be shipped - in cartons just glued together, not particularly well.  It may be a good buy, and very welcome in the food pantry for which I order it, but I won't be buying it again.
These are the absolute best mararoni, period.  Right size, right texture.  None of that big, fat, mushy stuff.  As far as mararoni goes, there is no other.  Without Meuller's, it's mostly ruined.

This is the brand I grew up on... when we moved away from the east coast, visiting family always meant picking up Mueller's.For some reason, the supermarket selection for elbow macaroni stinks in my area.  This is where the internet, and Amazon, came to the rescue.Unlike the other reviewer, my order showed up fine.  Everything was in great shape, and I'm only now realizing just how long 20lbs of macaroni can last.

My min-pin loves this food.No cans to recycle and Amazon has unbeatable prices on this product.Join SUBSCRIBE AND SAVE and you will save even more and no more running to the supermarket and standing in line to pay more when you run out.....

I purchased because of one good review !!! Surprising my dog hated it, wouldn't go near it, much less try it. I didn't care for the smell much. She likes the beef stew a little more, and loves the chicken. My son's dog ate it like it was his last meal. Will not buy again.
My dog loves this product.  When she sees me open the pouch she just start to jump up and down.  And if you don't give it to her at the time she thinks you are suppose to she will let you know.
These are delicious and only 50 calories. They help my husband and I stay away from the really cholesterol laden desserts. They are a diet saver for us.

column9: One of the best chocolate's for people watching their weight
column10: I'm a die hard chocoholic but I'm trying to maintain a slim figure too, which gets harder and harder the older I get!  These Weight Watcher's pecan crown chocolates are the most delicious chocolate you can get in the "diet" food category (they taste as good as any non-diet chocolate) and they are high in fiber and low in calories and fat.  They simply can't be beat!  I haven't had any side effects whatsoever from them and I eat them all the time.  My only complaint - they are hard to find!

Taste wise these babies get 5 stars.  But it contains sugar alcohols, and the side effects for some of us are simply not worth the sweet treat.  Until some genius figures out how to use stevia instead of the evil hell creature that is maltitol, I will not touch these things ever again.  If you love em, have some pepto or activated charcoal next to you and prepare to isolate yourself in a well ventilated room for a day.  You have been warned.
Best low cal substitute I have ever had for chips. A few with lunch makes me enjoy my diet without feeling deprived. The multi-grain are the best.

I purchased these using the new "add on" program, mostly out of curiousity. I'd been looking for a new snack item that wasn't over the top with fat and salt.These sticks are light and delicious, and I have since tried them in nearly every flavor available. The sea salt flavor is on the light side, but they're still very good, and are wonderful with a sandwich or salad.Give them a try ... you may be pleasantly surprised ... as I was :)

Historic Lynchburg Tennessee Whiskey Jalepeno Hot Sauce. C'mon guys - this is Jack Daniels hot sauce. And, it's pretty good. One of my favorites. It won't fuse your tongue to your lips or anything but it has great flavor and controlled heat. Enjoy.

Lately I've been trying about 20 or more sauces to find just the right one that balances flavor and burn.  But, to put this into perspective, I really go for the insanely hot so this may need to be measured by that.  This sauce is not really that hot, but the taste is awesome.  It definately has heat, but doesn't really have much burn.  In short; if you want something that shames commercial pizza place hot wings in both heat and taste this is a great choice.  In fact I'm browsing the internet to see about ordering a case.  (for those days when I don't want my food to have the last highly pronounced word if you follow my meaning.)

In an effort to save during hard times, we decided to turn our once-a-week outing with our daughter and her family into a cereal supper at her house. During home school lessons, her elementary age children have learned to read labels, and they are set free at the grocery store to choose their own cereals and other products. I found this particular cereal one day while shopping and called to make sure it fit into all the required guidelines. My two grandsons and I eat almost a box of this by ourselves on Cereal Supper Night! My daughter enjoys the Pumpkin Seed flavor best, and I routinely contribute other organic cereals. As soon as we drive up on Wednesdays, I am greeted with enthusiastic greetings and cries of inquiry, "What did you bring this week, Gran?" Three days ago, my eight year old granddaughter told her neighbor that Wednesdays were her favorite day of the week. I highly recommend this cereal no matter what your age may be!

column9: Great taste, one of my favorite Natures Path products
column10: If you like a solid, sweet granola this is your boy. It does have a strong vanilla taste which I found very pleasant but not too over powering. The nutritional values aren't too bad, but high in sugar, as you would expect from most granolas. In summary, if you like almonds and vanilla I think you will love munching down a bowl of this stuff.
I first tried the Nature's Path Flax Seed with pumpkin which was very good.  Then, I saw this one and tried it and it was absolutely delicious.  Good with cold or hot milk.
Call it "evaporated cane juice" -- call it moogabooga -- it's still sugar and this stuff has waaaay too much of it!
Nature's Path Organic Flax Plus, Vanilla Almond Flax Granola Cereal, 11.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) by Nature's Path was not as fresh as expected!
Tastes good. Seems healthy. But too much sugar. The cereals is also dense. So to feel full I kind end up eating more of that I should.
I have tried quite a few of the similar type of cereals but without doubt, this is the best granola cereal i have tried. The distinctive vanilla almond flavor provides a refreshing taste.
Much to like about this coffee. Not too acidic, well-balanced flavors. The beans roast evenly for me at full-roast. Very happy to be drinking Panama Boquete any morning.

Ever since I visited the fincas of Boquete in '08 I have looked for these beans, so when I started roasting my own this is where I go for dependable flavor at a reasonable price.  These beans like a darker roast, to city or better.  They produce a rich mouth, not too acidy, and a smooth finish.  I'm not one to note hints of berries, pepper, etc., just a good cup'a joe.

Been roasting green coffee beans for many years. It's the best and cheapest way to get the best tasting coffee. Panama Boquete from Amazon is one of the tastiest coffees I have tried recently. I will deninitely be purchasing more. I can strongly recommend this coffee. Thank You.

These beans have produced some enjoyable cups of coffee with a medium roast (dark brown beans with no oil on their surfaces) at 455F for 17 minutes. We have experimented, using the same roasted beans with different water sources. We have learned that the beans alone do not make the coffee. The WATER that is used also plays an important part of how your coffee tastes. Try your tap water one morning and spring water the next morning, using the same beans! SURPRISE !

The coffee is tasty but little more acidic than other kinds i tried.  May be my roasting is suboptimal and leads to the heartburn i get every time i drink this coffee.  Overall, the smell and taste is better in other kinds of unroasted coffee.  I wish the package is smaller so i get to try different kinds.

I purchased these Beans via Amazon, and have made 3 batches using the gas grill method of roasting Beans. They roast very evenly, and I seem to getting them to the 2nd crack stage in that the beans are very dark brown, split, and oily. The beans made a good cup of coffee, and we tend to like very robust, strong coffee. Since this is the first bag we have tried I do not have others to compare them to, but it makes good coffee. The price with free shipping is a winner!

As a home coffee roaster finding good quality beans at a good price can be a task and gamble. If you find a good source chances are you will stick with them. In this case the outcome was excellent. Using an air popper the panama beans cooked cracked and cracked again just fine. Taste is fantastic and I am very happy. I found these beans as good as any out there at a decent price.

column9: Quinoa is alwasy good but this is not a particularly great deal
column10: Trader Joe's sells Quinoa for pretty much the same price but if you don't mind waiting for it to be delivered, the quality is comparable.

column9: Most dog foods are not human-grade. There simply is no better dog food. You'll see it in your dog's coat.
column10: I spent 5 years studying canine nutrition and sadly, learned that vets don't ever get this chance. Veterinary colleges are funded by dog food companies and unfortunately, as one famous vet who wants to change all that, Dr. Pitcairn, realized, taught to treat the problem rather than discovering what's causing it and that usually relates to the diet. In fact, a tremendous increase in dog health issues can be traced back to the time that dog food companies started...when they stopped eating table scraps and began an all-processed high grain and high allergen and unnatural diet. Even though table scraps were full of dog toxins like onions, they STILL had less health issues than their process food preservative and poor balance counterparts of today.Funny how we wouldn't feed our kids crackers every day but feel it's okay to only feed our dogs that--high grain, poor protein, cooked out vitamins, highly processed, low nutrients...dogs who, in nature, seek out more protein.In fact, that is how new dog food nutrition studies began. Because vets realized that wolves and coyotes in the wild brought in for treatment if hit by a car, etc do not have the health issues our INDOOR dogs have. A wolf might be old and without fleas or tartar or itching and with a glossy coat.So vets like Dr. Pitcairn began studying the cause of pets with chronic issues or developing common issues too young and finding what things were toxic and unnatural and what helped prevent poor things in their diet.I live in the woods and have 3 dogs and have yet to have one flea because I follow this advice. In fact, I have strangers tell me (often) that my dog's fur looks like a cat's because it's so shiny. No itching. Never grew up begging for my food because theirs is complete. (It may be hard to break this habit once begun but easy if it never starts.)I will only feed them 3 things: a diet I make from Dr. Pitcairn's recommendations, ( I have no ties to any of these but am an activist about sharing anything good or bad for pets)  Newman's Own canned dog food, or Flint River Ranch.Why? First of all, as part of my own studies I visited dog food plants. Actually this was like the biggest wakeup call on the planet for me.  I watched as I was told the "brilliant" model of putting the factories near cattle processing. When a cow is dead or dying of anything...they never determine the cause...they pick it up in a bulldozer and go take it to the dogfood plant. I WATCHED this.How can they do this? Do you see how you rarely see the term "human grade meat" on dog food? They don't have to be inspected if it's dog food. There are two different levels of acceptance...people cannot eat food riddled with tumors from lesions or cancer, it's okay if dog's do. According to the government regulations.  Humans are required to eat inspected meat of certain cleanliness standards and from cows processed for this reason (I don't eat meat anyway but still....)Dog food companies are not required to have such standards.For reals.So if you will recall the huge outbreak of botulism a few years back with sick dogs going to vets, dying, etc that they linked to dog foods then it happened a few months later...do you remember there were only about 5 companies that were labeled as unaffected? This was one, Newman's Own was one....why? They only use HUMAN GRADE meat. Their meat is inspected. They do not buy meat from downed cattle plants so they were released from any recall or report of possible affected products. The others bought meat from across the country at these places and it was found the cows were diseased but because they never have to check to find out what they cows died from when making them into food, it was passed along. Then it happened again a few months later. Then it happened again a year later. Yes, we hear about these things when dogs die en masse. We never, however, hear about dogs that just fall ill....But it gets worse.  You may see a list of vitamins and nutrients across the back of a bag of dog food. But due to the way meat is processed, they bake it at astronomically high temps to try to kill off any lesions, puss, etc. I"m not making this up. But they ARE required to have these in there...so what happens? They all bake off. You are left with some grains, high allergens like corn, and you are basically feeding your dog crackers and by-products of downed cattle.So, does your dog beg and salivate when you eat meat or any dinner for that matter? Does your dog dive into the grass to try to get greens and nutrients by eating grass when you go for a walk?There is a reason.  In nature, if you gave a human baby a banana and a bunny they would pet the bunny and eat the banana. If you gave a hungry dog the same for dinner, they'd eat the bunny first. What part of the bunny do they eat first? the stomach.  Why? This is where they get their greens and nutrients...then the meat protein. The raw bones clean their teeth without splintering.Yet, although we are against eating an all-processed diet, dogs in spite of begging and pleading, are now living shorter lives, with the highest health issues ever due to our thinking that it's better for them because a dog food company told us so...or vets who don't have classes in nutrition tell us so. But this isn't taught in veterinary schools and dog food companies fund and provide text books etc. I didn't say this...vets say this.That is changing. There is a huge off-shoot of vets now learning to find the issue and the cause (usually food related) rather than treating the issue alone.  And it turns out most issues are cured by a proper diet.In fact, look at your dog treats. If you see sugar in them you will realize how many dog food companies are motivated by money. And there are lots of dog treats even TARTAR CLEANING (they say) dog treats with sugar. Why? Your dog will crave them just like people do. You may also see loads of unnnatural ingredients and even toxins such as onion powder. Milo's dog treats have these. Your dog can't tell you what is slowly hurting their kidneys. It's up to you to read the labels. Dog food is not regulated. It's up to us to do that.The first thing you will notice about this dog food is that it looks like cookies broken a part rather than machine-made little round circles. Why? Because it it. They use inspected human-grade meat and a balance of carbs, protein, etc. that is closer to the natural diet and what a dog needs. Then they can bake it at a regular temperature that doesn't bake these out, just like you would at home. The nutrients aren't baked out. They bake it in sheets, naturally, then just break them apart.You may be skeptical...so give it a month or two. Take a picture of your dog's fur before (dead serious) then compare it to when it has time to grow after eating this....you will be SHOCKED. We show poor health in our hair and so do they.I can actually walk up to people at a dog event and tell them what they feed their dog. I have yet to be wrong and I do it often. I don't mean what brand but even people who think they are feeding their dog premium food like Iams have no idea it's just processed crackers marked up and grains and downed cattle.I actually point out to people the difference. I kid you not, a family barbecue, a neighborhood "house crawl", a restaurant that allows dogs outside....I can walk up and tell who gives their dog table scraps (without toxins like onions or avocados) or real food, or human grade food....I just say "what do you feed your dog?" and I've never been wrong. Their coats are SHOCKINGLY different and shinier, the dogs aren't itching, and they usually have better teeth and gums.  I have yet to be wrong.One lady told me how she took her dog to vets for years and it had to have steroid shots, then she finally found a vet who knew about nutrition rather than saying "feed him expensive dog food" and assumed that was good...and the dog was cured.Do I work for this company? No. I am a very active Amazon reviewer who speaks up heavily, especially when it comes to pets, in all my reviews of things I love or things I don't.  My dogs thrive on this but I will say, they are not fans of their dog treats. So I just look at labels and find all natural dog treats (charlee bear brand has good ones) I have no ties to this company whatsoever except for the fact that I used to only feed my dogs food I made until a vet who was an expert in nutrition told me about this (In fact this vet ALWAYS treats from the cause rather than the symptoms first...a rarity as to how vets are taught to heal.)this was at a time I was too busy to cook and I didn't want to give my dog just canned food even though Newman's Own is equally as good as this...the difference in coat was striking.  I have tried a couple other brands and one of my poms always starts scratching. This has amino acids and things that treat the coat and skin and it's perfectly balanced.Depending upon where you live it may be cheaper to buy direct. I anxiously await the day they finally get this on Amazon with free shipping but it has not happened yet. I'd get it on subscription then.There is a difference. There is a huge difference. I've spent years studying in order to be informed and I recommend few dog foods. This, however, in my opinion, is simply one that no other dog food has ever come close to when I read ingredients and balance of ingredients and look at how it's made and what kind of meat.If you ate artificial and processed chicken mcnuggets every day you'd fall ill too. When our dogs do people rarely suspect the dog food...they live such short lives anyway....nothing should be off balance, artificial, preservative-laden, processed, etc in their diets either so that even if they live a long life it is a full and healthy one with less arthritis, less kidney issues, less scratching etc.I am a raving fan.

column9: The best dog food on the market.
column10: *Note: This may seem like a shill review, but I am in no way affiliated with Flint River - I am just one happy customer (well three counting my wife and pup)!This is without a doubt the best dog food on the market. Forget all of these pet store-sold brands that use words like "plus", "pro-formula" and "healthy" - it's marketing hype and is not beneficial for your dog. After talking with Chandler (see first reviewer) my wife and I decided to give Flint River Ranch a go. We had been using Blue Buffalo Dry Food for Small Breed Dogs and we were generally quite pleased. They at least used natural ingredients in beneficial amounts (meat always main ingredient) - but after reading up on the difference in meat quality used, as well as several recalls over the past 3 years, we decided it was time for a change. Chandler's helpful post has already outlined why using human-grade meat is important so I won't go over that, but to highlight one important thing every dog owner should realize: your dog is not a wild wolf! It has been domesticated over generations, changing its genetic makeup; he or she can't handle poor quality meat.Our pup had recently been suffering from allergies - Blue Buffalo helped a little but they were still present. As cute as it is to have our little pup bound up to us with a runny nose every now and then, we knew that she must be uncomfortable! We were going to go with Newman's Own Dog Food but our dog is a 24lb. whippet mix and an examination of the kibble at a friend's place showed it to be a little too big for her. So, we jumped on Flint River's website and put an order in. We were a little nervous about our picky eater - she has a hard time with  Eukanuba when visiting the in-laws, and even when we tried a different Blue Buffalo food to mix things up she was hardly enthusiastic. Luckily for us, she jumped right on her bowl of Flint River the first time around! The kibble itself is more like broken up dog biscuits:PROS- Human-grade meat is used- No artificial preservatives or fillers- NO ANIMAL BY-PRODUCTS- Food is twice-baked to preserve healthful properties- Nicely sized, even for smaller dogs- Food has never been recalled- Customer Service is excellent- Our dog seemed to love it"CONS"- PriceI put "cons" in parentheses because while you are paying more for your food, you are (a) looking out for your buddy which in my mind is worth it, and (b) you may be saving money of vet visits down the road. Dogs are genetically quite similar to humans. If a person takes care of themselves by eating well and exercising often, doctor's visits are only necessary for injuries and check-ups (at least in my experience). The same goes with dogs and vet visits!Listen, no dog food is going to magically make your dog run like a greyhound and pull people out of burning buildings like Lassie, but smart choices lead to a better life for your pup. Heck, we don't even know how old our dog is (looks like a puppy but has some grey on the muzzle), but we want to invest in her life by making good choices! Nothing irks me more than reviews on pet food that say "My dog didn't like this food, ONE STAR!" - your dog can't smell what food is best for them. Give it time, allow them to get used to this food and for their body to reap some of the benefits, and I hope you will find it as worth it as we did! We have only been using it for a few weeks now, but I will updated this review in a couple of months when we really start to see the positive effects!Still not convinced? Flint River offers four sample meals of their food for less than five bucks shipped. Give it a try before you drop the premium price!This food is recommended by my wife and I (and our little girl, Poppy) without reservation - if you can't afford to cook fresh chicken and rice for your dog each day, this is the next best thing! Absolutely worth the price!

column9: My picky eater yorkie loves it!
column10: This is the only dog food that my picky eater yorkie likes. The dog next door (dash) is also picky but when he tasted this food - he devoured it. According to the dog reviewer they consider this under the "average" category and that we should supplement with protein. I have been giving my dog ground beef once in awhile. Finally, something that my dog will eat!

I have been looking for a high quality dog food for quite some time now, and I was especially motivated to find a company that has never had any recalls on its food. I also really wanted to look for a company that makes its product in the USA, after what we went through with the poisoned Chinese dog food scare. (My thoughts are with you if you are one of the families that lost a pet to this tragic situation).I found Flint River and ordered their free samples (just paid for the shipping) and my dog loved the food instantly. We just invested in the 20 pound bag after my little pup's product testing went so well last month. I can have the food delivered straight to our door and the shipping is LIGHTNING FAST!This food is expensive compared to what you can get at a pet food store. HOWEVER, it is definitely worth it. My little pup is very picky with dry food and this one has been a success with him. It's got top quality, human grade ingredients. Pup's coat is so shiny and soft, and he's all muscle and incredibly healthy. He's stopped scratching all the time because we've eliminated all the old, cheap food that had corn and wheat in it. He's much healthier and we have less visits to the veterinarian, too! If people eat good food to stay healthy, then our furry family members should be able to also. It turns out that many of the big brands have corn, wheat, soy and animal by-products in their dog food. Plus, the big brands bake the dog food at such high temperatures to burn off the undesirable tumors and other undigestible matter that are an inevitable part of animal by-product meal. This removes much of the nutrients from the food which have to be added back after processing, and then sprayed with special flavoring and oils to make the food palatable to your pet. The truth is that dogs got along just fine before the big dog food industry took over, eating homemade meals from their owners. Flint River Ranch will deliver this home made, wholesome meal to your dog or cat without the hassel of having to cook for Fido or Kitty every night. I will never have to darken the doorways of another big box Pet Supply store ever again. Thanks again Flint River!

So I had a trainer recommend this food for my dog about a year ago and I have been hooked.  My dog LOVES this stuff.  I buy the puppy and dog brand and have no complaints.  I like that it really does look oven baked and all natural.  They also have the fastest shipping you can imagine.  I believe mine came next day, which is nice because I often forget to order the my dogs food until she is completely out.

column9: Raspberry Tea with Hibiscus--What a Combo!
column10: ****Stash's Wild Raspberry Caffeine Free Herbal Tea is strong and fruity, great if you love the taste of raspberry and hibiscus, which I do. It contains hibiscus, orange peel, lemongrass, rosehips, natural raspberry flavor, licorice powder, and citric acid. The package says it also contains soy, but that makes little sense to me--you should know this in case you are allergic. It is a fine tasting herb tea.If you like a more subtle tea, you may not be crazy about Wild Raspberry. But if you like Celestial Seasonings and other commercial teas, I think that this is a good one. The reason I gave this tea four stars instead of five is that it isn't as pure as it could be (contains additives and flavorings) and I can tell. I prefer a more subtle tea. And I save five stars for the very best teas I've tried. But for those of you who like a lot of flavor, and can't taste the additives, it's just fine!Recommended.****

I decided that i should first research how to germinate acorns, they said you should soak them in hot water for 24 hours. I did. None of the seeds sunk, I know that it is not a completely reliable method to prove the viability of the seeds, but still! out of the 10 acorns that I bought, none sunk! They floated like dead fish.
