I will finish the sample package I was sent, as the taste isn't as off-putting in fruit based items like herbal tea or yogurt.  But, I wouldn't buy this, regardless of the price.

column9: A serious contender in the sweetener marketplace
column10: I'm pleased to see another one of the big companies jumping into the natural sweetener ring with this offering.  Meant, I'm certain, as direct competition for Truvia, this is a really nice product.  Monk fruit is the primary sweetening force in these little packets as opposed to stevia in Truvia.  Monk fruit (also known as luo han guo in China where it originates) and stevia have a lot of molecular properties in common.  They are kissing cousins in the natural sweetener world, with monk fruit offering a slightly more positively robust flavor profile with tasters offering descriptors like:  honey, fruity, molasses, brown sugar.The best products containing stevia, by comparison, have a stronger more streamlined flavor that just screams:  sweet! for the most part, yet there is high variability between stevia strains which you will quickly learn if you start tasting all the various products in the marketplace.  The cleanest stevia flavor is to be found in a single ingredient, pure stevia product made by KAL.  Others tend to have some off flavors like licorice or bitter notes and lingering unpleasant aftertastes.  Yet, for me, it's been a long time since I've partaken in any of those, having found the KAL product years ago, I began mixing my own blend with Erythritol, Xylitol, KAL's stevia and pure glucose to round out the flavor profile.  I occasionally use truvia or splenda when away from home.Extracts like stevia and monk fruit offer some interesting problems for the manufacturers.  The sweetness factor is incredibly high--miniscule amounts approximate a couple of teaspoons of sugar--something like 1/128 of a teaspoon or the like.  How do they deliver that in a packet?  Well, they have to mix it up with something else that adds bulk, of course.  A sugar alcohol is the obvious choice because it tastes so much like sugar yet delivers very few to zero practical calories.  The manufacturers lean toward erythritol because it results in zero net calories in such small amounts.  They might be better served by combining it with xylitol and/or something else like pure glucose or fructose because anyone with sensitive, um, digestive functions are going to find that using a lot of this product is going to send them running for the bathroom--though they probably won't make the connection.  The sugar alcohols (as those who have partaken of diabetic candies quickly learn) can wreak havoc with the gut.That said, this product contains 2 grams of erythritol per packet, while Truvia contains 3 grams per packet.  That's a significant difference if you are a heavy coffee drinker.  And, in addition, Nectresse is a far superior product taste-wise.Artificial sweeteners tend to hit one 'note' of sweetness and clang that single note with gusto which tends to fall flat.  The problem is real sugar is a clamor of notes--thousands of little sweet notes of varying degrees and ranges that culminate in one mental rapport--satisfying sweetness.  Monk fruit naturally hits more of those notes and the additional ingredients the manufacturer has added tinkle a few more in the background which is why this is really a superior product.  I have always found that a more satisfying approach is to combine many sweeteners in smaller amounts, trying to hit as many notes as possible.  I can't go back to sugar--my body just doesn't process it properly and I'm working hard to avoid the genetic tendency toward diabetes that runs in my family by eating a low glycemic index diet.So, all that said,  I was truly impressed with this product and its clean, simple, sweet flavor.  If I could only use one commercial product, this one would be it.

My name is Steve and I have always been leery of the many artificial sweeteners fearing their long-term health effects.  I tried several Stevia products but the taste just fell short.  This one while discernibly not sugar to me, could fool some people.  It is the best yet and I will buy it again.

Wow I really really liked it. Stevia is way bitter compared to this. Necteresse has a very pleasant honey like taste and absolute no bad bitter one. Its great in tea, but I haven't tried in coffee yet. Im very surprised that some people didn't give it give stars. Its natural and zero calories what more can you ask for?

In the past 6 months I've had fun sampling the many new varieties of low-calorie and/or artifical sweeteners that have come to market.  I tried this Nectresse about a month ago but couldn't decide if I liked it or not, so this morning I did a side-by-side comparison of Splenda Nectresse with Wholesome Sweeteners Organic Stevia, 75-Count (Pack of 3).  First I simply dipped a damp pinkie into each packet and tried them straight-up. BIG difference in taste.  The stevia shocks your tongue with how sweet it is.  The Nectresse on the other hand doesn't convey much sweetness at all and also has a unique taste that is hard to describe.  Next test...half a packet of each in a hot, regular coffee with half-and-half creamer.  Side-by-side tasting yielded a clear winner for me:  the stevia would be my first choice every time in a cup of coffee.  The Nectress adds a funky little taste that I don't enjoy in coffee.  Now, it's possible that the Nectresse would be fine to sweeeten a cold glass of a fruity iced tea. I tried it in plain iced tea and still wasn't crazy about it because that funky little taste still was detectable.  In general I don't want my sweeteners to have any taste of their own - other than just plain old SWEET - so, while it was okay, I probably wouldn't buy Nectresse again.

column9: Tastes good, and probably safe for diabetics
column10: This a good sweetener, with no aftertaste. It is described as being "suitable for people with diabetes", despite sugar and molasses being listed as ingredients. It has zero calories, so the amount of sugar must be miniscule. See the product website, particularly the tab for `Health Care Professionals': [...]  . The full list of ingredients: erythritol, sugar, monk fruit extract, molasses. It would appear that moderate use would be fine for diabetics, but if that's you, I would advise checking with your doctor.

I use artificial sweeteners all the time, and I'll admit I was skeptical about trying this one. However, it surpassed my expectations. It's sweet like table sugar right out of the package and the grains look similar to sugar. I like the texture better than Nutrasweet, Splenda, and Truvia. It dissolved quickly in my iced coffee, which is the main place I use sweeteners. I don't drink hot beverages, so I didn't try it there.I like the taste better than the Splenda and Truvia that I've been using and I thought this had less of an after taste. I made some iced coffees for friends with it and they said they couldn't tell it had an alternative sweetener. I say alternative, because it isn't exactly artificial like some are. Anyone who uses alternative sweeteners knows that there is some sort of after taste to all of them, so it really depends on your taste preferences. This one really scored high for me and I'd definitely buy it again.

column4: Julie A. Dawson "Bards and Sages Publishing"
column10: The problem with a lot of artificial sweeteners is that they tend to have an odd aftertaste, particularly when used in cold beverages. This tasted naturally sweet, dissolved completely, and had no aftertaste. I was also able to substitute this in some recipes that required a couple teaspoons of sugar with good results.

column9: Has what you want, doesn't have what you don't
column10: As a near-daily coffee drinker, I've had ample opportunity to try just about every sweetener on the market. Thanks to Amazon Vine, my "go-to" sweetener" has been Splenda Essentials No Calorie Sweetener with B Vitamins, Net Wt 2.8-Ounces (Pack of 4), and although I don't particularly have a natural or organic bent, I'm okay with using all natural products that are effective and don't cost more than the competitors. It seems Nectresse fits in that niche.This is an all natural sweetener derived from monk fruit (whatever that is), it has a texture and flavor pretty close to a "light" sugar, much like another all natural sweetener, Truvia Natural Sweetener, 1000-Count Packages. I found the flavor adequate and the sweetening amount pretty much in line with other artificial and natural non-sugar sweeteners. There aren't any vitamins or extras in this product, which is fine if you just need to sweeten something and nothing more. The individual packs are single serving size and convenient as always. The orange color is eye opening and easy to find in my cluttered tea-bag, coffee filter, other-sweetener-laden morning drink drawer. That is to say, this is a product that does what it should in an all natural fashion at what looks like a reasonable price. It's maybe not outstanding, but I just want my coffee a little sweet, and Nectresse delivers. That rates at least four stars in my cup, all morning long.

Nice little well sealed packets of sweetener made by the Splenda people.  I usually use 'the pink stuff' and I found this to be a nice change. Dissolves very easily, somewhat powder-like and made from monk fruit.  (Had to google that one)I use it in coffee and found it quite acceptable.  The reason I only gave it 3 starts is I had 3 of my co-workers try it and they claimed a strong aftertaste.  I did not notice this myself.I would use this product again.Thank you.MEF

Nectresse is really tasty. Out of all the sweeteners I've sampled, it's the one closest in texture and flavor to real sugar. I didn't notice any bad aftertaste and unlike saccharine, it is a full-bodied sugar clone.However, my one complaint is that the box and company's web site doesn't give enough information about what Nectresse really is. I know it's made from natural monk fruit, but according to the product site, the monk fruit extract is then blended with other natural sweeteners to create NECTRESSE(tm) Sweetener. So obviously, there are other ingredients not listed. And I want to know what those are. I want to know if those other natural sweeteners have the same glycemic effect as sugar. Calories are not the only consideration.I think Nectresse tastes better than Stevia, but until I know what's in the orange packets, I'm not sure about trying more.

column9: Sorry, Not For My Cup Of Tea
column10: I am used to artificial sweeteners, although I have and do use regular sugar. That makes it surprising that this sweetener struck out so badly with me. It is far too sweet for me. I thought of all things, it would go well with a bowl of oatmeal, not so! It just tasted kind of strange.This sweetener is not really for diabetics. It has both sugar and molasses in it, although low enough to slip under the amount to trigger sugar carbs on the label.To my taste, this is super sweet stuff, and I do not care for this particular combination of sweeteners. This is my subjective opinion, and someone else's could be entirely different.

I am disappointed with this product. I used it in my coffee on several different days but I can't force myself to like it. It is not very sweet at first taste. Then the sweetness starts coming as almost an after taste. Then there's a strange after taste that follows the sweetness. I'm trying hard to like this but just can't.

I like this for a zero calorie sweetener. It is sweet and has a fruity taste that I think suits drinks like ice tea better than coffee, although I have used it in my coffee and it tastes very decent. The texture is like granulated raw sugar, and I like it and think it could even be sprinkled on berries or other fruit if it needed sweetener.  I have not researched the health effects of this product and don't know how it compares to Equal and Splenda, which I personally shy away from because I worry about whether they are good for you. If this is healthier, then it is definitely worth switching and is very good in my opinion for a zero calorie sweetener. Personally, I like the taste as much or better than Stevia.

column9: NOT as sweet as SPLENDA, but still good.
column10: I am a long-time Splenda user.  I use both Splenda and Jay Robb Stevia combined to sweeten my ice tea.  (I drink about a 1/2 gallon a day.)  So, I substituted the Splenda with the Nectresse (and still used the same amount of Stevia).  My tea was noticably less sweet, but I still drank the whole gallon of tea.  The next gallon of tea, I made with 1/4 Splenda, 1/4 Nectresse and 1/2 Stevia and my iced tea tasted perfect.  Nectresse is definitely not as sweet as Splenda (which may be good for some people).  Also, the texture of Nectresse is closer to sugar (versus the powdery texture of Splenda), which I liked.  I think for now I am going to stick with Splenda for my ice tea.  But I do plan to try Nectresse in some of my recipes that require sugar since I don't really like Splenda in some of my recipes that require sugar.  I will update my review after trying it in food.

I am no great fan of artificial sweeteners in general.  Still holding on to the belief that nothing tops sugar for taste and I use so little I do not worry a lot about the number of calories.  As for health affects of sugar, I am hesitant to find fault with it over what we are hearing now concerning some of the artificial sweeteners. However, this appears to be a good alternative to nutrasweet and is quite good.  The familiar crystal form seems to give it the texture of sugar as well.  Unlike many sweeteners, there is no chemical aftertaste.  All in all, a this appears to be a great product if you are attempting to avoid sugar.  Only time will tell if it falls to the same health concerns of others as it becomes more popular.

column9: Good, but I prefer Splenda; concerns about tooth decay
column10: Nectresse is great for those who will not use artificial sweeteners but still want to indulge in sweet things. It is all natural, made from monk fruit, but has zero calories. It is made by the same company that makes Splenda. One packet of Nectresse is equivalent to two teaspoons of sugar.I am a big user of Splenda so that is what I will compare it to. How does it taste? To me it is slightly less sweet than Splenda. It lacks that sharp, sweet taste, but still imparts a nice sweet flavor. The texture? It is much more grainy than Splenda -- more like regular sugar, which may or may not be a plus for you. I prefer the finer powdery texture of Splenda as it blends more easily when sprinkled over food and used in liquids.So why did I knock it down a star? Because there was no notation anywhere on the box or on their website about Nectresse and tooth decay. The fact is artificial sweeteners will not promote tooth decay. But since Nectresse is all natural, it could promote tooth decay just like regular sugar. I searched their website but could not find any information on this, but I'm pretty sure this is the case. So, from this perspective, I feel the artificial sweeteners like Splenda may be better for oral health.Because of all these reasons, I'm sticking to Splenda. But if you are one of those people who do not like using artificial sweeteners, then Nectresse is the perfect alternative.

column9: First there were pink packets, then blue, then yellow. NOW we have ORANGE! It's all subjective
column10: I received a sample packet of this new sweetener from Amazon as part of their Vine Reviewer program.I'll say up front that my "regular" sweetener is Sweet `n Low and I guess I'm accustomed to it. I use about 2/3 of a "pink packet" in an 10 oz cup of coffee or 12 oz glass of iced tea and it's just the right sweetness. I've tried both Splenda (the company that makes Nectresse) and Equal and I find that a full "yellow" or "blue" packet is not sweet enough. So this was a good chance to try something new.Honestly, while it didn't have an "after taste" it didn't blow me away. There are other things to consider when choosing a "calorie-free" sweetener that I'd like to point out:1- These zero calorie sweeteners will help those on a diet but only so much. A teaspoon of sugar contains only 15 calories. So we are talking about saving 30 calories here; that's not much.2- There are four  ingredients to Nectress and one of them is "sugar".  Here's the description: Ingredients Erythritol, Sugar, Monk Fruit Extract, Molasses. But still no "calories". The Monk Fruit is the difference. Note also that the product is white so the sugar is obviously "refined".3- If I read the package correctly it is not made for baking. So consider that. It comes only in packets that are about twice as thick as a normal SUGAR packet. Someone did point out - see their comment - that the website says it can be used in baking.)And then there is the issue of cost. You will note that - at least as of today (July 4th) the product is "not yet available" and there is no price. I think people consider their sweeteners also based on cost. So I can't pass judgment on the value or cost/benefit of Nectresse until pricing is available.I'll finish using the 40-pack samples that Amazon sent to Vine reviewers as it still works. But I'll withhold final judgement until the product becomes widely available.And, like any food product, remember that TASTE is SUBJECTIVE.I hope you found this review both informative and helpful.Steve Ramm"Anything Phonographic"

column9: surprisingly neutral flavor with no aftertaste, but perhaps less sweet than some sugar substitutes
column10: As some background, I should disclose that I regularly use Splenda -- most frequently in plain greek yogurt, either mixed in with some fruit or some other flavoring such as vanilla beans.  In the past I have regularly used Nutrasweet.  I have tried Stevia but I found that I did not like its aftertaste.  I never warmed to saccharine because of its bad aftertaste, too.  I have used Splenda blends in baking with good results as well, though I seldom bake any sweets any more due to dietary reasons.What I liked about Nectresse was that it didn't seem to add any flavor to my yogurt beyond sweetness.  I detected no aftertaste at all, and the sweetness itself was fairly mild.  By comparison, the same amount of Splenda (one packet per 8 ounces of yogurt) has a higher level of sweetness.Just to confirm my perceptions, I decided to taste both Nectresse and Splenda by themselves.  In this taste test, I again found Nectresse to have a slightly lower level of sweetness.  Nectresse looks a bit more like sugar -- small grains versus fine white powder.  Beyond the different appearance and slightly different intensity level, the products were nearly identical in that they both taste clean with a hint of an aftertaste that is apparent when consumed alone but is masked when used as they normally would be -- mixed with other ingredients.I'll leave it to others to debate how natural this product is.  In addition to the hyped monk fruit extract, it also contains erythritol, sugar, and molasses.  In fact, erythritol is the first ingredient listed, so I assume that means that the product, by weight, contains more of that than the other ingredients.  According to what I read online, erythritol is much less likely to cause intestinal discomfort than other sugar alcohols because it is largely absorbed in the small intestine.  I've never been bothered by any sugar alcohol in this regard, however, except on the lone unfortunate occasion when I consumed WAY too much sugar-free chocolate and had a regretful afternoon.

I am disappointed in this product. First, there's a distinct aftertaste. Secondly, it is not as sweet as they promise, and doesn't work at all in cold drinks.  If you need a sugar substitute I suggest Somersweet, not perfect either but better than this.  Sorry I was taken in by the promises.
This is an OK produce to help sweeten coffee but if your wanting a high sweet this isn't one that will do that.  I will use it but keep hoping they can come up with one safe and SWEET.
I've been trying to use less artificial sweeteners and this product is here to the rescue.It's sweet and does the job on cold and hot drinks. I haven't used it for cooking yet. Can't wait.

column9: Nectress not "natural" like they claim & contains refined sugar
column10: They claim this product is all natural and made from monk fruit.  But monk fruit is not the only ingredient in Nectresse, nor is it even the primary ingredient. The first and most abundant ingredient in Nectresse is actually ERYTHRITOL, a sugar alcohol commonly derived from corn, the vast majority of which has been genetically modified (GM) in the U.S.  As some others here have attested, sugar alcohols give some people cramps or other digestive issues.The second ingredient in Nectresse is REFINED SUGAR, which more than likely comes from GM sugar beets.The third ingredient in Nectresse is monk fruit, which they claim is extracted using a natural process involving both water and heat rather than chemicals -- this is good.But the fourth and final ingredient in Nectresse is MOLASSES which, once again, is a sugar more than likely derived from GM sugar beets.  (Producers that use sugar from sugar cane, after all, typically indicate this on their ingredient labels!)So three out of the four ingredients used in Nectresse appear to be derived from bioengineered crops, and two of these ingredients are refined sugars! And since erythritol is a sugar alcohol, as well as the most abundant ingredient in Nectresse, they can legally claim under F.D.A. guidelines that it has zero calories per serving.But the fact that Nectresse more than likely contains ingredients derived from GM sources means that it is hardly the "natural" product that they're hyping it up to be. Sure, Nectresse contains a little bit of monk fruit which, like the stevia plant, contains compounds that are naturally very sweet, but that do not provide the body with calories in the same way as sugar. But the other ingredients found in Nectresse can hardly be considered natural.

I'm not sure how this monkfruit thing works, and I keep feeling like there must be some trick.... but so far I love this sweetener. It's excellent in tea, on cereal, and on fruit. If anything, it seems to make me feel good. (It is used as a medicine by the Chinese.)My only real gripe is that I can't compost or recycle the foil-lined packets... but that's really not a deal breaker. :)

column9: Finally a no calorie sweetner I can use!!!
column10: I don't know what it is but I have never been able to handle no calorie sweeteners. I've tried them all. In some it's the aftertaste but in ALL of them I would get a horribly upset stomach within minutes of ingesting it. I saw a commercial for Nectresse and decided to give it a try. I had my first packet of it yesterday in a cup of black coffee. I added nothing else except the Nectresse. No after taste at all. Tastes just like I used regular sugar. Then I waited for the stomach upset. It never came!!! I believe the folks at Splenda have hit the nail on the head. This stuff is good. Real good! I'll be using Nectresse from now on.

To me, sweet is sweet and that's what my sweet tooth demands! And, though, I didn't find Nectresse to taste EXACTLY like sugar or EXACTLY like Splenda, the alternative sweetner that I use, Nectresse DID satisfy my nagging cravings and tasted pretty darn good in things that I need to liven up like a boring dollop of cottage cheese. What is most sweet is that Nectresse is an all-natural, zero calorie sweetner; this fact alone has now made it my number one sweeter OVER Splenda, in light of all the health concerns that the chemical mix of Splenda has posed throughout the health-conscious community.I mean anything made of fruit, in this case, monk fruit sounds just darn right good to me. What is even better and really sweetens the brand name even more is that monk fruit is harvested from small family owned farms; this deserves an A-plus alone!I also like the durable packets that manufacturers have packaged Nectresse in. They are stiff enough to stand upright on my kitchen counter as opposed to the flimsy paper on the market that drops the granules everywhere.My only qualm, as others have stated, is that Nectresse does contain some sugar; not a good thing for those of us who are trying to eliminate the additive from our diets. In my case, however, health rules out, and Nectresse has found a permanent place on my shelf in the cupboard as an RX to sprinkle sweet in a moment's notice for that unpredictable monster of temptation!Stacy Lytwyn, Marketing Guru/Motivational Speaker/JournalistAuthor: CONSUMMATE CONNECTICUT: DAY TRIPS WITH PANACHE

Nectresse is definitely a viable alternative to sugar and other artificial sweeteners. The only thing I didn't like was the fruity after taste, which is understandable since it's made from monk fruit. However, I fear that the fruity after taste might conflict with whatever you happen to sprinkle it on. I probably wouldn't purchase this in the future, but for those who are looking for a healthier sugar alternative, this might be worth a try.

As my husband and I are big fans of Splenda, I thought I'd give this a try. I nearly bought the neat little jar of it, but then decided on the small box of packets. Wise choice!  It would have been an even bigger waste of money.  I tried this in iced tea tonight, and while I was game to try to finish the glass, my huband took one drink and got a horrible look on his face.  And as much as I tried to give it a go, I couldn't finish my glass.  The Nectress first hits your tongue with sweetness, then the sweetness seems to go away. But after you swallow, your entire tongue is engulfed (or attacked) in an unpleasant aftertaste. My husband desribed it as bitter, but I thought of it more as chemical.  Then it kind of burned on the way down.In a word: yuck. It's not as bad as Sweet-N-Low, but it's down there.

Usually picky about my sweeteners but unable to use sugar for a family member, I approached a new product with both anticipation and trepidation.  Into the coffee it went and, lo and behold, it was good.  Not real sugar good but way better than other non-sugar sweeteners.  Then the best surprise came when I made vanilla ice cream - the stuff was great!  Now, remember, tastes are all personal matters and I hate stevia which other folks love but, I would recommend this and I would (make that have) buy again.

column9: Passes the game night taste test.
column10: I put Nectresse out on the table when the coffee and tea was served. The people who used artificial sweeteners were offered only Nectresse on the table. There was no unpleasant after-taste that I detected myself. And, the best observation was that my usual crowd actually made no comment about this product at all, proving that it was as effective as all the other sweeteners that we have previously used, but has the added benefit of being a more natural product.Hardly a ground-breaking scientific discovery. However, when it comes to an everyday item like sweeter for coffee or tea, sometimes the best comment is that the sweetness is as expected, requiring no comment whatsoever.

I purchased this from Kroger as an alternative to a stevia-based sweetener (which I am pleased with).  Currently I'm non-diabetic and eat ludicrous amounts of cold cereal, plants, and dairy.  I just tried four packets of the Nectresse in a five-cup peach flavored hot tea.  I like it.  My palate is usually more bitter-sour so I can be turned off by too much empty sweetness.  I agree with another review that this product's taste is fruitier than other sweeteners.  Aftertaste doesn't affect my favorable opinion.Ingredients: erythritol, sugar, monk fruit extract, molasses

This artificial sweetener is not the worst I've ever tasted, and it is a plus that it is a so-called 'natural' artificial sweetener. But it does leave a definite unpleasant after taste to my palate. As such, I can only give it 3 stars.

As someone who tried many sweeteners, I was tempted to try Necrtesse.  In a nutshell, it seems to vary sweetness from one beverage to another.  I had to put several packets in a regular cup of tea to make it sweet, but not too sweet.  I then tried using it with peppermint tea.  Usually I do not need much sugar with my peppermint tea, but for some reason it made peppermint tea turn a tad bitter.  I guess this was a case of aftertaste.  In other words, this sweetener was all over the place on a sweetness scale.  That being said, I would still prefer this sweetener over aspartame.

I have a total sweet tooth, and routinely get shocked looks when people see how much sugar I add to my tea. To the extent possible, with cold drinks, I try and use Splenda, since it dissolves quickly and evenly. However, I've never liked it for hot drinks -- that wisp of bitterness and artificial taste comes across stronger. This new sweetener solves that problem, I've used it in a variety of hot teas and found it to be uniformly superior in taste to Splenda. I'll admit that I have no idea what monk fruit is, and obviously I haven't researched the effects of using this stuff for twenty years, but I'll certainly look at making the switch for my hot drinks!

There's not too much to say about this sweetener. I tested it in tea and coffee to see if the monk fruit would have any affect on the taste.In a regular-sized mug of coffee, I used 3 packets and I must say that I could taste a fruity twinge. It wasn't overpowering but it was definitely there.In the same size peppermint tea, the fruity twinge was still noticeable but less concerning, likely because it was tea.I would say that even if you like your food/drink extra sugary, you might want to use maybe one or two packets of this and then finish it off with general Splenda if bypassing the fruity taste is a big concern for you.

This variation of splendor imparts an undesireable fruity flavor in additon to sweetening you beverage.  I did not like it in coffee, but it may be okay in some types of herbal teas.  I definitely will not be jettisoning my Sweet and Low for it.

I have used sweeteners for as many years as I can remember...Being in a family with diabetes, I can well remember my aunt stockpiling sweeteners that were available then because she knew she needed to always have it available...guess it stuck with me...Now, I have to say that "taste" is most important to me, so I was prepared to be unsatisfied if it didn't taste good...Actually, the taste was somewhat surprising--it was very mild, so much so that I didn't think of its being sweet. However, I did like it in tea which is my normal morning drink.Now, the "only" thing that would prevent my using this product because of its being natural is...cost... We do not yet know the cost, but since the product comes individually packed in a special foiled container and since there is already a Splenda product, my ranking is based upon anticipating that this product will cost more than other sweetners (as many natural and low-calorie products do, which is sad but true...)In the past, for a regular cup of tea, I would use half a package of sweetner...so the mild flavor worked for me...If somebody really likes lots of a sugar taste, one package would probably not work for them...I would recommend it with my noted concerns...GABixlerReviews

Full disclosure: my doctor is one of the people responsible for bringing this product to market in the US. He had been telling me about monk-fruit based sweeteners for a few years prior to Nectresse being produced, so I was really excited to test out this sample.I've added this to berries and smoothies, so far, and all I can say is two thumbs up. No aftertaste, micro-granules dissolve quickly, and it's great to not be worrying about this being an artificial sweetener. Recently I thought I'd try cooking and baking with xylitol, let's just say there were mixed reactions to that. Xylitol, even in small amounts, can give you wicked bad gas. Nothing like that with Nectresse. I'm hopeful that they'll offer bulk quantities soon. Due to its concentrated sweetness, I imagine baking with it might present some logistical challenges, but if you've ever used stevia or any other non-bulking sweetener, then you already understand about that.

I've been using the original Splenda in my daily morning coffee for a very long time. I like how sweet it is and is zero calorie. But I must say that it does taste very "artificial" and almost slightly chalky just by itself. This new  creation from Splenda does taste much more like a real fruit. In other words, it tastes "more natural" and less chalky. And, it's still very very sweet, just like the original Splenda is.

We started with good ole pure cane sugar but medical and weight issues soon brought a plethora of substitutes for the original.  The search for the perfect artificial sweetener has not been without its hills and valleys.  The pink packets are just plain awful, the blue packets are a great improvement but a little on the chemical side, the yellow packets are not quite as sweet but a much better flavor and can be used easily in cooking.  Now we have the orange packets.  I am always up to try something new and glad to see a sweetener that is 100% natural after all the chemical controversy about other products.  However, my Nectresse results were mixed.  The flavor of Nectresse is definitely sweeter than Splenda (its parent company) and the Nectresse seems to pleasingly cut some of the bitterness in my super strong French roast coffee.  But the large grain size makes it less easy to shake evenly over cereal, yogurt or fruit and makes it quite difficult to dissolve.  The cold cereal test was not very successful for the same reason -- the Nectresse did not dissolve in the cold milk and was left as a super sweet residue in the bottom of the bowl.  If I don't do a lot of stirring while it is hot, it also does not dissolve well in the hot coffee.  It is unclear from the package whether it would work well and retain its sweetness in baking or cooking as Splenda (the yellow packet) does.  So I have a mixed review -- great taste but not so easy to use.

column9: I've tried a lot of sweeteners . .
column10: . . . And this is one of the best I've tried.  No after taste, it's not too sweet, it looks just like sugar; it doesn't act like a powder.  I've used it in hot drinks, iced drinks, on top of fruit and cereal and it tastes good on and in everything I've tried it with.No calories means a lot to me - I like some things to be sweet (iced tea, for instance), but worry about ingesting too many chemicals or calories.I especially like the fact that there are no chemicals, just natural products.  I'll definitely be buying this in the future.

I'm always on the lookout for ways to cut calories without sacrificing flavor, so I jumped at the chance to try Nectresse. In the past, artificial sweeteners have disappointed me with their fake flavor or icky aftertaste (especially Stevia--gross). Nectresse, so far, has struck just the right balance of natural flavor in my coffee and tea.

column9: Not bad, but regular Splenda is better.
column10: This product does have a nice flavor. However, it is somewhat more granular than regular Splenda. Also, I don't think that I would it for baking purposes.Overall...not bad though.

I ordered this on a whim one day when browsing around the internet for a decent tasting sugar substitute that was a natural as possible with no aspartame or saccharin.After reading up and doing some research on Nectresse (which is from the makers of Splenda), I was pleased to discover that it is advertised as being 100% all natural as it's made from the extract of Monk Fruit.  Apparently, Monk Fruit use dates back to the 13th Century in which monks in China began to utilize it for its natural sweetness and its health benefits.With this in mind, I decided to order this on Amazon, and as soon as it arrived I decided to give it a try.  I must say that I'm impressed.  The taste is very similar to sugar and in my opinion leaves no bad aftertaste.So far I have only used this in coffee and tea, as a topping for fresh fruit, and on oatmeal and cereal, but I have only great things to say about it.According to the label, this has 0 calories, 0g of fat, and 2g of carbs per serving, and each packet provides the same sweetness as 2 teaspoons of sugar.Will buy again!

I've struggled for years to find the right sweetener. Just when I think I've found it, the negative reviews start to emerge about possible health problems. This happened first with Saccharin, Equal and then Splenda. I used Equal for years then switched to Splenda, which I like but of course the health concerns again. I don't enjoy Stevia at all, it has a bitter aftertaste that's very unpleasant. Xylitol can cause stomach upset, plus it's way too sweet for my taste.Today I discovered Nectresse and love it. It has the same consistency as sugar and dissolves easily. I hate the way Stevia sits on top of the surface of liquid and takes many stirs to dissolve.I used two packets of Nectresse in a cup of tea and it was perfect, just as sweet as Splenda but without the powdery feel.MY only concern is the cost, loose Nectresse comes in a small 5.9 oz canister. That doesn't seem like enough to cook with and the price is around seven dollars.I may have to continue to use Splenda for larger recipes, since it's more cost effective. If the company offers a bigger canister or package of loose Nectresse in the future then I would consider switching from Splenda permanently.I will definitely buy this product again. Finally I might have found THE ONE!!

column9: Pretty good, but I still prefer Stevia
column10: In the last year I've switched from saccharine, NutraSweet and Splenda to more natural, low-carb or no-carb sweeteners.  I've read too many bad things about the artificial ones, and my low-carb diet doesn't allow sugar, honey or agave nectar.  I'm in love with liquid stevia, because it works equally well in hot or cold beverages, and also bakes well.  It's somewhat expensive, but I feel confident that it's not poisoning me.Nectresse Natural No-Calorie Sweetener is a close second to Stevia in my personal preferences.  I found it to be easy to use in measured packets, and has a similar consistency to table sugar.  It sweetens well, although I thought it had a strange aftertaste (but some people say the same thing about Stevia).  It's also less expensive per serving than Stevia.I will probably look for this product again, when my box is empty.  It's nice to have  several options for natural non-caloric sweeteners.  But I still prefer Stevia.

...a natural sweetener that taste great with no aftertaste! I've tried plain stevia and the ones that are a blend of stevia with other sweeteners, and I still can't get past the aftertaste. I've been buying "Ideal" but it's still not "all natural".Nectresse is just what I've been looking for. I do need 1 1/2 packets to feel the sweetness in my coffee, but that's not a problem for me.  I only wish it would come in 100-count, instead of 40.

column9: not as sweet as it claims
column10: It is just an OK product, I don't feel it is that sweet and does seem to have an odd flavor to it. I guess it depends on the person some love it some hate and some just like it. I won't buy it but it isn't horrible. I have been using stevia and some honey for sweetening most of the time so maybe my tastes are different.Get a sample of it before you buy a large container to see if you like it

There are several things I like about this new sweetener: zero calories, zero fat and only two grams of carbs per 1 packet serving. I also like that it's "100% natural," and that it definitely does sweeten whatever I add it to. But for me (and this may not apply to ALL tasters) there is a slight taste that is hard to identify. Not exactly a bitter aftertaste but a taste I'm not used to associating with sugar. Whatever the nectresse taste is, I'm not crazy about it; but I will say this -- it doesn't last long, and the sweetness does last.

column9: worst aftertaste of all sugar substitutes
column10: My primary application for sweeeteners is in Iced Tea.  Though I don't like the tea-flavored syrup served in some southern states (and now spreading), I do like a moderate level of sweet in my iced tea.  My personal opinion is that all sugar substitutes so far (saccarine, aspartame, sucralose, stevia, nectresse) have bad enough aftertastes to make any of them unacceptable.However, In the interests of calorie-reduction I have experimented with mixtures of sugar and the pretenders.  I can tolerate blends of sugar with aspartame or sucralose with approximately 50% of the sweet coming from sugar.  Aspartame seems to work best, with the sugar eliminating the aspartame's aftertaste.  With sucralose a touch of the chlorinated solvent aftertase still leaks through. ( Note, I think the soda companies have made the same discovey.  Pepsi Next and Dr. Pepper 10 are both mixes)I just tried Nectresse and the bitter, metallic aftertaste was not improved, and may have been amplified, by the mix with sugar.  Nectresse is definitly off my shopping list.  But try it for yourself, because everyone's taste varies.  Some people even like brussel sprouts!?!

column9: Stevia In The Raw is better
column10: Nectresse, from the makers of spelnda needs improvementThe main reason -  using the semi-sweet sugar alcohol erythritol as it's main ingredient was a mistake. It's not sweet enough.I have to use twice as much as I do With Stevia in the raw to get the same sweetness.It's not worth it. a 40 count box didn't even last a week

The ingredients of this sweetener are as follows:  Erythritol, Sugar, Monk Fruit Extract, Molasses.  Erythritol is a sugar alcohol that can occur naturally.  So that makes this sweetener "100% Natural," as emblazoned on the box.  The problem is, I detect a distinctly chemical aftertaste.  It could be the molasses, but it tastes more chemical than molasses to me.I am not such a purist about my artificial sweeteners.  But I do expect them to taste like sugar - and one would think, with sugar being the second ingredient, this one would have an advantage.  Not so.  (Don't get me started on the "Made from Monk Fruit" labeling.  When it is the 3rd of 4 ingredients?  And what does a monk fruit look like anyway?  Or taste like?  Does it taste like Nectresse?)My favorite sweetener is Splenda Essentials with B vitamins.  Nectresse is also made by Splenda.  It has a sugarlike consistency and dissolves easily in my coffee.  However, as artificial sweeteners go, it is my least favorite.  I might actually forego sweetener if this were the only one available.

Though this product is pitched as being made from monk fruit nectar, its primary ingredient is Erythriol, a semi-sweet sugar alcohol that has been around for a long time and is nothing new. This is just another marketing gimmick to spin off a new zero-calorie sweetener under a different label. It is a ruse not based on predominance of monk fruit sweetness which is comprised mainly of fructose and mogrosides. You could get something very similar tasting if you mixed Stevia with Erythriol, but I guess they can't do that because that's already been patented as another product sold as Truvia. My guess is all they have left is a product that combines Thaumatin with Erythriol and call it something else.

column9: It is long over due for the Splenda Company to make a natural sweetner.
column10: This is a natural sweetner made by the company that makes Splenda.  I have waited for a long time for these companies that make artificial sweetners that can potentally be dangerous to us to come up with something healthier that does not cause tumors and things in humans. I wanted something safer.  This new one  is made with monk fruit and lists real sugar in the ingredients as well,  which I was surprised by.  Also, it taste okay but not as good as some of the Stevia products.  I will wait until they come out with something better before switching from pure via and other natural sweetners made with stevia. This simply does not tase good enough for me to use regularly.

Ok, just to let u in on soomething. I received some samples of nectresse. I tried it this morning on my cereal. Well, the taste was fine, BUT.....all afternoon I have the worst stomach cramps and dry heaves. Has to be that as I really haven't had anything else since I felt so crummy. Take heed-if u r gonna try it-use a small amount, or don't use it at all.

column9: I don't recommend this treat for your dog.
column10: From a taste perspective, your dog will probably love this product; however, I do not recommend that you buy it for your dog.  As with any dental treat, the purpose is for the dog to chew it and work the toothpaste that is in the treat around the teeth to get them nice and clean.  The problem with this treat is that dogs will literally eat them in three bites, which means that the treat is not working on the teeth.  Also, because the dog eats them in three bites, this product is much more likely to put your dog at risk of choking on them.  This product is very expensive and, from my opinion, I just don't recommend them.
Gave them away to Gleaners food bank at Christmas time, I hope they help brighten someones Christmas and New Year.

I got these for something different.  I LOVE the High Protein Almond Balls and like some of the other nut butter balls.  These are just OK and I doubt that I would buy them again.  I'll just stick with the others.
My health food store no longer stocked this item & I was thrilled to find it on Amazon.  A healthy snack option for the chocolate lover!

This product is absolutely amazing. I bought this deodorant in July, at the worst of the sweating/body odor season. Any deodorant I bought wasn't working (my issue was body odor, not really sweating as much), and it was getting to be so frustrating. I did a lot of research before buying this (mainly trusting reviews from various internet sites), because I couldn't justify spending so much money on a product that might not work. Well, I am certainly thankful for all of those reviews of it. I can't adequately express how happy I am with this deodorant. To say it is "life changing" might seem a little dramatic, but I truly think it has been. I am no longer self-conscious, I feel comfortable with myself throughout the entire day, and it just makes me feel so much better about myself. It does not have a strong smell during the day, which I really like. I don't walk around smelling like "cotton" or "lavender" or whatever else I've been forced to smell like for the past many years. I just smell like me.I have waited this long to review the product because sometimes my deodorants work for a week or two, but then stop altogether. But I can safely say that I have been using Clinical Protection (Motion Sense) for four months now, and I have not once been unhappy with the results.The most important thing, though, is to USE IT AS DIRECTED!! You HAVE TO apply it at night, and just at night!! It took me a few days to get used to, and once in a while when I'm tired I forget, but if you follow the directions (two clicks to each underarm, AT NIGHT), you will be amazed with the results. I carried regular deodorant with me for the first few days because I was afraid I might start smelling mid-day, but I did not once have to use it.I would recommend this deodorant to anybody! I rarely, rarely review products online, but I am so happy with this deodorant that I felt the need to spread it's wonder with everybody else.Good luck! If you buy it, you will not be disappointed!

column9: Great product (if you follow the directions)
column10: Most complaints about this product is that it doesn't work as well as anticipated. I will say this, if you follow the directions and apply the product at night you will be amazed the next day. However, if you throw caution to the wind and put it on in the morning expecting it to work as it should, you will be terribly disappointed. The only reason I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is simply because it made me have to change my routine a bit, which is a little tough to get used to. Otherwise, this is a great product!
Lift mechanism to deliver deodorant to top for application to the skin is broken on both containers. This renders it useless. I will not purchase this packaging again.
Hands down. the. best. deodorant.After working for 10 hours, my underarms still smell and feel powder fresh.  It is so effective that you don't even need to use it everyday.

column4: Superstar "It is only by risking that we live...
column10: I must admit, I don't have the odor I once had with other deodorants. I really like the clean smell and have finally followed the instructions...I apply at night and see the difference during the day. I will continue to use this although a bit expensive. I purchased this size for $10. It's $11 on this site. But, if it works, it is worth it. I am curious to see how it holds up during the summer!

This product is the best!!!!!!1 I've tried almost every brand out there--clinical and non-clinical, and I work out every day, so I sweat a lot. So far this is the best deoderant/antiperspirant out there!!

I have tried many brands over the years.. I was introduced to this one out of a waft of a friend who was wearing it, it smelled clean and fresh like it was just applied.. I can't for the life of me understand why I give into the hype and try other brands, they have ALL failed me.. I don't know if it is the new formulations or my own body's chemistry has changed since grad school.. but this is the only one that keeps me from smelling unpleasant. I appreciate that it is a bit expensive but it is larger and it lasts, you don't have to reapply midday..

The Degree Women Clinical Protection deodorant I bought was less expensive than buying it at a local pharmacy or supermarket and the shipping was fast.  I would definitely consider purchasing this again.

column9: One of the worst antiperspirants I've tried
column10: I used to use Secret Clinical but I noticed it wasn't giving me the same results now that it used to.  I thought I would give Degree Clinical a try.  When I use it, I sweat a LOT...far more than I ever did with Secret Clinical, and far, far more than I did using Sweat Block.  I was very disappointed in the results I got with this product.

I love peanut candy.  Unlike peanut brittle, which I also adore, the peanuts are in a not too sugary clear candy that has a hint of molasses I believe.  I grew up eating Lance's brand peanut candy.  This was the first time I'd had the candy made by another company.  It was very good and hard to share.  It's crunchy, sweet, and peanutty.  Yum!

I've been buying this brand for years just because it is one of the few available. It has basic simple ingredients (no chemicals or artificial additives) but many times, even 'fresh' it has a slight off flavor. But as I said, it's hard to find any and this will do. I do have a problem with the price - I can buy a 9 oz. can for 2.99 at my dollar store, so even two cans amounting to 18 oz. will still not cost as much as this one 16 oz package. I guess they have to get their shipping costs in SOME where, but to me, that should be a perk of being a Prime member. Prices not so high as to infer that they are sneaking the shipping cost into the bottom line. This is not always so, though - many times amazon's cost is very competitive - And I LOVE the two day shipping. Instant grat!

Unfortunately I am unable to give a positive review because the product was stale, all the squares were stuck together and literally "hard as rocks". Such a disappointment since I've been anticipating their arrival...
Don't know if I should review this product. Afraid everyone will by them out and I won't be able to get them any more. If you like good peanut brittle that you will love these little morsels.

I gave this to my son as a stocking stuffer because he loves popcorn, and I was trying to find a way to make it more fun. He wasn't sure about it at first, but it was surprisingly good, and really does taste like chocolate and marshmallows! We generally won't use it on all of the popcorn, but we'll separate a portion out so we can have some sweet and some salty.

I am a Pac-Man fan from way back and when I saw this can of energy drink, I had to add it to my collection.  It makes a fine piece of memorabilia for any collector of Pac-Man, 80's, or soda cans.  Unfortunately I can't comment on the taste of the product inside...I don't do energy drinks.FYI...although this is listed as a "toy", it is certainly not meant for children to play with.

I am so disappointed with my candy boxes.  I bought 4 boxes 40, 80, and two 90s.  Each box had pretty much the same candy with the exception of maybe three different ones.  One of my boxes arrived with a torn handle.  I will never order these candy boxes again, and I really wish that I could return them without paying a mountain load of money for the shipping and handling.  I give the boxes two thumbs down.

If I had the time I could probably hunt down all these candies and package them in a basket for 33% of the price, but who wants to go through all that trouble.  This was nicely packaged and the 28-year-old friend I gave this to loved it!  It was all the candy he wasn't allowed to buy as a pre-teen kid!  Some memories from the snack bar at my little league games were also in there.

column9: good amount but missing key items
column10: i purchased this one and the 80's one and they basically had the same candy in each.  there were some differences, but were missing popular candy that we remembered at each time.the amount of candy and the freshness were great, but for the price of the box and shipping- i could have put something cheaper together myself.it was a cool concept and gift, but disappointing when opened.

column9: Great gift idea for young and old.
column10: Bought 60s for daughter and 90s for granddaughter. What a conversation gift. It turns out I should have bought one for everyone at our Christmas party. The gift box made it perfect.

I can go into any store that sells candy and find everything that they have in the 90s crate and it would cost MAYBE $10 and get a nice REUSABLE basket to put it in from the thrift shop. They don't even have Crybabies or Warheads or Bubble Tape!!!!! RIP OFF!!!!!!!!

Opening the box gives a sensory sugar rush!  It would have been difficult to collect all the different candies represented in this collection, so you can justify the cost.  I got it for my son to remind him of his childhood favorties.  It is a fun gift for the drug store candy lover.

I wouldn't give this as a gift, the amount of candy is kind of pitiful, it's like, < $10 worth, and the box is mostly stuffed with paper space-fillers. There are several full-sized candies and then a handful of jolly ranchers, fireballs, bazooka gums, etc. Perhaps use it as a base and then put some more candy in it before gifting it.As others have said, none of the candy is particularly "90's" - it's all stuff that is still sold today.Basically, cute idea, poor execution.

I purchased this for $7.40 for my husband and had it shipped to his office. The candy was a big hit with he and his coworkers! That being said, I would never pay full price as there's not a whole lot in the box. If you can grab this when it's <$10 and get free shipping I say go for it! :)

I was very unhappy.I have bought stuff from them befor and was quite pleased. But..... When I received this item I was furious. There was not even close to $26 worth of candy for one.And it was just candy did not seem to be from the 90's. Just not happy at all.

My Mother bought the 90's box for me as a Christmas present, and it was BY FAR my favorite gift of the season! LOL! I am a huge candy freak, and this box had all of my favorites: apple heads, pop rocks, airheads, nerds, blow pops, you name it. It came packaged well, and was such a fun surprise when I opened it and dug through all of the candy inside. I loved it so much that I just ordered another one for myself! I think this makes a great gift, especially for people who you know just absolutely LOVE candy. 5 stars!

I bought this for my nephew's "sweet sixteenth" birthday. He lives in another state and I wanted to get a little something extra for the special day. I ordered it w/ my prime membership and it was delivered on time. My nephew and all of his friends absolutely loved it!!! It was a huge hit!

My son turned 18 this year, and what do you get an 18 year old?? This candy box was a lot of fun for him. He reminisced with his brothers about their childhood and the memories the different candy brought back. I recommend this for a fun gift idea. And for a trip back in time!!
I lived for my weekly (sometimes daily) astro pop in the nineties. WHERE IS IT? I couldn't be more disappointed.
I bought this for My little brother for his 13th Birthday gift and he told Me I was his coolest sister & he loved all the candy that came with it

column9: Best and finest tequila to date
column10: There's no much to say - If you want to taste the best Tequila Mexico has ever produced, buy this bottle.If you think you have tasted Tequila because you tried one like "Tequila Jose Cuervo Especial", let me start by telling you that's simply the worst Tequila flavor I have ever tasted. It doesn't even taste like real Tequila - I don't even know what that thing is, but I definitely hate it and it causes me the worst hangovers.Tequila Herradura is one of the best Tequila producing houses in Tequila Jalisco (the best one in my opinion), and this one (Herradura Selección Suprema) is to Tequila like Cognac is to wine. It has a lot of body and an extremely good flavor. While it's strong, it doesn't burn like plain alcohol. It just brings Tequila heaven to your mouth.Don't use it for Margaritas, with lemon or any mix for that matter. That's just as bad as mixing a good Cognac with Coke. Taste it alone and slowly if you want to have the right experience.TIP on buying Tequila: Always check that the bottle says this (no exception!):1) 100% Agave.2) Made in Tequila, Jalisco.

column4: Robin Thomas "CEO, Really Great Freaking Things"
column10: I'm drinking this stuff as I write this, and have been for several weeks. My business involves me working some very long hours, often late into the night, and it's all thanks to my Sodastream Energy that I survive.Bear in mind it's HIGHLY CONCENTRATED. No kidding around. Even just licking the drips from the neck of the bottle is enough to give me a buzz. When I was first trying this, I didn't realize that it's more concentrated than regular Sodastream syrups and so much less syrup is needed per unit of water. So I mixed it with some seltzer water in the same quantity I would any Sodastream mix.Whew. It made me all jittery and I swear it gave me heart palpitations -- and mind you I'm a perfectly healthy and fit 23 year-old male.DO NOT drink any of this stuff undiluted because it will, no joke, kill you.That said, it tastes just like Red Bull (maybe even better!) and by no means do you need a Sodastream machine to use it. I just mix it with cans of seltzer water from the supermarket or even regular uncarbonated tap water, and it's great.
LOVE THIS PRODUCT! Tastes just like Red Bull and is WAY cheaper. Don't drink the whole bottle as it will keep you up even hours later. I mix it half strength with other flavors.

column9: Superior taste and nutrition among the puffed cereals
column10: I have enjoyed standard puffed wheat for more than 30 years. This puffed Kamut performs similarly but is superior in taste and texture. I find it delicious and a favorite of my young grandchildren. Longer grains and somewhat more chewey than standard puffed wheat, this product ranks especially high for a wide range of vitamins and minerals. Very satisfied with the product and find the pricing here provides a substantial savings over even supermarket prices.

Puffed Cereal Granola2 cups oats (not quick-cooking)1 cup puffed kamut1 cup puffed rice1/4 cup canola oil1/4 cup pure maple syrup (or to taste)chopped nuts, optionaldried fruits, optional(This recipe is easily doubled, tripled, quadrupled, or whatever)Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.Mix first five ingredients in large mixing bowl. Add nuts, if using, and mix. Spread mixture onto cookie sheet, bake about 15 minutes or until mixture is lightly browned. Add dried fruit, if using, and mix. Let cool on cookie sheet. Store in airtight container (lasts quite a while) or in ziploc bag. Makes about 4-6 servings.Arrowhead Mills Puffed Rice, 6-Ounce Units (Pack of 12)Brown Family Farm Pure Vermont Maple Syrup, 32-Ounce JugEden Dried Cranberries, Organic, 4-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 5)

column9: Excellent alternative to Cheerios for your baby
column10: I bought this as an alternative to Cheerios for my baby when he started learning how to eat finger foods.  In my quest for the Cheerio alternative, even the organic cereals had ingredients (ie sugar, salt) that I didn't want to feed my son.  Just because something is organic, doesn't mean it's healthy.I like this because it's minimally processed.  It has one ingredient: Kamut. No sugar or anything else.  It's organic and just the right size for him to pick up with his fingers.  I can feel good feeding this to my son.I've tried it and I like it, too!

I'm a big fan of puffed wheat because it's very Weight Watcher friendly.  I usually buy the Arrowhead Mills Puffed Wheat from Amazon (link below), but alas, it was out of stock!! So I bought this as an alternative in the meantime.  The label describes it as The "Great Grandfather of Grains", being a close relative of wheat.The taste is pretty much the same as puffed wheat, maybe not as sweet,  but the puffs are much bigger, and more elongated.  Also a little different in color - slightly darker.My favorite is still puffed wheat, but this gets an "A" from me for a suitable alternative.Arrowhead Mills Puffed Wheat Cereal, 6-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)
taste great,organic, good value ....kids love em.. i add a lil honey and bam u have smackstry it , get some oh yea.
These puffs are light but quite satisfying. Delicious with or without milk. A healthy munching food to be enjoyed any time of the day.
I'm watching my weight & this is wonderful & low calorie!  My 2 year old loves it - thankfully because I'm moving her away from the sugary cereals.

I purchased the cases of this cereal because it is organic, it fills me up, and due to the nose dive recognized within the U.S. economy over the past four years, I am no longer able to afford much.Unfortunately, the last three cases I have ordered via Amazon have been stale.  I contemplated leaving this feedback because I am just thankful to have anything to eat.  However, after three cases of stale cereal that leaves an after taste due to the stale quality, I am having a difficult time stomaching this cereal anymore.For a couple more dollars, which I really did now wish to spend, but I am going to try to do so now, I have found that Nature's Path Kamut Puffs are "by far" extremely fresh in comparison.  It may be the Eco-bag that Nature's Path packages their cereal in, verses the softer plastic that Arrowhead packages their cereal in.  Not sure.
Puffed Kamut is a very good cereal and it has no salt which is wonderful for those of us on a low salt diet.  I love it with a sliced banana.

column9: Organic puffed kamut at a great price
column10: Excellent quality, and a very good price... especially if you have an Amazon.com Prime membership and get free two day shipping. The price is quite a bit better than those in our local health food stores and supermarkets. Arrowhead Mills is a premium brand in organic grains, and their puffed Kamut is an excellent product.  While you do have to buy a dozen six ounce bags to get the best deal, the two of us don't seem to have any difficulty using it up in a reasonable time period... the cereal is really good.As a vegetarian I appreciate having a source of top quality cereal grains at reasonable prices (we buy Arrowhead  puffed rice through Amazon.com as well).  I try to keep the amount of modern day wheat to a reasonable level in my diet, and find that Puffed kamut provides a similar flavor, without the concerns some experts have about wheat. In addition puffed kamut tastes great with fresh fruit, soy milk, and a light drizzle of honey.We also like having it delivered right to our door for less than two-thirds of what we'd pay for the Kamut alone in our local health food store. Less trips to shop, less stores to make the rounds of when we do go out, less things to lug home, and a noticeably lower price... what's not to like?

This Puffed Kamut is a real bargain.  I was looking for Puffed Rice online(store prices are way high) and had read about this product.  It's healthy for you and the price is very reasonable.  A pack of 12 seems like a lot at first but around here it goes pretty fast.  I sometimes eat it as a low fat snack right out of the bag, finger food that won't add sugar, salt and pounds.

column9: This is just what I wanted!
column10: I ordered this cereal on subscribe and save for the cheap price and because I enjoy the puffed grain cereals. I know the quality of most Arrowhead Mills products to be superior, so I took a chance on this puffed Kamut. It is perfect! Low calorie and low sugar! I put two cups into a bowl, pour some non-dairy milk over it with some vanilla stevia drops and it is the perfect under 200 calorie breakfast!

column9: The Best Wheat in the World
column10: Kamut....so what's this stuff. As they tell you on the package it's the grandfather of all wheat. It's bigger, better tasting and contains the stuff that's good for you. I try to find it locally in the store but no one (not even Wally World) has it. Being a diabetic makes any cereal selection tough but this is easy. Try it with unsweetened almond milk and a couple packets of sweetener. A great way to start the day.

I really like this cereal a lot..it's organic, has one ingredient, is tasty and stays crunchy in almond milk.  I eat it all the time and add some fresh fruit (blueberries or strawberries) and have a great, quick breakfast!

I have purchased these cereal for about four years now. I am in love with this flavor. It has such a more distinct flavor than regular wheat. The kernels are about twice the size of puffed wheat as well. You can not go wrong with this. I have it on autoship. I eat it with soy or almond milk for breakfast most days. If you are looking for a new cereal without all the sugar and high fructose corn syrup try this organic deliciousness for a change.
I use Arrowhead Mills Puffed Kamut as my breakfast (with milk) and snakes (eat dry). This is a king of suger free food you can use again and again. Amazon's price is about 20% lower than local store.

I like to mix puffed kamut with other cereals.  It tastes great!  After my local grocery store stopped carrying this item, I decided to order on-line.  My order came packaged well, in great condition, and I'm saving money by buying in bulk!

column9: Less than 5 months before it expires
column10: I love this cereal but I don't know if I'll be able to eat 12 bags of it in less than the 5 months I have before it expires.  You get a larger window of opportunity when you buy it in the store :(

What nicer thing to hear than your best friend telling you that his husband blurted this out with a big smile when they opened the package I sent them for their anniversary!  I had decided only days before I placed the order that I wanted to give them a bonsai tree if I could possibly afford it.  I was pleasantly surprised to see how reasonable this tree was, but admit I was worried: could it possibly be as lovely as the picture?  It was! The lovely juniper bonsai was almost an exact duplicate of the online image, with the same graceful lines and attractive traditional bonsai bowl.And although there was no option to enclose a gift card when I checked out (which is something I suggest the seller correct) I sent an email asking if a gift note with my specific wording could be added.  The seller did so: accurately written and at no charge.  In addition, my friends received their gift at the very earliest date within the window of time projected.  A wonderful gift at good price; delivered with better service than I could have expected.  What more could you ask for?

These are really great little trees, i have a 21 year old Japanese Garden Juniper bonsai tree and I love it! If you take good care of them and put them outside during the fall and the winter they will grow a ton in the spring when you bring them back inside. They are the perfect beginner's bonsai!

I thought the bonsai was a cute little tree at first, but I noticed little bugs on my desk where I kept the tree.  I didn't think about why they were they at first, but after 2 weeks, I noticed the tree was crawling from little mites that were coming up out of the soil.  I'm sure the seller didn't intend on this happening, but I'll never order another bonsai.Addition - Seller was great.  They recieved my email about the bus & offered me a full refund.  They explained it was not intentional & that flooding in their area may have caused it.

I bought this as a Christmas present for my boyfriend in 2009.  I was a bit nervous purchasing something so fragile..didn't know how the shipping and handling would treat it.  It arrived on time and very securely wrapped/packaged leaving no room for ruin.  Most importantly, it looked great- very similar to the picture.  This is our first experience with a bonsai tree and it continues to be a very healthy little plant.  Perfect for starters I'd say.

Bought this tree as a birthday gift for my mother. She has told me before that she always wanted one. :-) She loved it and was so excited!! She said that it came through the shipping process wonderfully and that the tree was beautiful. I would for sure buy from this seller again!

It looks almost identical to the one in the picture except for the bowl.  The bowl in the picture is BLUE.  The one I got was in a BROWN bowl!  The rock in the picture is black but the one I got is red but oh well.  It is very easy to care for and it is nice to look at.

Great price and it was very well packaged.  I kept it for 2 weeks before giving it as a gift and new branches were already starting.  the person I gave it to was very pleased with it.  I will buy another one in the near future.

Got this for my fiancée and he loved it! Unfortunately, he was not blessed with a green thumb and our tree passed away a couple months after getting it.Tree was in great health when we received it. Good packaging, too.
The tree came nicely packaged and was in great condition. I have had it for over 3 weeks now and it is still perfect.

I have NEVER written a review for ANYTHING before this Bonsai tree. I ordered it for my boyfriend's birthday and he absolutely loves it. It is larger and more impressive than I had imagined. It was delivered in less than a week. It was packaged  very well and arrived in perfect condition. I can not recommend this gift enough. It will not be the last one that I give.

I bought this bonsai tree as a Christmas gift for my dad, a total bonsai nut. It arrived in the mail in absolutely healthy condition - no brown, all in tact. It looks exactly like the picture! It looks so neat, I wanted to go order one for myself but now they are currently unavailable. Once they are available again, I definitely plan on purchasing it and to anyone debating purchasing it: do it. You will not be sorry.

Just received my first Bonzai tree - a 4-5 year old Juniper.  This thing is absolutely beautiful and well represented in the photograph provided on Amazon.  I also received the Bonzai Survival Manual.  Here's hoping I can use the second gift to learn enough to keep the first gift alive!
Got my tree a couple of weeks ago, and it's doing great! Contacted the seller about a couple of informational items and they responded quickly and cheerfully. I plan to purchase more :)
I thought this was A very good product and I'm very happy with it, this bonsai is very healthy and being a seventeen year old who collects bonsais and bamboo I was really satisfied

I just received my tree, and it is very similar to the one pictured. The tree made it through the USPS (Priority Mail) intact and looking quite healthy.The seller watered the plant just before packaging, sealed over the soil / base of the tree with plastic, and packaged the bowl and tree securely in a specially sized box. They also provided a guide for caring for my juniper bonsai and a small amount of fertilizer to be applied every 2-3 weeks. They really couldn't have done more to ensure my tree is and will remain healthy and beautiful.They left the tree quite bushy and the trunk has a nice shape, so with a little trimming I'll have the perfect tree.I hope it'll have a long and happy life on my desk for years! I'll update later with continuing status.Great product!EDIT: The branches of the tree were all curved up and the foliage's shape didn't look as great as I'd like it when the tree arrived. However, the branches lowered into much better positions in a few days. Now the tree looks gorgeous, and I'm not sure I'll trim it at all! It was the secure packaging that caused the branches to look mooshed, so wait a few days before you decide upon a foliage verdict (or begin trimming).I forgot to mention before, the tree is planted in a sandy soil to ensure optimal drainage. I water every 4-5 days by immersing the lower half of the bowl in water for 15 minutes.

I bought one of these for my dad for his birthday and he loved it.I also bought one for myself and my son to enjoy as we explore bonsai as a new hobby. The tree arrived safely and was vigorous and healthy. It is styled just like the Amazon picture, in a dense bushy head of foliage.I decided to re-style it. So I pruned and wired it into a more dynamic shape. It ended up in a striking diagonal, with nice movement in the branches and nice bushy foliage pads on each one. I think it came out great.  I like it even more this way than in its original styling.

I am very pleased with the packaging and arrival of the bonsai.  I decided to risk wasting the money and shipping in case it turned out and it is great.  I now have a lovely addition to my desk and something that will sooth my mood for years to come.

I bought this as a christmas gift for my mother who is hard to shop for. It arrived with the bowl and tree saran wrapped together and then the box was filled with styrafoam peanuts.  The tree was healthy and watered when it arrived.  Includes brief description of care and small bag of fertilizer. A+ two months and tree is growing day by day.

column9: A bit smaller than I expected
column10: The bonsai tree shipped to me was rather small. However, I don't have much experience with bonsai trees so I wouldn't be able to tell you if the tree is too small to be 5+ years old. The bowl it came in is nice, but does not have as ornate of a design as depicted in the picture, but the seller did state that bowls would vary. I will say this for them though, I was debating whether or not to order the tree for my father for Christmas; I thought that he would like it, but according the shipping tables, the tree would not arrive before Christmas. I contacted the seller about this and they offered me a free upgrade first class.

column9: pretty tree, but it didn't last
column10: The tree is beautiful, but ours died within a month.  Not sure what went wrong; we have other plants in our house that have lived without a problem; my husband even works on a farm!  Not sure if it was diseased or we just over/under watered it.  It seems like a finicky plant.
Nice bonsai.  The picture shows the tree in a blue bowl.  The tree is was sent is in a beige bowl. So I suggest you specify the color of container when you order.

Sent quickly and safely, it's a cute little tree, I love the bowl. This tree is very nice and I appreciated the care instructions that came with it. I was extremely happy with this order and will defiantly purchase from this company again in the future.  The tree I received was very similar to the one pictured :)

This turned out to be a very nice little tree for a great price.  Several months later, I still haven't managed to (completely) kill it.  I'm back on the product page because I looked up from the sofa and realized I hadn't watered the thing for a month, so the tree is starting to turn a little brown.  It's a long way to the sink, so maybe I'll just order another one.

column9: nice looking tree but it died after a month: o
column10: Nice looking tree that came well protected against shipping damage. Unfortunately, it didn't last and died after a month; it was a gift that was sent with not one, but two books on how to look after bonsai trees! I am no horticulturalist, so I really cannot determine the cause of death, but it seems these trees are not as sturdy as some other plants and trees. Next time I will send a cactus; can't go wrong there!

This product is FABULOUS!  I had a cat impacted with hairballs who wouldn't eat.  I literally squirted this down his throat twice a day.  Kept him going until he could throw up the hairball and begin to recover on his own.  Now, my 15 year old cat wants some every morning.  Has increased her weight a little, has made her coat look better, and she is generally quite happy.  LOVE THIS PRODUCT!

The ad was for CatSure Meal Replacement, and what we received was the Meal Supplement. I went ahead and used the product as we have difficulty finding this locally,  but next time will ensure that what we receive is the meal replacement and NOT the supplement.  Advice would be to contact seller to make sure what you receive is what was advertised and visa versa.

We wern't sure what to give our old cat (21 years old) seemed she didn't like anything and she was loosing weight.We tried Cat-Sure she loved it.we would open a can pour it into ice cube trays and freeze them.Thaw and warm at least one a day and she loved it. We think her last days were a bit easier because of it.

My 14 year old cat wasn't eating, had to have a tooth pulled, and was generally miserable.  He's always been thin and a picky eater.  After the tooth was pulled, he was interested in food, but wouldn't eat.  I had to squirt it in his mouth a few times before he got the idea I wasn't going to give up.  Once he started drinking it, he loved it and began asking for it.  His coat is thicker and doesn't fall out as much.  He's put on weight, and even if he's having a 'sick day' from hair balls, he can drink this without throwing up the rest of the day.  He's so much happier and plays more.  Now even if there's a day when he isn't interested in food, I don't worry as much because he's so much healthier now.  Thank You !!
