Here in California, we have an ongoing threat with natural disasters, and I'm thinking specifically of earthquakes. All electricity, natural gas, most communications and transportation could be out of order for unspecified times and It is advised that the populace ought to be prepared for such an event. Foodstuffs, water, batteries, temporary lighting and a variety of other provisions ought to be in supply to last at least a week. Well, no one can ever be totally prepared for a natural disaster, but I try to at least keep the food and drinkable water cabinet full. Fruits and veggies are real easy in canned or dried forms. Nuts, dried foods of other kinds and crackers are a snap. Good sources of protein are another matter and a little more difficult. Here I've gone with a number of canned items and one such item is Kirkland Signature Roast Beef in Beef Broth which comes in four-can packets and which I get at my local Costco warehouse store. It's fairly economical and easy to use. It's rather tasty for a canned meat product and can be eaton as is or cooked into a variety of meals. It's vary low in fat and consists of chunks of top and bottom round. It's fully cooked, but might be heated if you like. Now and then, in non-emergency times, I use a can so that there is a gradual turnover. Plus, I like to take a can or two along  when I go on camping trips. It suits these purposes well and I'm very satisfied with this product.Gary Peterson

Here's the content for this product:Beef, Beef Broth, Salt, Modified Food Starch, and Sodium Phosphates.12 ounces; recommended serving size: 2 ounces; servings per can: about 4 (that recommendation probably takes the presence of the liquid into account); calories: 80; calories from fat: 15.Total fat: 1.5g, 2%; Saturated fat: 0.5g, 3%; Cholesterol: 40 mg, 13%; Sodium: 180 mg, 8%; Total carbohydrate: 0; Sugars: 0; Protein: 15 g; Iron: 6%.Distributed by Costco Wholesale Corporation; 1-800-774-2678; [...]I pronounce this product good and low in salt.  The only drawback might be the phosphate content, but if that doesn't kill me, something else most definitely will.I'm a skinny person, but whatever food providers claim to be a serving never works for me.  The most I'll get out of this can is two servings; a larger person might have to eat the entire can's content, which contains a lot of broth.  I had my serving with mashed potatoes and peas, and it was good after I doctored the meat with curry, onion, Tobasco sauce, sesame oil, and garlic.  Although olive oil makes a lot of things taste delicious, my body behaves better when I feed it sesame seed oil.  Next time, I'll try the beef in spaghetti sauce or tomato sauce with vegetable puree.  However, I'm okay eating insipid stuff, so I could have easily eaten the meat as a sandwich with just lettuce and tomatoes.  For people who can't eat anything without flavor, you will need to add whatever you prefer; think of it as plain beef because that's pretty much what it is, with plenty of beef broth that you can use as a stock for stew, gravy, or any other concoction.  I used a portion of the broth over my potatoes; it made them smoother.The meat comes in stew-size cubes that were apparently pressure cooked to tenderness, since they flake apart with a fork - I like tender meat.  The meat has almost zero fat; much of which was solid and stuck to the lid, so I guess my apartment is comfortably cold.  The pack comes with three Mexican-style recipes, but you can definitely do your own style of cooking; a beef stroganoff would be nice.When I used to drive along the east coast and stay at the Days Inn, I always carried my own canned goods with me that I warmed up at the motel because a can of Health Valley soup, Del Monte vegetables, Progresso tuna fish, or Crown Prince salmon is always healthier than eating at one of those fast food chains.  I suspect that eating this Kirkland roast beef is also healthier, despite the sodium phosphate.  As the daughter of a cook, I can prepare fine fresh food, but I choose not to because I don't like kitchen duty.  So, whenever I don't order take out, canned or frozen items and baked potato work fine for me.  Conclusion: I recommend this product and will buy it again.

These are Pajarero figs from Valencia, Spain.  They are delicate, sweet figs that have thin skins. They're naturally dried then hand dipped in Caro Dark Chocolate . I discovered these at a boutique grocery in mid December. They were a little pricey ($10.00 for 4.9oz), but I love figs and chocolate. So, I decided to give them a try.  I'm glad I did!  It's nearly mid January and I'm still enjoying these little babies.  The figs are still soft and delicious.  The amount of dark chocolate to fig ratio is perfect.  I agree with another reviewer who said that just one was enough to end a meal.  So true.  If you like fig and dark chocolate, you won't be disappointed!

These are pure ambrosia if you love figs as well as dark chocolate and even worth the cost for only a quarter pound... But the shipping prices are insane. Nearly three times the cost of the item? I don't think so - hence only 4 stars.

column9: China? Or has anybody not read this company's food/safety report?
column10: Here is Brothers All Natural food and safety report.  It sounds better than our own food guidelines. :-(Here is an small excerpt from their report:"Our product is freeze-dried and is made without any preservatives or chemicals using our own internal safe inspections and 3rd party inspections to make absolutely sure that our process is secure and safe.  In fact we go well above and beyond any US company that we know in regards to food safety and quality.  We test all our raw material and finished products 4 times so that all our customers have peace of mind.  Pesticides, heavy metals, allergens, extraneous material and many other items are all checked on every single batch.Our product is pure and safe.  We are a very responsible company.  What we are suggesting is that when it comes to food safety and quality it all comes down to the company and the brand, not just the country of origin.  There have been so many recent recalls on food products produced in the USA and unfortunately even deaths that have happened due to the sloppy and total lack of concern from USA food producers...peanut butter, beef, eggs, and so many more prove that product of USA does not ensure safe food products.  You do not have that concern with Brothers-All-Natural products."So let's give this company the benefit of the doubt since they make such a good product. We think it's great but we aren't allowed by Tyson (the largest chicken supplier in our country) to see the chickens living conditions. I wonder why? Are they hiding something. Obviously they are because the chicken farmers tell us that if they say or let anyone look at the chickens, they are OUT. How do we know what is going into our chickens or how they live? Check this out: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Foods. Maybe they eat other dead chickens or droppings from other chickens. We don't know because our great USA Tyson chicken company won't let us see....it's all a big dark secret. One chicken farmer got tired of keeping the public in suspense (it just made her sick, so she gave up) so she showed what the chickens went through. It was HORRIBLE! Dead and sick chickens all over the place because they cram them up so tight and feed them corn and who knows what else, to make them fat fast. Some chickens can't walk because they are so big that they just lay there until someone takes it away to be slaughtered. They are kicked and thrown when they are going to the slaughter house. It's awful to see. But I am greatful to that farmer for showing the public what Tyson chicken is doing.And we're concerned about this apple treat? Let's try to be fair to this company. At least they claim to be on the legit. Maybe,  have the dried fruit checked out if if there is that much concern. :-/The only thing I wonder about is why isn't there more vitamins in the package or fiber if it's 2 fruit servings?I hope that this company survives because they do make a good product.Good luck!

Gunpowder tea is green tea, most of which comes from a city named Pingshui in the Eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, south of the Yangtse River Delta, where it has been cultivated for centuries and is known as the "green pearl" of tea. Pingshui tea market records date as far back as the Tang Dynasty (AD 618 - 907). The area's gunpowder tea was an important tribute traditionally given to the Chinese emperors; and with the growing trade volume between China and the West it also acquired an increasing number of lovers in Europe. Particularly during the second half of the 19th century, when gunpowder tea export reached its peak, its price on the London market was second only to then-popular Wu Yi Oolong (also from China). Even today, Zhejiang Province still proudly calls itself "home of silk and tea" for its two primary natural products.The name "gunpowder" derives from the tea's elaborate method of processing, which traditionally lasts several hours and during which the tea leaves are withered, steamed or stir-fried and individually rolled into small pellets. Early foreign traders mistook these pellets for gunpowder or gunshot.Gunpowder tea has a delicate aroma with a slightly smokey note. It should *always* be enjoyed without milk or cream.

column9: good chili, but a little sweet
column10: This is the spicy version of the Amy's chili line, and it is pretty tasty. Soy "beef" makes it look as hearty as "real" chili, and the taste is decent. The beans are perfectly cooked, and the sauce is a great consistency, not as thick as paste or thin as soup broth. This is a good chili to have with grated cheese, onions, and a side of cornbread. The only thing I'd change is make it less sweet. It's like someone thought, "hey, we've gotta keep this from being TOO spicy. What can we do? Oh, yeah! Make it sweeter!" Not my idea of top-notch, but it's not terrible. I add a pinch of salt to mine, and it's perfect.Enjoy!

column9: Good Stuff From a Chili Head
column10: I was pretty leary considering this is a no meat product.  I have been making my own chili since I was in my 20s and am not a vegetarian.  This chile is very good for a canned chili and I have tried almost every brand.  I really had a hard time believing this was vegan and organic to boot.  The Tofu "meat" really makes it seem like "real" Chili.  I highly recommend thisWill

I think that this chili is an aquired taste. The first time was ugh, gonna have to throw these away. The second time eating it was better. I think this could be a really good product if they dropped the sugar content down. The spicyness is a good warm feel. but not take your breathe away hot by any means. It was also a little thinner than I had hoped for, I tend to like my chili thicker so it stays piled up on a spoon. Overall the taste of the spices were pretty good, except for the sugar of course.

This chili is pretty tasty, and it's a great option for people who are vegetarian or vegan but who don't have the time, skills, or desire to cook for themselves.  I wouldn't describe this chili as spicy, but I think that's might be more of a personal taste.  My one qualm is that this chili is a bit expensive at about $3.00/can.  When I bought the case at Costco, it was probably about a dollar cheaper per can, but overall a decent value, as one can=one meal for me.

Admit it: during finals, when the baby will not stop crying, or when you are moving into a new place, you may want to avoid cooking at almost all costs. You want to avoid using the microwave sometimes too. You may not even have a microwave unpacked, or if you step away the baby will scream again. You may not believe in a microwave and cannot bring yourself to throw a pot on the stove for times sake. I am familiar with all of these situations, yes I am even a mom and a late start student. And you probably have been in a similar, if not the same, situation. In my personal opinion, this chili is good enough to eat from the can. Strangely, during this semesters finals, I found that experience moving enough to bring me in to write a review. This chili perfect, in my Californian opinion. I would say the best in the west, it is organic, spicy, perfectly sweet, and made just north of me in Petaluma. Come on now, this is what I will want to eat when the next natural disaster hits. This is what I will keep sitting in the back and not mind if it is 10 years old, canned food has that secret 30 year shelf life, and I will eat this. This is it :) Okay, sounds a little too passionate, but I am a big Amy's fan. The can liner has brought up debate, but the canned foods are the only ones with any form of BPA. Frankly, at least they are upfront about it. The rest of the products have not had the issue. By now the BPA may not even be in there, the issue is some years old now. Good and bad things considered, I still buy this chili. I love it!
The chili is only slightly spicy.  It contains no meat but the flavor and texture is good.  I consider this to be a much healthier product than meat based chilis.

I love this chili! I've seen Amy's products in the supermarket and have been really tempted to purchase any of their products. I've had other meatless products that were awful but this was entirely different experience. I'ts spicy but still holds it flavor and you would never know it's meatless.  I Will definitely order this again.

To perk it up, I add freshly chopped veggies and chili paste.Also- it's great that I can order this online.  It's cheaper than the natural foods store, and someone else gets to lug it up to my third floor condo.  :-)

My family loves this chili so much that I totally gave up cooking my own.  This just can't be beat.  It's one of our favorite meals and we are having it tonight.  I love being able to keep it on hand easily by buying at Amazon.

column9: The only chili I haven't liked...
column10: Hi!I'm easy to please when it comes to chili. I've enjoyed everything from cartons of Wendy's fast food chili to home-made gourmet vegetarian chili. In fact: until now, I thought it was near to impossible for me to be unsatisfied by anything even approximating a chili. This afternoon, I was craving a bowl but also felt to lazy to make up a batch of my own. As I've been pleased by many Amy's products in the past, I thought I'd spring for a can of spicy Amy's chili. Well, that was a mistake! I was grossly unsatisfied by a chili. Its spicy and also sweet, and not much else. The only reason that I finished my bowl was because I hate throwing food away. I'm starting to think that sugar is the secret ingredient in a lot of Amy's products (at least with this chili and a lot of their soups: especially tomato), and given the nature of the product I find that deeply frustrating! Obviously I am in the minority by disliking this chili, given the many positive reviews, but you may not want to buy a lot of it until you know you like it!Best regards,Ryan

column9: Tastes good, but BPA is a dangerous toxin
column10: This product contains BPA, which is known to be very dangerous to health. The following is a quote from the Wikipedia article on BPA:"Bisphenol A is an endocrine disruptor, which can mimic the body's own hormones and may lead to negative health effects.[23][24][25][26] Early development appears to be the period of greatest sensitivity to its effects.[27] Regulatory bodies have determined safety levels for humans, but those safety levels are currently being questioned or under review as a result of new scientific studies.[28][29]In 2009 the The Endocrine Society released a scientific statement expressing concern over current human exposure to BPA.[30]"The Wikipedia article is much longer and contains lots of information on BPA. It's all bad news. Amy's canned products all contain BPA. This is unfortunate because Amy's recipes are good tasting. Amy's is aware of the problem and have been "researching it" for years now. But they can't seem to get around to removing this dangerous poison from their products.It's not worth the risk to yourself, your children, and your unborn children. So please avoid this product and any other that contains BPA. When Amy's does the right thing and stops using BPA in their canned products, they'll be fit to eat. But not until then.Update: See comments section for an update to this review.

I use a LOT of garlic when I cook, so, this was a very convenient item to keep stocked in my pantry.My only complaints are as follows:A. The jars REEK of garlic even though they weren't leaking (I inspected them all very well). In fact, even the box they were shipped in stank to high heaven like garlic. So, I had to ziplock bag the jars before I put them in the pantry which solved that conundrum.B. This chopped garlic has metabisulfite in it and if you have a sulfite sensitivity this is definitely not the product for you.C. I'm not a big fan of soy oil and this product uses soy oil as the 'oil' in this garlic.Regarding the consistency of this product...this is partially a paste with chunks of chopped garlic so it's more of a mix of paste and chopped garlic rather than just chopped garlic. You definitely need to give it a good stir before you refrigerate it after opening because the oil floats to the top of the jar.The flavor is excellent and worked great in my ginger/lemon/garlic/pepper/honey/mustard/tarragon salad dressing. It cooks up fine as long as you add it AFTER some other food is already in the pan (veggies or meat etc.) because this will pop and splatter (especially at high cooking temps). It worked great in my Italian meatballs and mixed with butter and paprika on my garlic bread.Bonus: The jars are super cute and I'll be keeping them and re-using them for other things.

This has got to be the worst chopped garlic I have ever used, and I've been cooking over 50 years!  It's like a paste rather than chopped, with a consistency of pudding. The worst part is the garlic explodes like popcorn when you saute it in oil. It shoots oil and garlic about a foot in the air and, if you do not cover the pan, it will burn you. It even explodes in prepared foods that need to be fried, like meatballs. KEEP AWAY FROM THIS PRODUCT!!!!

I have been a fan of S&B Golden Curry since I found a box in SF's Japantown.  I wasn't able to read the preparation instructions since they were in Japanese, so I had a friend translate for me.  Then I found it in the U.S. and realized that the instructions he gave me were not at all a translation, but they are better than what's printed on the box.  So disregard the printed directions and use my recipe instead!  1 lb. chicken, 1 large onion, 3 medium potatoes (peeled), 2 carrots (peeled).  Cut all the preceding into medium-sized pieces.  Brown the onion and chicken.  Add 3-4 cups of water and the potatoes and carrots.  Cook for 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are done.  Remove from heat and add the Golden Curry (cut it into pieces for easier melting).  Mix well and it's soooooo tasty!  Serve over rice or udon noodles.  5 servings?  HA!  3 servings for people with normal appetites.

Curry is a hit in my family and with the Golden Curry bricks it makes life soo much easier for me.  I like to slow cook the curry in my crock pot and instead of potatos and onions...we use pinneapple chunks, carrots, celery, and chicken.  It makes for a nice sweet twist.

As the previous poster has said, this curry is beautiful.  I usually boil the potatoes and carrots for a bit to get them soft, and then add them to the chicken/onions so that the chicken doesn't get too tough from overcooking.  And if you like a slightly sweet (and smoother) tasting curry, and a chopped up banana to the mix!  I know it doesn't sound good, but it's magical.

I got these because Fig Newtons are my all-time favorite cookie; the Fruit Thins are light and tasty, but the fruit filling tends to stick in your teeth. It's a good, light snack, but I'll take a Fig Newton over this any day.

These cookies are light and crisp with a hint of fruit flavor. According to the label, a serving (3 cookies) contains 140 calories, 45 calories from fat and 7 grahams of sugar. That makes it a fairly good snack in my book. These cookies are also excellent for dunking. I will definitely buy these again.

I'm a long-time fan of Fig Newtons. So I saw these Fruit Thins and just had to try today's offering from our favorite cookie monster - maker, I mean.  Newtons Fruit Thins do not disappoint! The dried cranberries are tasty, chewy and plentiful. Then there's the citrus tang over a bed of oatmeal. Hmmm mmm! Perfect to grab and munch on the go, as I do - or to dip in a hot beverage like tea and savor slowly - my wife's preference.  Looking over the ingredients, there is no corn syrup, a plus (although there is sugar in the recipe), and no mouthful of unpronounceable chemicals.  For those who aren't fig fans, you'll want to try these. The cranberries are a flavorful alternative.  I'd say these are as close to health food as anything that tastes this good can get.

This is definitely an adult cookie, not too sweet, with the consistency of a graham cracker and about the same thickness. An English person might refer to such a cookie a *tea biscuit*.Each cookie contains dried cranberries (not nearly enough of them for me) and you'll definitely need something to dunk them in if you going to eat more than a couple, either coffee or milk.If you like the taste of home-made scones then you'd probably like these. I don't know that it's a great compliment but these cookies, unlike chocolate chip or oatmeal raisin cookies, *are* resistible. You can set a limit on how many you plan to eat and then lay the package aside. So that might be a left-handed inspiration for me to continue buying them.Three cookies (the serving size) yield 140 calories. There are about 30 cookies to a package.I'd buy them again for myself but they're not a cookie that I would serve to guests if I were trying to impress them.

The Newton brand has extended its profile into these "Fruit Thins". The package is well designed and easy to open and looks nice. There are two rows of cookies (as I call them, I don't know what a "thin" is), each about 2-inches in diameter.. It looks like about 50 cookies in a package. Biting into it, it has a firmness, but not over-cooked where it crumbles, but not too soft where it melts. Its somewhere in the middle. The cranberries here are the winners. They are what keeps this cookie together! They have a vibrant taste to them and contrast the oats very well with a hint of citrus behind it. There are a few other flavors, but one I am sampling is the Cranberry Citrus Oats. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because I wonder if this something I would seek out myself to buy. I enjoyed them very much and will have no problem finishing off the package, but whether or not I will return to buy them again is debatable. I have not had a fig newton in such a long time that I dont foresee this replacing any memories of the fig, or even any inclination towards a cookie in the near future (maybe that is not something that should be considered as part of my review, but I am). But if you are a cookie person who likes that snack to have in the house, I would definitely recommend this as something new to try out. You will probably enjoy it as much as I did.

column9: An interesting change for this brand, but good

I am not sure about idetifying any citrus taste however.  The ingredients listed natural flavors, so I guess that is where the citrus is.With the wheat and grain content, the cards are there. I am going to see how long it takes the family to finish the box off before buying a replacement.Overall they were good.  Not exciting, not bad.  Just good.**Updated: After a few days I found myself going back to the box and enjoying them more.  I think the initial expectation of Newtons threw me off.  Plus the fact that two others loved them and then the kids devoured them at the first chance had me come back and update and raise the rating.

column9: NEWTONS FRUIT THINS CRANBERRY CITRUS OATS 10.5-OUNCE - Chic, tasty and appealing

They are a plain biscuit cookie with an earthy oat and lemony citrus hint to them.  Kid cookies, probably not.  Adult cookies with coffee or tea, absolutely. especially good as a breakfast cookie.  nice & crunchy, thin & the bits of fruit are chewy & substantial.

Eating two for an afternoon snack provides nourishment without overloading a moderate diet.Not only are they great on the healthy scale, they are also very tasty. The little fruit beads add flavor to the oat base, but they do not overpower the overall taste of the snack. The cookies are excellent for dunking in either milk or coffee.The cranberry fruit thins are very good. I look forward to trying out the other fruit flavors in the near future!

column9: I like these, but the kids are not sure...
column10: So, everyone in the family tried a cookie. The grownups liked the cookies, the kids were split. These "Fruit thins" have a little bit of a European taste about them in that they are not really very sweet. The fruit bits are chewy and there is quite a bit of Citrus flavor in the entire cookie. Healthy continues to be the marketing tool du jour. Newtons Fruit Thins from Nabisco is no different. Just putting the word "thin" in the name has a subtle effect on the buyer: These cookies are healthy and will help be thin. I don't mind marketing tactics, but the buyer needs to go into the purchase with eyes open.Newton's Fruit Thins are a thin wafer-like cookie with some fruit bits in it. Not real sweet and they definitely have the flavor of whole grains.If spite of the packaging labels that will attract the buyer -- "real fruit," "whole grain," "no corn syrup" -- the cookies still have five grams of fat and 140 calories per three cookie serving.The cookies are dry, but not crunchy. They are perfect for those who like to dunk cookies in their drink. For those seeking a sweet snack, the thins will seem bland, only one or two bites actually had a piece of fruit large enough to taste.I prefer the less sweet snack so will probably purchase this product for those nibble cravings. I do recommend that buyers read the label before deciding that this product is really as healthy as it may sound on the outside.

column9: Crisp Cookies with Hints of Cranberry and Orange
column10: Don't make the mistake of leaving this bag of cookies around for someone to find if you want to eat some of them yourself. They are quite the tempting snack! These cookies are made with whole grain wheat flour but you'd never guess it. These have the texture of a kid's animal cracker with the grown-up taste of cranberry and orange. I like to have a few of these as an afternoon snack with Bigelow's Constant Comment tea. It has an orange flavor so the two pair nicely.~The Rebecca Review

I just love these cookies! They are not tacky sweet, just a little sweet. They have a healthful oat graininess to them which makes them nice and crisp which I so much prefer to a chewy cookie. They are wonderful dunked in milk, tea and especially good in coffee! The cranberry offers a little chewy tangy sweetness with a touch of orange fragrance and flavor in a thin and crispy cookie. These didn't last long and I found them rather addictive. I will be buying these again they are delicious little crispy treats!

At first, I couldn't put my finger on it. But then I focused on the scent coming from the package. There it was! That smell brought me back to my childhood, a gentle, slight hint of citrus that transported me back to my grandfather's house and our big family gatherings decades in the past. It was a world of home-baked goods that we lost when a generation moved on, a whirl of cookies and cakes and pies pleasantly devoured with every passing holiday.The Newton's Fruit Thins surprise you when you open the package not only for their scent, but their taste and the sheer number of them. In this world of "100 calorie packs" it would be easy for a company to skimp on a new product, but Nabisco did not go that route. They're advertised on the package as crispy, but that should not be read as potato chip crispy, instead as butter cookie crispy. And the fruit - in this case cranberries - add a burst of flavor that mixes perfectly with the crunch, the texture and the pleasant scent.It's been three days since I opened the package, and that smell is still there, even after the Fruit Thins are long gone. I almost don't want to throw the bag away.
These are light cookies with nice flavor.  Not overpowering but you definitely get the citrus in the background.  I found them a bit on the dry side but my husband loves them!

column9: Not bad but not great either.
column10: Taste is very a subjective thing.  What one person loves, another may hate.  I did not love these crackers but you may.  They are not bad but I did not care for the taste or texture.  They are also fairly caloric for a small cracker.  I don't agree with the other reviewer who said they have no cranberry flavor.  They have subtle but distinct cranberry and citrus flavors.  The fruit is rather sticky and chewy.  I think that was the main thing I disliked about these crackers.  It is not your typical "Newton" texture.

Nabisco has a winner with this latest cookie...'cranberry citrus oat' is DELISH!!  I took these cookies to a meeting of health professionals today and they were a hit with the entire committee...words such as light, tasty, healthy, not too sweet, flavorful, good texture were heard around the table.  From the moment the package was opened these special treats were DELIGHTFUL!Newtons Fruit Thins Cranberry Citrus Oats, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4)

column9: A Crunchy Cookie with Mixed Results
column10: I'm not a fan of fig newtons, mainly because of the figs, so when I saw the new Newton Fruit Thins I thought I would give them a try.  I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised.  While I like cranberries, I don't like a lot of them and the cracker/cookie definitely had a little cranberry taste to them.  As with the Fig and Honey flavor, the cookie/cracker very much had a graham cracker taste to it, so I could easily have one or two of these as a snack.  However, I doubt I could eat more than that in one sitting.  While they were good, they were a bit on the dry side and even the dried fruit didn't help with that.  So I would have to say, if you're trying to diet and looking for a quick snack, the Newton Fruit Thins are a good choice.  For a larger snack, not so much.I did have my husband and son try them, with mixed results.  While my four year old loved them and wanted to have more, the hubby wasn't sold.  He thought that the dried fruit was barely noticeable (he likes cranberries a lot more than I do) and they could've definitely use more.  Also, the crunchy factor took away from the whole experience.Edited on 5/3/11: One thing I have noticed, if you leave the crackers/cookies out, unsealed, a lot of the crunchiness disappears; they are a little softer without taking any of the flavor away.  I'm actually liking them a lot more this way too.

column9: Name is misleading-Hard to identify what is really is by package
column10: ok, when i saw this, i first thought "cranberry fig newtons", hooray. This is a cross between a fruit roll up snack and a flatbread biscuit.  The fruit was very tasty and chewy and the best part.  I had to dunk the cookie into milk to soften it up a bit and smooth the texture since it was very dry.  While it is good, i would choose something else as a snack if I had a choice.  This is not a "fruit thin", it's biscuit with fruit.  I wasn't even sure what to expect by the packaging.  Either make the cookie more like a cookie or make it a flavored biscuit in a different shape (like for high tea).  But I did eat them all and enjoyed every bite.

"Newtons Fruit Thins" were a very pleasant surprise. I've never been a fan of the old standard Newtons - too soft, too figgy. These crispy cookies are quite delicious. They are a fairly thin crisp, lightly sweet cookie with bits of fruit baked right into them. There is no fruity filling like there is in the original Newtons. The flavor of the chewy bits of cranberry, combined with light citrus elements offer just the right flavor balance to the sweetness of the cookie, and the oats add a nice wholesome texture. The package says each serving contains 8g "whole grain", even though 3 cookies offers only 1 gram of fiber, and "whole grain wheat flour" is listed on the ingredients below "sugar". But, considering this is a cookie, how healthy can one expect it to be? I will definitely buy these again.

These "Fruit Thins" are the perfect treat. Crunchy, flavorful, sweet but not TOO sweet, and satisfying. I really love the cranberry citrus flavor, as it has just the slightest amount of tart to balance the crunchy and sweet. They are my new favorite snack!

I got the citrus cranberry oat..these really are good!  They taste to me like graham cracker w/dried cranberry pcs in it.  The citrus/oat was not distinctive.  They come in thin cookie shape, several to each tray..makes you feel like you can eat several and not be loaded up on calories.  Needless to say, tasty w/cold glass of milk or some nice hot tea or coffee.  Definitely going to try the other flavors..this is certainly not just a squished fig newton! No cholesterol and I think 3 cookies were 140 cal

column4: P. McCoy "Friend of Bill W. and Dr. Bob"
column10: I just received this item yesterday, April 27th, and I have been munching on them off and on since then.  They taste SO GOOD that it's hard to stop with just one!  *SMILE*  As I was munching, this food reminded me of Vanilla Wafers with cranberries in it.  (Vanilla Wafers are another weakness.)I do wish it were a lower calorie item without the ingredient of fructose.  Having it higher in fiber would be even better as long as they are able to keep the DELICIOUS taste!

column9: Better - and different - than I'd anticipated
column10: These are thin and crispy/crunchy - which makes them somewhat distinct from other cookies.  I liked that texture very much.  There is a good blend between cookie and fruit, and the blend of fruit selected was different but good.In addition, for me they had just the right amount of sweetness without being overly so.  Sometimes I want a cookie that isn't incredibly sweet, but still satisfying.  These fit the bill.  A nice surprise.

column9: Not a cookie - more like a digestive biscuit
column10: I wasn't sure what to expect from the name "Newton Fruit Thins" and the picture on the box. Given that fruit newtons slogans have been "the cookie that thinks it's a fruit" and "a cookie is just a cookie, but a Fruit Newton is cookie and cake", I had thought it might a sweet, crisp thin cookie, similar to a ginger thin. However, this is more like a digestive biscuit (such as McVities) or tea biscuit. It's very crumbly and feels as though it contains healthful ingredients.While it claims oats and whole grains, oats are the 5th ingredient, and whole wheat is the 3rd. It also says "citrus", which is not listed under the ingredients, unless it's part of the "natural flavors". The cranberries are dried and chewy and tend to stick to the teeth. This cookie has no high fructose corn syrup, using sugar (ingredient #2) and fructose as sweeteners.3 cookies are listed as the "serving size" and have 5g of fat, 95mg sodium, 22g carbohydrates, 1g of fiber, and 2g protein. There are about 30 cookies in each package.If you're looking for a sweet fix, this would not be the "cookie" for you. It would, however, go nicely with an afternoon pot of tea and a chat. The good news is that you'd be unlikely to want to polish off the entire box at one sitting!

column9: Crispy Chewy Fruity Oaty - And That's A GOOD Thing!
column10: I wasn't quite sure what to expect with the "Newtons" name on the box, but these definitely aren't "fig newton" style cake cookies with gooey filling. Rather, these fruit thins are a thin but hearty oat cookie with a semi-crisp quality, embedded with chewy, flavorful bits of cranberry and citrus.I found them to be very tasty, and a great match with my (all-important) morning coffee. Because the cookies are thin, they'd also make for a nice presentation when having guests. Although personally, I think I'll just hog my box (grin).

I recently picked up the blueberry flavored cookies to try and liked them.  But this Cranberry Citrus Oat flavor is even better.  It's a thin cookie made with real fruit and whole grains.  The cookies are crispy and sized right. They are in a tray which keeps them from breaking and they stay fresh in the package. I'll buy these again and want to try other flavors.

column9: Newtons still comfort food, but can't beat the originals!
column10: Upon opening the package, the smell of the cookies instantly reminded me of animal cookies in the little circus box.  The taste, although fruitier, was similar as well making for a nice combination of sweet without being too sweet.  I had mixed feelings about the fruit, it was fun to get a different texture with different bites, but the fruit also seemed to stick to my teeth which was a bit annoying. The cookies are a simple snack, not something I'd put on a platter for company, but they would be nice for backpacks, stroller bags, or office desk drawers.  They have the feel of a healthy treat, although reading the nutritional information they only contain 4% of daily fiber (as opposed to Wheat Thins' 8%), 4% of iron, and nothing much else, so that was a bit disappointing.  In any case, I'd buy them again, the crunch and taste were pleasant and the eating was fairly guilt free.

First of all, do not let the "Newton" name lead you to expect something that this cookie is not. This is not a Fruit Newton type of cookie. No.It is a thin and crispy cookie, with a nice flavor and some nice chewy bits of fruit sprinkle throughout. Is it in anyway 'healthier' than other cookies? Well, I am but sure. 3 cookies/140 calories is pretty average for store bought cookies I think. No corn syrup, 8g per serving of whole grain..both pluses, if small pluses, I think.Overall, a nice little treat if you like a tasty, thin, crispy bit of a sweet.

column9: Possibly the best tasting cookie ever
column10: I couldn't believe how good these cookies tasted when I first tried them.  I was actually shocked, shocked I tell you, at how incredibly perfect a cranberry based cookie could taste.  I'm a big chocolate addict from way back, so I'm usually not that enamoured of anything that doesn't include chocolate.  However, I actually liked the taste of these BETTER THAN any chocolate cookie I've ever had (with the possible exception of the old Fudgetown cookies, but those haven't been available for years).  Even if you think you don't like cranberries, you should try these.  They're really amazingly flavorful.  So, you're asking me, why did I only give them four stars if they're so great?  Because I didn't particulary like the crunchiness of them.  I like my Newtons to be chewy, like the regular old Newtons of yore.  I know, that's just a personal preference.  You may actually like the crunchy style cookies better.  But the taste is unbeatable.  If they could just take the exact taste from this product and put it in a regular chewy Newton, I think that might be the perfect cookie.

Everyone I let try this cookie liked them.  I gave them to kids, adults, men, women and without a doubt everyone said they were good.  They taste like cranberries and cookie.  They dont have a lot of calories per three and come in at 150 calories with a minimal amount of fat.  I am not advocating eating the whole thing at once but you can rest assured eating one or two wont load you up on fat.  I would have to say that these are one of my favorite things I have tried in a long time.  My son who wont eat anything ate these as well and I think that should say it all.  I was worried at first about what they might taste like but one bite in any fear I had was gone.  Great item, I will definitely buy it again.

column9: One out of two in my family like these
column10: I liked these, and would have given them a 4/5, but my wife felt they taste like cardboard.They are cranberry and orange flavor. The cranberry is chopped up and is candied/chewy, and is integral to the cookie. The orange is like an orange extract. The cookie itself tastes like a oat cookie (e.g., a Walker oat cookie), but flatter, with bit of chewy cranberry.There are not a lot of cookies in a package. There are 2 trays/rows of cookies. The packaging says serves 10, but I found that I'd tend to eat 1/3 or 1/2 a row, which would be around 5 servings per package. A lot of cookie packaging is being downsized during our recession, but there's less to eat in here than a typical pack of fig newtons.And again, my wife said no.

OK...I am a freak...I have always loved Fig Newtons..... since forever.....what the 60's.  Absolutely NOone in my family likes Fig Newtons.  Is everyone brain dead or what!  Anyway, these fig (fruitlike) Newtons come out and I am thinking.....OK, I could be eating these.  All I can say is WAY.....they are way cool.  I can't say I like them better than Fig Newtons....but I am sure my doctor would tell me bad things about Fig Newtons I would not want to hear.  This new stuff is light.  It doesn't have all that bad-I-will-kill-you-stuff in it.  They taste so light, but you get this fruit taste in them.  I could say I have died and gone to heaven....but I want to be straight here.  I am a true blue Fig Newtons guy who thinks these new pieces just ROCK.  Get some.

column9: Delicious but calories add up quickly
column10: These cookies are quite good.  One of my favorite combinations is cranberry and orange, so these hit the spot.  The cookie is very think and crispy.  Shipping was a bit of an issue as several cookies were broken in half (and a couple into smaller pieces).It's pretty easy to consume a serving because the cookies are not that large and quite thin.  Serving size is 3 cookies and has 140 calories and 5 grams of fat (1 saturated).  But it is a cookie, so we're not trying to diet on these, right!  I think the description of this item...Newtons Fruit Thins, with the emphasis on 'thins' on the box could be a bit misleading, there is nothing thin about the caloric and fat content of these cookies! I could easily eat 10-12 of these in a sitting if I wanted to.  I do think companies could do a better job with low fat ingredients.  I started buying the low fat fig newtons and they taste just fine compared to the regular kind but have a fraction of the fat.Calories aside, these cookies taste great!

I found these fruit thins to be pretty good.  They taste a bit like shortbread to me.  There is not a lot of fruit in them -- significantly less than in a regular fig newton, for example.  So, any cranberry fans may well find them to be disappointing.  All-in-all, assuming that I can find them at a good price, I may well buy some.

I've always liked Fig Newtons. Now, there is a new cookie with the same great fruit taste and a whole lot of "good stuff". Of course, it's made with real fruit; but the 8 grams of Whole Grains really caught my eye. In addition, there is no corn syrup in this product. The thin cookie is about 50 calories....but who can eat just one? I would definitely buy this product again!

I was excited to have the opportunity to try these cookies. I've been a big fan of Fig Newtons (and the other fruity varieties), and the description of these sounded like something completely different.They are definitely different from the other Newton fruit cakes.  These are crispy, more like a cross between a graham cracker and those wonderful Moravian thin spice cookies we get sometimes at Christmas.  They are laced with chopped cranberries and a hint of orange flavor, and a nice size -- about 3" in diameter with a scalloped edge.  The orange flavor isn't overpowering, but it's not too subtle, either; and the tartness of the cranberries came through as well.These would be perfect with a cup of tea as an afternoon snack, and the nutrition stats show that these are not going to totally destroy a diet.I'll definitely purchase again, and look forward to trying some of the other flavors.

Perfection embodied in a flaky, tenderly crispy wafer of delight. They were so good and so addictive I ate half the package in no time at all, with the other half following behind the next day.I love pretty much anything with cranberries, and the subtle zing added by the orange was a brilliant finishing touch.I really never buy store cookies. I would, however, buy these. They were THAT good.

I received this from Amazon.com for free as part of there Vine program to generate reviews. Well I have never reviewed something edible before, so hear goes. I like them, there very tasty. In moderation there a good healthy snake, and there quit fulling. You can eat them as there are, or you can add a spread to them. I looked at the ingredients and there all natural, my only concern is that they use fructose. Would I buy this product, Yes. Would I recommend them, yes. I like them!

column9: The whole family loved it, but...
column10: Newtons Fruit Thins Cranberry Citrus Oats received a huge thumbs up for taste from everyone in my family, but as the mom and grocery buyer in our household, I have some reservations about them. Here are our pros and cons:Pros:1. Really tasty!2. Not loaded with lots of ingredients you can't pronounce.3. Cookies are thin but big...about 3" across.Cons:1. Expensive! Amazon's price is $27.30 for a 4-pack. That's almost $7 per 10.5 oz package.2. Crumbly. About half the package I received through the Vine program were broken.3. Even though the ingredients appear to be pretty healthy, they are also high in calories and fat. According to the information on the package, a serving of 3 cookies has 140 calories and 5 grams of fat (1 g sat fat).Overall, good but too expensive for me to buy on a regular basis.

column9: great cookie but not a filled cookie like everything else called Newton
column10: Because These are called Newton Fruit Thins I was expecting a thin  filled cookie, however, these are not filled. They are thin crispy shortbread like cookies  with a nice texture and a dash of citrus flavor. There are a few bits of dried cranberry scattered throughout, the  fruit adds some texture but does not dominate the flavor. I probably would not have known the bits were cranberry if it had not said so on the package. The cookies are not very sweet and are a good tea or coffee biscuit. These are very good served with cheese as well as being a traditional cookie. The oats and lower sweetness made them appeal to my healthy eating daughter  though they are not actually health food.We all liked these a lot and will probably get them again. They were eaten very quickly. family members who were not aware that these  were called Newtons (fruit thins) loved them unconditionally. The  family members who knew that the word Newtons was part of the name were initially disappointed because they are not filled cookies.

I chose these cookies because I was lead to believe that they were some sort of really thin Newton (as the package implies) with the expected chewy/moist texture.  Instead these are crispy cookies with a cracker like texture.  While I was initially a bit surprised, I think that the Newton Fruit Thins are a great product.  The cracker itself is subtle in its taste (only moderately sweet), crispy in texture,  and contains bits of citrus flavored cranberries.  I enjoyed them.  They are good in isolation as a snack, but I would also recommend them with jam or cream cheese.  My 19 month old daughter loves them.The serving size is a little on the small side (3 crackers), but they don't appear horribly unhealthy.

The new Newtons Fruit Thins are like a tradtional Fig Newton, only in crispy form. The Cranberry Citrus flavor is very tasty. The cookies are thin light cookie with lots of flavor. I'll be interested in trying the other flavors available. If you like the Newton line of cookies, you'll want to give these a try, you'll be glad you did!!

Newtons Fruit Thins are a diabolically good cookie, and cranberry citrus oat version is no exception. They have a light crisp texture and would make an excellent sandwich cookie to serve with ice cream or fruit. I have tried the blueberry version but I think I like this version better.  Each wafer comes with slivers of cranberry and a healthy wholesome light citrusy taste.  These cookies are made by Nabisco, an American company and are actually baked in Canada- which is a bit disappointing. The packaging contains some plastic, but not as much as some.  3 cookies are 140 calories which makes each waver about 46 calories.If I had my druthers, I would prefer less vitamin fortification since I am sensitive to eating enriched foods, but for a less vitamin-sensitive person I'm sure they are fine. Overall, I liked the cookie, and think this is a fine addition to The Nabisco/Kraft Foods line.

column9: If you really like graham crackers...?
column10: Newtons Fruit Thins (Cranberry and Citrus) / B004FEJ968I was really excited about receiving these cookies through Amazon Vine - I'm a big fan of the Newtons "fig newtons" line of products and always have been. It seemed like a transition to "cookie" would be inevitably good, but... these cookies just didn't do it for me or my family.I guess I should have been concerned when my husband bit into one of these and said, "These taste like sand!" I didn't feel like they were quite *that* bad, but it's true that these are *very* dry and somewhat crumbly. They remind me a little bit of dry graham crackers or dry "nilla wafers" - I ended up dunking these cookies in milk to make them a little more palatable.The dried fruit bits in these cookies are nice, but not anything to really write home about. The cranberry and orange flavoring is very subtle and seems to come across more in the scent than in the actual taste.Overall, I like the sweetness balance of these cookies - they're not overpowering, and the flavor is nice - but the intense dryness of the cookie combined with the sticky chewiness of the dried fruit was just too toothsome for me. If the cookie had been softer, I would have liked these a lot more - as it was, I felt like I was eating very dry crackers and I didn't enjoy the experience.I don't like to waste things, so I'll try to finish the entire bag, but the rest of the family has already informed me that I'm on my own.NOTE: This review is based on a free review copy of this product provided through Amazon Vine.~ Ana Mardoll

When I saw these Fruit Thins they piqued my interest.  I have not had Fig Newtons in a long time and I love dried cranberries.  They were a nice surprise.  It seems like a combination of cracker and cookie, kind of like Animal "Crackers" which all adults love but try not to admit while we snack some of the kids!  The fruit thin was crisp but not hard and the slightly sweet taste of the chewy cranberries was very nice. Between me and my mom we ate most of the package before we knew it. I will definately get more and try the other flavors.

On the cookie-cracker spectrum, these definitely tend more toward cookie but are also no where near the typical chocolate chip cookie.  They are fairly thin and crisp, yet still soft.  I'm a fan of cranberry, so I could've done with more cranberry bits throughout the Fruit Thins but they are flavorful enough.  These make for a satisfying snack.

column9: Buy these cookies! Delicious, crunchy treat.
column10: Never having been a fan of Fig Newtons, I approached this new product with some trepidation.  Wow!  I was very pleasantly surprised at how delicious these new cookies are.  Three of the large crispy cookies are only 140 calories (two cookies are less than the magic 100 calories) but they are packed with fruit and flavor!  The cranberry citrus oat flavor are delectable nuggets of cranberries and orange in a buttery tasting cookie that is low in fat.  I also purchased the chocolate raspberry flavor and it is just as good having a rich dark chocolate flavor and large tasty pieces of raspberry.Newton seems to have come out with several new products recently after sticking with their "tried and trues" for many years.  I predict that these new fruit thins (there are four different flavors) will definitely be keepers.  They are delicious and worth going back for more again and again.Buy these cookies!

I got theses yesterday, tried a couple, and put them out on the counter. Everyone in the house has been grabbing one as they walk by. There are only three left.These cookies are light,crispy and flavorful. They're just sweet enough to satisfy without loading you up with sugar.These are a winner. I'm going to snag one of the last ones now while I have a chance.

column9: If you like the slight taste of fruit....
column10: and I do!!  This new product from Nabisco is definitely worth your money.  If what you want is a light cracker/cookie with a hint of cranberry taste this is the one for you.  Although the label says "oats" I cannot detect the taste or consistency of oats in this product.  It crunches in your mouth like a graham cracker but has that slight taste of cranberries in it.  This would be nice with a cup of tea or coffee by your side.  Definitely would buy this again.

I tend to favor fruit desserts and cookies and cakes over chocolate, so be aware of that as you read this review. I like Fig Newtons and all the different fruit Newtons, but I wasn't sure what to expect in these cookies. I was pleasantly surprised.Unlike Newtons, these cookies are very light and crispy. They're a bit delicate, and they broke easily, which is probably why they're packaged in plastic trays in the bag as opposed to simply being free roaming in the bag. I think if I were to put them in a ziplok bag, they'd all break into pieces. Not the sturdiest of cookies, but very delicately crispy.The flavor is good. There are bits of cranberries that aren't too big nor too small. The package says "citrus" and there are pictures of oranges on the front, but I thought these tasted more lemony than orangey. I think I would have liked more cranberry flavor and less lemon flavor. The cookie was also not too sweet, which I tend to like better. This was definitely less sweet than a chocolate chip cookie.The texture is nutty and you can definitely taste the whole grains and fiber, which I like, but which other people may not care for. It's also a drier cookie, not as oily as normal chocolate chip cookies bought at the store or on the grocery shelves. I tend to favor this, but other people used to more butter or lard might find the cookie a bit dry.I enjoyed eating these with sweetened tea. I really think this is my new favorite store-bought cookie.

A pleasingly chewy, thin cookie with distinct cranberry flavor. It tastes fresh and oatey, with flavor notes that are more bakery than supermarket cookie aisle.There's a good balance of quantity vs calories: three cookies are just 140 calories, and there are about 30 cookies per package.I'm usually not a fan of big-brand packaged cookies.  They are invariably full of artificial ingredients and excessive calorie-counts, while tasting anything but fresh, and trying to mask that lack of freshness with excessive sweetness.  These Newtons Fruit Thins surprise me with their balance of fruit and grain without delving into dull health-food territory.  Recommended.

column9: A snack the whole family can enjoy!
column10: Seriously.  When you have someone who has a whole mouthful of sweet teeth instead of just one (me), someone who doesn't really enjoy sweet stuff (my brother) and someone in between the two (my father), and we all thought these Newton Fruit Thins were delicious, I think it's safe to say that these crispy cookies will appeal to everyone.  With a lovely citrus flavor, chewy cranberry pieces and hearty rolled oats, these are cookies you can feel good about letting your kids snack on.  Not only are they made with real fruit and whole grain, they don't have high fructose corn syrup, the biggest selling point for me.  No matter what propaganda the Corn Board puts out, HFCS is not an ingredient I want to put into my body and is, in fact, something I cut out of my diet several years ago (and by doing so, I lost about ten pounds without doing anything else to my diet or lifestyle).With a serving size of three cookies--and each cookie is 2 1/2" in diameter, so these aren't small treats--at 140 calories per serving, you can indulge your cravings without totally derailing your diet.  The cookies are quite filling as well.  I'm not saying these are a health food item; after all, they are cookies.  However, at 7 grams of sugar per serving, they're a better alternative to many of the sweet treats being offered today.  And these will satisfy your sweet tooth just as effectively.The only quibble I have is that the cranberry flavor isn't as strong as I thought it would be.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, as the overall flavor is light and refreshing.  It's just more on the citrus side than the cranberry side.  However, that's perfectly okay with me and it's certainly not going to stop me from purchasing this flavor again.  These are yummy!

column9: Good oat & fruit taste, all-natural cookie snack
column10: While these cookies taste nothing like the original Newtons, they're really good in their own way. They are fairly thin with a oatty, slightly buttery taste with the addition of dried cranberry bits and natural citrus flavor. The all-natural ingredients gives them their all-natural taste. (Real fruit, whole grain, no high fructose corn syrup, 3 cookies are 140 calories and only 7 grams of sugar) They're crunchy but not hard and taste great with beverages like tea or milk. If you are looking for a lighter, healthier cookie with a touch of natural fruit flavor, these make a delicious snack.

column9: Delicious Addition to the Newtons Family
column10: A little bit of fat and carbs, zero cholesterol, and a fabulous crunch!  These snack cookies are definitely worth the roughly 45 calories per cookie, though you probably won't stop at the suggested serving size of 3.  I didn't.  If you're dieting, don't pass it by, just plan ahead.The cookie has a light flavor reminiscent of the cake-type cookies of the regular fruit Newtons line, just pressed thinner and dotted with lovely, tiny chunks of cranberry and citrus, just enough to add a bit of flavor and zing without overpowering the taste buds.  Though it's labeled a cookie, I can easily see this little gem smeared with cream cheese (or better yet, sandwiched with the stuff and a touch of whole-fruit jelly) for a special treat.  A gob of ice cream between two of them would be amazing!  The fact that it's not a sugary item makes it a great pairing with a nice cup of tea or coffee or a glass of wine as much as doled out with milk for the younger humans in your family.I rate this one a keeper!  Its nutritional count is bolstered with rolled oats and whole-grain whole wheat flour.  If it had a smidge of flax or some other additional holy grain, it would pass the tipping point and actually be a legitimate dietary necessity!

I expected these to be a soft cookie, similar to the traditional Newtons. Instead, these are more of a crunchy cracker. They taste like a cross between a graham cracker and an animal cracker, with a cranberry zing.

The Newton Fruit Thins are part cracker, part cookie.  They are not too sweet, have a natural taste, and a good texture.  They are perfect for a wide variety of toppings and spreads to perk things up if you want.  They are not just a new product for the sake of a new product.  If you are looking for a a new snack or even a breakfast cracker, give these a try.  The best cracker I've tasted in quite a while.

The worst thing I can say about these cookies is the "Newton" name.  You'd think they were variant of the wonderful Fig Newtons with lots of fruit filling.  Nope.  There's a TINY amount of fruit filling in these thin, tasty cookies.  So if you're looking for the gooey goodness of Fig Newtons... keep looking.However, these Fruit Thins can stand by themselves.  Crispy.  Not too sweet.  Nice texture - easy to nibble on.  Interesting taste.On the nutrition side, there's not a lot to be worried about.  A mere 5g fat and 7g sugar per 3 cookie serving.  And the cookies are a decent size.  It's not hard to limit yourself to one at a time after a meal - so now you're looking at a nominal 1.7g fat and 2.3g sugar.  What's the problem!?Summary: Tasty AND not as unhealthy as the typical cookie.  I like 'em!

column9: Wonderful snack.  Way to go Nabisco!  A+
column10: I'll start off by saying that there is no hydrogenated oil in this product.  The second major plus is that the list of ingredients is small and I can pronounce everything on the list!  The final huge plus is that these wafers taste incredible.  The fruit bits are chewy and the wafer crisp.  Perfect with tea.  These snack wafers are officially on our buy list.  Great job, Nabisco!

While there may be some fruit in these cookies, there isn't enough to even notice when you are eating them. The taste is bland and mediocre. These cookies were supposed to be Cranberry Citrus Oat. I can't taste any Cranberry or Citrus or Oats, not sure what I am tasting. Given that these are called Newtons, I also expected them to be soft cookies (like fig newtons) but they are hard not soft. They also don't have much of anything beneficial in them either, no vitamins, essentially no fiber and very little protein but they do have some fat in them and lots of calories. They also contain fructose but not specified as to what type.To me, these are nowhere near as tasty as graham crackers. Honey Maid Low Fat graham crackers are healthier, lower in fat, higher in fiber, with some calcium and with no fructose.However, I would agree that these Newtons Fruit Thins are somewhat healthier than most other regular cookies.

I like these because they're not too sweet. But of course that also means you can just keep eating and eating them without realizing how many you've plowed your way through, so be careful...  a three-cookie serving contains 140 calories and 5 grams of fatLots of fruit, and the citrus flavor REALLY comes through. And as they're thin and crisp, they're the perfect accompaniment to a cup of tea because they don't immediately go soggy. I'm not usually a big cookie person, but I'll probably be getting these again.

I'm not a big fan of the original Fig Newtons; I don't like the chewy texture. That's why these Newton Fig thins appeal to me- I love the crispy texture! I love cranberry orange muffins, and I get that same taste profile with these flat cookies. The serving size is three cookies, which has 140 calories, and it's a good sized serving.I would have thought that there would be more fiber in these cookies, but there is only 1 gram per serving. That is kind of disappointing, but nowhere on the bag does it claim to be a 'healthy snack'.I like that the packaging allows you to keep the bag sealed so the cookies don't get stale.These are tasty cookies, and if you are just looking for a little afternoon treat at work or to got with a cup of tea, these cookies will more than satisfy that.

If you liked those, you'll like these!  I happen to have been a BIG fan ... HUGE ...  So, the only thing that perturbed me about the old lemon coolers (which share exactly nada with these in the appearances department) was the the powdered sugar was messy.  These Newtons have none of that, and still remarkably similar taste.  I can't imagine they have any more calories than the oldies, and DO have a little fiber (1g) and protein (2g).  I wouldn't call 'em health food, but then again, it's hard to find true, dyed-in-the-wool health food with this kind of taste.  I love 'em, and will buy them.  They're large, thin cookies, about the consistency of animal crackers with dried fruit bits in there to yield chewy, crunchy and citrus twang all at once.  I'm really happy with them (and I'm usually a Keebler guy, thru & thru).  My take on it: try 'em.

column9: Tasty and not too bad for you
column10: I enjoyed these little thins "cookies". I've never reviewed food before, so please bare with me.The cookie part is very tasty, kind of like a graham cracker or teddy graham...I can't quite put my finger on it. The bits of cranberry in the cookie are real pieces, real enough to get stuck in my teeth (as dried cranberries do). There is a citrus taste, but no mention of "citrus" anything can be found on the ingredients list...unless you count "natural flavors". Three of these thin cookies is 140 calories, which I didn't think was too bad.We enjoyed them a lot. They're quite addicting. Good light snack cookie.

column9: Light, delicious cookies without a lot of sugar
column10: These are delicious and slightly crisp, with dried cranberries, tangy natural fruit flavors, no ingredients with long, chemical names and only 7 grams of sugar for every three cookies you eat.  It's a happy marriage of very tasty and fairly healthy, combining unbleached enriched wheat flour with whole grain wheat and rolled oats. There is fructose but no high fructose corn syrup.  Fruit Thins are good choice when you want to satisfy your sweet tooth without abandoning natural food principles.

column9: Delicious Alternative to the Graham Cracker
column10: The cookies (crackers) are about as round as a baseball.  They are crispy and crumbly like a graham cracker.  I shared both boxes I received with my co-workers and the comment I heard most often was that they tasted like a graham cracker. I also heard quite often, "Mmmmm, I would buy these."  We tasted both these and the honey-fig flavor and this was the favorite.I thought they tasted very nice. The cranberries added just the right amount of tart to the cookie.If healthy was a taste then that is what I would describe them as. They aren't unhealthy from what I can tell but they aren't exactly low fat or low calorie.  5gs of fat. 140 calories.They really did make for a nice little snack.

column9: Better than I thought they'd be!
column10: Okay, first, you need to know that I usually don't buy cookies, we try to really limit our sweets intake and we also try to eat things that are 100% whole grain, so cookies just don't fit into that, we also shop almost exclusively in the natural/organic section.  I love regular Fig Newtons, but stopped eating them when we started eating whole grain and no/low sugar.  Also please know, I do not like crunchy cookies, I like soft cookies.  That said, I was surprised by how much I liked these.  They are thin and relatively crispy without being dusty/messy crispy.  I definitely taste the orange and oat more than the cranberry, but over all the flavor is nice and there is enough flavor, some plain cookies of this type are just like sugary cardboard, but these have flavor.  Now, what surprised me the most, how not-that-bad-for-you these are.  There are no preservatives which is nice.  The first ingredient is enriched flour, but they do have some whole wheat flour and whole oats in them too, the are sweetened with sugar, not HFCS, and has fructose listed near the end.  We won't buy treats or sweetened cereal where a serving has more than 9 grams of sugar, and guess what?  These only have 7 grams of sugar per serving which is three cookies.  I will not at all feel bad letting my kids eat these cookies, especially since a serving for a preschooler would be one cookie.  I only wish there was more fiber (more whole grain) in these.  I also like that they bag is re-sealable.

Excellant. I do not like cranberries or fig newtons so I wasn't expecting much from these but I got a very nice surprise. They taste fantastic. I got the cranberry citrus oat. Very crunchy with great sweet taste and the fruit is definitly in every bite. They are about 2 1/2 to 3 inches across and about the thickness of 2 wheat thins. There were 30 in the 10.5 ounce package. I already ate 10 of them, hard to put them down once you start eating them. What a great way to get your daily fiber as well. They have 4% of your daily allowance in just 3 cookies. The best used by date was August 23 & I got them April 25 so plenty of time to eat them while they are fresh. Who am I kidding..... They won't last until tomorrow.... Order these or get them in your store, either way you won't be disappointed & I'm sure the kids will love them too, even babies just old enough to have crackers will love these. Gotta go, have some new cookies waiting for me to eat them....

column9: Decent Healthy Cookie But Needs More Cranberry
column10: Let me say upfront that I am hardcore cranberry lover.  What are my credentials?  I drink 12-16oz glasses of 100% cranberry juice undiluted, often snack on unsweetened dried cranberries, and smother my Thanksgiving turkey in cranberry sauce.  So one could say I was looking forward to these cookies.Each cookie has about 6-8 fragments of cranberries which probably equals around 3-4 whole cranberries.  A light amount indeed unless these are some hidden fragments in the cookie that escaped my eyes.  Yes, it is a thin cookie but it is also a wide cookie measuring around 2.5 inches in diameter.  I'm not sure if it is the dry baking process or because the cranberries are often fragmented, but compared to say wonderful cranberry muffins, you don't get the strong cranberry punch unfortunately.  You can definitely taste the cranberries, but only in light form.  These cookies also provide multiple layers of flavoring with the orange "natural flavor".  I'm not big on mixing orange with my cranberry but I know some people like this combo and this might be the cookie for them.The bag is easy to open and has plastic covered metal band to help hold the package closed.  Given how dry these cookies are, though, I'm not sure it will matter much.  Cookies are made with non-bleached wheat which is a plus in my book.  Also contains no high fructose corn syrup.  A single bag contains two rows of cookies with 15 cookies per row (30 cookies total).

column9: Nothing at all like Fig Newtons, but still tasty.
column10: Ok, I think that Fig Newtons are the greatest cookie ever sold in a package (sure, I like homemade chocolate chip cookies even more, who doesn't?). I agree with the late-great Jean Shepherd in that one should eat those tasty cake like creations by the fistful.  Not only are Fig Newtons tasty, they are fairly healthful, as snack products go.Nabisco has made quite a few Newton spin offs and most have missed the mark in my opinion.These "Newtons Fruit Thins" are nothing at all like Fig Newtons. While Fig Newtons are cake like and soft, these are cookie like and crispy.But once I got over that, I found these little crisp wafers rather endearing and tasty. I found they go very well with ice-cream. They have a subtle fruit taste, and a nice crisp texture.They do share one thing with the Real Thing- as snacks go, they are also moderately healthful- eaten in moderation, of course!

Tried by myself and 3 children ages 7, 9 & 11. Not super healthy but probably healthier than most store bought cookies. The taste is akin to animal crackers with little pieces of cranberry. I did not taste any cranberry flavor, the bits just added to the texture. The kids liked them but it wouldn't be something they clamored for.

I have always liked Fig Newtons and I was curious what these "Fruit Thins" would taste like.  I was plesently surprised and I really liked them.  I find them good for a quick pick up in the afternoon at work.  They are a good break from protein bars and that type of pick up.  I highly recomend this product.

I wasn't sure what to expect with these. They're not quite a cracker, and not quite a cookie. The ... wafer? biscuit? ... has that Newton-y flavor, similar to the cake of the original cookies, and the fruit flavor isn't overpowering. I'm not a big fan of this particular flavor combination though (cranberry citrus). I would try another flavor, though, before dismissing them.All in all, I'm not sure which snacking niche this is looking to fill. It isn't health food, isn't a sweet treat, isn't a kid's snack, isn't a dessert. It's a munchable, I suppose, for adults around the kitchen.

I love these cookies: crunchy, citrus-y, yummyness! The complimentary flavors of orange and cranberry are a favorite of mine, and having those packed into a thin, crisp cookie, well that just makes my day. The cranberries are a tad tough for my liking, but that's a teeny-tiny nitpick. As far as cookies go, Nabisco has come up with a winner that isn't completely bad for the body: there's no high fructose corn syrup (sugar and fructose are used to sweeten the cookies), artificial flavors or colors. Some of the better ingredients are unbleached enriched flour, whole grain flour, rolled oats, and dried cranberries.At 140 calories a serving (three substantial-sized cookies), they are a nice treat that include 1 gram of fiber, 2 grams of protein, and have 7 grams of sugar. Not bad. Have only two cookies and that's less than 100 calories for a quick snack. Perfectly doable in my diet. They aren't too sweet and they satisfy my craving for a treat without the feeling of guilt left behind (which may or may not happen with other cookies). While these aren't a health food by any means, they're far better than most other cookie choices out there. I'll be sure to try the other flavors in the Newtons Fruit Thins line, as well. Newtons Fruit Thins Cranberry Citrus Oats, 10.5-Ounce (Pack of4) are a great, flavorful, totally scrumptious morsel that I heartily recommend!

Really good cookies.  But they're not quite cookies.  Like a biscuit with a touch of fruit taste, 140 calories in three fruit thins.  The problem is can you only eat three.  Trust me that's a serious problem.

column9: Well, Its Not Bad for FREE
column10: When I opened the bag the first thing I noticed was that even after being shipped, most of the cookies were complete and not just pieces.  Saying that, maybe I should have stopped there.  The cookie (cracker) is two inches in diameter and looks like a 'big' Ritz cracker.  The outside in scalloped and there are nine wholes in the center (maybe for more even cooking), but there are few pieces of fruit visible.  The flavor is 'cranberry citrus oats' but there are just a few dried cranberries and the citrus flavor must be from the 'natural flavor' mentioned as the last ingredient on the label.The serving size is three cookies which have a total of 140 calories with 45 calories (3.5g) coming from 'fat'.  With 22g of carbs it's a very fat cookie.  For the flavor you get versus the calories you get, it's not a very good trade.  On the plus side it only has 95 mg of sodium and 7 g of sugar (yeah!).  Try some sugarless gum instead.Zeb Kantrowitz

These comments are for "Newtons Fruit Thins - Cranberry Citrus Oat" sold by Nabisco.The package states "crispy cookies" think the firmness and thickness of a graham cracker - yes that firm. These 3-inch round wafers come in a rigid plastic tray that slides into a foil-lined package. Nonetheless several cookies in the two packages I sampled were broken into several large pieces upon opening. Probably not typical but that's what I observed.I found the cookies brittle; they had a tendency to break into several pieces after a bite. As an adult I could compensate be adjusting my method of holding the wafer but children will have a problem.The cranberry citrus oat had a pleasant flavor with a hit of citrus. The package state "made with real fruit" therefore what you have are many small pieces of dried cranberries throughout the cookie. I like cranberries but after they are dried and baked they become semi-hard and chewy and tend to stick to your teeth.I was somewhat taken back by the work "Newtons" in large letters on the package. My understanding of this term is of a soft chewy fruit filled cookie like a fig or apple Newton. I do not see the connection then again I am not in Sales or Marketing where these decisions are made.

when i see the name newton i expect to taste a lot of fruit.  this product fell short of my expectations, the cranberries lack taste.  the cookie is flat and crispy and the flavor is similar to an oat ginger snap, not unpleasant, but not a cookie i would buy.

column9: Enjoyable alternative to the classic Newton!
column10: The Newtons Fruit Thins in the cranberry citrus flavor are a surprisingly good addition to the Nabisco snack line. I was expecting them to be more akin to the original Newtons, but the Fruit Thins are more like a shortbread cookie: thin with a good snap. The fruit pieces are flavorful and chewy, and the cookie itself is very satisfying, having a flavor not unlike animal crackers.Packing 140 calories in just one serving (three cookies), the Fruit Thins are a better alternative than some snacks out there, and are a good source of mono- and polyunsaturated fats. For those who are interested, here's a breakdown of nutritional content:CALORIES: 140 Calories from Fat: 45TOTAL FAT: 5g (8%)Saturated Fat: 1g (5%)Trans Fat: 0gPolyunsaturated Fat: 2.5gMonounsaturated Fat: 1gCHOLESTEROL: 0mgSODIUM: 95mg (4%)POTASSIUM: 40mg (1%)TOTAL CARBOHYDRATES: 22g (7%)Dietary Fiber: 1gSugars: 7gPROTEIN: 2gAnd there is no high fructose corn syrup, which I greatly appreciate.Overall, I would recommend the Newtons Fruit Thins to anyone looking for that classic Newton flavor, but in an updated, refreshing, crispy cookie form!

These cookies are tasty and crunchy. The remind me of tea biscuits with more flavor. The orange flavor is not too strong, as some orange flavors can be, but it does dominate the taste. I do not taste any specific cranberry flavor at all, but the cranberries are present like raisins would be. I do not know that I would order them from Amazon or anywhere again. The package came with many broken cookies. I would prefer to buy from the local store.

I love the Newtons Fruit thins and my wife loves them even more.  They have a pleasant taste and light crispy texture to them.  One should expect to have broken up cookies if not careful with a product that is baked and is crispy and light.  I'm not sure the town we are living in now has them, but when my wife and I visited family in Fargo, I "let" her stock up on a ton to bring back.  "Let" being that she only grabbed 4 packages and I told her to go ahead and get 10.Great product and we hope they never go away.  Ingredients and check the clearer nutrition fact pic I provided.Ingredients: UNBLEACHED ENRICHED FLOUR (WHEAT FLOUR, NIACIN, REDUCED IRON, THIAMINE MONONITRATE {VITAMIN B1}, RIBOFLAVIN {VITAMIN B2}, FOLIC ACID), SUGAR, WHOLE GRAIN WHEAT FLOUR, SOYBEAN AND/OR PALM OIL, ROLLED OATS, DRIED CRANBERRIES, FRUCTOSE, SALT, BAKING SODA, SOY LECITHIN, NATURAL FLAVOR. CONTAINS: WHEAT, SOY.

This was my first time tasting these and all I can say is OMG! They are SO good and not fattening. My whole family loved them--even my picky child!I want to try all the flavors now. This has quickly become one of our favorite cookies.

These arrived in the mail at about the same time my children came home from school.  They were literally gone in five minutes.
