My mom and sister were here and we were all fighting each other off to get to the last one. These are not necessarily a healthy snack when you eat the whole bag but they sure tasted great!! :)

column4: Jeffrey S. Andrews "Once on a Desperate Highway"
column10: At first I didn't think that this was going to be a good cookie...it looked thin and it said Oats...which left me a little uninterested.  Then I ate one...Wow, I nearly ate half the package before my wife came by and tasted one then we finished the package together.  These are awesome cookies, with cranberries in them and just the right balance of sweetness.  I can eat them any time of day...and they seem to be good for you!  On a scale of 1 to 10...these are a 10 in my book!

column9: Not at all like a fig newton and not a cookie
column10: I know this says that it is a "thin" Newton but I expected it to be a cookie and it wasn't.  It was super thin, crispy and crunchy like a cracker.  It had a slight fruit flavor and just not at all what I would associate with Newtons as a soft cookie or even cookies in general.  I was disappointed with the flavor (not fruity enough for me).  I was disappointed with the texture (super thin, hard, crispy).  I think if you are looking for a cracker that is not salty you should try these, but if you want a cookie look elsewhere.

The old Newtons have gotten a makeover. These 'cookies' have a light, tangy flavor to them. They're not too sweet and the cranberry and citrus blend is a terrific combination. I definitely prefer these to the old fig newtons. My one complaint is the weak packaging. The thin plastic tray doesn't hold up well during shipping or any handling. A good portion of my cookies were crumbled and in pieces.

Newtons Fruit Thins Cranberry Citrus Oats are really tasty. They're light and crispy and a little chewy.I eat these for a snack with coffee mid-afternoon and they satisfy the craving for a light snack. They're especially good with coffee. The cranberry citrus is my favorite flavor, too. The cookies are not too sweet and just right.

column9: It's a cracker, it's a cookie. maybe it's a biscuit
column10: Newton's Fruit Thins combine pieces of cranberry with an orange flavor in a crunchy bite. The the thin is like a cracker, but sweet like a cookie. Makes me think of some biscuits I had in England. Right after these were delivered, my mom came over to our house with a wedge of brie. A slice brie on these Fruit Thins goes perfect. I also think cream cheese would be nice. Whether eaten as a snack or served with cheese for tea/coffee or a light desert, these thins are highly recommended.

These cookies are really quite delicious.  I have been sampling them with a nice cup of hot tea and find them both delicious and delightful.  They remind me of a shortbread with fruit in it.  The 2" cookie is very thin and crisp.  The flakes of cranberry are not only large enough to be recognizable visually, but also to get the taste of cranberries in each bite.  The citrus flavor is there also, just much more subtle.  The cookies come packaged in a plastic two-compartment tray.  Considering that my package had traveled through the mail, I still had 27 completely intact cookies.  I have great hopes for getting unbroken cookies from the grocery shelf packages.A recommended serving of 3 cookies has a calorie count of 140 with 45 of those calories coming from fat.  According to the label they contain 8 grams of whole grain per serving.  Unlike some whole grain products I've tried, these cookies did not have that slightly unpleasant 'dry' feeling in my mouth.  All in all, my family enjoyed this flavor combination so much that they want me to buy the other two varieties.  With 30 cookies per package these Nabisco Newtons Fruit Thins will last for a reasonable length of time around the house.  Always considering that we will have to be reasonable in our consumption habits first!

I received this today and was very anxious to pop open the bag and dig in.  I was a bit curious.  I am a lover of Fig Newtons, and thought this would be a fun thing to try.  By just the picture, one may wonder if the cookies would be a bit on the dry side.  I can say, enthusiastically that they are not.  Fruit Thins are delightfully crispy (not hard), they have a light sweetness, are moist (as crisp thins go) and truly mouth-wateringly tasty.  The first word to pop into my mind, after taking a bite, was a very firm "YUM!"  The crispness combined with the chewy cranberries is positively addicting and oh-so-good.  Newtons Fruit Thins is a snack that will be loved by kids and adults alike.  Lower in fat (5 grams of fat and 140 calories per 3 cookies) than an average cookie, made with real fruit, whole grains and no high fructose corn syrup, these are the perfect solution when the sweet-tooth munchies rear it's ugly head.Though I'm not a huge lover of cranberry, the taste is just perfect in these thins.  There is a tasty and chewy tang provided by the cranberries that is light, not overpowering and truly lends a great amount of flavor and texture to these thins.  Please note that there are additional flavors available in the Newtons Fruit Thins line, including: Blueberry Brown Sugar, Fig and Honey, and Raspberry Chocolate.  I have not tried any other flavor except the Cranberry Citrus Oats, but truly plan to.  I loved these and highly recommend them!!

The label says one serving is 3 cookies, totaling 140 calories, but I'll bet you can't stop at three.I'm not sure what I expected, but the flavor is delightful. To my palate, the orangey and oaty flavors dominate and the cranberries whisper to me as an aftertaste.The packaging, with its plastic inner tray and metal tab closures assures that the cookies (or should I call them Newtons?) stay fresh and intact. There are 30 (10 servings) to a package, which works out to 22.75 cents per cookie, a little pricey.Nevertheless, they're a fun alternative to other snacks and well worth a try.
These snacks are great but the price is beyond absurd.  These are $3 - $3.50 each in Wal-Mart.  Here it is $7 each.  Price gouging at it's best.  What a joke.

column9: Tasty and relatively healthier cookie for a snack.
column10: This is a nice cookie for snack time if you don't want a really big and sugary cookie. It is thin like some teatime cookies but is made with real fruit and whole grains (whole wheat flour and rolled oats but also bleached wheat flour). They also don't have any high fructose corn syrup. The cookies are crispy but also crumbly, if you know what I mean. The flavor is nice and orangey citrusy with little bits of real cranberries. I really like this flavor but haven't tried the other flavors yet.Nutrition facts: Serving Size 3 cookies (30g)All information below based on serving size of 3 cookies:Calories 140 from fat 45Total fat 5g, no trans fatTotal Carbs 22 g, Dietary fibre 1g, Sugars 7gProtein 2gCholestrol 0mgSodium 95mgPotassium 40mgThese cookies are for $2.49 for the 10.5 ounce bag on regular price at my local supermarket. May be cheaper at a supercenter. The Amazon price seems to be too high.
These Newton Fruit Thins in Cranberry Citrus Oat flavor taste just like the McDonaldland cookies I used to eat in the 70's! I love these!!!

These are very tasty, although the "Newtons" name threw me a little.  I do like Newtons cookies, and I opened these expecting something soft and fruity.  Instead, I got something crisp and fruity.  To look at them, I didn't think they'd pull off the "fruity" part -- again, thinking of a fruit-filled Newton -- but the fruit flavors do shine through.The ingredients are relatively straightforward, easily in line with "don't eat it if you can't pronounce it" guidelines (although I flinched a bit when I saw "...and/or palm oil").  I do think the 3-cookie serving size is a little unrealistic, but then again, many products use unrealistic serving sizes in their nutrition assessment.  It's easy enough to figure out where you'll be if you eat, say, a 6-cookie serving, and they do well in terms of sodium and overall fats -- even better if you score a box that uses unsaturated soy oil instead of saturated palm oil, although there's no way to select for that.My only dilemma now is choosing among these tasty cranberry ones, or trying the blueberry brown sugar or raspberry chocolate next time.  Not a bad dilemma!
I never would eat the original fig newton cookie, but I love these. They are light and crisp and only have 5g of fat per 3 cookies. My whole family loves these.

column9: Tasty cookie from trusted Nabisco, but too fragile for shipping
column10: Nabisco is a brand I trust and it didn't disappoint with this crisp cookie alternative to the classic chewy Fig Newtons, which are more cake-like in texture. I enjoyed the not-to-sweet flavor of the cookie & fruit combo and have added these new Newton Fruit Thins to my regular snack purchases.Unfortunately, having them shipped resulted in over half of the cookies arriving broken. The packaging & cookies themselves just don't lend itself to normal shipment wear & tear. Though the price point is better on amazon.com subscription service than what I pay at my local grocery, the breakage doesn't make the price savings worth it.

column4: Alan Taylor "Music Addict, Pop Culture Guru, ...
column9: Seriously Addictive - Not all All Like a Newton.
column10: Why Nabisco decided to call these cookies Newtons is a bit puzzling.  I'm not a fan of Newtons, but these fruit cookies are simply to die for, perhaps a little too good if you lack the will power to prevent you from finish off the entire bag. Definitely more of a crisp shortbread cookie than a newton. Recommended!

These are very flavorful little cookies. Something you can eat and not feel bad about since they are small and have healthier than average ingredients for a cookie. I don't know if the other varieties would be as flavorful, since the orange flavor is there in every bite. The chewy bits of cranberry are a pleasant surprise. They're great with a cup of Earl Grey Tea. Looking forward to trying the Chocolate raspberry.

These Newtons Fruit Thins 'Cranberry Citrus Oats' flavor are quite good!  They are tasty, with a nice balance of sweetness and a good balance of flavor...the oats, the cranberries, the citrus tang - these are good cookie crackers!  They are good, not amazing, but I enjoyed them: they are the kind of semi-healthy treat that I would love to serve to friends, but I will say that there were a few broken cookies in the pack, which is not exciting when you have a brand new package.  These are chewy, crispy, thin cookies - a nice treat!

After I brought these home for the first time, my husband was hooked! I love how the flavor is not overwhelming and they are a one handed snack. My husband loves the flavor and was excited to see that you can find many different flavors available in our local grocery store. Even my toddler daughter is a fan and thinks they are a treat. :)
These cookies are simply delicious.  The fruit element is not overpowering in the same way that I have found traditional fig newtons to be.  I highly recomend these as a light snack.
I love these cookies!  They taste wonderfully fresh and different from most other packaged cookies and the cranberry-citrus combo is great.

I'm a big fan of cranberry and orange flavors along with traditional style Newtons, so I jumped on the chance to try these out. I think they got the cranberry and orange combination just right, sweet but not overpoweringly so, tart but nothing that will make your mouth pucker. The crispyness of the cracker was a nice surprise, not chewy but not so crispy that it fell apart into crumbles. I really liked the resealable package, although really these didn't last long enough that going stale was an issue. I'd definitely buy these again when I'm craving something that's tart and tangy.

Newtons Fruit Thins are a crispy and tasty snack. The flavor of orange and cranberry is subtle, but adds a slight sweetness to the cookie. They are not as sweet as a cookie, but have just enough sweetness to satisfy a craving, much like a graham cracker. They are a great snack with some healthy ingredients, so if you have a sweet craving, these are a much better option than a typical cookie.

I used to eat Fig Newtons as a child but they fell out of favor in my house after about a decade. They were "OK" at best to me but nothing I'd ever go out of my way to pick up. These things on the other hand are another story.Package:The bag is resealable and the thins sit in a plastic tray. So that's a big plus. It's also bright and will stand out in your cabinet. I doubt that you'll lose sight of these with all the other cookies and what not that you may have.The Thins:They are thin of course and break easy but not into a bunch of little pieces like a Nature Valley bar will. The flavor is fantastic. I like cranberries and I like all citrus fruits (orange being the case here) so the two together in this oaty cookie thin are delicious. I don't find the flavor to be overwhelming either. Everything is baked into harmony so each thin tastes as good as the last.I don't pay too much attention to nutrition facts but I know that they are healthier than your typical cookie. If you are like me and grow tired of the heavy sweets and just want something light but flavorful, these thins might be just the snack you were looking for.

I'm not a fan of fig newtons so I was skeptical about these, but I thought they would be worth a try. I'm glad I did - they're surprisingly tasty! They taste kind of like a thin shortbread biscuit with a hint of citrus and little pieces of cranberry. The biscuit flavor is the strongest, but they definitely don't skimp on the cranberry. In fact, one of the drawbacks (kind of an obvious one) is that the cranberries can get stuck in your teeth.I really like the ingredient list:unbleached enriched flour, sugar, whole grain wheat flour, soybean and/or palm oil, rolled oats, dried cranberries, fructose, salt, baking soda, soy lecithin, natural flavorIt's not a long list and recognize almost everything on that list - always a good sign! And health-wise, they're low in fat but still provide some (though little) nutritional value by way of protein (2g for 3 cookies) and fiber. I sometimes eat them after lunch when I crave something sweet and they actually keep me satisfied for longer than most post-lunch snacks I've tried!I can't say that I'd reach for this time and time again because I like to go all out with cookies since I don't indulge in them that often and I'm not the biggest fan of shortbread biscuits, but I think most people will like these (especially good as a tea time snack).

column9: Love the cookie not the price
column10: Delicious cookie.  Walgreens had these on sale last week 2/$5.00.  CVS this week on sale 2/$5.00!  Pack of four would be $10.00.  Did you all really pay $27 for four packs of cookies?  Just saying.

This have been a huge hit with the whole family.  They remind me of a tea cracker more than a cookie or anything "Newton".  They aren't overly sweet and have a subtle orange and cranberry flavor.  The cranberries can be a bit chewy but add to the overall texture of the cookies.  They also travel well and are great cookies for lunch boxes and toddlers!

column4: J. Loscheider "No one knows I'm a radical"
column9: More a cookie than a "thin", but that's not a bad thing.
column10: I ordered the Newtons Fruit Thins because they were intriguing. As a long-time fan of the Newton cakes (Fig Newtons, Strawberry Newtons, etc) I was expecting either a soft, chewy product or some kind of a cracker.It was neither, but rather a fruit cookie that in some ways reminded me of the stained-glass cookies my mother used to bake at Christmas (these had chopped up bits of colorful fruit candies in them, hence the resemblance to stained glass windows). They've got a satisfying crunch, and they're more aromatic than most packaged cookies I've had. The citrus and cranberry flavors really come off with a scent that's like cranberry-orange juice, which may not appeal to your average chocolate chip cookie fan, but my 2-year-old certainly enjoys them and I feel better giving her these rather than some Chips-A-Hoy.These really fill a snack/dessert niche better than a fruit or healthy snack niche, so long as you order them with that expectation you won't be disappointed.

These are quite tasty and filling to boot. I much prefer them over granola or cereal bars for a snack.  I don't think they should be called Newtons though, as that brings to mind a moist chewy treat and these are not.  Still, I would have given them a higher rating if they were even remotely good for you.  For the amount of calories and fat in these, I will usually choose to eat regular fruit Newtons.  In summary; these are tasty and a nice treat on occassion but not a healthy alternative to regular Newtons.

I received this product in the mail, opened it and all the people in the house tried it. It is nothing like the original Fig Newtons, it is thin and crispy with a delicious flavor.  It was gone in a flash but it was good, we kept eating it until it was gone.  Yum yum.

I enjoyed this product and have purchased several bags since having received one from Amazon. They taste good and give me a bit of sweetness to satisfy my sweet tooth without being as unhealthy as many of the other snacks that I tend to eat. I have yet to try another flavor, but highly recommend these.

First things first, I was struck by how hard and thin these cookies are. They don't look appealing at all, but somehow got eaten REALLY fast.They're super addicting. The cranberry/citrus is not the first thing you taste, but you get bits of the flavor as you eat the rather standard-issue cookie.I can't remember the serving size, but it's more than 2 cookies so you get a good amount of cookies for your WW points plus value.

column9: Filling and Delicious Crisp Like a Cracker but SATISFIES like a cookie
column10: DELICIOUS ! These fit the bill for my snack needs.  The 3 cookies fill me up with only 173 calories.  AMAZING.  Fiber and Fruit in a cookie that is crisp like a cracker.  Not one of those dry bars that tastes like cardboard.
These cookies have a great combination of flavors.  The cookies are crunchy and the fruits are chewy.  Overall, they are sweet and would compliment black tea perfectly.

column9: Tasty alternative to a Fig Newton
column10: Gramma and I tried these tasty Newtons. The taste of the orange & cranberry was a bit adventurous for my nearly 90 year old Gramma, not your normal Fig Newton. As with most orange cookies we have tried in the past, the orange did not over take the cranberry, the 2 tastes complimented one another. The texture is that of a nice English tea biscuit and we did have ours with tea. Per Gramma, the sodium was not too bad, she is always reading the sodium content in BOTH of our foods and letting me know when mine is too high.Some have noted that the taste is not very fruity, my cousin stated such to me, but I enjoy my treats (desserts & snacks) not to be to heavy in their taste, whether that be sweet or sour. I know many prefer a very sweet treat when eating a cookie, whether that cookie or treat be sweet or not.As some have stated, these are not moist, nor anywhere near as soft as normal Fig Newton. If you are looking for a soft, moist & chewy cookie, these will not be your ' cup of tea'. They are more cracker like, as some have opined, as they are more like tea cookies.If I were having any kind of group over, I would serve these amongst the fruits and other offerings I would have available. I would recommend these cookies to anyone wanting a different or unique treat. But, if you are looking for a soft, sweet and moist treat, these will not be satisfy for your craving as they are definitely more cracker-like.

The taste of the Newton's Fruit Thins was pretty good. It's a nice crunchy treat, and I really enjoyed the cranberry citrus and oat flavor. It was like a really thin and crisp designer oatmeal cookie.  I would have liked the product more if the cookies were smaller in size.  The snacks are rather large and round in shape, and being so thin they easily break and crumble. If they were 1/4 of the current size you could easily consume them in one or two bites and eliminate the crumbs.  The packaging leaves a lot to be desired. The outer foil bag isn't bad, but the inside plastic tray is clumsy and tough to slide back into the resealable wrap, and combined with the large crumbly nature of the cookie already mentioned above I doubt very much if anyone buying these in a store ends up with more than half of the cookies actually being whole by the time they get home.  Ordering them from Amazon easily guarantees half the product inside will be in pieces -- but like I said... the smaller size (even if they are broken pieces) makes 'em easier to eat!

column4: Just a Mom with her thoughts
column10: First of all, I have to say that I am not a fan of cranberry or citrus (of any kind), so I was a little worried. But I opened the bag, called my two boys over and we dug right in. I was pleasantly surprised (and shocked) that I did like the flavor--a lot. And both of my children loved them! It's been a long time since I've had the original Newtons cookies but I can tell you I like these much more. Newtons Fruit Thins remind me of thin shortbread cookies with little bits of fruit in them. And I guess I shouldn't say "little bits" since they are more like swirls of fruit. Regardless, they were absolutely delicious and nutritious. Newtons Fruit Thins are my new go-to late night snack. They're definitely a healthier, low fat, high fiber alternative to a piece of chocolate or candy.

column9: Mrs. Fields, They're Not...But Still Darn Good
column10: So, OK. The Mrs. Fields thing is a cheap shot. Newton's fruit thins are packaged cookies or cracker-like cookies. So gotta compare apples with apples (or, in this case Cranberry Citrus Oat with, well, I know of nothing to compare them with!)Let's try comparing them with Newton's Fig Newtons. These are a hundred times better and I always liked fig newtons OK.The best part, of course, is "no high fructose corn syrup," "whole grain," "natural fruit flavors," "made with real fruit."  And they don't taste all that natural. They taste as good as the worst junk food around. High praise, huh?  Try them dunked in milk--nonfat, of course.----The reviewer is working on a book called "Here's How I Don't Cook."

I love these, along w/ the Fig and Honey flavor, but the Blueberry Brown Sugar and Raspberry Chocolate, not so good.Cranberry Citrus Oats: you can really taste the citrus, its so good, citrus and cranberries are such a balancing combinationFig and Honey: kinda forgot but a good flavor alsoBlueberry Brown Sugar: doesn't stand out that much between these 4, just....blueberry-ishRaspberry Chocolate: pretty disappointing, i was expecting something really chocolate like oreos, but it was kinda bland for that partoverall, I think its tasty and crunchy, which makes it a great snack to nibble on (:

Newton's Fruit Thins are a delightful "cookie biscuit" that satisfied a wide range of ages.  We had the Cranberry Citrus Oats and found them to be reminiscent of the flavor of a cranberry/citrus muffin but with the satisfying crunch of a cookie.  The thins are drier in texture than cookies but the fruit makes them enjoyable and kids as young as 10 enjoyed them immensely in place of traditional cookies. They are a bit pricy but they create a "full" feeling that helps you curtail eating too many (and since they are thin you get quite a few in your 10.5 ounce package).  We are looking forward to trying some of the other flavors and if you are looking for a change from your everyday cookie this is a nice option and appealing to kids and adults.

I was pleasantly surprised by how good the cranberry Newton thins tasted considering that it is a healthy snack. It is difficult to find the right healthy-tasty balance in snacks. I think they have struck the right chord with my taste buds and will definitely make this a regular in my grocery list. A great snack to keep at the work place too, when you are feeling pecky in the afternoon.

The first thing that stands out about these "cookies" is that they are packed with fruit.  You cannot ignore the amount of real cranberry in each one.  They are crisp yet chewy at the same time.  they are great light snack with a flavor that cannot be beat.  These are a wonderful alternative to some of the heavier items out there.

column9: Very tasty, relatively healthy snack; a little on the expensive side
column10: As with the blueberry version, these essentially taste like crispy muffins. The taste is strong on the cranberry and not overly sweet (probably due to the lack of partially hydrogenated corn crapola). That said, I did have them approved by a kindergartner -- it's not that they aren't sweet at all.  While I wouldn't exactly call this a health food, it's not too bad in that department for a snack food without artificial sweeteners. The only downside is that at nearly twenty bucks for 4 bags, they're kind of pricey. I slightly prefer the blueberry version, but that's a matter of personal taste -- both are good.

column9: Good Cookies but Palm Oil is a Concern
column10: Recently, I tried Newtons Fruit Thins Fig and Honey cookies.  Then someone brought a package of the Cranberry type to work.  I like the cranberry cookies better.The cookies themselves are good. They are thin, but that was the idea, wasn't it? The cookies have a nice texture. You can taste the cranberries. The calorie count, 140 for three cookies, is about the same as the granola bars that I sometimes snack on. Just don't eat the whole box at once.The ingredients are also reasonable with the exception of the use of palm oil. As palm oil use has increased dramatically over the past ten years, commercial growers have been clearing rain forests in Indonesia and Malaysia to create palm oil plantations. The palm oil is used in food production, as in these cookies, and in the manufacture of bio-fuels. The result is a loss of endangered species and ironically increased carbon emission. There has been some movement to either reduce palm oil use or use only palm oil from sustainable sources. There have even been stories of girl scouts agitating to sell only palm-oil-free cookies.Kraft is aware of the palm oil situation. It is not clear that they are doing anything about it. This is from a July 15, 2009 Wall Street Journal article: "Kraft spokesman Richard D. Buino said that while the company supports the RSPO's [Roundtable for Sustainable Palm Oil] efforts, 'it is clear more work is needed to consolidate standards, enforce principles, verify traceability along the supply chain and ensure competitive pricing to bring certified palm oil to market. We're monitoring the RSPO process and actively engaging our suppliers to monitor their certification efforts to find viable options for sourcing sustainable palm oil.' Neither Nestlé nor Kraft directly addressed purchases of Malaysia's certified palm oil."

I am going to say: unless your world perception actually contains the world, it might be hard to sell a product called "digestive biscuits" in the US.  (Let me take this time to tip the hat to jolly ol' England for their lovely biscuits.  Thank you.)Please, please, please, don't be put off by the name "digestive biscuits"!  They are freakin' delicious!Wait, that's not in the product name?  Errr... uhmmm.... Ignore everything I just said.Here's what Nabisco Newton's Fruit Thins has going for it:1. Semi-sweet - Can't wait for the day when I bite into a dessert and no longer swearing that I can feel the sugar granules on my tongue. Yet with this cookie, I feel like we have a taste of the future.2. Uh, real fruit - Oranges, yes!  Cranberries, yes!  What more needs to be said?  Except, the orange flavor is slight and the cranberries comes on strong.  Meh, I like it.3. 3 cookies (serving size) = 4% Dietary Fiber, 8g of whole grains.  Holla at your boy.  Honestly, because of the whole grain, I can't eat more than three because meh belly is gettin' full.I hate packaged foods.  I dislike sweets.  I don't care for cookies.  But I do like these a whole lot. This might convince me to visit the middle of the grocery story to pick up a package of these from time to time.
These are a pretty healthy, tasty snack.  They are more like a cracker, with a bit of dried fruit baked into the product.  My kids loved them!

This cookie is better than expected.  They are larger than regular cookies and thinner, more like a cracker.  There is a chewy and crunchy aspect as the texture of the cookie changes with the sections that have more fruit.  I can honestly say that I was pleasantly surprised.  Cranberry Citrus may not be your favorite flavor, but it wasn't for me either.  So this leads me to believe that these really are that good.

These remind me of the English tea biscuits that are nearly impossible to find anddon't have this wonderful flavor.  Yeah, real cranberries in the cookies and the citrusdoesn't overwhelm the berry flavor.And for those wondering if they are dry... no where does the descriptionsay this is a soft cookie, so you can't assume they wouldn't be what they are;a thin, crunchy, cookie.Excellent flavor and I hope these stay around for a long time. These are excellent,just as delicate as the Blueberry. The Chocolate/Raspberry worked better with coffee or a darkhot chocolate, basically a stronger drink.The Fig is good, but I have to be in the mood for them as their flavor is very unique.If you are looking for a Tea Biscuit these are excellent and they are great for milk dunking.These were easy to find locally as well and at a much lower price.

These taste pretty good, but be cautious about the whole grains and rich fiber claims.  The label trumpets that it contains whole grains, but be aware that regular flour and sugar are the first two ingredients, and whole wheat comes in third, and fiber content is quite low, so there isn't a lot of whole wheat here.  These taste OK; my wife liked them a lot, but I ate them only because they were sitting on the table.  The picture on the box showing lots of bits of cranberries was pretty optimistic; there usually aren't that many bits of fruit in them.

I quite enjoyed these cookies.  They are reminicent of a shortbread cookie with a hint of orange and some chewy Crasins thrown in for good measure.  Fairly reasonable stats for a cookie (140 calories, 5 grams of total fat and 7 sugars)---until you see that is only for THREE cookies.  No way you're going to hold yourself to 3 lousy cookies in one sitting so you'd better plan on doubling that.  But it is still a better choice that a lot of offerings in the cookie isle.  And that is just where I'd go to purchase these.  They didn't hold up well in shipping and I wound up with a lot of crumbs.  Which I ate anyway.  Because they were too yummy to let that stop me.  Enjoy!

My entire family enjoyed these cookies.  They were gone surprisingly fast!  As far as packaged cookies go, they seem like a healthier choice than most.  The ingredients list is fairly short and includes wheat and oats.  I appreciate that these cookies do NOT contain high fructose corn syrup.  I applaud Nabisco for that.The citrus flavor is very mild, and I enjoyed the chewy cranberries and crisp texture.  A good, flavorful cookie!

First, a couple of minor negatives with these cookies.First is the name. For years Nabisco advertised, "A cookie is just a cookie, but Newtons are fruit and cake." Why the Nabisco marketing gurus would think that it was a good idea to associate the "Newtons" name with these thin, crisp cookies is beyond me.Next is the packaging. The trend today is toward recycled-content paperboard packaging, such as the one Nabisco used for their new Ritz Crackerful Multigrain Crackers. These cookies come in a foil-lined bag with a plastic liner, neither of which can be recycled.The cookies themselves are quite good. They have a light texture similar to that of a shortbread or butter cookie. There is a nice light orange flavor that is not overpowering. As is often the case when you use dried fruit in a cookie, the cranberries are a bit chewy. I thought these go best with a beverage. Tea, coffee, soft drink, and even (according to Mrs. Boilermate), wine. We both agreed these are "adult" cookies.
these are great, can't wait fr them to come to a store near me.  great for a snack, full of flavor and you get the crunch that you need.  especially if u b dieting

These are a different type of cookie, and also come in some other flavors than cranberry - blueberry, fig and honey, and raspberry chocolate. The dough is like the dough in a fig Newton only crisper, except after the humidity gets high, when nothing is crispy. They taste very good although there was no trace of the labeled citrus; and not an extreme amount of cranberry either.They were a hit in this family and we will purchase them in the future as an alternative to more sugar laden cookies. Three cookies are considered a serving with 149 calories and 8 g. of whole grain per serving. They can serve as a quick grab and go breakfast or as a more wholesome snack.

At my title says...these ARE good cookies/crackers/biscuits but there is something missing. First of all, when I think of "Newton" I think of the familiar cookies which have a moist and fruity taste.  Obviously these are "thins" and less calorie, but they lack something I expect of a "Newton."  The packaging makes me think more of a "Wheat Thin" and maybe it is subconscious, but this does taste like a Wheat Thin version of a cookie!  It is mildly moist, almost dry...but not quite.  It is enjoyable, and the fact that one can eat three of these for "1 serving" is a plus.  All in all this is something I would imagine munching on during a high tea, not my usual snack.  It is good, but is only disappointing when one considers who the manufacturer is.

I want to call these cookies, but they aren't, quite. Nabisco calls them "Thins". Okay, they are very thin, so I guess that is the most appropriate term.My thins arrived from Amazon in rather poor shape. At least half of the cookies were smashed beyond belief. I rescued a half dozen large pieces to try and threw out the rest.I can almost tell you exactly what they tasted like if you ever ate Fig Newtons. I found it very interesting that the crispy cookie parts tasted just like the cake part of a Fig Newton, with crispness gone wild. They are very crisp!!Apparently embedded in the newtony stuff is the fruit parts. They looked like dried fruit. Mine was cranberry citrus. Frankly, I didn't expect much, but I was really wowed. The thins, cookies, whatever, ended up being very tasty.Would I recommend this product? Depends. I would personally not buy them again. I would myself buy the old fashioned Fig Newtons. I just really liked them. I eat very little sugar these days, so what I eat has to count, meaning really work for me. These do not fulfill that requirement, but for a lot of people I suspect they would.

These Newton Fruit Thins are delicious!! They are not overly sweet or tart but just right with a pleasant taste of cranberries combined with a slight crunch. They are definitely one of my favorite cookies.For a cookie, I think that they are healthier than average because they are made with whole grains and do not contain high fructose corn syrup.

There's nothing wrong with being "mild and understated." None of the tastes in this treat jump out at you but, instead, they're a good blend of several flavors and textures. My first impression was that I needed to get me a glass of milk since they're a tad dry, but not terribly so. I was expecting a cookie and these really aren't. They aren't as sweet as a cookie and that was a crowd-pleaser among my friends. They're a terrific, light snack, with an interesting taste.

I was never a big fan of fruit Newton cookies, so I was a bit wary of these. I do, however, love cranberry citrus sweets, so I gave Newtons Fruit Thins a chance. They're, as the name suggests, thin cookies with a nice bit of crunch to them, but they're not hard at all. They have a hint of sweetness without being too sweet, and the citrus gives them a nice bit of tartness. The dried cranberries add a good, chewy texture to the crispy cookie. These are great to keep on hand when you want something a little bit sweet, but not overpoweringly so. Yum!

column9: A healthy little snack that actually tastes good!
column10: Hi!Thee are a new entry by Nabisco - instead of the thick and soft fig newtons (and later other flavors), they have gone in different direction with these. These are crisp thin cookies, (more like a wafer) with real fruit bits in them. They are a nice size for a cookie about 3" each, so these are not a tiny cookie -- just thin! (about 1/8" thick) They do NOT use High Fructose corn syrup and each serving (3 cookie as 8G. of whole grainWhile the cookies themselves are nice and crisp, the fruit still has a nice fruity chew to it, and give them a nice balance.Ok.. the rundown -Serving size3 cookies - 130 cal, 45 from fat.8 G. of Whole Grain per serving22G Carb1G Fiber7G SugarTotal Fat 5G (Sat. fat 1g 0 Trans Fat, 2.5g PolyUnsat. fat, 1.g Momounsat. fat)Sugars 7gThey are Made in Canada.On the whole, I like them, these are a good alternative, and they are crisp enough to have with tea. I tried the Cranberry Citrus, they also come in other flavors (like blueberry) which I am sure taste just as good!Jim

Nabisco Cranberry Citrus Oat flavored Newton Fruit Thins is a pleasing new snack. The bits of dried cranberry are nice and the texture and flavor of the "thin" itself is pleasant, somewhat reminiscent of a graham cracker. One of the best things about this product is that the sweetness is not overpowering. The ingredients are not especially offensive, even though this reviewer has an, admittedly, semi-unreasoning prejudice against any sweetener where fructose is part of the name, in this case simply "fructose." I am not much of a sweet eater or a consumer of highly processed foods, so I find the name "Newtons" somewhat puzzling. It is suspected that the flavor and texture of the "thin" itself is supposed to taste like the outer layer of a Fig Newton. I also understand modern branding, and this "thin" comes close enough. All-in-all this is a nice little snack and I recommend it. This review cannot end without my mentioning that my roommate enjoyed these. Were this product to become regularly available locally, it would be a staple in this household.

column9: Great! I like them just fine but my ex LOVED them
column10: OK OK so I admit when my ex asked for something sweet (waiting for the kids to be ready) I offered up these cookies. I thought they were pretty good - but not terribly outstanding. He's very picky. VERY. So I *might* have had a thought * a teeny one* that I could give him some of these instead of heading off to my stash of M and M's and other scrumptious goodies - because, you know, feeding my ex is not something I do very often. He is an ex after all. However I try to be agreeable to get along.Lo and behold he positively loved them. Imagine my surprise when he gave me the container back, EMPTY, and said "Thanks". So yeah Newton's people..way to go..now my ex will be asking for food everytime he comes over!I compromised on the rating - I'd of said 3 because I liked them - but for my ex clearly these were a 5. Too bad he didn't get the same rating as a husband!

column9: I shall call these... crookers. That is, part cookie, part cracker.
column10: With the density and shape of a cookie and the fragility of a cracker, it's an interesting combination. They have a shortbread-like consistency, a cranberry chewiness, and a bit of oatmeal flavor as well. Each time I open the box (which has re-sealable tabs I've never seen before), I get a waft of fruitiness. I'm hooked!The ingredients aren't listed on the product page, so I had to seek them out elsewhere. These cookies are dairy-free, and it appears they may even be vegan.UNBLEACHED ENRICHED FLOUR (WHEAT FLOUR, NIACIN, REDUCED IRON, THIAMINE MONONITRATE (VITAMIN B1), RIBOFLAVIN (VITAMIN B2), FOLIC ACID), SUGAR, WHOLE GRAIN WHEAT FLOUR, SOYBEAN AND/OR PALM OIL, ROLLED OATS, DRIED CRANBERRIES, FRUCTOSE, SALT, BAKING SODA, SOY LECITHIN, NATURAL FLAVOR.Allergens and Nutritional Considerations: Added Sugars, Gluten, Soy, Wheat

column9: Tastes yummy, but where did nutrition go?
column10: Cranberry Citrus Oat Newton Fruit ThinsThese are very pleasant.  They are similar to a graham cracker but they are a littly chewier and sweetier (though not extremely sweet).  The citrus and cranberry flavors are a very good combination.  We have purchased more.What disappointments me is the nutrition information.  I expect something with cranberries and citrus to have a little more nutritional value than this.  4% Iron and 1% Potassium is all the vitamin and mineral content described (unless you want to count Sodium, which thankfully is only 4%).  Where did vitamin C go -- the heat probably killed it, right?  The ingredients list B vitamin enrichment but the nutritional information doesn't list it leaving me wondering with the vitamins were killed by heat in the cooking process (in which case why bother) or whether they just think no one cares that they are there (we do, but I have to believe it isn't there since it isn't listed in the nutritional information).

column9: Delicious and a relatively healthy snack
column10: Made with whole grains, these fruit thins are a relatively healthier choice if you're looking to satisfy a sweet tooth.  They have a crunchy, crumbly texture.  The taste is something like a butter cookie/ animal cracker/ nilla wafer, with a hint of refreshing orange flavor, and chewy pieces of cranberry sprinkled throughout.  It was enough to satisfy my sweet tooth, but they were also enjoyed by my husband, who typically isn't that fond of sweets.  The sweet taste of the cookie contrasts nicely with the very subtle tartness of the cranberries.  It was nice to enjoy something other than the same old, same old cookies, and these disappeared quickly in our house!

I liked the taste of these cookies overall, although cranberries were a little hard to chew on. I however have to say that half of the cookies in the box came crushed when I opened it and I seriously doubt that it was a post office, when I take cookie or two with me for lunch, it is crushed when I get it out of my bag.

Three of these cookies are 140 calories, but more importantly, since I'm perpetually on diet, these actually taste good.  They remind me of shortbread cookies, even having a somewhat buttery taste, but you don't get the calories, plus, OMG, they don't even have any cholesterol.  Unbelievably to me, three of these cookies supposedly provide 4 percent of your daily iron.  Of the ingredients that I can pronounce, they are made with unbleached enriched wheat flour, sugar (no wonder they taste good), soybean and/or palm oil, rolled oats, whole grain wheat flour, dried cranberries (which are plentiful and will get stuck in your teeth), fructose, salt, and baking soda.  If you are in search of the 100-calorie snack that satisfies, this one will.  I was also thinking that crumbled up, these would make an excellent cream pie crust, but ... !

I have, in the past bunch of years, tried many different breakfast/snack bars/squares/thins. Even those that I find tasty usually turns tiring and stale - in short, no staying power.  I tried this new Newtons Fruit Thins and it is surprisingly good. It has a consistency of graham crackers (maybe not as crunchy - it's made partly with whole grain), but with a mildly sweet taste of cranberries.  It's not too heavy or sugary and not too plain, like saltine crackers.  I've tried it for a few days now and I have not gotten tired of taste yet. In the world of snack food, this is a little gem. No high fructose or corn syrup to boot.

The best way I can describe the taste of these cookies is that they are very similar to the flavor of the Starbucks Cranberry scone that you would buy in their stores.Strong cranberry notes, sweet but not too sweet, hint of citrus, and sort of a crunchy yet fibery texture. The texture is like someone crossed a Girl Guides Peanut Butter cookie with a shortbread cookie.  Additionally some chewiness is added by the cranberry pieces  which seem right in proportion (not too much, not too few).This isn't an indulgence cookie, more of what I would call a snack or breakfast cookie.  Tasty if this is what your looking for in a cookie.

Is it a cracker?  Is it a cookie?  Is it a Newton?  The correct answer?  All of the above!  I was surprised at the amount of flavor in the Newtons Fruit Thins.  Perfect with coffee or on the go, these tasty treats are perfect for that pick me up snack at any time of day.  A serving of three Fruit Thins is 140 calories, so this is really a better choice than most of those pre-packaged "100 calorie" snacks.  I would give this snack five stars, but like one of the photos demonstrates, many of the crisps had broken in transit.  All in all, a great crispy, sweet treat.

column4: ChibiNeko "Sooo many books, so little time!"
column9: Not really a huge fan of these
column10: I ended up bringing these in to work to sample & my coworkers (who are able to sniff out treats a mile away) ended up eating some as well. The overall consensus was that these were "OK" but generally most didn't really care too much for these. My opinion is as follows:PROS: Healthier than eating some of the other cookies on the market, has a decent taste when it's present.CONS: The cranberry was a little too chewy at times, which was kind of a little annoying. Even worse than that is occasionally the cookies were pretty bland tasting. I don't know if I got a bad batch or if it's just me, but these just didn't have a lot of flavor. (However, the blueberry ones I also got to try had a lot of flavor, so it's possible I just got an underseasoned batch.)These weren't horrible, but I don't think I'll be putting my own money towards this flavor anytime soon. When the cookies had a flavor I could taste, they were pretty good. It's just that these were sort of bland tasting that makes me not really like them as much. I might give them another chance somewhere down the line, but offhand I'm going to stick to the blueberry flavor. These were just "OK" & that's about all I can say for them.

column9: C+ Concensus on Crispy Cranberry Cookie
column10: First impression: meh. I sampled a few more, and the flavor kind of grew on me. You can taste all the ingredients you're supposed to notice--oats, cranberries, a little hint of citrus. Then I tried it with my coffee, and it was GOOD.I think that's the key--other reviewers have noted that tea or coffee goes great with this snack. It's not something you can mindlessly shove into your mouth while watching reality shows, not that I ever do that, but if you need a little treat in the afternoon, it's tasty with a cup of joe.The cranberries made this chewy, which was a nice combination (like pinwheel cookies). Putting two textures together can be tricky, and if not done correctly, is a real turn-off for me. But here the crunchy/chewy textures enhance each other.My family tasted these, as well. One of my kids liked the cookie but thought the calorie count a little high for a serving of three (140 calories). Not a big deal, but if you're going for the health-conscious crowd, that may be a little too steep. Other household members said these cookies were average, but then they lean toward big gooey chocolate desserts.So try these--but don't forget to fire up Mr. Coffee first.

When it has came down to the newtons family over the years, they've really made some fantastic cookies and snacks over the years, from fig newtons to blueberry. For their latest products, they've decided to make it thin cookies. But is the taste strong with this one, yes and no. The new Newtons Fruit Thins, Cranberry Citrus Oats taste pretty good. It has a simple blend of cranberry, with the mist of orange into the taste of the cookie. While it does taste good, I do honestly wish that there was more zest into the cookies, but it is better than most lackluster snacks that've came out recently. Hopefully, there can be a more newtons cookies like this soon.Price: BTaste: B 1/2-Overall: B 1/2-

I shared these with my co-workers to get a wider range opinion. There were 8 people trying them. There was 3 - 5 stars, 1 - 4 star, and 4 - 3 stars. Overall most everyone enjoyed them. The ones that gave 3 stars said they were good but not anything outstanding. The only complaint were a couple people found the cranberries to be a bit hard and sticky. They said it was like chewing on a sucker. Most liked the crispness of it. Ones who liked the Newton bars didn't like the thins as much and ones who didn't like the bars liked the thins better.Overall, I would have to say it was a good cookie. Most of the group came back for more than one. It's a nice light treat.

What I liked about this product was first, the way it was packaged.  Inside there are several rows of thin cookies in a plastic tray.  You can grab to your heart's content.  When eaten, the cookie and the bits of fruit blend and make a great taste.The only qualm is the package wire on the top.  It is not really easy to close and that may need to be redesigned.  But the product itself is tasty and I can't get enough of the bits of fruit.  What a good idea!

column9: light and crisp with just the right amount of sweet fruit
column10: These new Newtons Fruit Thins are delicious. They have a really natural fruit flavor, and the texture is very light and crisp. Perfect for a snack, because they are not too sweet like so many other cookies. I think they are especially good with a cup of tea. They are my new favorite because they are not overly sweet but have a real fruit taste.

column9: Oatmeal with a Touch of Fruit
column10: My first impression was of oatmeal cookie and a little like a shortbread cookie.  The cookies are pretty flat (1/8" thick) but dense. The fruit tastes like dried fruit so you get a taste of chewy cranberry fruit in between the cookie taste. I'll post the nutrition information above but there are about 45 calories per cookie and about a third of those calories are from fat. Probably the most notable thing about these cookies are how filling they are. After 3 or 4 cookies I feel satisfied. A good snack before or after a workout. The label says "cranberry citrus oat" and I can't help but think that the addition of a little orange zest/peel would make these even better. I'll try the fig flavor next since that's what I think of when I see "Newtons" on the label.

column9: Too Many Broken Cookies and Fruit Too Chewy
column10: Received this product and upon opening the package, I found over 30 percent of the cookies or fruit thins broken. They were broken into two pieces and some were smashed into many pieces. I found the taste to be OK, but the fruit content was of the consistency of "gummy bears" and tended to be excessively chewy and to stick to my teeth. The product had a sugary taste and a crumbly consistency. The Thins were easily broken. This is not a product that I would purchase again. Other Nabisco cookie products and the famous Fig Newtons are superior in flavor and durability. The packaging was not strong enough to protect the product. You can see images which I will post on the main product page.Thin and easily broken product ought to be packaged in stronger boxes and not in flimsy plastic trays and paper bags. I gave a 2 star rating because of mediocre taste, poor mouth feel and flimsy packaging.  But, in fairness, the Vine product was shipped as an individual bag inside a larger shipping box with only two pieces of bubble pack so it is possible it rattled around and pieces of cookies broke.  The full size multi-pack that one would receive on a regular order should not suffer as much in transit.

column4: LaughingLion "I am Lion, read me review!"
column10: I like the flavor, its smooth without being overpowering. A little sweet, and a touch grainy. Very nice overall but possibly designed for the cookie dunkers out there and a little bit dry.Great treat over all, packaging is tough enough that none of them were broken when I opened the pack shipped to me.

This delicious goodness comes directly to us from a name we've grown to love. Nabisco!Remembering the gooey rich flavor of Fig Newton's when growing up, I simply had to discover if something with the name "Newtons" could be as good!I was pleasantly surprised to discover that Newtons Fruit Thins are absolutely amazing!As part of the Amazon Vine program, I received the Cranberry Citrus Oat cookie thins. When paired with either hot tea or coffee, these little bites of goodness absolutely came alive! Pleasant also was the fact that 3 cookie crisps were 140 calories, 22g of carbs, 5g fat, 2g of protein and a low 95mg of sodium! That makes these the perfect snack for the dieter or weight watcher as well as those who can liberally imbibe in them!Each package contains about 30 cookie crisps.Best of all? Even the grandchildren love 'em!I highly recommend these for your next coffee date or tea!****DISCLOSURE: As a member of the Amazon Vine program, I was provided with product for review.

When you say newton,I think of fig newtons, the cake like concotion with the fig filling.  These cookies bear no resemblance to their softer anscesters. Thin and crisp they are studded with dried cranberries.  The tang of the cranberries is delightful against the orange crisp.  Made with oats and whole grains, they are not too sweet and surprisingly refreshing.The cookies are placed in a plastic tray in a foil lined bag with an attached wire tie.  They stayed crisp after opening.  There are about thirty cookies to a package.  My package arrived with about four cookies broken into pieces.I have been trying to integrate more whole grains and fruit into my diet and this is an easy way to do it.  Light, crispy and tasty they provide a refreshing respite from the super sugary gook that populates grocery shelves.  While not health food, they are certainly a healthier alternative.  I would buy again.

column9: Tasty but Those Troublesome Dried Fruit
column10: Envision [whole grain] animal cracker cookie dough with dehydrated cranberries mixed into it. Now, shape into oversized Ritz cracker shapes and bake. That nails down my impression of both texture and flavor on these - whole grain animal crackers with cranberries. I suppose I can detect that citrus essence on the crackers upon placement on the tongue as well.So I do find these edible...kind of tasty too when I've got the craving. I'm not too crazy about the occasional dehydrated cranberry getting stuck behind my back teeth though - that's really my only negative about these otherwise well-flavored thins.

column9: A low-sugar, high-flavor snack. I'm in love!!!!!!
column10: I am always on the lookout for a pre-bedtime snack that won't load me up with sugar or caffeine. These are actually pretty large, so if you eat just half a serving (1.5 wafers), you've got only 3.5 grams of sugar and 70 calories. Just enough to make you feel satisfied and keep you away from the box of Oreos.The taste is great---just a tad sweeter than a cracker, with chopped up dried cranberries to add some interest to the texture (and again, to make you feel like you are having more of a dessert than a cracker, so your mind doesn't scream for ice cream).These are obviously drier than fig newtons, so you'll probably want a glass of milk or a cup of tea. I can't wait to try the other flavors. Heavenly!!!

column9: Lighty Sweet, Crisp/Chewy at the Same Time, and Great for Kids
column10: When I first heard about Newtons Fruit Thins, I was under the impression that these cookies would be soft like the traditional Newtons.  However, these Fruit Thins are nice and crunchy without being hard, and have little chewy bits of dried cranberries sprinkled throughout.  The taste was hard for me to pinpoint at first - it doesn't really taste citrusy - the closest thing I can compare it to is to a non spiced gingerbread.  It may seem bland to some people, however, I found that the lightly sweet taste was just right for me - I'm not particularly fond of overly sweetened cookies. If I had a choice of choosing between these and the traditional Newtons, I would definitely pick these!The best part about Newtons Fruit Thins is that they're great for kids.  My two toddlers couldn't get enough of these cookies!  Both of them love dried cranberries and crunchy snacks, and I love the fact that when they ate it, it didn't crumble and get bits and pieces of cookie everywhere.  Two cookies were about enough for each of them.  When paired with a glass of milk and some apple slices, it made for a nice snack!The bag is easily resealable, and there are lot of these cookies in there...but they will go fast!  Highly recommended!

I've never reviewed a food before. So this'll be really interesting. I'm going to start by saying that these cookies are DELICIOUS. I'm always nervous of fruit in cookies because it can often be really rubbery and gross, but Fruit Thins have just the right amount of real fruit and graham-cookie base to be absolutely wonderful. I can't get enough of them! Which bring me to my next point:Just because Nabisco has called these FRUIT THINS, you should not be deceived. Just to check, I compared a serving of Fruit Thins (30g) to a serving of Chips Ahoy classic cookies (32g).CHIPS AHOY:Calories: 160Fat: 8gSugars: 10gProtein: 2gVitamin A: 0%, C: 0%, Calcium: 0%, Iron: 4%FRUIT THINS:Calories: 140Fat: 5gSugars: 7gProtein: 2gVitamin A: 0%, C: 0%, Calcium: 0%, Iron: 4%So for certain, Fruit Thins have less fat, calories, and sugar. But a lot? No. Just because the cookies are called Fruit THINS, don't be thinking that you won't gain weight if you're constantly snacking on them. Like everything, they should be eaten in moderation. The cookies themselves are very thin (perhaps that's what the name refers to) but they are still COOKIES.I'll end by repeating that these are DELICIOUS. The cranberry citrus flavor adds a wonderfully original spark to the classic graham cookie. If you're looking for treat that you can feel [a little bit] less guilty about eating, this is the one for you.And now I'm off to eat a few.

I grew up on the Classic Fig Newtons and still love them to this day. These Newtons take the soft, chewy fruit cookie in the opposite direction with the perfect amount of snap and crunch. The combination of cranberry and citrus with vanilla/oat overtones make a delicious combination. My favorite way to enjoy these is with a cup of coffee. I think they have a new classic on their hands. Can't wait to try the other flavors.

I love margaritas, but I hate all the calories. Was excited to hear about the new Skinny margarita by Bethenny.  Tried it, and UGH--so disappointing.  If you like really salty tasting drinks, then you will like it, but it didn't taste like a margaria to me, and it was very salty.  Next I tried the skinny cal-o-rita and was so pleasantly surpised!  No salty taste--a little tart, but I had mine with lots of ice, used tequila to mix it with, and it was delicious!  For such a low calorie yummy cocktail, I am hooked.  Am ordering more right now.

I have been using sugar alcohols and stevia is various things for a while now. When I saw this online with all the great reviews I was so excited. However, when I received the product and tried it, I was gravely disappointed. It tastes artificial with lots of aftertaste. In my opinion, it does not in anyway taste like sugar. I did appreciate the small packet to try it before I wasted all that tequila in the powder and water as instructed. I thought there was such high shipping cost because it was a liquid and then what a surprise when I got it that it is a powder in an empty bottle. I would never have ordered it if I knew that upfront. I really want to return it but because it was such a large cost for shipping and then I have to pay the shipping back, it would really not be worth it so I'll just suck it up and throw it away!!!

I have not had any of this tea yet as it only arrived today. I was told by the company that I would receive a ten percent pay back if I left feedback. It was packaged pretty, however, it is NOT a lot of tea and it was expensive, especially considering the shipping and handling. I am going to be one ticked off mommy if this tea does NOT alleviate the itchiness that I am getting from eczema as that is my SOLE reason for ordering this product. If if doesn't I will be back to amend this review.

My kids (18 mo and 3 yrs) love the HappyBaby Tots.  We have tried every flavor and they eat all of them.  I love that they are getting good, organic nutrition, and that the ingredients are wholesome.  They are very convenient to throw in your diaper bag or purse on-the-go, or to stick in a lunch box for a snack.  We use a spoon and sometimes a bowl at home for self feeding with my little one, but you can also give the pouch to them to eat directly from the squeeze pouch.  Thank you, HappyBaby, for such great products!!

My kids (18 mo and 3 yrs) love the HappyBaby Tots.  We have tried every flavor and they eat all of them.  This is one of my favorite flavors, because how often do kids get beets otherwise?  I love that they are getting good, organic nutrition, and that the ingredients are wholesome.  They are very convenient to throw in your diaper bag or purse on-the-go, or to stick in a lunch box for a snack.  We use a spoon and sometimes a bowl at home for self feeding with my little one, but you can also give the pouch to them to eat directly from the squeeze pouch.  Thank you, HappyBaby, for such great products!!
this is so easy on the go!  I typically make my own food for my little one but this makes it so easy when we are out running errands!  my baby loves it!

column9: Great organic on the go snack
column10: My daughter, who is in preschool, loves these Happy Baby organic pouches-her tops flavor are the apple-cherry, pear, mango, banana kiwi.  They are perfect chilled and very nutrient dense.  Easy to throw in bag as the package is soft and BPA free.

My 8 month old son loves these. I keep one in my purse at all times. He is breastfeed and we make his other solid foods (cook, puree and freeze)--but this is what I use when we're out so that I don't have to worry about microwaving or his fresh food going bad from being out too long. He really likes this flavor and I'm happy because it includes three foods that I haven't been making for him. I'm trying to introduce him to all the fruits and vegetables that are OK for him to eat at this age, and I'm hoping that eating the spinach in this will make him less likely to reject it later... Only downside that I can think of is that these are rather watery. Not sure if that is solved if you move to the Stage 3 ones.
My 10-month-old LOVES these and my 3 yr old even sneaks bites from them! They both think they are really tasty, and I feel good feeding them an organic product. I would DEFINITELY buy these again.

My 8 month old isn't quite capable of sucking the food out of those things yet, but if I squeeze it out into a bowl and spoonfeed her, she LOVES them! Mommy thinks they're rather tasty too ;) I felt like it was great value for our money, as we will be using these on vacation to lighten our loads (versus glass jars) but they're not cheap enough to buy for everyday use. I normally make my own baby food.

column9: Great product, just a little pricey compared to other baby food
column10: If you want/need convenience, this item is fabulous!  We always rate the organic baby food pouches high and our only concern is the price.  We find the pouches great for taking to restaurants, in the car, on picnics, to the zoo, etc.  Also, it continues to be an easy way to get super foods into our toddlers without the preparation of the fruits and vegetables!  We still keep them on hand even after the baby food days are gone.

column9: Baby loves it, its a little liquidy though
column10: This is a fine product.  My daughter eats it right up and seems to enjoy it.  I will say however that it is very liquidy (no texture) so I have more drips when feeding her.  I wish it were a bit more solid in texture (I really like Plum Baby Food due to the texture).  Again, daughter loves it.

I love this baby food for my baby and I like that it is as affordable as the Gerber, preservative laden non-organic baby food when purchased on subscribe and save through Amazon. It tastes fresh and good and I like how the packaging is created to be convenient on the go. I always have these packets of food in my purse with the little screw on spoons in case my little one gets hungry while we're out.

column4: R. Mastromauro "Loving life as a Mom"
column10: I got my son used to these a a young age, and if it weren't for them, I'm not so sure he'd get as many veggies as he does.  Somedays he will have some veggies, and he eats fruits with no problem, but I'm always looking for snacks that incorporate veggies and these are great, especially before a meal as a late snack, or after lunch as an afternoon snack.

column9: A must have for the diaper bag!
column10: My 9 month old started eating this flavor at about 7 months old and loves it!  She isn't really a picky eater, but she likes some things more than others.  When its time for the spinach/mango/pear she takes one tastes then asks for more!  I've tasted it, its pretty good.  The only reason it doesn't get 5 stars is because the consistency is a bit watery and difficult to keep on the spoon when feeding the baby.  I'd love it if they just didn't puree it quite as much or didn't add quite so much water, then it would be perfect.
he loves the flavor..i tried one from the market to make sure he likes it.i get it on amazon now..its good price and alwasy have them on the go...they are great
My son loves the purees in the pouches, except this one is way too tart.  He took one sip, made a funny face and handed it back to me!
My 13 months old son generally liked the concept of eating by himself but not this combination of beet, berry and banana. It tastes sour probably

Anyone who has a child that refuses veggies should try this! It's a great combo of fruit and veggies- and so easy to feed to older babies- my daughter feeds herself and NO mess! It's great for on the go. Love them!
This actually tastes really good.  All my kids (ages 6,5 and 22 months) love these.  I just throw one in my bag and give to the baby.  No need to carry a spoon.  It's a healthy little snack for all.

This flavor is great, I love the fact it has veggies and fruit together. I gave this flavor to my 6 month old baby and he loved it. If you have problem with this blend being to runny I solved it by using Boon spoon or Plum organics boon spoons for pouches which made it breeze to feed the baby.My son loves all the other flavors he tried as well ( pear; pear & peas & broccoli; apples & cherry; banana & blueberries & beats ), he did not like sweet potato & apricot flavor, it was too tart and sour for him, but I contacted Happy Baby customer service and the next batch should have more sweet potato to help with the sour taste, but if you can buy just one pack and try it you might have a baby that likes it either way.Most of all I love the packaging, it is perfect since we travel a lot and it is so much lighter then glass jars and easier to pack as well.

We tried this flavor when my son was almost 6 months and he wouldn't eat it. It is too sour even for me. I have talked to customer service and they had complains from other people and the next batch will have more sweet potato in so it should taste better. I will give it try again when the new batch is out. Otherwise my son loved all the other flavors we tried so far ( pear, mango&spinach&pear, Pear&peas&broccoli, apple&cherry, banana&beat&blueberries ). So try one before ordering bunch on Amazon.The pouch idea is great, so easy to travel with! Some of the flavors are little runny but I am using Boon spoon and it works great. I am also going to try out the Plum organic Boon spoon for pouches, should fit Happy baby pouches as well.

I start giving these flavor to my son when he was 5,5 months and he loves it. Great mix of veggies and fruit that isn't too sweet. The pouches are great, we travel a lot and spend lot of time in our second home in Costa Rica and these are very easy and much lighter then glass jars to bring with us.My so likes all the flavors he tried so far ( pear, mango&spinach&pear, apple&cherry, banana&beat&blueberry ) he didn't like apricot&sweet potato it was too sour for him, but I heard that the next one should have more sweet potato so it should not be as sour anymore.... have to wait to see when the new batch is out.

This is another one of my daughter's favorite snacks.  She seems to prefer the varieties with pears in them, and I do like that is is getting some spinach and that she actually likes it!  She does prefer the Peas, Broccoli, & Pear flavor, but this is also a favorite.  The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the smell of the mango can be pretty overpowering.  I like fresh mango, but for some reason the smell of mango baby food is just awful to me!  Other than that, a good product that I'll be ordering again.

I've tried a few of these fruit and veggie squeeze packs (for my toddler primarily) in a few different brands.  This is the only flavor she didn't like.  She did try it, but gave it back to me after one bite.  Later, I tried to feed it to my baby with her oatmeal, and she didn't like it either!  I am a little surprised, since sweet potatoes are her favorite.  Maybe if your kids like apricot they will like this flavor, but mine didn't.  We'll be sticking with the Pears, Peas, & Broccoli flavor.

I originally bought this after my toddler had tried some squeeze pack apple sauce and enjoyed the novelty of it.  She likes applesauce anyway, but I thought I might be able to get her to eat some veggies if I could find them in a squeeze pouch too.  This fruit and veggie mix is perfect -- she gets some green veggies, but it really does taste just like pears!  I've tried several flavors, and this is her favorite by far.  My baby is starting solids now and she likes this one too.

column9: Easy, convenient, organic - pay for convenience
column10: As far as flavor, our boys really like these!  We like to keep organic pouches on hand for things like restaurants, traveling, and quick healthy snacks while preparing their meals.  The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is the price, but like anything, you pay for convenience.  We have gotten good deals on Amazon though, just wait for a good price then stock up!
My six month old cannot get enough of this food. He prefers it over the other pouch items by far!!!  I love the mix of veggies and fruits.  So easy to travel with as well.

These are the best! They may be a little more expensive then regular applesauce in a cup but it is so worth it when your kids (any age) suck them down one after another and you have NO mess to clean up. They don't even know they are healthly!

column9: Even my husband says it tastes good
column10: My husband said this Happy Baby flavor is really good.  I love the mixture of fruit and veggie.  If you haven't tried this company before, you are in for a real treat.  The food is delicious, and it is never too sweet or fake tasting.

Another great flavor from Happy Baby.  The first one I got, I shared with my daughter because it is so tasty.  It is a nice cherry flavor, not fake or too sweet.  These pouches are great for babies who can use straws.

My 5.5 yr old son LOVES apricots and sweet potatoes so I was excited to try this flavor. I tried a sample package sold at Target and it tasted pretty good so I ordered a bunch online. He took one taste of this batch and handed it right back to me. I tasted it and whoa- it is SUUUUUPER SOUR - much more so than the one I tried at the store!?!? It gave me goosebumps! Wha???? I now wonder if they changed the recipe, started using unripe apricots or I mistakenly bought the wrong brand of this combo??? I'll have to try mixing it with some applesauce in a GU bottle or try to add it to my baked sweet potatoe/apple dish so it's not a total waste of money. Beware of this flavor!
My daughter loves this flavor and the pouch makes it so easy to use on the go.  She doesn't need a spoon, just drinks it from the pouch. Thank you Happybaby!
My son loves these.  They're very tasty (yes I tried it) and I love that they're organic and have some veggies as well as fruit in the easy to use smoothie!

This food is tart, I was surprised.  I guess it is good because so much baby food is so sweet.  My daughter still likes it, though.  I wish Happy Baby had more food in these kinds of packets, as she can eat them right out of the container by herself at 10 months.

I bought this for my 15 month old son who has become a VERY picky eater.  I wanted a fun and easy way to make sure he gets his fruit and vegetable servings each day.  This does NOT do the trick!  He took one suck, made a horrible face, and has refused it since.  I tried it thinking it couldn't be THAT bad.  It was.  Terribly bitter (just the thought makes my mouth water) and runny.  No wonder he wouldn't eat it.  I wouldn't either!  I did buy some of the other varieties offered by HappyBaby and he loves them.  I think this is just a bad taste combo.  Yuck!

column9: Very sour but baby loves it
column10: This is probably my toddler's favorite pouch.  I have to admit, there's a lot of lemon juice in this mix, which makes the pouch somewhat sour.  My toddler loves lemons though so this is just exactly his taste.  If you're unsure whether your baby likes sour, don't buy this in bulk - it's probably for an acquired taste! :)

This is such a great product.  My son loves it and I just put it in the diaper bag when we are in a rush to leave the house and have a healthy snack for the way.  I tasted it and thought it was good.  great help for moms on the move.

My children love the happy baby organics. I just wish they had more of a selection on Amazon. I have tried the food, as I try everything before giving it to my kids, and they taste great. I highly recommend it to any mom that wants their children to eat organic. It is easy to use, easy to travel with, and healthy for them!

My one year old can actually "drink" these right from the package, using the spout like a straw, which makes these a super convenient option to have for snacks when we're out and about--no bib or spoon needed. He has food allergies, so finding processed foods that meet his needs and are still healthy and conveninent can be tough. He has loved all of the Happy Baby products we've tried. The multi-packs are a great deal and it is nice to be able to stock up this way instead of just buying singles from the only store around here that carries them.

I found these at Target a few months back and decided to give them a try for my dairy/soy allergic one year old son. It is tough finding on-the-go food options for him that meet with his dietary needs and satisfy my pickiness for healthy kids food. The deals for the multi-packs are great. My little one is old enough now that with a bit of help, he can just suck the food straight from the "spout" of the package like a straw and he LOVES them. He gets so excited when he sees me pull one out and they are so easy to throw in a purse or diaper bag so that I always have a good snack for him with me, no bib or utensils needed.

column4: Cat In The Hat "twin happy mom"
column9: Tasty & Nutritious in one easy to administer pouch!
column10: My 15 month-old twin boys aren't big fans of spinach, but they LOVE these pouches. This is a great combination with the mangos and pears and you can still taste the spinach. Anytime my boys need a quick snack, I whip out one of these pouches and can be assured they are getting their fiber, vitamins, and nutrients.  Also try the Beets, Blueberries, and Banana combo!!!These pouches are especially helpful during teething time or when your babies get to the 'picky eater' stage. For the teethers, it's been helpful for us to place a few pouches in the fridge. For the picky eaters, we administer a swig of this inbetween bites and we can cram in a few more bites. These pouches are much better than giving pure juice and aren't messy. If you do give them the pouches to eat on their own, just be wary that they may squeeze too hard and up comes all of the food. The screw on top helps if they don't finish it all. Just place it into the fridge for the next day or later and if you're out, pace it back into your diaper bag with a cold pack. No yucky jar top taste, no spoons to mess around with, and the combinations are tasty.  Just make sure your little one doesn't place the tops in their mouths.  Mine have done that a couple of times but with all the advantages of these pouches, I can keep an eye on the top a bit more.With the subscribe and save through Amazon, it's so much more cost saving than purchasing these in the stores.

column4: Cat In The Hat "twin happy mom"
column9: Great, tasty nutrients in one easy to deliver pouch!
column10: Beets!!!  How many of you out there have babies/toddlers/kids who eat beets?  Well, mine aren't big fans but they LOVE these pouches.  This is a great combination with the blueberries and bananas and you can still taste the beets.  Anytime my 15 month-old twin boys need a quick snack, I whip out one of these pouches and can be assured they are getting their antioxidants and nutrients.It's especially helpful during teething time or when your babies get to the 'picky eater' stage.  For the teethers, it's helpful to place a few pouches in the fridge.  For the picky eaters, it's helpful for us to administer a swig of this inbetween bites.  These pouches are much better than giving pure juice and aren't messy.  If you do give them the pouches to eat on their own, just be wary that they may squeeze too hard and up comes all of the food.  The screw on top helps if they don't finish it all.  Just place it into the fridge for the next day or later or if you're out, pace it back into your diaper bag with a cold pack.  No yucky jar top taste, no spoons to mess around with, and the combinations are tasty.With the subscribe and save, it's so much more cost saving than purchasing these in the stores.

My toddler LOVES these!!!  She begs for them the moment we get into the car when I pick her up from preschool.  The only hard this is that she can't open the cap by herself (which I don't mind, or else, she's "break into them").  The cap is also resealable, which is nice in case.  I highly recommend these. I used to buy Ella's Kitchen Organic Smoothies and baby food pouches, but they are WAY more expensive!  The taste is just as great!  Buy these!

The last couple of days, my son has been more of a fussy eater.  We even gave him pizza and he had a few bites and was frustrated by bite 5 or 6.  These had just come in the mail and I cracked one open.  He HOUSED the whole pack! That's a lot to be said for a child who eats a couple ounces at a time!  If I need a failsafe food, this flavor combination has done it!  5 Stars ALL THE WAY!
